Common multiplier

Make certified common-multiplier repair more useful through four investigations: a complete geometric application with protected survival and explicit costs; structural joint-error savings beyond summed ranks; effective homological and localization bounds for surviving annihilators; and a hardness-preserving extension with efficient extraction of a hard object. Pursue them in that order, preserving the Braun/Pang theorem and all foundational bridges.

Starting point

User-directed Common multiplier investigation. Braun's affine-block elimination and Pang's relative approximation-error annihilation motivate this thread. It is separate from the interrupted main-notebook IPS cycle. Braun's construction and the recorded Pang audit retain their original scopes.

Where we stand

The geometric application is complete; three objectives remain open. Marked curve recovery constructs a locator from unknown errors, recovers the message and fixes its value at a protected point. The explicit Hermitian family has unbounded positive genus, supplies its bases and points, and meets the complete pole and construction budgets. It applies established decoding.

Joint-error savings is open. Overlapping curve recovery gives one protected common locator below the summed-rank budget, but its saving is inclusion–exclusion of supports. Exact common-kernel selection lets composition's selection use any certificate of the exact stacked-rank criterion. For Braun's kernel step, shared-span exclusion gains only by domination, increment counts by at most \((d+k)/k\), and a ceiling bounds every certificate; on coordinate blocks the summed count reaches its main term, the Harris certificate never beats the greedy transversal or the count as computed, and small inventories (every prime) gain only at polynomial degree. In Pang's contraction, where the summed count sets the degree, the domain-only stacked rank is a union-of-supports rank, and domain-model savings need not survive in a proper quotient (correction). The goal review found the pigeonhole evidence a domain model: below degree \(n\) the product pigeon axioms are inert, these systems are never proper above it, single-input killers are supports, and their joint kernels are one annihilator (factor ideal domination). In the functional pigeonhole system at six and seven pigeons, where linear axioms act, the common kernels at \(K=1\) are still the frame's plus the relations (constructed kernels); transported killers are an instance of factor span domination, no stronger for survival than a direct common killer, and for Pang's errors the direct product of family killers has degree linear in the number of families, against Pang's multiplier of degree \(K\). Refining Pang's families singly or in one round need not shrink their joint rank (marginal refinement); at his full degree one native functional detects his stacked kernel when \((p-1)K\le\Delta+d\) (native detection), beyond his largest slack the count grows with \(n\) on the cube (lower bound), the same modulo the product system's top degree (native count), and on cube block families his criterion misses a transversal degree; module repairs certified linearly are scalar, so are multilinear ones certified along multiplication, cancelling product errors save repair degree on the cube, not on matchings, and twists split into substitutions. Inert-range kernels are restriction ranks. For effective-annihilator-degree (goal review), on the cube the first surviving killer degree of monomial errors is a transversal number; on product domains it is the cylinder transversal number, and at the top degree of the product pigeonhole system monomial errors gain nothing from the pigeon axioms (transfer). Graded duality pairs only cubes and bounds proper closures by leading forms; in domain models block-local errors have additive least killer degree, and a proper-closure test found no killer beyond the domain's.

Completed foundation. Certified repair composition remains the reviewed working theorem explaining Braun and Pang with original costs. No curve-error PC interpretation or circuit bound follows.

Route decisions. Pursue four priorities in order: geometric application, joint-error savings, effective homology and localization, then hardness-preserving repair. The user requires all four; completing an initial subset does not complete the goal. The order stands (the transfer review restored it after one cycle); the survival review reads the line's target as survival where summed ranks fail (the user may reverse this); its test found no linear joint killer. Both homology and localization require substantive development with separately recorded outcomes. Every research entry retains the Selection gain duty: identify an independently proved selection, survival or hardness-preservation improvement, or say unchanged. All six foundational bridges remain preserved.

Open statements

  1. Geometric application — resolved as a working proof. Marked curve recovery and the Hermitian family supply independent locator, detection and survival certificates, unknown-error recovery and explicit construction on unbounded positive-genus instances. The pole filtration and rational-function evaluation are specified. This application of established decoding does not settle the remaining objectives.
  2. Joint-error savings — open; second priority. Give independently checkable structural hypotheses and an all-parameter bound on the joint action of actual errors, strictly better than the sum of their individual ranks on a nontrivial unbounded family. Measure every rank in the same protected quotient and show that the saving improves a sufficient multiplier budget or admissible instance range after all composition costs. Duplicating errors, changing coordinates or merely representing the same kernel does not meet this endpoint. Nor does union-of-supports counting in an evaluation model, nor domination, the common kernel being the annihilator of one element of the window (factor ideal domination), nor a span of products of killers of individual factors, whose degree grows with the number of distinct factors (goal review, which flags this last exclusion as a change of target). The domination clause is read as a mechanism, over any field (selection review): excluded is a proof that only exhibits the common kernel as one element's annihilator; principality over an extension (principal kernels) excludes nothing by itself.
  3. Effective homology and localization — open; third priority. Develop both bridges toward a structural theorem bounding the first filtered degree of an annihilator that preserves a specified nonzero class, or constructing a strictly cheaper useful certificate on an unbounded family. Verify the hypotheses, nilpotent behavior and total costs in a faithful model, and show the consequence for repair. Identifying a Hom or Koszul cohomology space, or clearing finitely many denominators without a useful cost bound, does not resolve this obligation. An obstruction closes only the formulation it actually rules out; it does not count as completing the other bridge.
  4. Hardness-preserving repair — open; fourth priority. Extend certified repair with independently verified structural conditions yielding an efficient extraction of a specified hard object from every eligible repaired proof image or certificate. Prove the resulting circuit lower-bound transfer in a stated field and circuit model, with explicit size, depth, degree and representation overhead. Supply a nontrivial unbounded application. Nonzero survival, one hard certificate, an assumed hard output or uncosted division by the multiplier does not suffice.

Completed original obligations. Effective repair principle and portable composition are resolved for the original sufficient endpoint by certified repair composition. External application was resolved through established error-correcting pairs, with finite-grid repair adding a domain extension. These stable anchors preserve earlier links; the new goal does not retract those results.

The remaining route

  1. Effective homology and localization now. The goal review switched cycles here, since the functional pigeonhole test found only the three excluded kinds. Seek an explicit bound on the first useful surviving annihilator degree or a cheaper independently constructed certificate, retaining nilpotent behavior and the protected class. Killer degrees are now exact in domain models; the route review adopted a sandwich: killing in the domain sub-closure, survival in the proper closure through a normal form; at \(K=2\) on two functional pigeonhole boards the test found no killer beyond the domain's (conjectured at every proper degree), so survival is the open half. Record each approach's outcome separately.
  2. Joint-error savings next, restored by the transfer review. Every saving found is a union of supports, domination by one annihilator, or a product of killers, and in domain models with monomial supports every killer is a product of literal killers. Savings modulo a closure are bounded above by the domain's (saving monotonicity), so the goal review works through survival: a common killer outside the proper closure where the summed condition fails, which feeds exact selection; its test found no linear pigeon-axiom killer of two Pang families on two boards (two-family kernels), where errors use every hole and the proved numbering transfer stops; the collapsed form has none at every size (two-factor kernels). Support counting, domination and identical locator kernels are insufficient.
  3. Hardness-preserving repair fourth. Develop hardness-preserving-repair with a hard target, affordable extraction and universal coverage of the eligible certificate class. Preserve the matched field, generators and circuit size/depth budget. Nonzero survival does not certify hardness.
  4. Geometric application complete. The marked Hermitian recovery theorem supplies the first objective. Further geometric work must bear on one of the remaining open statements rather than repeat this endpoint.

Working mathematical context

Foundations and bridge map

Geometric recovery. On a smooth curve of genus \(g\), \(n\) distinct received points and disjoint pole divisors of degrees \(a,m\), two-system recovery works for \(t\) unknown errors if \(a\ge t+g\) and \(n>a+m+t\). A separate protected point can be normalized when \(a\ge t+2g\). Solve for locator and weighted message, then the message; never divide evaluation vectors. The Hermitian construction supplies all inputs in cubic field-operation cost. Its pole weights are not total polynomial degrees. For several words with support union \(u\), one common locator needs \(a\ge u+2g\); the exact criterion of exact selection holds there although summed and joint rank conditions cannot certify a protected point.

For effective-annihilator-degree. Boolean ideal quotients are products of copies of the field, so an ideal defect there is a reduced point set; nilpotents arise only modulo a degree-\(D\) pseudoideal, which defines no scheme, and an unsatisfiable source generates the unit ideal (note). A regularity bound needs a pseudoideal analogue or a non-Boolean encoding. An element acting as the identity on the defect factors and killing a protected class gives a surviving common killer of its own degree; in a domain model the first surviving degree is an interpolation degree on the point set.

Native and auxiliary observations. The diagonal principle gives faithful scalar moments when the common diagonal kernel kills mixed products. Ordinary restriction satisfies it and retains Braun's ledger. Paid native moments use the sufficient reserve \(b+e+pK\le D\). Pang's recurrence needs only \(\Delta+K+d\le D\), plus its separate replay ceiling. After its adaptive choices, independent coordinate rows give a base-field symmetric form with the exact kernel, without native products. This construction works for every linear map and yields no rank estimate. The observable coding tester has the error kernel without knowing the error. Finite perfect-field diagonal zero remains weaker than radical membership.

Product-code limit. The primary Schur-product Kneser theorem bounds product dimension from below using its stabilizer. The existing paid stable-core construction already turns small absolute growth into a conditional source repair. The comparison found no independent small-growth estimate; the graded-envelope and selected-feature limitations remain applicable.

Fixed-action compression. For prime-field \(J_D,w,U\) and errors of degree at most \(e\), with \(\deg w\le b\), \(U\le V_K\), the generic pencil captures the joint kernel if \(b+K+e+(p-1)\min(K,e)\le D\). The multiplier-side proof uses a rational \(p\)-basis; a finite field of size larger than the joint rank admits a good specialization. Preserve the forbidden weight kernel when descending. This does not justify changing source coefficient domains, nor does it lower the separate old-kernel-preservation and gained-class-killing costs in Pang's contraction step.

The organizing principle is multiplicative separation: one affordable, operation-compatible multiplier annihilates every actual defect while preserving a protected class. Compatibility, annihilation and survival are separate obligations. The foundational investigation contains the full reviewed arguments, source attributions, Braun/Pang comparison and falsifying controls; the following map is navigation, not a replacement for those proofs. User direction, 15 October 2026: preserve every bridge as the foundations for a general theorem covering Braun, Pang and future applications.

  • Compatible repair and cyclic modules. A linear map commuting with the allowed variable actions is multiplication by its image of one. This explains why one shared weight preserves an argument. It supplies no cheap selection theorem; the filtered action and any weight-dependent substitution must be justified.
  • Coding theory and error-correcting pairs. A locator kills unknown errors while retaining the message. Product orthogonality, error detection, rank and distance give an explicit constructive theorem and polynomial-evaluation application. The unresolved transfer is an independent quantitative bound for the actual joint error action; a faithful tester alone preserves its kernel and rank.
  • Frobenius and Poincare duality. A fixed perfect multiplication pairing converts a linear separator into a multiplier preserving the protected element. Complementary degree gives the cost. A pairing chosen from the desired answer is circular, and a perfect pairing can still require an unaffordable degree.
  • Geometry and localization. Clearing finitely many denominators produces a common annihilator with additive filtration cost when the protected element survives localization. Nilpotent multipliers can work even when localizing at them destroys the whole algebra; reduced support alone cannot control the required degree.
  • Homological algebra and the Koszul complex. The common annihilator is degree-zero cohomology, equivalently a cyclic-module Hom space. This identifies the object precisely; a bound on its first useful filtered degree or on protected survival still needs a theorem.
  • Field descent and the Galois question. Fixed linear kernel-survival problems descend across finite field extensions without increasing degree, by coefficient extraction. This needs neither Galois symmetry nor norms. Joint nonlinear choices of approximators are outside that statement and retain their own descent obligation.

Completed repair theorem. The composition theorem selects an exact weight from observations whose total rank is below the surviving capacity at the final cutoff. Freeze its coefficients, then apply finite-grid adaptive repair: over \(\mathbb F_q\), let \(\mathcal N_A(j)\) count exponent-box monomials through degree \(j\), \(\Delta=(q-1)dt\), and \(\eta=(1-1/q)\mathcal N_A(K-d)/\mathcal N_A(K)\). If \(b+K+\Delta+d\le D\) and \(M(1-\eta)^t<1\), a degree-\(K\) factor leaves \(wf\notin J_D\) and kills the residuals. Earlier \(wE\in J_D\) persists when \(\deg(wE)+K\le D\). Fixed-substitution replay costs \(b+K+TB\le D\); Pang's approximate-map replay has its own retained ceiling. Explicit dense inputs give a Las Vegas construction with at most \(Mt(\mathcal N_A(K-d)+1)\) expected sampled rank tests, plus matrix formation, stacked ranks and final solving. This is not an implicit-PC-basis runtime claim. The curve provider retains degree bounds \(e+g\) for a nonzero section and \(e+2g\) for a protected value, with rational-function vanishing only under the stated support condition.

Write \(J_D\) for the old bounded-degree consequence space, with paid multiplication closure. Actual defects must satisfy \(fe_i\in J_D\), while the protected multiplier class satisfies \(f\notin J_D\); every product must fit the same declared window. Braun uses ordinary affine restrictions and bounded cofactors, followed by a weight-dependent substitution. Pang chooses approximators and controls ranks of their error multiplication maps modulo PC. The full ideal of an inconsistent system contains one and cannot replace \(J_D\).

The first record proves the cyclic-map universal property, bilinear error recovery, marked Frobenius separation and precise localization/descent limits. In recovery, beta is bilinear, Q kills clean products, Q detects every possible nonzero error product, each error action has rank below the multiplier dimension, and nonzero multipliers are injective on the clean code. These are independently specified coding hypotheses, not automatically PC hypotheses. In Frobenius separation, the algebra and perfect pairing are fixed before the ideal and protected element; a degree-d protected class may need multiplier degree s-d. Nilpotent multipliers can be useful even though localization at them kills the entire ring. Formal nonzero, point support and rank of the listed errors do not replace paid class survival and rank of error multiplication. Existing colon and adjoint results remain the comparison baseline; a faithful tester preserves the exact kernel. No formalization is assigned.

Gaps identified by formalization

No formalization is assigned. Inherited PC degree accounting uses upper bounds for companion degrees; equality requires the original hypotheses. The main notebook records the partial downstream audit. No Lean verification of this new abstraction is claimed.

Research record

Compatible repair, error correction and multiplicative separation

15 October 2026 · Working proofs of established mechanisms and transfer limits · Common multiplier abstraction. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Question. On effective-selection, effective-common-multiplier needs an independently checkable quantitative selection theorem recovering Braun and Pang and giving another useful application. The user asked for the hidden abstraction, including bridges to other fields. This entry tests coding-theoretic detection and Frobenius duality against that requirement. Success means an explicit existence or construction theorem with survival and costs; a common-kernel renaming alone does not suffice. This is a new investigation, not resumption of the interrupted main-notebook cycle.

General statement. The all-parameter claims are lem:cyclic-repair-map, thm:bilinear-error-recovery, prop:frobenius-marked-separation and prop:multiplier-transfer-limits. The first is the elementary cyclic-module universal property; the second isolates a standard decoding mechanism and proves the error-correcting-pair specialization; the third is the standard Frobenius double-annihilator mechanism with a protected element; the fourth records precise transfer limits and counterexamples. No historical novelty is claimed.

Record search. Searches for colon multipliers, common moment adjoint, Pellikaan, error locating/correcting pairs, syndrome multiplier recovery, cyclic module intertwiners, Frobenius double annihilator, Poincare duality and bilinear error detection were followed by the exact relevant records. Read prop:colon-multipliers with its full support-absorption entry, lem:common-moment-adjoint, lem:weight-compatibility-factorization, lem:source-compatible-cover, prop:relative-code-bound-refuted and prop:freeness-propagation. The first already gives colon transport and warns against a duality pairing chosen from the desired answer. The adjoint gives a pairing for fixed paid error maps, not contraction. The cover result already models source-compatible cyclic actions. Freeness propagation already uses a complementary-monomial Poincare pairing. The relative-code counterexample forbids replacing an ambient rank bound by a quotient-normalized one without proof. Graph queries for the colon and adjoint claims were checked; missing edges do not establish independence. The present proofs are self-contained; these records calibrate what the synthesis does not newly solve.

Compatible repair

Statement. Let \(R=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\), let \(M\) be an \(R\)-module, and let \(T:R_{\le d}\to M\) be linear. Suppose \(T(x_iq)=x_iT(q)\) whenever \(\deg q

Proof. Induct on monomial length, starting with one, and apply the assumed identity to its last variable. Extend by linearity. Conversely associativity gives the identity. The filtration assertion follows by the same induction. A map on \(R\) factors through \(R/I\) exactly when every \(a\in I\) kills \(f\). This proves all assertions. The claim concerns linear maps on the whole declared polynomial window, not an arbitrary nonlinear transformation defined only on the lines of one proof.

Meaning. A common multiplier is the forced form of a linear repair that respects every paid multiplication step in a cyclic model. Separate line-dependent weights generally lose this compatibility. For a fixed substitution \(\Phi\), \(q\mapsto f\Phi(q)\) is the same statement for the source action transported through \(\Phi\). Braun's substitution itself depends on the selected weight, so this observation does not turn his selection problem into one fixed linear map. A bounded PC consequence space is not automatically an ideal and is not automatically a module quotient; the finite-window operations must be verified individually.

Detection becomes annihilation

Statement. Let \(U,V,W,Z\) be finite-dimensional vector spaces over a field, \(C\le V\), \(\mathcal E\subseteq V\), \(\beta:U\times V\to W\) bilinear and \(Q:W\to Z\) linear. Assume (i) \(Q\beta(U,C)=0\); (ii) for each \(e\in\mathcal E\), \(\operatorname{rank}\beta_e<\dim U\), where \(\beta_e(a)=\beta(a,e)\); (iii) \(\ker Q\cap\beta(U,e)=\{0\}\) for each such \(e\); and (iv) for every nonzero \(a\in U\), the map \(c\mapsto\beta(a,c)\) is injective on \(C\). Given \(y=c+e\) with \(c\in C,e\in\mathcal E\), find any nonzero solution of \(Q\beta(a,y)=0\), then solve \(\beta(a,c')=\beta(a,y)\) with \(c'\in C\). These two linear systems recover \(c\) uniquely. If \(\operatorname{rank}\beta_e\le r\), the first solution space has dimension at least \(\dim U-r\).

Proof. By (i), the first system is \(Q\beta_e(a)=0\). Its kernel contains \(\ker\beta_e\), whose dimension is at least \(\dim U-r>0\). Every solution satisfies \(\beta_e(a)\in\ker Q\cap\beta(U,e)\), hence \(\beta_e(a)=0\) by (iii). Consequently \(\beta(a,y)=\beta(a,c)\). Existence of the second solution follows, and uniqueness is (iv). With bases and the bilinear map supplied, ordinary linear algebra constructs both systems. The theorem supplies no efficient method for finding spaces satisfying the hypotheses.

Error-correcting pairs. This is a self-contained derivation of the established coding-theoretic mechanism in Pellikaan's On the existence of error-correcting pairs, Definition 2.1 and Remark 2.2 (printed page 230), also attributed there to independent work of Kotter. Let \(A,B,C\le\mathbb F_q^n\), coordinate product \(*\), and integer \(t\ge0\). Suppose \((A*B)\perp C\), \(\dim A>t\), \(d(B^\perp)>t\), and \(d(A)+d(C)>n\). Set the minimum distance of the zero code to \(+\infty\). Take \(U=A,V=W=\mathbb F_q^n\), \(\beta(a,v)=a*v\), and \(Q(w)=(\langle w,b\rangle)_{b\text{ in a basis of }B}\), with \(\mathcal E\) the vectors of weight at most \(t\). Orthogonality gives (i). The image of multiplication by an error is supported on at most \(t\) coordinates, giving rank at most \(t\) and (ii). A vector in that image and \(B^\perp\) has weight at most \(t

Explicit degree budget. For \(n\) distinct field elements \(\alpha_i\), let \(1\le k\), \(t\ge0\), \(n\ge k+2t\), \(C\) be evaluations of polynomials of degree less than \(k\), \(A\) evaluations of degree at most \(t\), and \(B\) the orthogonal complement of evaluations of degree less than \(k+t\). Polynomial multiplication proves (i). A nonzero polynomial of degree at most \(rt\); evaluation is injective by the same root bound. The distance sum is greater than \(n\). Equivalently find a nonzero polynomial \(\Lambda\) of degree at most \(t\) and \(N\) of degree less than \(k+t\) with \(N(\alpha_i)=\Lambda(\alpha_i)y_i\). The true solution exists using the product of the erroneous-point factors; any solution has \(N=\Lambda p\) by the argument above (or the root bound), and division recovers the message polynomial. This is the familiar error-locator mechanism, not a new decoding algorithm.

What transfers. The useful additional structure is a tester with no nonzero low-complexity error in its kernel. Passing the tester then proves actual annihilation; a separate injectivity condition preserves the signal. The hypotheses are specified before the received word and do not assume its locator. This is stronger information than merely calling a desired multiplier a kernel vector. For polynomial calculus one would need an independently constructed tester on the actual paid error products that detects nonzero classes modulo the old consequence space, together with a surviving multiplier direction. Neither an arbitrary pairing nor a tester defined from the desired answer supplies that missing structure.

Duality produces multipliers

Statement. Let \(A\) be a finite-dimensional commutative unital \(k\)-algebra with a fixed functional \(\tau:A\to k\) such that \((a,b)\mapsto\tau(ab)\) is nondegenerate. For every ideal \(I\) and \(p\in A\),

\[p\notin I\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists f\in A:\ fI=0,\quad\tau(fp)\ne0.\]

If \(A=\bigoplus_{j=0}^s A_j\), \(\tau\) is supported in degree \(s\), and each pairing \(A_j\times A_{s-j}\to k\) is perfect, then for homogeneous \(I\) and homogeneous \(p\in A_d\setminus I\) one may take \(f\in A_{s-d}\). This is standard Frobenius duality, formulated to retain the protected element. It is not an assertion that a prescribed bounded PC space has these properties.

Proof. If \(p\notin I\), choose a linear functional \(\lambda\) vanishing on \(I\) but not on \(p\), by extending a basis of \(I\) through \(p\). Perfectness represents it uniquely as \(\lambda(a)=\tau(fa)\). For \(e\in I\) and every \(a\in A\), \(ae\in I\), whence \(\tau(aef)=0\). Nondegeneracy gives \(ef=0\). Conversely \(p\in I\) would force \(fp=0\). In the graded case choose \(\lambda\) supported in degree \(d\), zero on \(I_d\), and nonzero on \(p\); the perfect degree pairing represents it with \(f\in A_{s-d}\), and homogeneity makes it zero on all of \(I\). The preceding argument applies unchanged.

Geometric content. Perfect multiplication turns a linear separator into an actual multiplicative separator. The truncated polynomial algebra with complementary monomial bases is an explicit source of such a pairing, already used in prop:freeness-propagation. The same algebraic structure is often called a Poincare duality algebra; no theorem about arbitrary topological spaces is needed here. The concrete model \(k[u,v]/(u^2,v^2)\), with \(\tau\) extracting \(uv\), has dual basis pairs \((1,uv),(u,v),(v,u),(uv,1)\). For \(I=(u)\), \(p=v\), choose \(f=u\); then \(fI=0\), \(fp=uv\ne0\). Its one-point reduced geometry loses exactly the nilpotent information that makes the multiplier work. Miles Reid's Chapter 6 notes, Example 6.8, give the complementary-monomial pairing; the proof above uses the explicit pairing hypothesis, not an inferred pairing on the proof-complexity quotient.

Transfer and its limits

Statement and proof: localization. Let \(M\) be a module over a commutative ring \(R\), \(S\) a multiplicative subset, and let finitely many errors \(e_i\) become zero in \(S^{-1}M\), while \(p/1\ne0\). The definition of module localization gives \(s_i\in S\) with \(s_i e_i=0\); then \(s=\prod_i s_i\) kills all errors and \(sp\ne0\), since otherwise \(p/1=0\). In a multiplicative filtration the degree of this construction is at most the sum of the individual degrees. No subadditive improvement follows. The empty family uses \(s=1\). See the definitions of module localization in Stacks, Section 10.9. In the preceding duality example, localizing at \(f=u\) gives the zero ring since \(u^2=0\); thus useful common multipliers need not be localization denominators preserving the signal.

Statement and proof: scalar descent. Fix finite-dimensional \(k\)-spaces \(U,V_i\), linear error maps \(T_i:U\to V_i\) and a forbidden subspace \(L\le U\). A finite field extension \(K/k\) contains a vector in \(\bigcap_i\ker(T_i\otimes K)\setminus(L\otimes K)\) if and only if the base field contains one in \(\bigcap_i\ker T_i\setminus L\). Expand a vector as \(\sum_j\theta_j f_j\) in a field basis. Each \(T_i f_j=0\) by independence of the basis, and at least one \(f_j\notin L\). The reverse direction is scalar extension. Coefficients stay in the same degree-filtered base space, so there is no degree increase. This is linear descent, requiring neither a Galois extension nor norms. It does not descend a simultaneously chosen nonlinear approximation family, and does not replace Pang's Frobenius specialization argument.

Statement and proof: obstructions. In \(A=k[x,y]/(x,y)^2\), take \(I=(x)\) and \(p=y\). Then \(p\notin I\), but \(\operatorname{Ann}(I)=(x,y)\), whose elements all kill \(p\). Indeed \((a+bx+cy)x=ax\), so annihilation forces \(a=0\). Thus linear separation alone does not imply multiplicative separation without duality or another mechanism. In \(A_m=k[t]/(t^{m+1})\), \(m\ge1\), take \(I=(t)\), \(p=1\). Here \(\operatorname{Ann}(I)=kt^m\), so every nonzero annihilator has least representative degree \(m\). All these rings have one-point reduced spectrum, yet this degree is unbounded. Even perfect duality gives no uniform cheapness. Finally on \(t\ge1\) distinct evaluation points, the one-row error data matrix \((1,\ldots,1)\) has rank one, but a nonzero polynomial vanishing at all points has degree at least \(t\), by the root bound. Low rank of the error data is not low rank of its action on multipliers.

Homological reading. For a genuine module and \(I=(e_1,\ldots,e_r)\), the first map of the cochain Koszul complex is \(m\mapsto(e_1m,\ldots,e_rm)\). Its degree-zero cohomology is precisely \(\operatorname{Ann}_M(I)=\operatorname{Hom}_R(R/I,M)\), by the cyclic-map proof. This is an exact organization of the problem, not a bound on the first nonzero degree or a survival theorem. No assertion about higher Koszul homology is needed. For the definition of the Koszul differential see Stacks, Section 15.29.

What Braun and Pang share

Both exploit the compatibility of multiplying every relevant line by the same object. Both must annihilate actual defects and preserve a protected class within a paid degree window. Their selection engines differ. In Braun's affine-exclusion construction, the multiplier lies in a row-linear space and vanishes under ordinary restriction to every proper high-rank zero flat. The common-kernel estimate makes this possible; bounded cofactors express it in each input ideal, and Boolean idempotence makes the weight-dependent substitution eliminate companion errors. The final degree budget is \(k(D+1)\). Hardness of every nonzero row-linear separator supplies survival, not merely hardness of one.

In Pang's construction, the defects are \(g_{L,i}P_L\) modulo the old bounded-degree PC space \(C_D\), and the approximation polynomials \(P_L\) are selected along with a surviving multiplier. The recorded correctness audit retains the source's rank-contraction and degree hypotheses. The maps count the ranks of multiplication by actual defects on the allowed multiplier space. They do not count the rank of a matrix listing the defects. Pointwise vanishing on solutions of an inconsistent system cannot replace membership in \(C_D\). The coding decoder instead has real evaluation coordinates, a tester excluding sparse nonzero errors, and distance guaranteeing message survival. These are different realizations of compatible repair, not interchangeable hypotheses.

New mathematics. This entry proves a self-contained bilinear detection/recovery formulation and its quantitative coding instance, a marked Frobenius separation criterion, and the stated transfer/obstruction package. The universal property, decoding mechanism, duality and linear descent are established mathematics or elementary syntheses; no new literature theorem is claimed. There were no numerical computations or experimental checks. The controls are exact all-parameter algebraic proofs.

Goal progress. The effective-common-multiplier implication remains unchanged: no theorem with independently verified quantitative hypotheses yet recovers both Braun and Pang. The constructive coding application is established, but does not discharge that transfer. Transfer is settled for the operations explicitly stated, not for every possible encoding. The next necessary issue is an independently proved advantage for the actual joint action maps and protected survival, rather than just a smaller representation of those same maps.

Degenerate cases. The cyclic theorem at degree zero says only that a linear map on constants is determined by one; for no variables the same holds. In recovery, zero error has rank zero and every nonzero solution works; a zero multiplier space is excluded by (ii), and a zero clean code is allowed with distance infinity. For duality, \(I=A\) and \(p\in I\), including \(p=0\), make both sides false; \(I=0\) gives ordinary perfect-pairing separation. Nonhomogeneous data are covered by the ungraded statement but not its degree formula. An empty error family in descent leaves just \(U\setminus L\), so the same basis argument applies. The degree obstruction excludes \(m=0\), where the ideal is zero and one is an affordable multiplier.

Nonvacuity. In the decoding statement take five distinct points over \(\mathbb F_5\), \(k=2,t=1\). Then \(\dim A=2\), the root bounds give \(d(A)\ge4,d(C)\ge4,d(B^\perp)\ge3\), so all hypotheses hold and one error is corrected. For duality the displayed algebra \(k[u,v]/(u^2,v^2)\) has \(I=(u),p=v,f=u\). For localization take \(R=k\times k\), \(e=(1,0),p=(0,1)\) and \(S=\{1,(0,1)\}\). The projection multiplier kills the error and retains the protected element. These are explicit witnesses, not reported computation counts.

Verification gate. The sole fresh-context GPT-6.1-Sol medium reviewer passed all four algebraic claims and the Braun/Pang comparison, requesting a sharper follow-up and final status updates. The finite-extension scope is retained because it is the motivating field extension setting; the basis proof also works for arbitrary extensions and maximal scope is not needed here. Dependencies re-read are listed in Record search. No computation or new encoding was used. Process audit. The reviewer found the title matched the body, the inventory complete and goal-unchanged assessment appropriate. It identified that a faithful tester preserves the original ranks; the follow-up now explicitly requires an independently proved selection advantage. The title and status were finalized from the reviewed body. Review. The finisher's stand-in audit is handled when emitted; no earlier stand-in findings belong to this new cycle. The review record is saved with this entry.

Process assessment. The first proposed follow-up did not explicitly require an advantage over the faithful tester's existing rank identity; the reviewer caught this and the final follow-up does. No existence improvement is claimed. Initial orientation preceded instrumentation, and the setup timing's preparation category included preliminary mathematical planning. Prevention. This notebook now requires a Selection gain paragraph in each research entry: an alleged selection mechanism must state an independently proved improvement in the actual joint action or protected-survival condition, or say unchanged. The finisher enforces the paragraph through the living section's data-entry-paragraphs attribute; mathematical validity still needs review. This scoped duty strengthens the existing non-tautology rule without imposing this goal's mathematics on other notebooks.

Selection gain. Unchanged. If a tester \(Q_i\) is injective on \(\operatorname{im}T_i\), then \(Q_iT_i u=0\) if and only if \(T_i u=0\). Thus kernels, individual ranks and the joint kernel of all maps are preserved. The coding theorem obtains its rank bound from small support and signal survival from distance, not from faithful compression. No new joint-action estimate for Braun or Pang is supplied here.

Reviewer's suggestions, unverified

  • The reviewer suggested measuring protected survival by the stacked map \((T,P)\), where \(T\) collects actual errors and \(P:U\to U/L\) is the forbidden-space quotient. Author check: projection of \(\operatorname{im}(T,P)\) onto \(\operatorname{im}T\) is onto and has kernel isomorphic to \(P(\ker T)\). Hence the rank difference is \(\dim P(\ker T)\); positivity is exactly survival. When \(L\subseteq\ker T\), this is \(\dim U-\operatorname{rank}T-\dim L>0\). This is the existing useful-kernel criterion in different notation, not a new selection theorem. Its usefulness as a source of an independent estimate remains unverified. Record. Searches for common kernel protected quotient stacked rank survival and tester faithful rank injective error image were checked against the already-read lem:weight-compatibility-factorization and lem:common-moment-adjoint. \[\dim ST\ge\dim S+\dim T-\dim\operatorname{St}(ST),\qquad \operatorname{St}(C)=\{a\in k^n:aC\subseteq C\}.\]

The stabilizer has a basis of disjoint coordinate projectors; on full-support codes it gives the indecomposable direct-sum decomposition. Its finite-field descent preserves the stabilizer through its linear defining equations. These are actual coordinate products, not arbitrary quotient bilinear maps.

Common moment radical

Setting. Let \(p\) be prime and \(J\le V_D=\mathbb F_p[x]_{\le D}\) a proper degree-\(D\) pseudoideal containing the old Boolean or prime-field domain consequences within that degree window. Fix \(w\in V_b\), an \(\mathbb F_p\)-linear subspace \(U\le V_K\), and errors \(E_1,\ldots,E_m\in V_e\), \(m\ge1\). All are fixed before choosing the functional or scalar coefficients. Assume

\[b+e+pK\le D.\tag{1}\]

Write \(T:U\to(V_D/J)^m\), \(u\mapsto([wE_i u])_i\), \(N=\ker T\), and \(r=\operatorname{rank}T\). For a symmetric \(p\)-linear form \(B\) on \(U\), its radical means \(\{u:B(u,u_2,\ldots,u_p)=0\text{ for all }u_2,\ldots,u_p\in U\}\), not just the diagonal zero set.

Statement. Over any finite extension \(L/\mathbb F_p\) with \(|L|>2r+1\), there exist a linear functional \(\mu:V_D\otimes L\to L\) annihilating \(J_L\), with \(\mu(1)=1\), and coefficients \(a_i\in L\), such that

\[B(u_1,\ldots,u_p)=\mu\!\left(w\Big(\sum_i a_iE_i\Big)\prod_{j=1}^p u_j\right),\qquad \operatorname{rad}B=N\otimes L.\tag{2}\]

Equivalently the first-factor flattening \(U_L\to(U_L^{\otimes(p-1)})^*\) has rank \(r\). For a fixed finite family of such data over the same \(J\), one \(\mu\) works for every member, with separate error coefficients, whenever \(|L|>1+2\sum_a r_a\) and each member satisfies its own reserve (1). These are sufficient field sizes. The functional is chosen from the full old annihilator space independently of a prospective successful multiplier, though it may depend on the fixed error data.

Proof: the easy radical inclusion. If \(u_1\in N_L\), every \(wE_i u_1\in J_L\). Multiplying by the other \(p-1\) arguments costs at most \(b+e+pK\). Scalar extension preserves degree intersections and paid pseudoideal multiplication, so all terms of (2) vanish. Thus \(N_L\subseteq\operatorname{rad}B\) for every \(\mu,a\). Every product in the form is an actual polynomial inside the window; no multiplication on an unrestricted quotient algebra is assumed.

Proof: a generic form has no extra radical. Choose a prime-field basis \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_q\) of \((V_D/J)^*\). Introduce independent indeterminates \(t_1,\ldots,t_m,z_1,\ldots,z_q\), let \(F=\mathbb F_p(t,z)\), and set \(\mu_z=\sum_\ell z_\ell\lambda_\ell\), \(E_t=\sum_i t_i E_i\). For any \(u=\sum_j c_j u_j\in U_F\) in a fixed prime-field basis of \(U\), domain reduction through \(pK\) gives

\[B_{t,z}(u,\ldots,u)=\sum_{i,\ell}t_i z_\ell\sum_j c_j^p\lambda_\ell([wE_i u_j]).\tag{3}\]

Indeed \(u^p=\sum_j c_j^p u_j^p\), and \(u_j^p-u_j\) is a domain consequence through \(pK\); multiplication by \(wE_i\) fits (1). Each inner sum in (3) is a \(p\)-th power in \(F\), because the displayed \(\lambda_\ell\)-values lie in \(\mathbb F_p\). The monomials \(t_i z_\ell\) are linearly independent over \(F^p\). Clear denominators in the \(p\)-th powers: their exponent vectors modulo \(p\) have one in the specified \(t_i\) and \(z_\ell\) positions and zero elsewhere, distinct for different pairs. Thus if (3) is zero, every inner sum is zero. Injectivity of Frobenius in a field gives \(\sum_j c_j\lambda_\ell([wE_i u_j])=0\) for every \(i,\ell\), and the dual basis then gives \(Tu=0\). A radical vector in particular has zero diagonal value, so it belongs to \(N_F\). Along with the easy inclusion this proves generic radical equality. In fact the diagonal zero set equals \(N_F\) over this imperfect generic field; this stronger fact will not be specialized.

Proof: finite specialization and normalization. In bases of \(U\) and its \((p-1)\)-fold tensor power, every flattening entry is bilinear in \(t,z\). Generic rank \(r\) gives a nonzero \(r\)-minor of total degree at most \(2r\). Properness makes \(\mu_z(1)\) a nonzero linear polynomial. Their product is nonzero and has total degree at most \(2r+1\). A nonzero polynomial of total degree \(s\) on a finite grid of size greater than \(s\) has a nonzero value, by induction using the univariate root bound. Select such a value and divide \(\mu\) by \(\mu(1)\). The minor stays nonzero and the easy radical inclusion holds at every specialization, so rank is exactly \(r\) and the radical is exactly \(N_L\). If \(r=0\), use the empty minor one. For a finite family take the product of one such minor for each member and the single normalization polynomial. The polynomial ring is a domain, so the product is nonzero despite sharing all moment parameters. This proves the claimed common field size and common functional.

Protected weights. Put \(L_0=\{u\in U:wu\in J\}\), and \(H=\dim U/L_0\). Paid multiplication gives \(L_0\subseteq N\). The form descends through \(L_0\) in every argument, by the same reserve, and its radical there is \(N/L_0\). A common surviving multiplier exists exactly when the flattening rank is less than \(H\). If a useful vector is found over \(L\), coefficient components in an \(\mathbb F_p\)-basis give an original-field useful vector in \(U\). This is an exact detection criterion, not an estimate that makes the rank small.

Binary interpretation. At \(p=2\), (2) is one symmetric bilinear moment form with precisely the actual error kernel as radical, at cost \(b+e+2K\). It uses one old functional and one error combination. The earlier common-moment adjoint uses unweighted input/output pairings through \(2(b+K+e)\) and supplies adjoint identities; this form has a cheaper stated reserve for kernel detection but supplies neither that adjoint nor its squared-operator formula. The prime retained rectangular pairing already uses the Frobenius mechanism at cost \(pK\) when no error weight is present. Here the error and weight are paid once, and the right-hand test space is generated by \(p-1\) elements of the actual allowed \(U\), not necessarily all of \(V_{(p-1)K}\).

Moment degree limits

Odd-prime bilinear control. For every odd prime \(p\), let \(D=2\), \(J=C_2(x^2-x,y^2-y,(x+y)^2)\), \(f=x+y\), and \(U=\langle f\rangle\). The three generators' quadratic leading parts are independent, since the coefficient of \(xy\) in the last is \(2\ne0\). Their span has no nonzero affine polynomial, so no nonzero legal variable multiplication is available through degree two; it is the actual PC closure. It is proper, also witnessed by \((x,y)=(0,0)\), and \(f\notin J\). With weight and single error both one, the actual action on \(U\) has rank one. But every old annihilator satisfies \(\mu(f^2)=0\), so its bilinear moment form on \(U\) is zero, over every scalar extension. Thus the uniform binary bilinear reserve \(2K\) cannot simply replace \(pK\) at odd primes. This is a satisfiable two-variable control, not a claimed sharpness theorem for every alternative rectangular construction.

Perfect-field diagonal control. For a finite perfect field \(L\) of characteristic \(p\), the diagonal of a moment form (2), on a base-field basis \(u_j\), has the shape \(\sum_j d_j c_j^p\), by the same field reduction. It is \((\sum_j d_j^{1/p}c_j)^p\), so its zero set has codimension at most one. If the flattening rank exceeds one, that zero set cannot equal the radical. The familiar binary special case is prop:perfect-binary-moment-rank, reread in full. Finite specialization in the theorem preserves the flattening minor, not the generic field's anisotropic diagonal detection. Testing only \(B(u,\ldots,u)=0\) after specialization is therefore unsound for finding a common multiplier.

Normalization control. On the one-bit Boolean quotient, \(U=\langle1,x\rangle\), \(w=E_1=1\), \(K=1,e=b=0,D=2,p=2\), a normalized binary functional has Gram matrix \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&a\\a&a\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), whose determinant is zero for both \(a\in\mathbb F_2\). Over \(\mathbb F_4\), \(a\notin\mathbb F_2\) gives determinant \(a+a^2\ne0\). Thus even this old moment control may need a functional-value extension. It leaves source variable domains unchanged, and provides no nonzero annihilator of the unit error. The extension bound in the theorem is sufficient, not minimal.

Nonvacuity. Over every prime, in the one-bit Boolean quotient take \(U=\langle1,x\rangle\), \(w=1,E_1=x,K=1,e=1\), and \(D=p+1\). The joint action has rank one, its kernel is \(\langle1-x\rangle\), and that weight survives. Evaluation at \(x=1\) is an old normalized annihilator with \(\mu(x)=1\); coefficient one yields (2) with exactly that radical. Tensoring with any number of spectator Boolean variables preserves this witness. The odd-prime control has \(K=1,b=e=0\) but \(D=2

Degenerate cases. A zero error tuple, zero weight action or zero \(U\) gives rank zero and radical all of \(U\); no surviving conclusion is inferred when \(H=0\). Constant-domain \(K=0\) is permitted. Properness is used for normalization and would fail for \(J=V_D\). No unit is assumed in \(U\). The finite-family statement covers only fixed data specified before the functional; an unlisted later functional-dependent error choice is not automatically covered.

Coefficient moments preserve Braun's ordinary restriction kernel

15 October 2026 · Working proof and source calibration · Ordinary restriction moments. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Chosen. Continue idea:common-multiplier-duality on effective-selection and effective-common-multiplier, in its second development of the four-entry spell. The necessary unification must recover the motivating constructions with their actual hypotheses and costs. The previous moment theorem asked: “Next calibrate this interface against Braun's ordinary affine restrictions and its original cofactor/replay ledger,” while handling fixed PC error data itself. This cycle tests that mismatch directly. The target is the published restriction rank estimate and replay ceiling, not another abstract form without its source ledger.

I read Section 5 of the publication in full, the row-linear definition and separation theorem with proof in Section 4, and the exact ordinary-kernel and family-exclusion records. The construction below uses polynomial coefficient functionals on the restriction targets, not measures on their Boolean points. The finite-point alternative was also checked against its already recorded Boolean-relative cofactor proof; it is not substituted for the published argument.

General statement. thm:diagonal-observation-principle isolates the finite-dimensional structural hypothesis behind the preceding Frobenius moment proof. cor:ordinary-restriction-moments verifies that hypothesis for ordinary polynomial restrictions and matches Braun's quantitative source ledger. The corollary recovers an existing exclusion, not a stronger lower bound or new proof-system theorem.

Diagonal observation principle

Setting. Let \(U,V\) be finite-dimensional \(\mathbb F_p\)-spaces, \(p\) prime, with a specified \(v_0\ne0\) in \(V\). Let \(\beta_i:U^p\to V\), \(1\le i\le m\), be fixed symmetric \(p\)-linear maps. Define their diagonal maps \(d_i(u)=\beta_i(u,\ldots,u)\), and \(C=\bigcap_i\ker d_i\). Assume

\[\beta_i(C,U,\ldots,U)=0\quad\text{for every }i.\tag{DO}\]

Every \(d_i\) is \(\mathbb F_p\)-linear. Indeed expansion of \(\beta_i(u+v,\ldots,u+v)\) groups mixed terms with coefficients \(\binom pj\), zero in characteristic \(p\), and scaling by \(c\in\mathbb F_p\) gives \(c^p=c\). Let \(r\) be the rank of \(u\mapsto(d_i(u))_i\).

Statement. For any finite extension \(L/\mathbb F_p\) with \(|L|>2r+1\), some \(a_i\in L\) and \(\lambda:V_L\to L\), with \(\lambda(v_0)=1\), give a scalar symmetric \(p\)-linear form

\[B(u_1,\ldots,u_p)=\lambda\!\left(\sum_i a_i\beta_i(u_1,\ldots,u_p)\right),\qquad \operatorname{rad}B=C_L.\tag{4}\]

For a finite fixed family over the same \(V,v_0\), one \(\lambda\) works for every member, with separate coefficients, when \(|L|>1+2\sum_a r_a\). If a forbidden subspace \(L_0\le C\) is specified and independently established bounds \(\operatorname{rank}d_i\le R_i\) satisfy \(\sum_i R_i<\dim U-\dim L_0\), then \(C\setminus L_0\) is nonempty over the original prime field. In a filtered application the cost of realizing each \(\beta_i\) must be supplied separately; abstract vector-space scalarization licenses no unproved multiplication or degree reset.

Proof. Choose prime-field bases \(u_j\) of \(U\) and \(\lambda_\ell\) of \(V^*\), and independent parameters \(t_i,z_\ell\). Over \(F=\mathbb F_p(t,z)\), use \(B_{t,z}=\sum_{i,\ell}t_i z_\ell\lambda_\ell\beta_i\). For \(u=\sum_j c_j u_j\), symmetry and characteristic \(p\) give

\[B_{t,z}(u,\ldots,u)=\sum_{i,\ell}t_i z_\ell\sum_j c_j^p\lambda_\ell(d_i(u_j)).\]

The monomials \(t_i z_\ell\) are independent over \(F^p\), by clearing denominators and comparing exponent vectors modulo \(p\). Their coefficients are \(p\)-th powers, so a zero diagonal value implies \(d_i(u)=0\) for every \(i\). Conversely (DO), extended by scalars, makes \(C_F\) lie in the radical. The generic radical is therefore exactly \(C_F\), and the first-factor flattening has rank \(r\). Its entries are bilinear in the two parameter groups. A nonzero maximal minor has degree at most \(2r\). Multiply it by the nonzero linear polynomial \(\sum z_\ell\lambda_\ell(v_0)\), specialize over a field larger than that degree, and normalize \(\lambda\). The elementary nonzero-polynomial grid bound proves existence; the radical inclusion from (DO) holds at every specialization, so a nonzero minor gives equality. Products of the minors prove the finite-family assertion. When \(r=0\), use the empty minor one. Finally \(r\le\sum R_i\), and rank-nullity gives \(\dim C>\dim L_0\); all these are prime-field spaces. This proves the selection statement without selecting a field-valued source assignment.

Why the structural hypothesis matters. It says that diagonal vanishing of the vector observations already kills their mixed products; it is verified from the native algebra in the applications, not assumed from a scalar moment. It is not automatic for symmetric forms. Over \(\mathbb F_2\), let \(U=\mathbb F_2^3\), \(V=\mathbb F_2\), \(v_0=1\), and \(\beta((a,b,c),(a',b',c'))=aa'+bc'+cb'\). Its diagonal map is \((a,b,c)\mapsto a\), so \(C\) is a plane, but \(\beta\) is nonsingular. A nonzero scalar multiple has zero radical, and the zero multiple has radical all of \(U\); neither has radical \(C\), even after scalar extension. This is the already recorded perfect-field moment matrix used as a control on (DO). The generic diagonal argument is used only over the imperfect parameter field. Finite specialization preserves radical rank, not the stronger diagonal-zero criterion.

Relation to the preceding theorem. In the paid-PC setting take \(V=V_D/J\), \(v_0=[1]\), and \(\beta_i(u_1,\ldots,u_p)=[wE_i\prod_j u_j]\). At \(b+e+pK\le D\), field reduction gives \(d_i(u)=[wE_i u]\) on base-field \(U\), and paid absorption proves (DO). Thus the common-moment-radical theorem, with its exact normalization and finite-family bound, is recovered. The abstract statement isolates that proof mechanism; it supplies no new automatic rank bound.

Ordinary restriction moments

Statement. Let \(U\le\mathbb F_p[x]_{\le k}\) be finite-dimensional and let \(\rho_a\) be finitely many affine substitutions into polynomial rings \(\mathbb F_p[y_{a,1},\ldots,y_{a,d_a}]\). There is a scalar symmetric \(p\)-linear coefficient-moment form on \(U\), over a finite extension of cardinality greater than \(2r+1\), whose radical is exactly \(\bigcap_a\ker(\rho_a|U)\) extended by scalars, where \(r\) is the joint ordinary restriction rank. It uses restriction products of degree at most \(pk\). In the binary published affine-family setting below, this retains Braun's common-kernel dimension bound and the original old-PC ceiling \(k(D+1)\).

Proof of the restriction representation. Set \(V=\bigoplus_a\mathbb F_p[y_a]_{\le pk}\), and let \(\beta_a(u_1,\ldots,u_p)\) have only its \(a\)-th component nonzero, equal to \(\prod_j\rho_a(u_j)\). The diagonal observation is \(\rho_a(u)^p\). Frobenius is injective on the ordinary polynomial ring: a nonzero polynomial has a nonzero \(p\)-th power, since its distinct monomials retain distinct exponent vectors and nonzero coefficient powers. Hence \(\ker d_a=\ker\rho_a\) over \(\mathbb F_p\), and their joint ranks agree. If \(u\) restricts to zero in every target, all mixed products containing it vanish, proving (DO). Take \(v_0=(1)_a\) when the family is nonempty, and apply the principle. The scalar functional is a tuple of polynomial-coefficient functionals on the restriction targets; it is not asserted to annihilate the old pigeonhole axioms. Empty families need no form construction: every \(u\in U\) is in the common kernel.

Matched Braun parameters and replay

Use exactly the publication's \(\mathbb F_2\) one-level complete affine source on \(m\ell\) bit variables, with \(m>0\), \(\ell\ge2\), \(n=2^\ell\), \(h=3\ell\), and \(M,k\ge1\). Retain old-only inputs, disjoint fresh coefficients, all companions and all fresh Boolean equations. Assume

\[k\le m,\quad m\log(4M)\le k^2,\quad D\ge2h+1,\quad 4(k-1)

and at most \(M\) blocks have proper input spans of rank greater than \(h(k+1)\). Put \(U=\mathcal L_k\), the ordinary row-linear space, with

\[H=\dim U=\sum_{j=0}^k\binom mj\ell^j,\qquad q=\binom mk\ell^k>0.\]

For each proper high block of rank \(r_a\), take its ordinary affine restriction to \(d_a=m\ell-r_a\) free coordinates. Its rank is at most \(\binom{d_a+k}{k}\). If any such block exists, \(r_*=3\ell(k+1)+1\le m\ell\). With \(d=m\ell-r_*\), the source calculation gives

\[\frac{\binom{d+k}{k}}{\binom mk\ell^k}\le\left(1-\frac{k}{m}\right)^k\le e^{-k^2/m},\qquad r\le M e^{-k^2/m}q\le q/4

For completeness, \(k!\binom{d+k}{k}\le(d+k)^k\), \(k!\binom mk\ge(m-k+1)^k\), and \(d+k\le\ell(m-2k)\le\ell(m-k+1)(1-k/m)\), yielding (6). If no proper high block exists, the joint rank is zero and choose \(f=1\); no estimate with negative free-coordinate count is used.

The observation form therefore has a nonzero radical. Its radical is the scalar extension of the original ordinary restriction kernel, so coefficient extraction gives a nonzero \(f\in\mathcal L_k\) over \(\mathbb F_2\), of degree \(s\le k\), with every required ordinary restriction zero. The source's affine coordinate argument supplies literal identities \(f=\sum_i a_{a,i}g_{a,i}\), \(\deg a_{a,i}\le k-1\). It does not supply merely pointwise identities.

The rest is the existing simultaneous weighted removal, with its ledger checked here. Low ranks \(r_a\le h(k+1)\) use basis packing with coefficient degree at most \(k\) and weighted Boolean companion certificates through \(s+r_a+1\le s+kD\). High unit spans use a constant first row. High proper spans use the literal cofactors, giving product \(1-f\) and weighted companions \(-g_{a,i}(f^2-f)\), certified through \(2s+1\le s+kD\). Fresh coefficient-field images cost at most \(s+2k\le s+kD\); used old axioms cost at most \(s+D\le s+kD\). Thus every primitive substituted PC step fits \(kD+s\le B=k(D+1)\). A hypothetical degree-\(D\) source refutation would derive \(f\) from the old bit base at \(B\), contradicting the published row-linear separation theorem under (5).

No additional source charge. The moment construction handles coefficient data of ordinary restriction products through degree \(2k\) in auxiliary free coordinates. Those functionals and extension-field coefficients are analysis devices, not fresh-variable substitutions or PC lines. The selected multiplier is returned to the original binary row-linear space before choosing any source coefficients. The actual coefficient maps remain binary old polynomials of degree at most \(k\), and the source replay ceiling remains exactly the existing \(B\). The auxiliary moment functional is not confused with the separate old-PC functional that proves survival of nonzero row-linear polynomials.

Unbounded original regime. The publication's parameter lemma, read with its proof, gives for every fixed natural \(a,A,d\), eventually with \(m=n+1\), \(n=2^\ell\), \(k=\lceil(\ell+1)2^{\ell/2}\rceil\), inventory \(M\le A2^{a\ell}+1\), and degree \(D\le A(\ell+1)^d\), all conditions (5) after raising a smaller proof ceiling to \(\max(D,6\ell+1)\). The increase is covered there by the constants \(A+7,d+1\). The moment calibration changes none of those parameters. This is an application to the actual published regime, not just a conditional inequality without an instance.

Ordinary versus finite-point observations

For two bits \(x,y\) in distinct rows, the row-linear polynomial \(f=xy+x\) has ordinary restriction \(t^2+t\ne0\) on the flat \(x=y=t\), but vanishes at every binary point of that flat. Thus replacing coefficient moments by binary point measures changes the kernel. This persists among high-rank blocks: for \(k\ge2\) and \(m\ell\ge3\ell(k+1)+2\), use the equation \(x+y=0\) and pin \(3\ell(k+1)\) other coordinates to zero. The resulting proper flat has rank \(3\ell(k+1)+1\), retains a free \(t\), and has the same discrepancy. The large-board regime just displayed has room for these pins. Literal affine-ideal membership would force the ordinary restriction to be zero, so this example has no such literal representation.

This is not a claim that pointwise affine vanishing can never support removal. The earlier lem:affine-common-vanishing-learning and lem:mixed-packing-common-vanishing-learning already prove a different route: after affine coordinate change and Boolean reduction, pointwise vanishing gives \(f-\sum_i a_i g_i\in I_k(\mathrm{BOOL})\), with \(\deg a_i\le k-1\). Their weighted companion identity pays for that Boolean residual and reaches the same hybrid \(k(D+1)\) ceiling. Those full proofs and their listed later relative-learning/fresh-block variants were read and their distinct fields, PC/NS scopes and costs compared. The current calibration preserves the published ordinary kernel; it neither re-registers the Boolean-relative route nor rules it out.

Nonvacuity. Ordinary restriction to a point or positive-dimensional affine flat satisfies the structural condition by polynomial-ring Frobenius injectivity. The asymptotic published regime above verifies nonvacuity of the complete Braun ledger at unbounded variable counts. The alternating-form control falsifies deleting (DO), and the row-linear \(xy+x\) control distinguishes the two notions of restriction before any rank comparison. No finite computation or extrapolation was performed.

Degenerate cases. A zero observation rank gives the entire domain as radical. The abstract principle assumes \(v_0\ne0\) only to request normalization; zero target spaces and empty restriction families are handled separately. Zero \(U\) cannot satisfy a strict survival inequality. Zero-dimensional flats have constant polynomial targets and cause no Frobenius exception. Unit-span blocks are not nonempty zero flats and use the source's separate cleanup; zero spans are low-rank blocks. The Braun application requires \(k\ge1\), whereas the abstract principle has no degree convention of its own.

New mathematics. A finite-dimensional diagonal-observation formulation of the common moment mechanism, with the exact hypothesis that makes scalarization faithful, and its ordinary-polynomial restriction application. Braun's rank estimate and exclusion are recovered unchanged; no new bound or historical novelty is claimed.

Selection gain. The ordinary restriction case now has a faithful moment representation with an independently proved rank deficit (6) and the matched original source ledger (5). The deficit is Braun's existing estimate, not a gain from scalarization. The general principle still needs quantitative rank estimates supplied by each application.

Pang's adaptive rank estimate survives auxiliary scalarization

15 October 2026 · Working calibration and representation limit · Pang observation calibration. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Chosen. Continue common-multiplier-duality on effective-selection and effective-common-multiplier, its third development. The first development asked to “Next calibrate this interface against Braun's ordinary affine restrictions and its original cofactor/replay ledger”; the second completed that and asked to “Next test the diagonal-observation principle on Pang's actual adaptive error-selection recurrence and original degree window”. This has priority over the coding-rank head because a claimed unification must preserve both motivating arguments before seeking stronger estimates.

Owed attempt. Read Pang's primary TeX Theorem 4.3 first, then Sections 2–4 and Proposition 5.1 with proofs. Read the near-half notebook's complete binary rank proof, leveled selection proof and the newer derived-affine and weighted versions. General statement. lem:coordinate-radical-realization is elementary linear algebra showing that unrestricted auxiliary pairings always encode a fixed kernel, over its original field. cor:pang-observation-calibration preserves Pang's original all-prime quantitative theorem and the existing constructive coding application in that representation. It does not replace their rank estimates or create a new lower bound.

Coordinate radical realization

Statement. Over any field, let \(T:U\to W\) be a linear map between finite-dimensional spaces, of rank \(r\), and \(C=\ker T\). Choose \(r\) independent coordinate rows \(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_r\) spanning its row space. For every integer \(s\ge2\),

\[ B_s(u_1,\ldots,u_s)=\sum_{j=1}^r\prod_{a=1}^s\ell_j(u_a) \quad\text{has}\quad \operatorname{rad}B_s=C. \tag{1}\]

Here the radical uses all choices of the other arguments. The construction is over the original field, with no positivity or polynomial multiplication assumption. It preserves the rank exactly and supplies no bound on it. With matrices supplied it requires only a row basis. For \(r=0\) use the zero form. For \(L_0\le C\), the induced form on \(U/L_0\) has a nonzero radical exactly when \(r<\dim U-\dim L_0\).

Proof. The row-basis map \(R:U\to k^r\) is surjective and has kernel \(C\). If \(u\in C\), every term in (1) vanishes. Conversely, for each \(j\) choose \(v_j\in U\) with \(R(v_j)=e_j\); then \(B_s(u,v_j,\ldots,v_j)=\ell_j(u)\). A radical vector therefore lies in every row kernel. The quotient and rank statements follow immediately from this equality. In particular \(B_2=R^{\mathsf T}R\) in input coordinates, and \(R^{\mathsf T}\) is injective. No extension field is needed.

Relation to diagonal observation. Over \(\mathbb F_p\), when \(r>0\), put \(s=p\), \(V=\mathbb F_p^r\), and \(\beta(u_1,\ldots,u_p)_j=\prod_a\ell_j(u_a)\). Its diagonal is \(R(u)\), because coefficients are in the prime field; its mixed products vanish on \(C\). Thus it realizes thm:diagonal-observation-principle, and the explicit coefficient sum already works over the base field, normalized at \(v_0=e_1\). At rank zero handle the zero form directly, or take \(V=\mathbb F_p,\beta=0,v_0=1\). This verifies the previous reviewer's auxiliary-coordinate suggestion, in a stronger elementary form. The output rows are chosen from the full map; they need not arise from one old polynomial functional, a fixed trace, an operation-compatible projection or a low-degree multiplication pairing.

Control. Using every row without selection is unsound over finite fields: over \(\mathbb F_2\), \(T:u\mapsto(u,u)\) has zero kernel but \(T^{\mathsf T}T=0\). Its independent row basis \(R=(1)\) works. This is the duplicated-output control already recorded for lem:common-moment-adjoint, not a new counterexample. More generally any prescribed subspace \(C\le U\) is the kernel of a quotient map and hence a radical in (1). Consequently existence of an unrestricted auxiliary form imposes no extra restriction on which common kernels can occur. A structural selection principle must constrain more than this representation.

Matched Pang recurrence

Use precisely Pang, arXiv:2610.00837v1, Theorem 4.3: Boolean variables over \(\mathbb F_p\), old degree-\(D\) PC consequence space \(J=C_D\), \(1\notin J\), \(S\ge1\) families \(g_{\nu,i}\) of degree at most \(d\), and integers \(1\le d\le K\le n\), \(t\ge1\). Put

\[\Delta=(p-1)dt,\quad \Delta+K+d\le D,\quad N_n(k)=\sum_{j=0}^k\binom nj,\quad H=\dim V_K/(J\cap V_K),\quad \eta=(1-1/p)\frac{N_n(K-d)}{N_n(K)}.\tag{2}\]

Calibrated conclusion. There are prime-field choices \(q_{\nu,j}\in\operatorname{span}\{g_{\nu,i}\}_i\) and \(P_\nu=\prod_{j=1}^t(1-q_{\nu,j}^{p-1})\) with the actual maps \(T_\nu:u\mapsto([P_\nu g_{\nu,i}u])_i\) satisfying \(\operatorname{rank}T_\nu\le H(1-\eta)^t\). Once these choices are fixed, their stacked map on \(U=V_K/(J\cap V_K)\) has an auxiliary symmetric bilinear form over \(\mathbb F_p\) with exactly its kernel as radical, and also a \(p\)-linear diagonal-observation realization. If \(S(1-\eta)^t<1\), that radical contains a nonzero class; a multilinear representative \(f\in V_K\setminus J\) kills every actual error \(P_\nu g_{\nu,i}\). All original degree bounds remain (2). This is a representation of the source theorem with its quantitative hypotheses, not an improvement of its rate.

Where the contraction comes from. For a fixed prefix \(P\) of degree \(a\), write \(Z_P(k)=\{u\in V_k:Pg_i u\in J\ \forall i\}\) and \(c_P(k)=\dim V_k/Z_P(k)\). These kernels respect degree intersections and absorb multiplication inside \(a+k+d\le D\). Their standard monomials form a downward-closed family of squarefree monomials. Counting consecutive layers gives \((j+1)b_{j+1}\le(n-j)b_j\), so

\[c_P(K-d)\ge\frac{N_n(K-d)}{N_n(K)}c_P(K).\tag{3}\]

On \(V_{K-d}\), define \(M_i u=([Pg_\alpha g_i u])_\alpha\). Their stacked kernel is \(Z_P(K-d)\): absorption gives one inclusion; the diagonal products \(Pg_i^2u\), multiplied by \(g_i^{p-2}\) and corrected using \(g_i^p-g_i\), give the other. Pang's multiplication-map Frobenius descent at \(a+K+pd\le D\) equates generic pencil rank with stacked rank. Its rank-specialization lemma gives a prime-field \(q=\sum c_i g_i\) retaining at least \((1-1/p)c_P(K-d)\). Its proof uses the nonzero maximal minor, whose rank loss at a point is at most its multiplicity there, and the grid multiplicity sum bounded by its degree times \(p^{s-1}\); it does not assume a nonvanishing evaluation on the prime grid.

The retained rank is the dimension of \((qV_{K-d}+Z_P(K))/Z_P(K)\). For \(P'=P(1-q^{p-1})\), bounded absorption preserves \(Z_P(K)\), and \(P'g_i(qu)=Pg_i u(q-q^p)\in J\) puts \(qV_{K-d}\) into \(Z_{P'}(K)\). Both operations fit \(a+K+pd\le D\). Hence \(c_{P'}(K)\le c_P(K)-(1-1/p)c_P(K-d)\le(1-\eta)c_P(K)\). At round \(j\le t\), \(a\le(j-1)(p-1)d\), and

\[a+K+pd\le(t-1)(p-1)d+K+pd=\Delta+K+d\le D.\tag{4}\]

Initially \(c_1(K)\le H\). Iteration proves the stated individual bounds. Every final error map kills \(J\cap V_K\) by the same paid absorption; their stacked rank is at most the sum, below \(H\) under the strict condition. Formula (1) now preserves exactly this already constructed common kernel. A representative may be multilinearized because its change and every error multiple of that change are Boolean consequences within (2).

Adaptive choices. At each round the current prefix and family are fixed before the rank-retaining \(q\) is selected. The final coordinate form is constructed only after all approximators are chosen. It is not used to choose them, and no source coefficient is extended. For the already proved binary leveled lemma, choose families level by level before forming one final stack: \(\Delta_i=\Delta_{i-1}t_i\), \(\Delta_{i-1}\le K\le n\), \(\Delta_i+K+\Delta_{i-1}\le D\), and \(\sum_i S_i(1-\tfrac12N_n(K-\Delta_{i-1})/N_n(K))^{t_i}<1\). Lower-level choices fix the next inputs, and the final sum of ranks is still below the same \(H\). This uses lem:leveled-common-multiplier with its imported premise discharged by thm:binary-approximator-rank; it is not a new all-prime layered theorem.

Native versus auxiliary cost. A native moment \(\mu(P_\nu g_{\nu,i}u_1\cdots u_p)\) invokes the preceding full-space moment theorem under its sufficient reserve \(\Delta+d+pK\le D\). Condition (2) does not imply this: already \(p=2,d=t=1,2\le K\le n,D=K+2\) satisfies (2) and violates \(2+2K\le D\). Formula (1) instead multiplies scalar coordinates of an already paid map; it is not a new old-PC product. Thus the auxiliary representation costs no extra old degree but does not establish a native normalized old moment at Pang's cutoff. This is a missing implication for the native route, not a proof that no alternative native construction can work.

Downstream realization. Pang's Proposition 5.1 uses exactly these original error memberships and a degree-\(K\) multiplier. For equation degree \(r\ge1\), \(d=(p-1)r\), and clause width \(w(F)\), its separate simulation condition is \(K+\max\{2\Delta+2d,\Delta+w(F)\}\le D\). The expansion \(1-P_L=\sum_i U_{L,i}g_{L,i}\) has \(\deg U_{L,i}\le\Delta-d\). Reading its topological induction checks input clauses, Boolean/true axioms, weakening/contraction, linear combination and multiplication at that ceiling; the empty line gives \(f\in J\), contradicting survival. The auxiliary form enters none of these operations. No change to the syntactic DAG, prime-field, Boolean-variable or node-size conventions is claimed.

Constructive coding remains constructive

In thm:bilinear-error-recovery, the observable map is \(T_y:a\mapsto Q\beta(a,y)\), for \(y=c+e\). Since \(Q\beta(U,C)=0\), it equals \(Q\beta_e\); injectivity of \(Q\) on \(\beta(U,e)\) gives \(\ker T_y=\ker\beta_e\) and equal ranks. Thus a row basis of the received-word map supplies (1) without knowing the error. The rank bound \(\operatorname{rank}\beta_e\le t<\dim U\) supplies a nonzero radical, and the separate injectivity of \(c'\mapsto\beta(a,c')\) recovers the clean message uniquely. One can solve \(T_y a=0\) directly; constructing a tensor is optional and yields no speedup.

For error-correcting pairs over any \(\mathbb F_q\), the recorded hypotheses remain \((A*B)\perp C\), \(\dim A>t\), \(d(B^\perp)>t\), and \(d(A)+d(C)>n\). Error support bounds rank by \(t\), the dual distance detects the error product, and the last distance sum preserves the message. The bilinear realization works directly over \(\mathbb F_q\). To place it literally in the prime-field diagonal theorem, restrict scalars to \(\mathbb F_p\); all dimensions and ranks multiply by \([\mathbb F_q:\mathbb F_p]\), kernels stay the same, and use the \(p\)-linear coordinate construction. The actual decoder stays over \(\mathbb F_q\), with the recorded two linear systems and cubic field-operation bound. Polynomial evaluation codes still use \(n\ge k+2t\); no decoding radius or algorithm is improved.

Nonvacuity. For every prime and any \(n\ge1\), take only Boolean axioms, one family \((x_1)\), \(d=K=t=1,D=p+1\). Then \(\eta=(1-1/p)/(n+1)>0\), the strict one-family condition holds, and \(P=1-x_1^{p-1}\), \(f=1\) kill the error while \(f\notin J\). This gives unbounded variable counts and fits the selection ledger. It does not fit the displayed simulation reserve; the Boolean-only control is not a proof-complexity lower-bound instance. The unrestricted coordinate lemma also applies to identity maps of arbitrary rank, where the radical is zero: it cannot force selection by itself. The existing polynomial-evaluation code instances verify the constructive application's parameter range.

Degenerate cases. Zero maps and empty observation lists give the zero form and full radical; zero \(U/L_0\) cannot satisfy the strict survival inequality. An empty polynomial family has no error condition and may use all \(q=0\). Properness is required for \(H>0\), not for coordinate scalarization. Constant inputs are allowed within the positive upper degree bound \(d\). None of the arguments replaces bounded PC by the full ideal of an inconsistent system.
