Effective repair needs quantitative certificates, not a preferred pairing

15 October 2026 · Working architecture review and scope controls · Repair architecture. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Question. Six research entries have preserved the same effective-common-multiplier obligation. They produced a constructive coding theorem, transfer controls, cheaper Frobenius compression, native moment forms and matched Braun/Pang calibrations, but no new selection estimate. Does the user's generalization require a stronger estimate, or a theorem composing independently certified mechanisms? The goal is a reusable tool explaining both constructions and future applications, not an unrestricted Frege lower bound.

General statement. The route seeks effective multiplicative separation: one affordable compatible multiplier kills the specified defects while its protected class survives. This review adds the standard Riemann–Roch consequence cor:curve-locator-budget and the elementary scope controls prop:repair-cost-controls. They guide the choice of architecture; they do not prove the full synthesis.

Obstacle

The faithful kernel representations preserve the answer but do not predict it. lem:coordinate-radical-realization shows that every linear kernel has an auxiliary symmetric form, while a native old-functional form needs additional structure and degree. Thus demanding a nicer form can be a stronger convenience than the actual selection goal. What is missing is a complete composition theorem whose quantitative certificates are obtained from the objects themselves, with common survival and all costs verified. The existing weighted adaptive lemma already supplies a substantial composition step; it must be used rather than rediscovered.

Architecture review

Necessary target. Give a finite, constructive calculus of sufficient conditions for a multiplier in a filtered commutative action, valid for every instance satisfying those conditions. Its certificates must be independently checkable structural data: ordinary restriction dimensions, a proved adaptive rank recurrence, or a faithful error tester and signal-injectivity bound. Recover Braun's literal affine vanishing and replay at \(k(D+1)\), Pang's \(\Delta+K+d\le D\) selection and separate simulation ceiling, and at least one distinct constructive use. State input representation and construction cost; no efficiency claim can hide the cost of finding a bounded-PC basis. Downstream. cor:ordinary-restriction-moments already supplies Braun's original exclusion, cor:pang-observation-calibration preserves Pang's common multiplier and subsequent simulation, and thm:bilinear-error-recovery supplies decoding. Those exact applications are proved; composing their structural certificates into one reusable theorem is still weaker than any new unrestricted proof-complexity lower bound.

Extra requirements. A single normalized native functional, a perfect multiplication pairing, arbitrary source choices, or a better rank estimate are not logically necessary for this goal. A stronger bound would be valuable, but the user also asked for generalization and future use cases. Conversely, a generic kernel form is insufficient even when beautifully expressed: its existence holds for all maps. The constructive coding import must retain attribution and is not a newly discovered decoder.

Independent alternative. Before seeing the preferred moment route, the sole medium reviewer received only the goal and bounded available-result statements. It proposed an effective repair calculus combining exact cleanup with adaptive contraction, normalized to the protected image and an additive degree budget. It explicitly rejected imposing an improved-rank requirement on the user's goal. Its proposal and limitation are in the first-stage record. The current route is now revealed for comparison: its native forms are useful representation tools, but the coordinate realization shows why they need not be the organizing theorem.

Rank normalization. Always measure remaining errors on the same protected image \(V_K/\ker(f\mapsto[wf])\). Exact cleanup may change the weight and therefore that denominator. The weighted adaptive lemma already uses its actual dimension. Relative conditional ranks, including the existing Shearer criterion, can replace absolute summed ranks only with their dependence hypotheses proved. Disjoint polynomial support does not establish them after total-degree truncation.

Decision. Develop the compatible-repair item next, with a lemma-first synthesis of certified exact cleanup followed by the existing weighted adaptive step. Keep the duality item and its narrower native question queued, but do not require a native form to complete the general theorem. The Riemann–Roch and overlap leads below offer independent structural certificates. They are chosen for the actual unification goal, not as a promise of a new Frege estimate.

Decisive test. Trivial cases. Duplicating an error or changing its presentation leaves the actual kernel and protected quotient unchanged; a certificate may become looser, but may not claim an improved mathematical answer from duplication. Zero errors require no repair, and an injective unit error cannot admit a surviving annihilator. Power. The weighted adaptive lemma already proves contraction after a supplied surviving exact weight; the coordinate theorem proves that scalarization adds no selection power. The narrow rectangle control below rejects a gratuitous one-functional requirement at an original Pang cutoff. No finite computation is needed. Attempt. Substituting an exact-cleanup weight into lem:weighted-adaptive-approximation proves the algebraic composition in a few lines, provided that weight survives at the final cutoff and earlier products still fit. Therefore this is not posed as an unanswered rank experiment: the next entry must write the complete lemma, its certificate extraction, the Braun/Pang adapters and costs, and identify precisely what remains beyond the existing lemma. Test disposition. New operation: newly adopted in this notebook, using an already proved composition; no new contraction claim. Operation. Compose certified exact repair with residual adaptive repair in one fixed final consequence space, carrying the actual weight image between them. Prediction. The existing weighted lemma supplies survival and residual contraction; failure can occur only at an unproved certificate, changed input grammar, or unpaid preservation/replay degree. A composition that merely renames supplied final kernels does not meet the endpoint. Record search. Exact cleanup weighted adaptive composition common multiplier recovered lem:weighted-adaptive-approximation, the weighted binary refinement, and existing source-specific shared-core and codimension-batch tools; no novelty is claimed for that algebraic step. This is a lemma-first synthesis task, not an empirical test whose answer is already known.

Curve locator budget

Statement. Let \(X/k\) be a smooth projective geometrically integral curve of genus \(g\), \(A\) a divisor, and \(E\) an effective divisor of degree \(e\). If \(\deg A\ge e+g\), then \(L(A-E)\ne0\). If a rational point \(P\) lies outside the supports of \(A,E\) and \(\deg A\ge e+2g\), there is \(f\in L(A-E)\) with \(f(P)=1\).

Proof. Riemann–Roch gives \(\ell(A-E)\ge\deg A-e+1-g\ge1\). Under the second bound, the dual divisor \(K_X-(A-E-P)\) has degree at most \(-1\), hence no nonzero section. Duality gives \(H^1(A-E-P)=0\); the point-evaluation exact sequence makes \(L(A-E)\to k\) surjective. This is a standard consequence of Riemann–Roch and the negative-degree section criterion, not a new curve theorem. Vanishing along \(E\) is vanishing as a section of \(\mathcal O(A)\); the representing rational function vanishes there when the supports of \(A,E\) are disjoint. Evaluation at the stipulated \(P\) supplies protected survival.

Nonvacuity. On the projective line over any field with distinct finite points \(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_e,P\), take \(A=e\infty\), \(E=\sum_i\alpha_i\); the product \(\prod_i(x-\alpha_i)\), divided by its nonzero value at \(P\), realizes the bound. There are examples for every \(e\) over an infinite field, and over finite fields large enough to contain the named distinct points. For \(e=0,g=0\), the constant one works. At higher genus the stated degree bounds are sufficient, not asserted minimal. This is a function/section theorem; it does not identify a bounded PC quotient with a curve.

Repair cost controls

Native rectangle. For every \(n\ge3\), over the Boolean-only degree-four consequence space in \(\mathbb F_2[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\), take \(K=2,d=t=1\), family \((x_1,x_2)\), and any \(q\in\operatorname{span}(x_1,x_2)\). Let \(P=1+q\) and \(T:f\mapsto([Px_1f],[Px_2f])\) on multilinear \(U=V_2\) modulo Booleanity. No single scalar native rectangle \(B(f,h)=\mu(Efh)\), with \(E\) a scalar combination of the two written errors, full left space \(U\), full right space of degree at most \(L\), and reserve \(\deg E+2+L\le4\), has radical on the left equal to \(\ker T\).

Proof. If \(q\ne0\), the three possibilities are \(x_1,x_2,x_1+x_2\). A nonzero error component takes value one respectively at \((0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\). Varying the spectator \(x_3\) proves that its products by \(1,x_3\) are independent modulo Booleanity, so \(\operatorname{rank}T\ge2\). Every nonzero written error combination equals \((1+q)(a x_1+b x_2)\), of degree two, even over a scalar extension. Thus \(L=0\), and a single scalar rectangle has rank at most one. A zero combination has rank zero. If \(q=0\), its nonzero combinations have degree one and \(L\le1\), so rectangle rank is at most \(n+1\). A degree-two Boolean function killed by both \(x_1,x_2\) is a scalar multiple of \((1+x_1)(1+x_2)\): its function support lies at \(x_1=x_2=0\), and multiplying any nonconstant spectator term by that indicator has degree at least three. Hence \(\operatorname{rank}T=\dim U-1=n(n+1)/2>n+1\). Equal left kernels would require equal ranks, a contradiction. The original Pang selection window \(1+2+1=4\) holds. The result concerns the displayed single rectangle, not several functionals, a changed left domain, or arbitrary constrained pairings.

Artin–Rees delay. For every \(m\ge1\), take \(R=k[t]\), \(I=(t)\), \(M=R\), \(N=(t^m)\). The Artin–Rees equality \(I^nM\cap N=I^{n-c}(I^cM\cap N)\) needs \(c\ge m\): at \(n=m\) and \(c<m\), the left ideal is \((t^m)\) while the right is \((t^{2m-c})\). Conversely \(c=m\) works for every \(n\ge m\). Thus the theorem's eventual stabilization has no presentation-independent constant delay.

Observability horizon. On \(k^m\), let \(Ae_i=e_{i-1}\) for \(i>1\), \(Ae_1=0\), and \(C=e_1^*\). The first \(h\le m\) observations \(C,CA,\ldots,CA^{h-1}\) are the first \(h\) coordinate rows. Their common kernel has dimension \(m-h\), and it becomes zero only at \(h=m\). This is the sharp elementary shift control for the observability horizon; stabilization alone does not give a short degree budget.

Degenerate cases. The rectangle assertion excludes \(n<3\); its rank comparison uses a spectator. The zero error combination never increases rank. Certified repair composes exact cleanup with finite-grid approximation

15 October 2026 · Working proof with explicit structural certificates · Certified repair. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Chosen. Develop common-multiplier-compatible-repair on effective-selection and effective-common-multiplier, its first development. The scheduled review selected a lemma-first composition from structural certificates, rather than requiring a preferred pairing or an improved unrestricted rank bound. The missing implication is a complete costed construction recovering Braun and Pang and supporting a distinct use. The construction below separates exact certificate extraction, adaptive contraction, protected survival and final replay.

Owed attempt. The review's exact-cleanup-then-adaptive operation is carried out with all earlier products charged at one final cutoff. The known Boolean weighted lemma already gives that algebraic composition. The additional work here is an explicit sampling cost and an extension to finite coordinate grids over any finite field, using the normalized-matching theorem for products of chains. The input representation is stated; a bounded-PC basis is not assumed inexpensive in the original formula length.

Architecture test. Decided. The proposed composition works under its supplied structural certificates and joint ledger, as predicted. It does not automatically extract such certificates for arbitrary source families. The finite-grid and sampling statements provide a concrete generalization and construction guarantee beyond a scalar kernel representation. General statement. lem:rank-retention-sampling gives a checked Las Vegas choice rule for a finite-field matrix pencil. thm:finite-grid-repair extends the weighted adaptive mechanism from Boolean variables over a prime field to product grids over every finite field, with the appropriate rank profile and original-style degree reserve. thm:certified-repair-composition combines independently bounded exact observations with this adaptive provider while preserving previous repairs at the final cutoff. Novelty of the underlying linear algebra, product theorem or approximation method is not claimed.

The core abstraction. A common multiplier repairs a finite algebraic process on a surviving cyclic part of its target. Every approximate relation has a defect; multiplication by the same weight kills those defects while commuting with the permitted paid operations. Survival prevents the repair from being the zero map. The power comes from selecting that one weight by a quantitative dimension certificate, rather than multiplying a separate locator for every defect. Braun obtains the certificate from ordinary restriction geometry and then chooses a weight-dependent substitution; Pang first reduces the defect ranks by adaptive approximation and then selects the weight. The common algebraic structure does not erase this difference in how the certificates are obtained.

Rank retention sampling

Statement. Let \(k=\mathbb F_q\), with \(q\) any prime power, and let \(M_1,\ldots,M_s\) be matrices over \(k\). Suppose their generic pencil has rank \(R\), and that \(R\) is known or structurally certified. A uniform independent \(a\in k^s\) satisfies

\[\Pr\!\left[\operatorname{rank}\sum_i a_iM_i\ge R-\lfloor R/q\rfloor\right]\ge\frac1{R+1}.\tag{1}\]

Repeated independent draws, accepting only after an exact rank test, therefore terminate almost surely in at most \(R+1\) expected draws. At \(R=0\), choose the zero vector immediately. This is a bound in matrix-rank tests, not a promise that the input matrices or generic rank are cheaply available.

Proof of the rank expectation. Pang's rank-specialization proof works over every finite field. To make the extension explicit, take a nonzero maximal minor \(H\) of the generic pencil, of total degree at most \(R\). At a point \(a\), constant row operations make at least \(R-\operatorname{rank}M(a)\) rows of that minor vanish, so its multiplicity at \(a\) is at least that deficiency. For a nonzero polynomial of degree \(d\) on \(k^s\), the sum of point multiplicities is at most \(dq^{s-1}\). Here is the induction: write \(H(y,z)=\sum_{j=0}^tH_j(y)z^j\), \(H_t\ne0\); at \(y=b\), a lowest-degree nonzero coefficient of \(H_t(b+y)\), of degree \(\mu\), is the leading coefficient of a degree-\(t\) polynomial in \(z\). Thus each full multiplicity is at most \(\mu\) plus that univariate multiplicity. Summing over \(z\in k\) gives at most \(q\mu+t\); induction on \(H_t\), and \(\deg H_t+t\le d\), finish. The univariate case is the root-multiplicity bound. Averaging the determinant deficiencies gives \(\mathbb E\operatorname{rank}M(a)\ge(1-1/q)R\).

Integer acceptance bound. Write \(R=qv+r\), \(0\le r<q\), and \(b=R-v\). If acceptance has probability \(\theta\), the rank is at most \(b-1\) on failure and at most \(R\) always. Therefore \(\theta\ge(q-r)/(q(v+1))\). This is at least \(1/(R+1)\), since \((q-r)(R+1)-q(v+1)=R(q-r-1)\ge0\). The geometric waiting-time formula proves (1). For \(q=2,R=1,M(a)=a\), acceptance probability is exactly one half, so the bound is attained in a nontrivial case.

Finite-grid repair

Setting. Work over \(k=\mathbb F_q\). Fix nonempty sets \(A_i\subseteq k\), \(a_i=|A_i|\), on variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\), and their monic domain polynomials \(F_i(x_i)=\prod_{\alpha\in A_i}(x_i-\alpha)\). Put \(L=\sum_i(a_i-1)\). Let \(J_D\le k[x]_{\le D}\) be a degree-\(D\) pseudoideal containing all degree-at-most-\(D\) domain consequences. Thus \(u\in J_D,\deg u+\deg v\le D\) implies \(uv\in J_D\). An actual bounded-PC consequence space containing the \(F_i\) is an example. It is not replaced by an unrestricted ideal.

Let \(V_k=k[x]_{\le k}\), and let \(\mathcal N_A(k)\) count exponent vectors \(0\le\alpha_i<a_i\) with \(|\alpha|\le k\). Equivalently it is the coefficient sum through \(k\) of \(\prod_i(1+z+\cdots+z^{a_i-1})\). Fix \(w\notin J_D\) of degree at most \(b\), \(M\ge1\) finite tuples \(g_{\nu,i}\) of degree at most \(d\), and integers \(t\ge1\), \(1\le d\le K\le L\). Assume

\[\Delta=(q-1)dt,\qquad b+K+\Delta+d\le D,\qquad \eta=(1-1/q)\frac{\mathcal N_A(K-d)}{\mathcal N_A(K)},\qquad M(1-\eta)^t<1.\tag{2}\]

Statement. There are \(q_{\nu,j}\in\operatorname{span}_k\{g_{\nu,i}\}_i\), \(P_\nu=\prod_{j=1}^t(1-q_{\nu,j}^{q-1})\), and a grid-reduced polynomial \(f\) of degree at most \(K\), such that

\[wf\notin J_D,\qquad wfP_\nu g_{\nu,i}\in J_D\quad\text{for every }\nu,i.\tag{3}\]

For each tuple, its final actual error rank is at most \(h_w(K)(1-\eta)^t\), where \(h_w(K)=\operatorname{rank}(u\in V_K\mapsto[wu])\). Every previously proved \(wE\in J_D\) persists as \(wfE\in J_D\) when its actual product ceiling \(\deg(wE)+K\le D\) holds. The output is constructed over the original field; no analysis-field extension changes source coefficients.

Grid reduction. Successive division by the monic \(F_i\) expresses every polynomial as its unique reduced representative, with each exponent below \(a_i\), plus domain multiples of no larger total degree. Uniqueness follows by induction from the univariate root bound on the distinct points \(A_i\). In particular a polynomial vanishing on the grid is a domain consequence through its actual degree. For \(g\in k[x]_{\le d}\), \(g^q-g\) vanishes there and is a domain consequence through \(qd\). This replaces Boolean reduction, with its full degree charge retained.

Imported combinatorial input. A product of finite chains has the normalized-matching property: for a subset of a rank level, its upper shadow occupies at least the same fraction of the next level. The full product theorem for normal posets with log-concave rank numbers is read in Madiman–Wang–Woo, arXiv:1712.00913v3, Section 3.2, Proposition 3.1, attributed there to Hsieh–Kleitman and Engel. Each unweighted chain is normal with log-concave rank numbers, so repeated products give the stated input, including singleton factors. This published combinatorial theorem is imported, not reproved here; it concerns integer counts and has no field-characteristic restriction.

Normalized error rank. For a fixed prefactor \(A\) of degree at most \(a\), define \(Z_A(k)=\{u\in V_k:Ag_i u\in J_D\ \forall i\}\) and \(c_A(k)=\dim V_k/Z_A(k)\). In the window \(a+K+d\le D\), these spaces respect filtration intersections and multiplication within degree \(K\). Their standard monomials under a degree-compatible order form a downward-closed subset of the exponent box: domain leading monomials exclude \(x_i^{a_i}\), and bounded absorption makes the excluded set upward closed within the window. A level's excluded monomials have their upper shadow excluded too. Normalized matching therefore makes the fractions of retained monomials nonincreasing by degree. Cumulative weighted averages give

\[c_A(K-d)\ge\frac{\mathcal N_A(K-d)}{\mathcal N_A(K)}c_A(K).\tag{4}\]

This uses the full degree domain, not an arbitrary selected subspace whose rank profile need not be normal.

One adaptive step. Suppose \(a+K+qd\le D\). On \(V_{K-d}\), put \(M_i u=([Ag_\alpha g_i u])_\alpha\). Its stacked kernel equals \(Z_A(K-d)\): one inclusion is absorption; the other follows from \(Ag_i^2u\in J_D\), multiplication by \(g_i^{q-2}\), and subtraction of \(Au(g_i^q-g_i)\). Those operations fit \(a+K+(q-1)d\le D\).

For independent parameters \(\lambda_i\), put \(E=k(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_s)\). The generic pencil \(M(\lambda)\) has the same kernel as the stacked map after scalar extension. Indeed \(g_\lambda=\sum\lambda_i g_i\) and \(Ag_\alpha g_\lambda u\in J_D^E\) imply \(Ag_\alpha g_\lambda^q u\in J_D^E\); subtracting \(\sum_i\lambda_i^q Ag_\alpha(g_i^q-g_i)u\) gives \(M(\lambda^q)u=0\), within \(a+K+qd\). Scalar extension preserves the degree intersections and bounded absorption: expand a degree-\(j\) consequence in a base-field basis of \(J_D\cap V_j\) before multiplying it. Corresponding minors of \(M(\lambda^q)\) are \(q\)-th powers of those of \(M(\lambda)\), so the inclusion of kernels is equality. The kernel is stable under coordinatewise \(q\)-Frobenius; the unique reduced row-echelon basis must have entries fixed by that map, hence in \(k\). Parameter independence then identifies it with the stacked kernel. This is Pang's descent argument with the field cardinality \(q\), not an assertion that an arbitrary extension-valued polynomial satisfies \(u^q=u\).

Consequently the computable stacked rank \(R=c_A(K-d)\) is the generic rank. By (1), choose an original-field \(q_0\in\operatorname{span}\{g_i\}\) with the rank of \(u\mapsto([Ag_\alpha q_0u])_\alpha\) at least \((1-1/q)c_A(K-d)\). For \(A'=A(1-q_0^{q-1})\), its kernel contains both \(Z_A(K)\) and \(q_0V_{K-d}\): preserve the former by absorption, and use \(q_0-q_0^q\) for the latter. Both cost at most \(a+K+qd\). Counting the gained subspace modulo the old kernel gives

\[c_{A'}(K)\le c_A(K)-(1-1/q)c_A(K-d)\le(1-\eta)c_A(K).\tag{5}\]

Iteration and survival. Start with \(A=w\). The kernel of \(u\mapsto[wu]\) lies in the initial error kernel, so \(c_w(K)\le h_w(K)>0\). At step \(j\le t\), \(a\le b+(j-1)(q-1)d\), and the maximum required degree is \(b+K+j(q-1)d+d\le D\). Thus each final tuple rank is at most \(h_w(K)(1-\eta)^t\). All final maps kill the same forbidden weight kernel. Their joint rank on its quotient is below \(h_w(K)\) by (2), giving a nonzero common kernel class. Choose a representative and reduce it on the grid; the changes to the weighted multiplier and every error product are domain consequences within the same bounds. This proves (3). The earlier-error assertion is direct bounded absorption of the already completed consequence \(wE\); it does not reweight its entire old derivation.

Construction cost. Given explicit dense polynomial coordinates and a basis/reduction map for \(J_D\), all maps above can be formed by bounded polynomial arithmetic and linear algebra. Each round computes its stacked rank once. Exact rank testing of independent coefficient draws finds its retained row in at most \(R+1\le\mathcal N_A(K-d)+1\) expected trials. Conditional on any previous choices this bound still holds, so all tuples and rounds use at most \(Mt(\mathcal N_A(K-d)+1)\) expected sampled rank tests, plus the initial stacked ranks and final kernel computation. Matrix dimensions and coordinate formation are polynomial in the explicit degree-\(D\) dense dimension, tuple lengths and degree parameters. This does not make them polynomial in \(n\), in a circuit description, or in the original proof size. Computing a PC consequence basis is part of the input-preparation cost, not free. Every accepted row and final multiplier is checked exactly, so randomness affects runtime, not correctness.

Certified repair composition

Static certificate. At one fixed final cutoff \(D\), let \(0\le b\le D\) and \(S\le k[x]_{\le b}\) be a supplied finite space, with a certified lower bound \(H_0\le\dim S/(S\cap J_D)\). Let \(\rho_a:S\to W_a\) be explicit linear observations with independently proved rank upper bounds \(r_a\), and \(\sum_a r_a<H_0\). Suppose that any chosen \(w\in\bigcap_a\ker\rho_a\setminus J_D\) admits a specified exact-repair construction: it freezes all earlier coefficient choices and yields actual old errors \(E_j\) with certificates \(wE_j\in J_D\). The observations may be ordinary polynomial restrictions, a faithful coding tester, or another proved provider; their implication to the exact errors must be established, not stipulated from the desired answer.

Statement. Such a \(w\) can be selected by linear algebra. If there is no residual family, take \(W=w\). Otherwise, when \(k=\mathbb F_q\) and the grid hypotheses and (2) hold for the frozen residual tuples, thm:finite-grid-repair constructs \(W=wf\) of degree at most \(b+K\), outside \(J_D\), killing every adaptive residual error. It also kills every earlier \(E_j\) whose certificate has \(\deg(wE_j)+K\le D\). If a fixed polynomial substitution \(\Phi\), possibly chosen after \(w\), has variable degree at most \(T\), a source derivation ceiling \(B\) replays under multiplication by \(W\) whenever all weighted image axioms have their certificates and \(b+K+TB\le D\). With no adaptive stage use \(K=0\). Construction cost is the static linear algebra and exact-repair algorithm, plus the explicitly represented adaptive cost above.

Proof. Rank-nullity gives \(\dim\bigcap_a\ker\rho_a\ge\dim S-\sum_a r_a>\dim(S\cap J_D)\). Therefore the common kernel contains \(w\notin J_D\), found by a kernel basis and reduction modulo \(J_D\), or by a separate injectivity certificate making every nonzero kernel vector safe. Freeze its exact-repair output before forming the residual maps. The preceding theorem supplies \(f\), and bounded absorption preserves the earlier errors at the displayed ceilings. For replay, linear combinations commute with \(F\mapsto W\Phi(F)\). A source variable-multiplication step becomes multiplication by \(\Phi(x)\); expand that polynomial into monomials and use the completed previous image line. Every intermediate product fits the original \(b+K+TB\) ceiling, using the actual degree of the source line before that multiplication. Constant or zero images only lower the degree. This gives the weighted derivation with the same fixed \(W,\Phi\), without assigning separate weights to its lines. The terminal image is \(W\) if the source terminal polynomial is one. This is the costed cyclic-repair principle, not a claim that every approximate interpretation is a fixed substitution.

Source adapters and a new domain

Braun. Use the published binary row-linear space \(S=\mathcal L_k\), its separation from the old \(J_D\) at the final \(D=k(B+1)\), and the ordinary high-flat restriction maps. The matched result cor:ordinary-restriction-moments supplies \(\dim S=\sum_{j\le k}\binom mj\ell^j\) and total restriction rank at most one quarter of \(\binom mk\ell^k\), under its full hypotheses \(m>0,\ell\ge2,M,k\ge1\), at most \(M\) proper blocks of input-span rank greater than \(h(k+1)\), \(h=3\ell\), \(m\log(4M)\le k^2\), \(k\le m\), \(B\ge2h+1\), \(4(k-1)<2^\ell\), \(2k(B+1)-1\le2^\ell\). The source is one complete old-affine level with disjoint fresh coefficient variables, all companions and all Boolean fields. Ordinary vanishing yields literal cofactors of degree at most \(k-1\); the existing low-rank packing, high-unit cleanup and high-proper cofactor construction produce the simultaneous substitution of degree at most \(k\), with weighted image certificates and replay through \(k(B+1)\). This is the static stage with no residual family. Its substitution depends on the selected weight, which is allowed because it is fixed before replay. No finite-point replacement is made.

Pang. Take \(S=\langle1\rangle\), no static observations, \(H_0=1\), \(w=1\), and Boolean coordinate grids \(A_i=\{0,1\}\) over the original prime field \(\mathbb F_p\). Then \(\mathcal N_A(K)=N_n(K)\), \(L=n\), and (2) is precisely \((p-1)dt+K+d\le D\) and \(M(1-\eta)^t<1\), with Pang's original \(\eta\). The one-step and final error statements reproduce Theorem 4.3. Its inference simulation is an approximate-map adapter rather than the fixed-substitution clause: Proposition 5.1 uses the same actual error identities at \(K+\max\{2\Delta+2d,\Delta+w(F)\}\le D\), giving the terminal \(f\in J_D\). That separate ledger is unchanged. The previously checked binary leveled choice order also remains available once earlier levels are frozen; no new all-depth source coverage is asserted.

Finite-grid application. The adaptive statement now applies directly to systems over \(\mathbb F_q\) whose coordinates have specified finite sets \(A_i\), using the product-of-chains profile rather than the Boolean binomial profile. For example, on \(\mathbb F_3^n\) it uses coefficient sums of \((1+z+z^2)^n\), with factors \(1-q_{\nu,j}^2\) and reserve \(b+K+2dt+d\le D\). This is a distinct native finite-domain repair theorem; it is not a claim of a new lower bound for such systems or a comparison with an unanalysed Boolean encoding.

Coding comparison. The structural pattern also retains thm:bilinear-error-recovery: the observable received-word tester has the exact error kernel, its rank is bounded by error support, and signal injectivity preserves the message. The original two linear systems and polynomial-evaluation budget \(n\ge k+2t\) remain the constructive application. This is an established parallel provider, not a new decoding algorithm. Curve locators remain a queued extension with their section and protected-value costs.

Nonvacuity. For the finite-grid selection budget, take every \(A_i=\mathbb F_q\), the domain-only \(J_{q+1}\), \(w=1\), one family \((x_1)\), \(d=K=t=1\), and \(D=q+1\). Then \(P=1-x_1^{q-1}\), \(f=1\) give \(Px_1=x_1-x_1^q\in J_D\) and a surviving unit, for every \(n\ge1\). The strict rank-sum condition holds since \(\eta=(1-1/q)/(n+1)>0\). This example verifies selection only. Braun's unbounded regime and its separate replay conditions remain those in the matched source adapter, not claims about this satisfiable control.

Nonvacuity. A mixed instance of the composition budget uses the Boolean-only \(J_4\), \(n\ge3\), \(S=\operatorname{span}\{1,x_1\}\), and ordinary restriction \(x_1=0\). Its rank is one and \(S\cap J_4=0\), so choose \(w=x_1\), which kills the exact error \(E_0=1-x_1\) through degree two. The residual tuple is \((x_2,x_3)\), with \(b=d=K=t=1,M=1\); its reserve is \(1+1+1+1=4\). Choose \(q_0=x_2\), \(P=1-x_2\), and \(f=x_2\). Then \(W=x_1x_2\) survives, kills \(E_0\) through degree three and both residual errors through degree four. Neither \(w\) alone nor the selected prefix \(P\) alone kills the residual error involving \(x_3\); the final multiplier is used. This is a concrete use of the known weighted composition, not a lower bound or a claim that every unweighted strategy fails.

Degenerate cases. Zero error tuples need no sampled row and have zero rank. At generic rank zero no random search is required. A zero protected image cannot meet a strict survival condition. The adaptive theorem assumes \(L\ge K\ge d\ge1\); an all-singleton grid is outside that stage and reduces to constant data. Singleton factors in a larger grid cause no problem. Static observations may be empty, as in Pang, and no adaptive stage is required, as in Braun. Two separately nonzero weights can multiply to zero; only survival of \(wf\) in the same final quotient is asserted. No basis of an inconsistent full quotient is substituted for the proper bounded consequence space.

New mathematics. A quantitative sampling rule and the finite-grid/all-finite-field extension of the weighted approximation mechanism, assembled with explicit exact-repair composition. The Boolean composition and source adapters use existing proofs with their costs unchanged. The product-of-chains theorem is an attributed import.

Selection gain. The gain is a proved selection theorem for additional finite domains and a checked construction cost, not a sharper Boolean/Pang contraction rate. Independent structural certificates are explicit; the theorem does not assume its final common multiplier. Its static rank input still needs a genuine geometric or coding bound, and its adaptive input needs the stated full degree domain and field equations.

Curve locators recover unknown errors while fixing a protected value

16 October 2026 · Working proof of an established geometric recovery mechanism · Marked curve recovery. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Chosen. Develop the curve-locator lead on application and geometric-repair-application, before the coding-rank head, following the user's priority order. The missing implication is recovery from unknown error positions with an explicit positive-genus family and complete construction and pole budgets. A nonzero locator for a known divisor alone does not supply it.

Owed attempt. The lead asks for a concrete additional provider retaining its genus cost and distinguishing sections from rational functions. This entry constructs an observable linear system, proves that every accepted solution kills the actual error, and supplies an explicit Hermitian family. There is no previously deferred attempt on this item.

General statement. thm:marked-curve-recovery gives geometric certificates for the established two-system recovery mechanism, including a prescribed locator value. cor:hermitian-repair-family makes the curve, points, bases, input representation and costs explicit at unbounded parameters. These are an application and synthesis of standard algebraic-geometry decoding, not a new decoding algorithm or a better decoding radius.

Marked curve recovery

Statement. Let \(X/k\) be a smooth projective geometrically integral curve over a finite field, of genus \(g\). Let \(P_1,\ldots,P_n\) be distinct rational points and \(A,G\) divisors of nonnegative degrees \(a,m\), whose supports avoid those points. Write \(L(B)=H^0(X,\mathcal O(B))\) as rational functions with \((u)+B\ge0\), together with zero. Let \(t\ge0\), and assume

\[a\ge t+g,\qquad n>a+m+t.\tag{1}\]

Given \(y_i=f(P_i)+e_i\), with unknown \(f\in L(G)\) and at most \(t\) nonzero \(e_i\), solve the homogeneous linear system

\[\lambda\in L(A),\quad N\in L(A+G),\qquad N(P_i)=\lambda(P_i)y_i\quad(1\le i\le n).\tag{2}\]

There is a nonzero solution, every nonzero solution has \(\lambda\ne0\), and every such solution satisfies \(N=\lambda f\) as rational functions and \(\lambda(P_i)e_i=0\) at every coordinate. Recover \(f\) by solving the second linear system

\[h\in L(G),\qquad \lambda(P_i)h(P_i)=N(P_i)\quad(1\le i\le n).\tag{3}\]

This system has the unique solution \(h=f\). If a further rational point \(R\) avoids the evaluation points and the supports of \(A,G\), and \(a\ge t+2g\), one may instead impose \(\lambda(R)=1\) in (2). That affine system is consistent, and every solution has the same recovery properties and satisfies \(N(R)=f(R)\). The value \(f(R)\) is recovered without receiving it. With bases and evaluation matrices for \(L(A),L(G),L(A+G)\) supplied, both variants use \(O(n^3)\) field operations and \(O(n^2)\) field elements of memory. Basis and evaluation construction is a separate input cost until an explicit family is supplied below.

Proof: existence. Let \(E=\sum_{e_i\ne0}P_i\), of degree \(e\le t\). Riemann–Roch gives \(\ell(A-E)\ge a-e+1-g\ge1\); this is cor:curve-locator-budget, whose full proof and defining hypotheses were reread. A nonzero \(\lambda\in L(A-E)\) vanishes as a rational function at the erroneous coordinates, since the support of \(A\) avoids them. Taking \(N=\lambda f\in L(A+G)\) solves (2). In the marked case, the same recorded locator lemma gives \(\lambda(R)=1\), since \(a\ge e+2g\). Its proof uses \(H^1(A-E-R)=0\) and the evaluation exact sequence. The algorithm need not know \(E\); it solves (2) using only \(y\) and the supplied spaces.

Proof: every solution works. A nonzero \(u\in L(B)\), with \(\deg B=b\) and with the evaluation points outside its support, has at most \(b\) zeros among those points: its effective divisor \((u)+B\) has degree \(b\). If \(\lambda=0\) in (2), then \(N\) vanishes at all \(n>a+m\) points, hence \(N=0\). For any solution, \(N-\lambda f\in L(A+G)\) vanishes at all \(n-e\ge n-t>a+m\) correct positions. It is therefore zero identically. Substitution in (2) proves \(\lambda(P_i)e_i=0\). If \(h\) also solves (3), the function \(\lambda(h-f)\in L(A+G)\) vanishes at all \(n>a+m\) points, so is zero. The function field is a domain and \(\lambda\ne0\), hence \(h=f\). This is injectivity on the clean message space, even though multiplication by \(\lambda\) need not be invertible on all evaluation vectors. In the marked case, evaluating \(N=\lambda f\) at \(R\) gives the asserted protected value.

Proof: representation and cost. Choose bases of the three Riemann–Roch spaces. Equation (2) has \(n\) rows and \(\ell(A)+\ell(A+G)\) columns, plus one row in the marked variant; (3) has \(n\) rows and \(\ell(G)\) columns. For any divisor of nonnegative degree \(b\) on this curve, \(\ell(B)\le b+1\). One proof extends the field to an algebraic closure and evaluates at \(b+1\) distinct points away from the support: the zero bound makes evaluation injective, and scalar extension preserves dimension. By (1), \(a+m

What is repaired and what survives

Set \(U=\operatorname{ev}L(A)\), \(C=\operatorname{ev}L(G)\), \(H=\operatorname{ev}L(A+G)\) on the \(n\) received coordinates, and let \(Q:k^n\to k^n/H\) be the explicit quotient tester obtained by elimination. Then \(U*C\subseteq H\). For an error supported on at most \(t\) positions, \(H\) has no nonzero vector on those positions, because its minimum distance is at least \(n-a-m>t\). Thus \(Q\) detects every possible nonzero product \(\lambda*e\). Its error-action rank is at most \(t\), whereas evaluation on \(L(A)\) is injective and \(\dim U=\ell(A)\ge a+1-g>t\). Multiplication by every nonzero locator is injective on \(C\), by the same zero bound. These verify each hypothesis of thm:bilinear-error-recovery from divisor data, without assuming a successful locator.

Equation (2) is the explicit lift of \(Q(\lambda*y)=0\): \(N\) witnesses membership in \(H\). In the marked case use the evaluation algebra on \(P_1,\ldots,P_n,R\) to view \(\lambda\) as one multiplier annihilating the defect vector \((e_1,\ldots,e_n,0)\) while fixing the \(R\)-coordinate idempotent. It fixes the protected value and permits full message recovery. The extra coordinate is not supplied to the decoding algorithm; it is evaluated after (3).

The multiplicative budget is \(L(A)L(G)\subseteq L(A+G)\), with total pole-divisor degree \(a+m\); the observable detection margin is \(n-t>a+m\). On a one-point curve \(F_b=L(bP_\infty)\), multiplication obeys \(F_bF_c\subseteq F_{b+c}\). Consequently a fixed multiplier of pole order at most \(a\) carries a source expression of pole budget \(B\) through \(a+B\), using the same completed-product argument as certified repair composition. This is the geometric provider of the repair principle, with the bilinear theorem as its precise existing interface. It is not an identification of pole filtration with total polynomial degree or of this evaluation algebra with an unsatisfiable bounded-PC quotient. The arbitrary-error finite-grid contraction theorem is not invoked on the curve.

An explicit positive-genus family

Statement. For every \(s=2^r\ge4\), work in a supplied representation of \(k=\mathbb F_{s^2}\) and take the projective Hermitian curve

\[Y^sZ+YZ^s=X^{s+1},\qquad P_\infty=(0:1:0),\qquad R=(0:0:1).\]

Use all affine rational points except \(R\) as the received coordinates. Put

\[n=s^3-1,\quad g=s(s-1)/2,\quad m=s^3/4-1,\quad t=s^3/8-1,\quad a=t+2g,\quad G=mP_\infty,\quad A=aP_\infty.\tag{4}\]

The marked algorithm recovers every \(f\in L(mP_\infty)\) after arbitrary errors at at most \(t\) coordinates and produces a locator with \(\lambda(R)=1\). The message dimension is \(m-g+1>0\). Points, bases and evaluation matrices can be constructed in \(O(n^3)\) field operations with \(O(n^2)\) memory, including the subsequent two-system decoder. Thus no Riemann–Roch-space oracle is hidden for this family. Field construction itself is excluded by the supplied-field representation; these are field-operation, not bit-complexity, bounds.

Geometry and point count. The three homogeneous partial derivatives are respectively \(X^s,Z^s,Y^s\) up to nonzero signs, so they never vanish simultaneously at a projective point. The curve is smooth over the algebraic closure. A smooth plane curve is geometrically integral: distinct positive-degree components would meet by projective Bézout and create a singularity, and a repeated component would also be singular. Its degree is \(s+1\), so the plane-curve genus formula gives \(g=s(s-1)/2\). Both formulas are standard imported curve facts, also stated for this family in Høholdt–van Lint–Pellikaan, Example 2.74; their specific smoothness and count checks are supplied here.

The only point at infinity is \(P_\infty\). For each \(x\in\mathbb F_{s^2}\), \(x^{s+1}\) lies in \(\mathbb F_s\). The trace \(y\mapsto y^s+y\) is a nonzero \(\mathbb F_s\)-linear map onto \(\mathbb F_s\), with kernel of size \(s\): it is not the zero map since the polynomial \(Y^s+Y\) has at most \(s\) roots in a field of size \(s^2\). Thus there are exactly \(s\) affine \(y\)'s for each \(x\), hence \(s^3\) affine points. Remove \(R\) to obtain \(n\).

Explicit bases and filtration. In the chart \(Y=1\) at infinity put \(u=X/Y,v=Z/Y\). The equation is \(v+v^s=u^{s+1}\). Since its derivative with respect to \(v\) is one, \(u\) is a uniformizer; \(1+v^{s-1}\) is a unit and \(\operatorname{ord}_{P_\infty}v=s+1\). Therefore the affine coordinates \(x=X/Z=u/v\), \(y=Y/Z=1/v\) have pole orders \(s,s+1\). The affine coordinate ring is \(k[x,y]/(y^s+y-x^{s+1})\), free over \(k[x]\) on \(1,y,\ldots,y^{s-1}\), by monic division. A rational function with poles only at infinity is regular on this smooth affine complement, hence lies in that coordinate ring. The weights \(si+(s+1)j\), for \(i\ge0,0\le j

\[\mathcal B_b=\{x^iy^j:i\ge0,\ 0\le j

is a basis of \(L(bP_\infty)\) for every \(b\ge0\). The reduction \(y^s=x^{s+1}-y\) never increases pole weight, although it can increase ordinary total degree. This distinction is retained in every cost statement.

Budget and construction. The identity \(a=t+2g\) supplies marked locator existence. The detection margin is

\[n-(a+m+t)=s^3/2-s^2+s+2>0\qquad(s\ge4).\tag{6}\]

Also \(m>2g-2\), since \(m-(2g-2)=s^3/4-s^2+s+1>0\) for \(s\ge4\). Riemann–Roch therefore gives the stated message dimension. List field elements in the supplied representation and enumerate the at most \(s^4\) affine pairs, testing the equation by repeated powering in \(O(\log s)\) operations per pair. This costs \(O(s^4\log s)\subseteq O(n^3)\), and only the accepted points need storage. Enumerate the integer pairs in (5) for \(b=a,m,a+m\). Each list has at most \(b+1=O(n)\) elements. At each accepted point, precompute powers of \(x\) and \(y\) through the largest needed exponents, then form all basis evaluations; this takes \(O(n^2)\) field operations and storage. Forming (2), its normalization row and (3) and solving them takes \(O(n^3)\). No numerical test is used to establish these asymptotic statements.

Nonvacuity. For the general recovery budget and explicit Hermitian budget, (4) gives a family for every \(s=2^r\ge4\). At \(s=4\), symbolic substitution gives \(n=63,g=6,m=15,t=7,a=19\), message dimension ten and margin \(63-(19+15+7)=22\). These are arithmetic consequences of (4), not reported computer output. The message space includes one, and every error pattern of the stated size is covered. The genus and length grow unboundedly, and \(s^3-1>s^2+1\), so this is not the previous projective-line evaluation construction on the same alphabet. No claim of a new code or superior decoding radius is made.

Degenerate cases. At \(t=0\), the proof still works; the homogeneous variant has a nonzero solution and the marked variant has its normalized solution. The zero message is recovered uniquely because the product argument uses \(\lambda\ne0\), not \(f\ne0\). Empty coordinate sets cannot satisfy (1). Repeated points violate the distinct-point hypothesis and cannot be counted as extra zeros. A protected point in the error support is excluded; the algorithm does not promise normalization there. Divisors meeting evaluation or protected points are excluded because ordinary rational-function evaluation would not supply the stated coordinates. Genus zero specializes to the recorded polynomial locator mechanism rather than a new result. A nonzero locator may vanish on some correct coordinates; recovery still follows from the whole product identity, not coordinatewise division.

Common marked locator for overlapping supports below the summed-rank budget

16 October 2026 · Working proof, elementary union-of-supports scope · Overlapping curve recovery and exact selection. Produced by claude-code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning medium).

The notebook's goal statement orders the four objectives, “Pursue them in that order”, and its Route decisions record that the user requires all four; joint-error-savings is the first open one. The preceding entry's reviewer suggestion, verified there by the author (Reviewer's suggestions of the marked-recovery entry), named this construction with simultaneous received-word systems and an explicit sum-of-ranks baseline. General statement. thm:overlapping-curve-recovery gives the exact joint error-action rank on a common geometric domain, simultaneous marked recovery, and an unbounded Hermitian family where the summed-rank sufficient criterion fails at a working pole budget. lem:exact-common-kernel-selection replaces the summed rank condition of the selection step in thm:certified-repair-composition by an exact criterion on the stacked observation map. In the evaluation model the joint rank is the size of the union of supports by definition: this is the elementary common-locator mechanism of interleaved decoding, not a new decoding algorithm or a bound on the joint action of paid proof errors.

Exact common-kernel selection

Statement. Let \(S\) be a finite-dimensional space over a field, \(J\le S\) a subspace, \(\rho_a:S\to W_a\) finitely many linear maps, \(\rho=(\rho_a)_a\) the stacked map and \(q:S\to S/J\) the quotient. Then \(\bigcap_a\ker\rho_a\not\subseteq J\) if and only if

\[\operatorname{rank}(\rho,q)>\operatorname{rank}\rho.\tag{0}\]

In particular (0) holds whenever \(\operatorname{rank}\rho<\dim S/J\), and so whenever \(\sum_ar_a<\dim S/J\) for upper bounds \(r_a\ge\operatorname{rank}\rho_a\). A basis of \(\ker\rho\) and reduction modulo \(J\) find a vector of \(\ker\rho\setminus J\) when (0) holds.

Proof. \(\ker(\rho,q)=\ker\rho\cap J\). Rank–nullity on \(S\) for both maps gives \(\dim\ker\rho-\dim(\ker\rho\cap J)=\operatorname{rank}(\rho,q)-\operatorname{rank}\rho\). The left side is positive exactly when \(\ker\rho\not\subseteq J\). For the sufficient forms, \(\operatorname{rank}(\rho,q)\ge\operatorname{rank}q=\dim S/J\), and \(\operatorname{rank}\rho\le\sum_a\operatorname{rank}\rho_a\le\sum_ar_a\).

Use in the composition. In thm:certified-repair-composition take \(J=S\cap J_D\). Its proof uses the summed bound only to obtain some \(w\in\bigcap_a\ker\rho_a\setminus J_D\); the exact-repair construction, the finite-grid stage, the absorption of earlier errors and replay all start from that chosen \(w\), as its full proof states. So the composition holds verbatim with its hypothesis \(\sum_ar_a<H_0\) replaced by any certificate of (0). This changes the selection hypothesis, not its later costs. A certificate of (0) is itself a cost: an independent bound on each \(\rho_a\) does not bound the stacked rank better than the sum, and for Braun's and Pang's adapters no joint bound is recorded. The curve theorem below supplies one in its own model. It is a linear-algebra refinement; by its registered statement, read in this cycle, lem:weight-compatibility-factorization already uses the predicate “common kernel nonzero in the quotient by the forbidden space” for two families.

Overlapping curve recovery

Setting and statement. Use a smooth projective geometrically integral curve \(X/k\) of genus \(g\) over a finite field, distinct rational received points \(P_1,\ldots,P_n\), a further protected rational point \(R\), and divisors \(A,G\) of nonnegative degrees \(a,m\) supported away from all these points. There are \(L\ge1\) received words

\[y^{(j)}=\operatorname{ev}(f_j)+e^{(j)},\qquad f_j\in L(G).\]

Let \(E_j\) be the exact nonzero support of \(e^{(j)}\), \(E=\bigcup_jE_j\), \(u=|E|\), \(t=\max_j|E_j|\). Assume

\[a\ge u+2g,\qquad n>a+m+t.\tag{1}\]

All ranks below use the same domain \(U=L(A)\). Define \(T_j(\lambda)=(\lambda(P_i)e_i^{(j)})_i\), \(H=\operatorname{ev}L(A+G)\), and the quotient map \(Q:k^n\to k^n/H\). Then

\[\operatorname{rank}T_j=\operatorname{rank}(QT_j)=|E_j|,\qquad \operatorname{rank}(T_1,\ldots,T_L)=\operatorname{rank}(QT_1,\ldots,QT_L)=u.\tag{2}\]

The common kernel is \(L(A-\sum_{i\in E}P_i)\), and evaluation at \(R\) on it is surjective. Thus a common locator \(\lambda(R)=1\) exists. It is found without knowing the supports by solving

\[\lambda\in L(A),\quad N_j\in L(A+G),\quad N_j(P_i)=\lambda(P_i)y_i^{(j)}\quad\forall i,j,\qquad\lambda(R)=1.\tag{3}\]

Every solution satisfies \(N_j=\lambda f_j\) identically and kills every actual error. Separate linear systems with this same locator recover all \(f_j\) and their protected values \(f_j(R)=N_j(R)\). With bases and evaluations, including the \(R\)-evaluation row, supplied, the algorithm uses \(O(Ln^3)\) field operations and \(O(n^2+Ln)\) memory. It may use supplied upper bounds \(u_0\ge u,t_0\ge t\) in (1); the actual supports need not be supplied or guessed. Finiteness of \(k\) is inherited from the dependency's statement and is not used by the new steps; the exact ranks need only \(a\ge u+2g-1\), and a nonzero common locator only \(a\ge u+g\); the full (1) is used for normalization at \(R\).

Proof of the rank identities. Since \(a-u-1\ge2g-1\), Riemann–Roch and the negative-degree dual-section criterion give \(H^1(A-\sum_{i\in E}P_i-R)=0\). The evaluation exact sequence makes

\[L(A)\longrightarrow k^E\oplus k,\qquad \lambda\longmapsto((\lambda(P_i))_{i\in E},\lambda(R))\tag{4}\]

surjective. This is the point-evaluation argument in the full proof of cor:curve-locator-budget, now for the whole finite set. Multiplication by an error factors through evaluation on its support, followed by an injective diagonal map because all its values there are nonzero. This proves the individual ranks. The stacked map factors through evaluation on \(E\), followed by an injective map: each union coordinate has a nonzero error value in at least one component, so an element killed in every component has every coordinate zero. Its rank is therefore \(u\), and its kernel is the stated vanishing space. Surjectivity in (4) supplies the normalized locator. In the language of lem:exact-common-kernel-selection with \(S=U\), \(J=\{\lambda:\lambda(R)=0\}\) and \(\rho=(T_j)_j\), (4) says \(\operatorname{rank}(\rho,q)=u+1>u=\operatorname{rank}\rho\), although \(\dim S/J=1\le u\): the sufficient forms of that lemma fail here and only the exact criterion applies.

A nonzero element of \(H\) has at least \(n-a-m>t\) nonzero coordinates, by the divisor-zero proof in thm:marked-curve-recovery. Thus \(Q\) is injective on vectors supported on any \(E_j\); applying it separately to the components preserves each individual kernel and the common kernel. Rank–nullity proves both observable identities in (2). All comparisons use \(U\), not separate quotients chosen for separate errors.

Proof of recovery and cost. Eliminating \(N_j\), a \(\lambda\in L(A)\) extends to a solution of (3) exactly when \(Q\operatorname{diag}(y^{(j)})\operatorname{ev}_A\lambda=0\) for every \(j\). Since \(\operatorname{ev}(\lambda f_j)\in H\), \(Q\operatorname{diag}(\operatorname{ev}f_j)\operatorname{ev}_A=0\), hence \(Q\operatorname{diag}(y^{(j)})\operatorname{ev}_A=QT_j\): the observable map of row \(j\) is \(QT_j\). A locator from (4) vanishing on \(E\), together with \(N_j=\lambda f_j\), solves (3), so that system is consistent. For any solution, \(N_j-\lambda f_j\) vanishes at the at least \(n-|E_j|>a+m\) correct positions in row \(j\); the same zero bound makes it identically zero. Since \(\lambda(R)=1\), it is nonzero. Recover each \(f_j\) by the second system of thm:marked-curve-recovery; its uniqueness proof applies verbatim to each row.

For the runtime bound, do not eliminate a single dense matrix with \(L\) separate numerator blocks cubically in its full width. First form \(Q\) once by elimination on the supplied evaluation basis of \(H\). In row \(j\) the observable map \(Q\,\mathrm{diag}(y^{(j)})\operatorname{ev}_A\) has at most \(n\) rows and \(a+1=O(n)\) columns. Form it in \(O(n^3)\) field operations and insert its rows into a maintained echelon system for \(\lambda\), including \(\lambda(R)=1\). Across all rows this costs \(O(Ln^3)\). The consistent affine solution is a locator. For each word solve \(\lambda(P_i)h(P_i)=\lambda(P_i)y_i^{(j)}\) in \(L(G)\), another \(O(n^3)\) operations. Compute \(N_j=\lambda h\), or just its evaluations and protected value, after recovering \(h\). Streaming the constraint rows requires \(O(n^2)\) workspace; retaining the received words uses \(O(Ln)\). Product coordinates, if requested, use the supplied multiplication representation or an additional solve in the injective evaluation basis of \(H\), again cubic per word. No search through supports is used.

One protected quotient

Let \(\mathcal A=k^{\{P_1,\ldots,P_n,R\}}\), with coordinate multiplication, and let \(\operatorname{ev}_{D+R}\) be the evaluation map from functions regular at these points. Its kernel is one fixed ideal. Its restriction to \(U=L(A)\) is injective, because a nonzero element of \(L(A)\) has at most \(a<n\) zeros. This identifies \(U\) with its image in that same algebra for every action in (2). Extend each error by zero at \(R\), and let \(p_R\) be the coordinate idempotent there. The selected multiplier obeys \(\lambda e^{(j)}=0\) for all \(j\) and \(\lambda p_R=p_R\). The \(R\)-coordinate is not discarded in a quotient or changed between rows. The tester quotient \(k^n/H\) is only an observation space, not the protected algebra. This section records the bookkeeping; it adds no constraint beyond (1).

Strict savings at unbounded parameters

Family. On the same Hermitian curves, received points and protected point as cor:hermitian-repair-family, take every \(s=2^r\ge8\) and put

\[n=s^3-1,\quad g=s(s-1)/2,\quad m=s^3/4-1,\quad d=s^3/16-1,\quad a=3d+2g,\quad A=aP_\infty,\ G=mP_\infty.\tag{5}\]

Choose disjoint sets \(I,J,K\) of received points, each of size \(d\), and take two error vectors with nonzero values exactly on \(E_1=I\cup J\) and \(E_2=I\cup K\). Arbitrary nonzero values are permitted. The decoder uses only \(u_0=3d,t_0=2d\). There are enough points since \(3d<n\). The supports and action kernels are distinct and incomparable: surjectivity in (4) gives a multiplier nonzero at a chosen point of \(J\) and zero on \(I\cup K\), and conversely for \(K\). Thus neither individual kernel contains the other.

The ranks are \(2d,2d\) and \(3d\) jointly. This is genuine overlap between different constraints on one domain, not copies of one error map or an invertible change of its output coordinates. It is elementary support geometry: the structural hypothesis, a bound on the union of supports, is in this model the joint-rank bound itself, so the saving over the sum is inclusion–exclusion. It supplies no bound on arbitrary PC error images.

Why one multiplier. Each word alone has a normalized locator at pole order \(2d+2g<a\), cheaper than both budgets below. Separate locators give separate multipliers. The selection step of thm:certified-repair-composition needs one weight \(w\) killing every defect while preserving the protected class, so the comparison below is between certificates for one common multiplier. The curve instance is an instance of lem:exact-common-kernel-selection only and an analogue of that selection step: the composition is stated for polynomial spaces \(S\le k[x]_{\le b}\) and a cutoff space \(J_D\), and no translation carrying \(L(A)\), its forbidden hyperplane \(\lambda(R)=0\) and its observations into that setting is given here.

Budget comparison. Since \(a\ge2g\), Riemann–Roch gives \(\ell(A)=a+1-g=3d+g+1\). Moreover

\[d-g-1=s^3/16-s(s-1)/2-2 =s^2(s-8)/16+s/2-2>0\quad(s\ge8).\tag{6}\]

Thus \(3d<\ell(A)<4d\). For a pole order \(b\), the individual rank of the action of \(e^{(j)}\) on \(L(bP_\infty)\) is \(\ell(bP_\infty)-\ell(bP_\infty-E_j)\), so the summed-rank criterion for a nonzero common multiplier reads \(\ell(bP_\infty)<\ell(bP_\infty-E_1)+\ell(bP_\infty-E_2)\).

  • For \(b\ge2d+2g-1\) both sides are nonspecial: \(\ell(bP_\infty-E_j)=b-2d+1-g\), \(\ell(bP_\infty)=b+1-g\), and the criterion holds exactly when \(b\ge b_{\rm sum}=4d+g\).
  • For \(b<2d\) the right side is zero and the criterion fails.
  • For \(2d\le b\le4d-g-1\), the upper bound \(\ell(D)\le\deg D+1\) for \(\deg D\ge0\) (used in thm:marked-curve-recovery) gives a right side at most \(2b-4d+2\le b+1-g\le\ell(bP_\infty)\), and the criterion fails.

The last two ranges and the first cover every \(b\) when \(4d-g-1\ge2d+2g-2\), that is \(2d\ge3g-1\); here \(2d-3g+1=s^2(s-12)/8+3s/2-1>0\) for \(s\ge16\). So for every \(s\ge16\) and every choice of \(I,J,K\), the exact summed-rank criterion first holds at \(b_{\rm sum}=4d+g\). At \(s=8\) the orders \(96\le b\le116\) are not covered by this argument; there the comparison is with the support-based rank bounds \(2d,2d\), which are exact at every \(b\ge2d+2g-1\) and valid upper bounds below, and the same threshold \(4d+g\) is that criterion's first order.

Two comparisons follow, with the same curve, point at infinity, supports and message divisor.

  • Nonzero against nonzero. The actual common kernel \(L(bP_\infty-E)\) is nonzero once \(b\ge3d+g\), by Riemann–Roch, against \(b_{\rm sum}=4d+g\): a saving of \(d\). At \(s=8\) this is established against the support-based rank bounds only, because of the uncovered orders above.
  • Protected against the summed baseline. The composition needs \(w\) outside the forbidden space, here \(\lambda(R)\ne0\). The summed and joint rank conditions of the composition both ask for a rank below \(\dim S/J=1\) and never hold. The exact criterion (0) holds at \(a=3d+2g\) by (4). Against the summed nonzero threshold, which gives no normalization at all, the saving is \(b_{\rm sum}-a=d-g>0\).

Neither \(3d+g\) nor \(a\) is asserted optimal, and other decoders are not compared. The saving survives detection and message recovery, because

\[n-(a+m+2d)=7s^3/16-s^2+s+5>0.\tag{7}\]

The baseline's larger pole budget also fits the observation window: \(n-(b_{\rm sum}+m+2d)=3s^3/8-s^2/2+s/2+6>0\). Thus the comparison is between two feasible pole windows, not with an impossible baseline. The weighted-message budget drops by the same \(d-g\), from \(b_{\rm sum}+m\) to \(a+m\). Points, bases and evaluation matrices use the explicit construction already proved in cor:hermitian-repair-family, at the new \(O(n)\) pole orders. For two words the complete cost remains \(O(n^3)\) field operations and \(O(n^2)\) memory.

Nonvacuity. The same-quotient protected ledger and full saving and recovery ledger are both realized by (5) for every \(s=2^r\ge8\). At \(s=8\), direct symbolic substitution gives \(n=511,g=28,m=127,d=31,a=149\), ranks \(62,62,93\), domain dimension \(122\), summed-rank threshold \(b_{\rm sum}=152\), and recovery margin \(511-(149+127+62)=173\). At \(s=16\): \(n=4095,g=120,d=255,a=1005,b_{\rm sum}=1140\). One may take both messages equal to one and each error equal to one on its prescribed support; the supports remain distinct. These are exact substitutions, not a numerical run. For lem:exact-common-kernel-selection, the same instance gives \(S=L(A)\) of dimension \(122\), \(\operatorname{rank}\rho=93\), \(\operatorname{rank}(\rho,q)=94\).

Degenerate cases. If every error is zero, the joint rank is zero and a normalized locator exists under (1). With one word there is no rank-sum gain. Disjoint supports give equality between union and summed ranks. Identical supports may have different nonzero values but the same kernel; they are not the claimed nonduplicate family. A zero error value removes that coordinate from its exact support, so it is not counted twice by definition. Repeated evaluation points are excluded. A protected point in the defect support is excluded. In lem:exact-common-kernel-selection, \(J=S\) makes (0) impossible, \(J=0\) reduces it to \(\ker\rho\ne0\), and no maps at all give \(\rho=0\) and the condition \(S\ne J\).

New mathematics. A complete simultaneous marked-recovery consequence with exact joint-action ranks; a pole-budget gain of \(d\) (nonzero) and \(d-g\) (protected) over the summed-rank certificate on distinct incomparable kernels, exact for every support choice when \(s\ge16\); and an exact selection criterion for the composition theorem. The curve instance satisfies that criterion, an instance of the abstract lemma where its summed form cannot certify a protected value; it is not itself an instance of the composition theorem. The support factorization and the decoder are established elementary tools; no historical novelty or improved decoding radius is claimed. Simultaneous decoding of several received words with one error locator for the union of their supports is the setting of interleaved codes; no source on interleaved decoding was read in this cycle, and nothing here relies on one.

Selection gain. lem:exact-common-kernel-selection widens the selection hypothesis of the composition from a summed rank bound to an exact rank criterion, with unchanged later costs. In the explicit family a protected common multiplier is certified at pole budget \(3d+2g\), where the summed criterion first gives even a nonzero multiplier at \(4d+g\). This changes the sufficient common-multiplier cost, not only its representation. Separate per-word locators are cheaper still; the gain concerns one common multiplier.

Goal progress. Unchanged. In the evaluation model, thm:overlapping-curve-recovery gives same-quotient distinct kernels and an end-to-end pole saving, but the saving is union-of-supports counting: there the joint rank is the union size by definition. The necessary implication of joint-error-savings, a structural bound on the joint action of actual errors from independent hypotheses, is not touched; lem:exact-common-kernel-selection widens a hypothesis of the composition, a stronger convenience rather than such a bound. Bearing. The protected quotient retains the same coordinate throughout, and the saving ledger pays observation and both recovery steps at unbounded parameters. Not covered. Arbitrary PC errors or Frege proofs, Braun's and Pang's adapters, optimal decoding algorithms, effective homology/localization bounds or circuit hardness.
