Product pigeonhole kernels as restriction ranks

16 October 2026 · Working proof (restriction ranks for K+e≤D<n or K+e<D=n) · Hole-occupancy kernels. Produced by claude-code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning medium).

Chosen. This entry continues fi-module-stability, which the last entry developed, with its sub-idea, instead of the head. It bears on joint-error-savings: the line's pigeonhole evidence for joint savings consists of computed kernels, and a closed form would say whether that system can show a saving of a kind the open statement admits.

Owed attempt. The FI-windows entry named closed forms for the common kernels of the product pigeonhole systems in the inert regime: “the next attempt is the sub-idea, closed forms for the common kernels there”. Made here, for every set of errors, except the top-degree case \(K+e=D=n\), which (d) describes but does not count.

Best outcome. At the goal's own parameters, a closed form that either exhibits a joint saving of an admitted kind in the product pigeonhole system or proves there is none in a stated range.

General statement. cor:hole-occupancy-kernels: in the product pigeonhole system over any field, for errors whose products with the window stay below the pigeon axioms' degree (\(K+e\le D<n\), or \(K+e\le n-1\) at \(D=n\)), every common kernel and stacked error rank is the restriction rank of low-degree functions on the hole-respecting assignments to the union of the errors' supports, with an explicit tensor formula when those supports are fixed by the occupancy of a set of holes; at \(K+e=D=n\) membership is membership of the restriction in the span of the indicators of unplaced pigeons.

Hole-occupancy kernels

Setting. Over a field, the product pigeonhole system with \(m\) pigeons and \(n\ge1\) holes in the multilinear ring: hole axioms \(x_{ij}x_{kj}\), \(i\ne k\), and pigeon axioms \(P_i=\prod_j(1-x_{ij})\) of degree \(n\). Let \(C\) be its degree-\(D\) closure with \(D\le n\), and \(Y\subseteq\{0,1\}^{m\times n}\) the hole-respecting assignments, at most one pigeon per hole; \(Y\) is the product over holes of the \(m+1\) states “empty” and “pigeon \(i\)”. Put \(U=V_K/(C\cap V_K)\). Let \(E_1,\ldots,E_s\) be polynomials of degree at most \(e\), \(S_j=\{y\in Y:E_j(y)\ne0\}\) and \(S=\bigcup_jS_j\). Call the range inert when \(K+e\le D<n\) or \(K+e\le n-1\) with \(D=n\).

Statement. (a) In the inert range, restriction to \(Y\) identifies \(U\) with \(V_K|_Y\), the functions on \(Y\) given by polynomials of degree at most \(K\), and the common kernel \(\{[u]\in U:E_ju\in C\ \forall j\}\) with the zero set of the restriction map \(V_K|_Y\to V_K|_S\); the stacked map \(u\mapsto([E_ju])_j\) has rank \(\dim V_K|_S\), and each \(u\mapsto[E_ju]\) rank \(\dim V_K|_{S_j}\). (b) If \(S=A\times Y'\), where \(A\) is a set of states of a set \(T\) of \(t\) holes and \(Y'\) all states of the other \(n-t\) holes, then \(\dim V_K|_S=\sum_{s\le K}\binom{n-t}{s}m^s\,d_A(K-s)\), where \(d_A(a)=\dim V_a|_A\) in the variables of the holes of \(T\); when \(A\) is all states, \(d_A(a)=\sum_{r\le a}\binom trm^r\). (c) In the inert range, for one monomial \(w\) on \(e\) distinct holes the kernel has dimension \(\sum_{k\le K}\bigl[\binom nk-\binom{n-e}k\bigr]m^k\); for the common kernel of \(x_{i0}\), \(i\in\Sigma\), with \(|\Sigma|=\sigma\ge1\) and \(K=1\), it is \(m+1-\sigma\). (d) At \(D=n\), for every polynomial \(c\) of degree at most \(n\), \(c\in C\) exactly when \(c|_Y\) lies in \(P_Y=\operatorname{span}\{1_{Z_i}\}\), \(Z_i\) the points of \(Y\) where pigeon \(i\) is unplaced. So for \(K+e\le n\) and \(K\le n-1\), where \(C\cap V_K=H\cap V_K\) and so \(U\cong V_K|_Y\), the common kernel is \(\{[u]:E_ju|_Y\in P_Y\ \forall j\}\); it contains the classes vanishing on \(S\), and modulo them it injects into \(\bigoplus_jP_Y^{S_j}\), where \(P_Y^{S_j}\) is the subspace of \(P_Y\) of functions vanishing off \(S_j\); hence the stacked rank lies between \(\dim V_K|_S-\sum_j\dim P_Y^{S_j}\) and \(\dim V_K|_S\).

Proof. (a) By lem:top-degree-axiom-inertness (b), the closure \(H\) of the hole axioms is the degree-\(D\) part of the vanishing ideal of \(Y\), and \(C\cap V_{D-1}=H\cap V_{D-1}\); for \(D<n\) no pigeon axiom has degree at most \(D\), so \(C=H\). In the inert range every product \(E_ju\) has degree at most \(K+e\), where \(C\) and \(H\) agree, and \(K\le K+e\) lies there too; so \(E_ju\in C\) exactly when \(E_ju\) vanishes on \(Y\), that is when \(u\) vanishes on \(S_j\), and \(C\cap V_K\) is the set of \(u\in V_K\) vanishing on \(Y\). So \(U\cong V_K|_Y\), and \([u]\) lies in the common kernel exactly when \(u|_S=0\). Restriction \(V_K|_Y\to V_K|_{S_j}\) is onto, so the rank of \(u\mapsto[E_ju]\) is \(\dim V_K|_{S_j}\); likewise for the stacked map with \(S\). This is lem:domain-model-stacked-rank for the point set \(Y\), whose \(B_D\) is \(C\) in this range. (b) The distinct-hole monomials of degree at most \(s\) on the free holes form a basis of the functions on \(Y'\) given by degree-\(\le s\) polynomials, by the triangularity argument of lem:top-degree-axiom-inertness (b) applied to \(Y'\), and \(\binom{n-t}{s}m^s\) of them have degree exactly \(s\); let \(B_s\) be their span. A monomial of degree at most \(K\) is the product of a monomial of degree \(a\) in the variables of \(T\) and one of degree \(s\) in the others, \(a+s\le K\), and on \(A\times Y'\) restricts to the tensor product of the restrictions; so \(V_K|_S=\sum_sV_{K-s}|_A\otimes B_s\), a direct sum since \(F^A\otimes\bigoplus_sB_s=\bigoplus_sF^A\otimes B_s\). For \(A\) all states the same basis count on \(T\) gives \(d_A\). (c) By (b) with \(t=n\), \(\dim V_K|_Y=\sum_{k\le K}\binom nkm^k\). For \(w\) on holes \(T\), \(|T|=e\), \(S\) fixes the states of \(T\), so \(A\) is one point, \(d_A\equiv1\), and \(\dim V_K|_S=\sum_{s\le K}\binom{n-e}sm^s\); the kernel is the difference. For the \(x_{i0}\), \(S\) is “hole \(0\) holds a pigeon of \(\Sigma\)”, \(t=1\), and \(A\) has \(\sigma\) states on which \(\sum_{i\in\Sigma}x_{i0}=1\) and the other \(x_{k0}\) vanish, so \(d_A(0)=1\), \(d_A(1)=\sigma\), and the kernel has dimension \((1+nm)-(\sigma+(n-1)m)=m+1-\sigma\). (d) By lem:top-degree-axiom-inertness (b) at \(D=n\), \(C=H+\operatorname{span}\{P_i\}\), with \(H\) the polynomials of degree at most \(n\) vanishing on \(Y\). If \(c\in C\), then \(c-\sum_i\lambda_iP_i\) vanishes on \(Y\) for some \(\lambda\), and \(P_i|_Y=1_{Z_i}\); conversely, if \(c|_Y=\sum_i\lambda_i1_{Z_i}\), then \(c-\sum_i\lambda_iP_i\) has degree at most \(n\) and vanishes on \(Y\), so lies in \(H\subseteq C\). For \(K+e\le n\) the products \(E_ju\) have degree at most \(n\), which gives the kernel. A class vanishing on \(S\) has every \(E_ju|_Y=0\in P_Y\). The map sending \(u\) in the kernel to \((E_ju|_Y)_j\) lands in \(\bigoplus_jP_Y^{S_j}\), as \(E_ju\) vanishes off \(S_j\); if all its components are zero, \(u\) vanishes on every \(S_j\); so the kernel modulo the classes vanishing on \(S\) injects there, and the bounds follow, since the stacked rank is \(\dim V_K|_Y\) minus the kernel's dimension.

Against the record. check:clique-factor-kernels at \(5\) pigeons, \(4\) holes, \(D=3<n\), \(K=1\): \(\operatorname{Ann}(x_{00})\) has dimension \(5\), \(\operatorname{Ann}(x_{00})\cap\operatorname{Ann}(x_{10})\) dimension \(4\), and the triple intersection dimension \(3\), which are \(m+1-\sigma\) for \(\sigma=1,2,3\). The check's family kernels, of the errors \(x_{i0}y\) with \(y\) outside hole \(0\), have union of supports \(S'\), the points with a pigeon of \(\Sigma\) in hole \(0\) and some other hole occupied; a function of degree at most \(1\) vanishing on \(S'\) vanishes on all of \(S\): with \(c+\sum a_{kl}x_{kl}\) restricted to \(S\), the points with exactly one further cell occupied give \(c+a=0\) for that cell's coefficient \(a\), and two further cells in different holes, available as \(n-1\ge2\), give \(c=0\) and then every \(a=0\); so these kernels also equal \(m+1-\sigma\), and the summed codimension \(165\) is (a) applied family by family: \(\dim V_1|_{S_j}=1+(n-2)m=11\) for \(S_j=\{x_{00}=y=1\}\) by (b) with \(t=2\), so \(165=15\times11\). At \(4\) pigeons and \(3\) holes only \(\operatorname{Ann}(x_{00})\), of dimension \(4=m\), lies in the inert range; the stacked kernels of the degree-\(2\) errors there, and those of check:truncated-kernel-beyond-support with ex:support-saving-not-inherited, have \(K+e=3=D=n\) and fall under (d), where the pigeon axioms act. The FI-windows count \(\dim Q_m=4m+1\) at \(n=4\), \(K=1\) is (b) with \(t=n\).

Degenerate cases. No errors, or every \(E_j\) vanishing on \(Y\): \(S\) is empty and the kernel is all of \(U\). \(E_j\) a nonzero constant: \(S=Y\) and the kernel is \(0\). \(K=0\): the kernel is \(U\cong F\) if \(S\) is empty and \(0\) otherwise. A monomial \(w\) with two variables in one hole: it vanishes on \(Y\), \(S\) is empty, and the kernel is \(U\). \(D=n\) with \(K+e=n\): outside the inert range; (d) gives the description and bounds, not a count.

Nonvacuity. In Pang's matched ledger with \(p=2\), checking only the hypotheses one by one: \(m=5\), \(n=4\ge1\), \(D=3<n\), \(K=1\), \(E_1=x_{00}\) with \(e=1\), \(K+e=2\le D\), inert; \(Y\) has \(6^4\) points and \(S=\{y:\text{hole }0\text{ holds pigeon }0\}=A\times Y'\) with \(t=1\), \(\sigma=1\), kernel dimension \(5\).

New mathematics. cor:hole-occupancy-kernels: in the inert range the product pigeonhole closure is the domain model on the hole-respecting assignments, so its common kernels and stacked ranks are restriction ranks to unions of supports, with the tensor formula of (b) and the closed forms of (c), which reproduce the kernels of check:clique-factor-kernels at \(5\) pigeons and the annihilator at \(4\); at the top degree \(K+e=D=n\), part (d) reduces membership to the span of the unplaced-pigeon indicators and bounds the stacked rank by restriction ranks.

Goal review: transversal killer basis and the switch to annihilator degree

16 October 2026 · Working proof (transversal killer basis); goal review · Goal review: transversal killers. Produced by claude-code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning medium).

Question. Six research entries since the goal review have tested joint-error-savings on the pigeonhole systems and the localization route on Pang's errors. That review set a rule: if its decisive test, on the functional pigeonhole system, found only unions of supports, domination by one annihilator and products of single killers, cycles move to effective-annihilator-degree. Its test, in the constructed-kernels entry, found exactly those. This review applies the rule, states what the line is stuck on, and proves the lemma that the next line starts from.

General statement. lem:transversal-killer-basis: on the Boolean cube over any field, the functions of degree at most \(d\) vanishing on an up-set \(U\) are spanned, with no relation, by the products \(\prod_{v\in T}(1-x_v)\) over the transversals \(T\) of the minimal sets of \(U\) with \(|T|\le d\); so the first degree of a common killer of errors with monomial supports that keeps \(1\) alive is a transversal number, and for a protected function \(p\) it is the least size of a transversal avoiding a point of its support.

Obstacle

Every joint saving the line has found is of an excluded kind, and the record now says why on its test systems. Where the closure is the degree part of a vanishing ideal of a point set, stacked ranks are restriction ranks to unions of supports (lem:domain-model-stacked-rank); the product pigeonhole system is such a domain model in its whole inert range (cor:hole-occupancy-kernels), and the functional system at six and seven pigeons still showed only the frame and its relations (check:functional-factor-kernels). The first exclusion of the open statement, union-of-supports counting, already removes every saving in every domain model; for monomial supports on the cube the lemma below adds that the killers themselves are combinations of products of single literal killers, though the degree qualifier of the third exclusion, a degree growing with the number of distinct factors, fails for a star family, whose transversal number stays \(1\). A saving of the admitted kind must therefore come from the part of a truncated closure that is not a vanishing ideal: at the top degree of the product system that part is the span of the unplaced-pigeon indicators (cor:hole-occupancy-kernels (d)), of dimension at most \(m\). The line is stuck on finding a system and error family where that non-domain part acts on the errors with rank growing with the family.

Transversal killer basis

Statement. Over a field \(F\), let \(Q=\{0,1\}^N\), identify points with subsets of \([N]\), and let \(U\subseteq Q\) be an up-set with minimal sets \(\mathcal M\). Call \(T\subseteq[N]\) a transversal when it meets every member of \(\mathcal M\). For \(d\ge0\), let \(W_d\) be the functions on \(Q\) given by polynomials of degree at most \(d\) that vanish on \(U\). Then (a) the products \(\pi_T=\prod_{v\in T}(1-x_v)\), over the transversals \(T\) with \(|T|\le d\), form a basis of \(W_d\); so \(\dim W_d\) is the number of such transversals, and the least \(d\) with \(W_d\ne0\) is the transversal number \(\tau(\mathcal M)\). (b) For a function \(p\) on \(Q\), the least degree of an \(f\in W_d\) with \(fp\ne0\) is \(\min\{|T|:T\text{ a transversal},\ T\subseteq[N]\setminus x,\ x\in\operatorname{supp}p\}\), and it is infinite when \(\operatorname{supp}p\subseteq U\). (c) In particular, for errors \(E_j=c_jx_{A_j}\) with \(c_j\ne0\), as functions on \(Q\), among killers \(f\) with \(\deg f+\max|A_j|\le D\), a common killer modulo the cube's degree-\(D\) vanishing ideal that keeps \(1\) alive exists exactly when \(\tau(\{A_j\})+\max|A_j|\le D\), and its least degree is then \(\tau(\{A_j\})\), attained by \(\pi_T\) for a least transversal \(T\); a nonzero constant error, \(A_j=\emptyset\), gives \(\tau=\infty\) and no killer.

Proof. Put \(y_v=1-x_v\); this affine change of variables preserves degree and sends the point \(x\) to its complement, so \(U\) becomes the down-set \(D'=\{[N]\setminus x:x\in U\}\). For a down-set, the monomials \(y_S\), \(S\in D'\), are a basis of the functions on \(D'\): their evaluation matrix on \(D'\) is triangular for inclusion with ones on the diagonal, as \(y_S\) at the point \(R\) is \(1\) exactly when \(S\subseteq R\). So the functions on \(D'\) given by degree-\(\le d\) polynomials have dimension \(\#\{S\in D':|S|\le d\}\), and restriction from \(Q\), where all \(y_S\) with \(|S|\le d\) are independent, has kernel of dimension \(\#\{S\notin D':|S|\le d\}\). For \(S\notin D'\), \(y_S\) vanishes on \(D'\): a point \(R\in D'\) with \(S\subseteq R\) would put \(S\) in \(D'\). So these \(y_S\) are a basis of the kernel. Finally \(S\notin D'\) means that \([N]\setminus S\notin U\), that is, \([N]\setminus S\) contains no member of \(\mathcal M\), that is, \(S\) is a transversal; and \(y_S=\pi_S\). This gives (a). (b) A combination \(f=\sum_T\lambda_T\pi_T\) has \(f(x)=\sum_{T\subseteq[N]\setminus x}\lambda_T\), since \(\pi_T(x)=1\) exactly when \(T\) avoids \(x\); so some \(f\in W_d\) is nonzero at \(x\) exactly when some transversal of size at most \(d\) avoids \(x\), and for \(x\in U\) none does, \(x\) containing a member of \(\mathcal M\). (c) The support of \(c_jx_{A_j}\) is the up-set generated by \(A_j\); \(fE_j\) has degree at most \(\deg f+|A_j|\le D\), so it lies in the degree-\(D\) vanishing ideal exactly when \(f\) vanishes on that up-set; the union \(U\) has minimal sets among the \(A_j\), with the same transversals; protecting \(1\) means \(f\ne0\) somewhere, and (b) with \(p=1\) gives \(\tau\).

Relations. It generalizes prop:independent-affine-common-kernel (main notebook, over \(\mathbb F_2\)), whose jointly independent affine input groups become, in affine coordinates, an up-set with disjoint minimal sets, its monomials meeting every group being the transversal products and its first degree \(M\) the transversal number; the lemma allows the minimal sets to overlap, as families sharing inputs do. The record of that proposition was read by the author in the main notebook. Historical lem:columnconditioning (a whole column costs one degree) is the same construction on the column-exclusive domain. In lem:greedy-transversal-certificate, with consistent pins, each block's flat becomes after one global complement the up-set generated by its pinned set, so its certificate is a transversal killer in a cube domain model, its savings are of the first excluded kind, and its numbers bound the transversal number from above; Braun's space \(L_k\) asks for literals in distinct rows, so there the lemma gives only \(\tau\le\) least degree \(\le\) least row-distinct transversal, and inconsistent pins lie outside it. It is the reviewer's disjoint-block suggestion of the family-killer entry in exact form: for families on disjoint blocks \(\tau\) is the sum of the blocks' transversal numbers. For Pang's families at \(t=1\) over \(\mathbb F_2\) with inputs exactly \(x_a,x_b\) and the choice \(q=x_a+x_b\), the errors \(Pg_i=(1+x_a+x_b)g_i\) agree with \(x_ax_b\) on the cube (for \(q=x_a\) the errors are \(0\) and \((1-x_a)x_b\), whose support is not an up-set, and a constant input makes \(P\) itself an error), so the least surviving killer degree in the cube's domain model is the vertex-cover number of the graph of input pairs, \(N-\alpha\) by Gallai's identity; so whenever that number exceeds \(K\), Pang's multiplier, of degree \(K\), relies on the system's own axioms, not on the cube.

Degenerate cases. \(U\) empty: \(\mathcal M\) is empty, \(\emptyset\) is a transversal, \(\tau=0\), and \(W_d\) is everything. \(U=Q\): \(\emptyset\in\mathcal M\) and no set meets it, so \(W_d=0\) and no killer survives. One error \(x_A\): \(\tau=1\), any literal \(1-x_v\), \(v\in A\). \(p\) supported in \(U\): no surviving killer, as (b) says.

Nonvacuity. Extra requirements. The route asks for a structural bound, not an existence count. The lemma gives one exactly where the closure is the cube's vanishing ideal: there the least killer of monomial errors is a transversal product, and when the transversal number exceeds \(K\), Pang's multiplier survives only because the system's axioms enter. So the demand that can be weakened is faithfulness to the cube: the target needs only the system's own domain, such as the hole-respecting assignments, where a hole-empty indicator \(1-\sum_ix_{ij}\) of degree \(1\) kills every error touching hole \(j\).

Independent alternative. Before seeing the route, the medium reviewer received the goal, the open statements and the registered statements of the available results, with no open conjecture registered on the route (review record). It proposed two architectures and found no third. The first is Gorenstein duality: in a graded Artinian Gorenstein algebra of socle degree \(\sigma\), the annihilator of an ideal \(I\) has dimension \(\dim(R/I)_{\sigma-d}\) in degree \(d\), so the first annihilator degree is \(\sigma\) minus the top degree of \(R/I\), and an annihilator preserving \(p\) exists exactly when \(p\notin I\); it breaks because the record's closures are truncated pseudoideals, not graded ideals, and the colon does not commute with the associated graded. This is the marked Frobenius separation of prop:frobenius-marked-separation, with its complementary-degree cost, whose development is the queued item common-multiplier-duality; on the cube's associated graded \(F[x]/(x_i^2)\), of socle degree \(N\), the common annihilator of the monomials \(x_{A_j}\) is spanned by the \(x_T\) over transversals \(T\), the graded shadow of the lemma below. The second is a pairwise-product lower bound on the saving, \(\operatorname{rank}T_1+\operatorname{rank}T_2-\operatorname{rank}(T_1,T_2)\ge\operatorname{rank}T_{E_1E_2}\) when \(\deg E_1+\deg E_2+K\le D\), the inverse-system Bonferroni bound of the goal review; it doubles Pang's reserve and is support counting in domain models. Compared with the route, both are recorded bridges; the first is the natural next item if the decisive test finds no non-domain killer, since a filtered duality on a proper closure is the one mechanism that would describe annihilators beyond domain models.

General statement. lem:cylinder-killer-degree: on any finite product domain with one-hot coordinates, a nonzero function vanishing on a union of cylinders has degree at least the transversal number of their coordinate sets, attained when each coordinate of a least transversal has a state no cylinder assigns there; lem:top-degree-killer-transfer: at the top degree of the product pigeonhole system, a multiplier \(f\) has \(fE\) in the closure exactly when \(f\) vanishes on the error's support, once the unplaced-pigeon indicators stay independent off the support, as they do when it misses the empty assignment and a single placement of each pigeon, and for every monomial error of positive degree on distinct holes.

Cylinder killer degree

Statement. Over a field \(F\), let \(X=\prod_{j\in[n]}A_j\) with finite nonempty \(A_j\) and a base state \(0_j\in A_j\); for \(a\in A_j\setminus\{0_j\}\) let \(x_{j,a}(s)=[s_j=a]\), and call the degree of a function on \(X\) the least degree of a polynomial in these variables that represents it. A cylinder is a partial assignment \(\alpha\) on a set \(\operatorname{dom}\alpha\) of coordinates; let \(\mathcal C\) be a family of cylinders and \(U\) the union of the points extending them. (a) Every nonzero function on \(X\) vanishing on \(U\) has degree at least \(\tau=\tau(\{\operatorname{dom}\alpha:\alpha\in\mathcal C\})\), the least size of a set of coordinates meeting every \(\operatorname{dom}\alpha\). (b) If \(T\) is such a set of size \(\tau\) and every \(j\in T\) has a state \(b_j\) that no cylinder assigns at \(j\), then \(\prod_{j\in T}[s_j=b_j]\), of degree at most \(\tau\), is nonzero and vanishes on \(U\). (c) For the product pigeonhole system, with \(Y\) the hole-respecting assignments as the product over holes of “empty” and the pigeons, base state “empty”, and monomial errors on distinct holes, whose supports are cylinders assigning pigeons, the least degree of a nonzero function on \(Y\) vanishing on the union of supports is the transversal number \(\tau\) of the errors' hole sets; when \(\tau\le K\) and \(K+e\) lies in the inert range of cor:hole-occupancy-kernels, or \(D=n\) with \(K+e\le n\) and \(K\le n-1\) by the transfer below, it is the least degree of a surviving common killer of \(1\), and when \(\tau>K\) there is none of degree at most \(K\).

Proof. On \(X\), \(x_{j,a}x_{j,b}=[a=b]\,x_{j,a}\), so every polynomial reduces, without raising its degree, to a combination of the monomials \(x_S=\prod_{j\in\operatorname{dom}S}x_{j,S(j)}\) over partial assignments \(S\) with non-base values; these are a basis of the functions on \(X\), since on each factor \(1\) and the \(x_{j,a}\) are a basis of \(F^{A_j}\) and the monomials are their tensor products. So the degree of a function is the largest \(|\operatorname{dom}S|\) with a nonzero coefficient. (a) Let \(f\ne0\) vanish on \(U\), and let \(T\) be the domain of a monomial \(x_S\) with nonzero coefficient and \(|T|\) largest. Fix any states \(z\) of the coordinates outside \(T\); in the restriction \(g_z\) of \(f\) to the fibre \(\{s:s|_{[n]\setminus T}=z\}\), a function on \(\prod_{j\in T}A_j\), the part of degree \(|T|\) comes only from monomials with domain exactly \(T\), by maximality, and is unchanged, so \(g_z\ne0\). If some cylinder had \(\operatorname{dom}\alpha\cap T=\emptyset\), choose \(z\) extending \(\alpha\): the whole fibre over \(z\) lies in \(U\), so \(g_z=0\), a contradiction. Hence \(T\) meets every \(\operatorname{dom}\alpha\), and \(\deg f=|T|\ge\tau\). (b) \([s_j=b]\) is \(x_{j,b}\) for \(b\ne0_j\) and \(1-\sum_ax_{j,a}\) for \(b=0_j\), of degree at most \(1\); the product is the indicator of \(\{s:s_j=b_j\ \forall j\in T\}\), nonempty, and every cylinder has a coordinate \(j\in T\) at which it assigns a state other than \(b_j\), so the product vanishes on it. (c) The support of \(\prod x_{i_kj_k}\) with distinct holes is the cylinder assigning pigeon \(i_k\) to hole \(j_k\); “empty” is assigned by none, so (b) applies with \(b_j\) empty, and (a) gives the lower bound. In the inert range, by cor:hole-occupancy-kernels (a), a common killer of the errors that keeps \(1\) is a function of degree at most \(K\) on \(Y\) vanishing on the union of supports and nonzero; at \(D=n\) the transfer below gives the same conditions, and \(f\notin C\) means \(f|_Y\ne0\) by the clause \(C\cap V_{n-1}=H\cap V_{n-1}\) of lem:top-degree-axiom-inertness (b), as \(K\le n-1\).

Relations. It is the reviewer's proof in the goal review (Attempt checked), stated on any product domain. On the cube with base state \(1\) for each coordinate it is the first-degree part of lem:transversal-killer-basis, without its basis count; lem:greedy-transversal-certificate, in Braun's row-linear setting with a greedy count, and historical lem:columnconditioning build products of the kind in (b). prop:polynomial-majority-rank-floor uses the same tensor support-degree argument for majority inputs on disjoint blocks.

Top-degree killer transfer

Statement. For the product pigeonhole system with \(m\) pigeons and \(n\ge1\) holes over a field, at \(D=n\), let \(E\) have degree \(e\), \(K+e\le n\), \(S_E\) its support on \(Y\) and \(1_{Z_i}\) the indicator of “pigeon \(i\) unplaced”. (a) If the restrictions of the \(1_{Z_i}\) to \(Y\setminus S_E\) are linearly independent, then for \(f\in V_K\), \(fE\in C\) exactly when \(f\) vanishes on \(S_E\). (b) The independence holds when \(Y\setminus S_E\) contains the empty assignment and, for each pigeon \(k\), an assignment placing only \(k\); it also holds for every monomial error of degree \(e\ge1\) on distinct holes, for all \(m\) and \(n\), by that condition when \(n\ge2\) and by a separate argument when \(n=1\). (c) For \(K+e\le n-1\) the conclusion of (a) holds with no hypothesis, by cor:hole-occupancy-kernels (a); the content of the lemma is the case \(K+e=n\).

Proof. (a) By cor:hole-occupancy-kernels (d), \(fE\in C\) exactly when \((fE)|_Y=\sum_i\lambda_i1_{Z_i}\) for some \(\lambda\), as \(\deg(fE)\le n\). The left side vanishes on \(Y\setminus S_E\), so \(\sum_i\lambda_i1_{Z_i}\) does, and independence gives \(\lambda=0\); then \(fE\) vanishes on \(Y\), and as \(E\ne0\) on \(S_E\), \(f\) vanishes there. Conversely, if \(f\) vanishes on \(S_E\), then \((fE)|_Y=0\). (b) At the empty assignment every pigeon is unplaced, so a combination vanishing there has \(\sum_i\lambda_i=0\); at an assignment placing only \(k\) it takes the value \(\sum_{i\ne k}\lambda_i=-\lambda_k\), so \(\lambda_k=0\). For a monomial error of degree \(e\ge1\) on distinct holes, the empty assignment lies off \(S_E\), which needs a placed pigeon; the assignment placing only \(k\) in hole \(h\) lies in \(S_E\) only if \(E=x_{kh}\), and then placing \(k\) in another hole works when \(n\ge2\), while for \(n=1\) the other pigeons' points give \(\lambda_i=0\) for \(i\ne k\) and \(\sum\lambda_i=0\) gives \(\lambda_k=0\). (c) For \(K+e\le n-1\), \(fE\) has degree below \(n\), where \(C\) agrees with the vanishing ideal of \(Y\).

Against the record. check:truncated-kernel-beyond-support lies at the top degree: \(4\) pigeons, \(3\) holes, \(D=3=n\), \(K=1\), errors \(Pg_i\) of degree \(2\) with \(P=1+g_1+g_2\), which on \(Y\) over \(\mathbb F_2\) agree with \(g_1g_2\). For the four families with \(g_1g_2\) on distinct holes, a monomial of degree \(2\), the transfer (b) applies, so each kernel is the zero set of restriction to the support: for \(S_E=\{x_{00}=x_{01}=1\}\) the degree-\(\le1\) functions on \(S_E\) are spanned by \(1\) and the four variables of hole \(2\), so the rank is \(5\), the recorded codimension, and the four ranks sum to the recorded \(20\); on the union of the supports the nine functions \(1\), \(x_{i1}\), \(x_{i2}\) stay independent, the hole-\(0\) variables being constant there, giving the recorded stacked rank \(9\). The two families in one hole have \(g_1g_2\) vanishing on \(Y\), codimension \(0\), as recorded. So for these errors the proper closure's kernels equal those of the domain model on \(Y\), and ex:support-saving-not-inherited compares the cube's support ranks with that domain model, although the closure at this degree is \(H\) plus the span of the pigeon axioms.

Architecture test. Decided. The goal review's test had the outcome its prediction named: no degree-\(2\) surviving common killer exists for the six errors \(x_{jj}x_{ll}\), \(0\le j<l\le3\), of the product pigeonhole system with \(5\) pigeons and \(4\) holes at \(D=4\), \(K=2\). Each is a monomial of degree \(2\) on distinct holes with \(K+e=4=n\), so by the transfer each condition \(fE\in C\) is vanishing on \(S_E\); survival is \(f|_Y\ne0\) by the clause \(C\cap V_3=H\cap V_3\), as \(K=2\le3\); and by the cylinder killer degree a nonzero such \(f\) on \(Y\) has degree at least \(\tau(K_4)=3>K\). The parameters run are those the review named, decided by proof rather than computation. The review's Prediction named this outcome as the one that sends the line to the duality item.

Degenerate cases. No cylinders: \(\tau=0\) and the constant \(1\) is a nonzero function vanishing on \(U=\emptyset\). A cylinder with empty domain: \(U=X\), no set meets \(\emptyset\), only \(0\) vanishes on \(U\), and \(\tau\) is infinite. A coordinate of a least transversal where every state is assigned by some cylinder: (b) does not apply there, and (a) still bounds the degree from below. Associated graded domain models are Gorenstein only for cubes

16 October 2026 · Working proof (standard computation) · Graded pairings of domain models. Produced by claude-code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning medium).

Chosen. This entry develops common-multiplier-duality instead of the head: the goal review named it as the line's next item if the top-degree test found no non-domain killer, which the cylinder-killers entry showed; it bears on effective-annihilator-degree.

Next test the diagonal-observation principle on Pang's actual adaptive error-selection recurrence”, and the calibration entry, whose follow-up reads “Continuing the duality item; its native cutoff question remains open”, with the open sub-idea below; none named an attempt this entry owes.

Best outcome. At the goal's own parameters, a fixed pairing on a faithful model under which marked Frobenius separation gives a surviving annihilator of degree below the recorded constructions, the item's own question; on the domain models it must beat lem:cylinder-killer-degree, which (as found in this entry) no construction can, so only a pairing beyond domain models could.

Question. prop:frobenius-marked-separation turns a perfect graded pairing into an annihilator of complementary degree. Do the associated graded algebras of the line's domain models, the cube and the hole-respecting assignments \(Y\), carry such a pairing, and how does graded annihilation bear on annihilators on the domain?

General statement. lem:graded-domain-pairing: for a down-set \(X\) of the cube, the associated graded algebra of the functions on \(X\) is the face ring of \(X\) modulo the squares, whose socle is spanned by the facets, so it is Gorenstein, the graded hypothesis of marked Frobenius separation, exactly when \(X\) has one facet; product domains with one-hot coordinates are such down-sets, Gorenstein exactly when every factor has at most two states; and graded annihilation is a lower bound for annihilation on the domain, not a source of it: the leading form of a killer kills the errors' leading forms.

Graded domain pairing

Statement. Over a field \(F\), (a) for a down-set \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^N\), a simplicial complex on \([N]\), with the functions on \(X\) filtered by degree, the associated graded algebra is \(G_X=F[x]/(x_v^2\ (v\in[N]),\ x_S\ (S\notin X))\), the face ring of \(X\) modulo the squares, with basis the \(x_S\), \(S\in X\); its socle is spanned by the \(x_M\) over the facets \(M\) of \(X\); so \(G_X\) has a perfect graded pairing into its top degree, the hypothesis of prop:frobenius-marked-separation, exactly when \(X\) is the set of subsets of one set \(M\), with \(s=|M|\). (b) A product \(\prod_jA_j\) of finite nonempty domains with base states and one-hot variables is the down-set of \(\{0,1\}^{\sum_j(|A_j|-1)}\) with at most one variable per block, whose facets choose a non-base state in every block with \(|A_j|\ge2\); its socle has dimension \(\prod_j\max(|A_j|-1,1)\), and it is Gorenstein exactly when every \(|A_j|\le2\). For the product pigeonhole system with \(n\ge1\) holes and \(m\ge2\) pigeons, each hole has \(m+1\ge3\) states, so \(Y\) has no such pairing; with \(m=1\), \(Y\) is the cube \(\{0,1\}^n\). (c) If \(f\) and \(E\) are functions on \(X\) with \(fE=0\), their leading forms satisfy \(\operatorname{lead}(f)\operatorname{lead}(E)=0\) in \(G_X\); so the least degree of a common annihilator of the errors' leading forms in \(G_X\) is a lower bound for the least degree of a common killer on \(X\). An annihilator in \(G_X\) need not lift: on the cube \(x_{[N]}\) kills every \(x_A\), \(A\ne\emptyset\), in \(G_X\), while on \(X\) the product \(x_{[N]}x_A=x_{[N]}\) is nonzero. On the cube both least degrees, for monomial errors \(x_{A_j}\), equal the transversal number \(\tau\): in \(G_X\) the common annihilator of the \(x_{A_j}\) is spanned by the \(x_S\) with \(S\) a transversal, and on \(X\) by lem:transversal-killer-basis.

Proof. This is the standard computation of the socle of a face ring modulo squares; we write it out. (a) On \(X\), \(x_v^2=x_v\), and \(x_S\) vanishes on \(X\) for \(S\notin X\), as \(X\) is a down-set; the \(x_S\), \(S\in X\), are a basis of \(F^X\) by triangularity, and degree at most \(k\) is spanned by those with \(|S|\le k\). In \(G_X\) the product of the classes of \(x_S\) and \(x_T\) is the degree-\((|S|+|T|)\) class of \(x_{S\cup T}\): \(x_{S\cup T}\) when \(S\cap T=\emptyset\) and \(S\cup T\in X\), and \(0\) otherwise, since then \(x_{S\cup T}\) has lower degree or vanishes on \(X\); this is the presentation. The socle is graded, since multiplication by each \(x_v\) is homogeneous; \(g=\sum_Sc_Sx_S\) is in it when \(x_vg=0\) for all \(v\); \(x_vx_S\ne0\) exactly when \(v\notin S\) and \(S\cup\{v\}\in X\), and distinct \(S\) give distinct products, so \(g\) is in the socle exactly when \(c_S=0\) for every non-facet \(S\). If \(G_X\) has a perfect pairing \(G_j\times G_{s-j}\to G_s\), then \(G_s\) is one-dimensional, as \(G_0=F\), and a homogeneous socle element of degree \(j<s\) pairs to zero with \(G_{s-j}\subseteq G_{\ge1}\), so it is zero; the socle is \(G_s\), one facet \(M\), and every face lies in \(M\); conversely \(F[x_M]/(x_v^2)\) pairs \(x_S\) with \(x_{M\setminus S}\). (b) The one-hot variables of a block satisfy \(x_{j,a}x_{j,b}=[a=b]x_{j,a}\), so a polynomial reduces to the monomials with at most one variable per block, \(\prod_j|A_j|\) of them, the number of points; they are a basis, and the domain is that down-set; its facets choose one non-base state in each block with \(|A_j|\ge2\), giving the socle dimension, which is \(1\) exactly when every \(|A_j|\le2\). (c) \(fE=0\) on \(X\) has every degree class zero, and its class in degree \(\deg f+\deg E\) is \(\operatorname{lead}(f)\operatorname{lead}(E)\); for common killers apply this to each error. In \(G_X\) for the cube, \(x_Sx_{A_j}=0\) exactly when \(S\cap A_j\ne\emptyset\), and an element kills \(x_{A_j}\) exactly when each of its monomials does, by distinctness of the products.

Relations. The computation of (a) is standard for face rings modulo squares; the entry registers it for its consequences here, not as new. On \(Y\) the question it was meant to answer, whether a pairing gives a killer below \(\tau\), was already settled by lem:cylinder-killer-degree (a): no function on \(Y\) vanishing on the error supports has degree below \(\tau\), whatever pairing produces it. A non-graded pairing changes nothing: \(F^Y\) is Frobenius under \(\tau_w(a)=\sum_yw_ya(y)\) for any nonvanishing weights, and the separators it gives have no degree control, choosing \(w\) being the same as choosing the separator.

Degenerate cases. \(X=\{\emptyset\}\): \(G_X=F\), Gorenstein with \(s=0\). \(X\) empty: \(F^X=0\). A product with all \(|A_j|=1\): one point, \(G_X=F\). The pigeonhole system with \(m=1\): \(Y=\{0,1\}^n\), Gorenstein with \(s=n\). In (c), \(E\) constant and nonzero: \(\operatorname{lead}(E)\) is a unit, so \(\operatorname{lead}(f)=0\), \(f=0\).

Nonvacuity. For (b): the hole-respecting assignments with \(m=5\), \(n=4\), six states per hole, socle dimension \(5^4=625\), not Gorenstein. For (a) and (c): the cube \(\{0,1\}^3\) with errors \(x_1x_2,x_1x_3,x_2x_3\), Gorenstein with \(s=3\); the least annihilator degree is \(\tau=2\) in \(G_X\) and on \(X\).

New mathematics. lem:graded-domain-pairing: the associated graded algebras of the line's domain models are Gorenstein only for cubes, so marked Frobenius separation applies on none of the hole-respecting assignment sets with two or more pigeons; and graded annihilation bears on domain killers as a lower bound, through leading forms, not as a construction.

The cycle tested the graded hypothesis of marked Frobenius separation on \(Y\), the item's question on the line's own model, and found where graded duality can bear: as a lower bound on proper closures.

Initial-pseudoideal bound for surviving killers

16 October 2026 · Working proof; finite check on six pigeons and five holes · Leading-form killer bounds. Produced by claude-code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning medium).

Chosen. This entry continues common-multiplier-duality, which the last entry developed, instead of the head; its named next attempt bears on effective-annihilator-degree, as a lower bound for surviving killers on closures that are not vanishing ideals.

Made: the bound is proved in a sharpened form and computed on the six-pigeon, five-hole functional system at degree \(3\).

Best outcome. At the goal's own parameters, a lower bound for surviving killers on a proper closure, beyond domain models where lem:cylinder-killer-degree already gives the exact degree, and above the trivial bound that no constant survives when the errors lie outside the closure; the bound to beat on the functional system is the least surviving killer degree found by direct computation, as in check:functional-factor-kernels.

General statement. lem:leading-form-killer-bound: in a degree-\(D\) pseudoideal \(C\) of the multilinear ring, the top parts of members form a graded pseudoideal \(T\) of \(F[x]/(x_v^2)\); within the window \(\deg f+\max_je_j\le D\), a surviving common killer can be reduced to one whose leading form lies outside \(T\) and multiplies every error's leading form into \(T\), so the least degree \(\beta'\) of such a graded killer bounds every surviving killer from below; errors spanning a unit modulo \(C\) leave no surviving killer at all, which \(\beta'\) can miss, since the graded algebra drops lower-degree parts.

Leading-form killer bound

Statement. Over a field \(F\), in the multilinear ring with the degree filtration, let \(G=F[x]/(x_v^2)\), \(\operatorname{top}(h)\in G_{\deg h}\) the top-degree part, \(C\) a degree-\(D\) pseudoideal, \(T_k\subseteq G_k\) the top parts of the members of \(C\) of degree exactly \(k\), with \(0\), and \(T=\bigoplus_kT_k\). Let \(E_1,\dots,E_r\) have degrees \(e_j\), \(e=\max_je_j\). (a) If \(fE\in C\) with \(\deg f=a\), \(\deg E=e'\), then \(\operatorname{top}(f)\operatorname{top}(E)\in T_{a+e'}\) (product in \(G\); \(T_k=0\) for \(k>D\)). (b) \(T\) is a graded pseudoideal of \(G\): for \(c\in C\) of degree \(k<D\), \(x_v\operatorname{top}(c)\in T_{k+1}\). (c) Reduction: if \(f\notin C\), \(\deg f=a\le D-e\), \(fE_j\in C\) for all \(j\), and \(\operatorname{top}(f)\in T_a\), there is \(f'\notin C\) of degree below \(a\) with \(f'E_j\in C\) for all \(j\). (d) Let \(\beta'\) be the least \(a\le D-e\) with some \(g\in G_a\setminus T_a\) such that \(g\operatorname{top}(E_j)\in T_{a+e_j}\) for every \(j\), or none. Every surviving common killer of degree at most \(D-e\) has degree at least \(\beta'\), and if \(\beta'\) is none there is none. (e) Unit combinations: if \(1-\sum_ja_jE_j\in C\) for scalars \(a_j\), there is no surviving common killer of degree at most \(D-e\).

Proof. (a) In the multilinear ring \(x_Sx_T=x_{S\cup T}\), so the degree-\((a+e')\) part of \(fE\) comes only from pairs of top monomials with disjoint supports, which is \(\operatorname{top}(f)\operatorname{top}(E)\) in \(G\). If it is nonzero it is the top part of the member \(fE\); otherwise it is \(0\in T\). (b) \(x_vc\in C\) for \(\deg c<D\), and apply (a) with \(E=x_v\). (c) \(T_a\) is the image of the members of degree at most \(a\) in \(G_a\), a subspace, so some \(c\in C\) of degree \(a\) has \(\operatorname{top}(c)=\operatorname{top}(f)\). Since \(\deg c+e_j\le D\), \(cE_j\in C\): multiply \(c\) by the variables of each monomial of \(E_j\) one at a time, every intermediate product having degree at most \(D\), and add. So \(f'=f-c\) kills every \(E_j\), is not in \(C\), and has degree below \(a\). (d) Iterate (c) from a surviving killer of degree at most \(D-e\); it stops at a surviving killer \(f'\) with \(\operatorname{top}(f')\notin T_{\deg f'}\), nonzero, and (a) puts \(g=\operatorname{top}(f')\) in the set defining \(\beta'\). (e) For \(f\) of degree at most \(D-e\) killing every \(E_j\), \(f=f\bigl(1-\sum_ja_jE_j\bigr)+\sum_ja_jfE_j\); the first term is in \(C\) by the closure argument of (c), as \(\deg(1-\sum a_jE_j)\le e\); so \(f\in C\).

Where it can miss. In (e) the relation \(1-\sum a_jE_j\in C\) has a constant term, which the graded algebra drops: \(T_e\) contains \(\sum_{e_j=e}a_j\operatorname{top}(E_j)\) when it is nonzero, a relation of positive degree, and no graded condition forces \(g\in T\). So \(\beta'\) can be finite where (e) excludes every survivor, as for the variables of pigeons \(0\) and \(1\) below. It is not always blind there: \(T\) contains the top parts of the inhomogeneous axioms, \(\sum_jx_{ij}\in T_1\), and for all thirty variables, another unit case, \(\beta'\) certified that nothing survives.

Relations. (d) refines lem:graded-domain-pairing (c): with \(D\ge\deg f+e\) and \(C\) the degree-\(D\) part of the vanishing ideal of a domain, \(T_k\) is the initial ideal in degree \(k\), and a nonzero function has leading form outside it. On domain models lem:cylinder-killer-degree gives the exact degree. (e) is the special case of a unit in the span of the errors; for one pigeon's variables over \(F_2\) it is \(f=fP_i+\sum_jfx_{ij}\).

Degenerate cases. \(1\in C\): \(T_0=G_0\), nothing survives, and \(\beta'\) is none. A constant error \(E=1\): (e) with \(a=1\); \(\beta'\) is none as well, since \(g\cdot1\in T_a\) contradicts \(g\notin T_a\). An error in \(C\): it imposes nothing. \(C\) with no member of degree at most \(D-e\): \(T_a=0\) below that, and \(\beta'\) is the least degree of a nonzero graded killer.

Computation

beta_prime.py (script, committed before each run with its expectations) computes \(T\), \(\beta'\) and the least surviving killer degree \(k^*\) for the functional pigeonhole system over \(F_2\) with \(6\) pigeons and \(5\) holes at \(D=3\), closure dimension \(4056\). Second run: for the single variable \(x_{00}\), the pairs \(\{x_{00},x_{11}\},\{x_{00},x_{10}\},\{x_{00},x_{01}\}\), the product \(x_{00}x_{11}\) and the pair \(\{x_{00}x_{11},x_{22}x_{33}\}\), \(\beta'=k^*=1\), the trivial bound, since each has a linear killer from a monomial axiom; for all thirty variables both are none up to degree \(2\); for the ten variables of pigeons \(0\) and \(1\), \(\beta'=2\) while no surviving killer of degree at most \(2\) exists, which (e) proves. Third run, after the review, adding \(\{x_{00},x_{11},x_{22}\}\) and \(\{x_{00},x_{11},x_{22},x_{33}\}\), whose common linear kernel is \(C\cap V_1\) (check:functional-factor-kernels): \(\beta'=k^*=2\) for both, the bound tight and above the trivial one. The constant-error control gave none for both in every run. The first run, on the first six sets, gave the same values (output).

Nonvacuity. The first six sets were controls that could not fail: by (d) \(\beta'\le k^*\), \(\beta'=0\) would need the error's top part in \(T\), and \(T_1\) is spanned by the \(\sum_jx_{ij}\), so only \(\beta'=k^*=1\) could occur. The informative sets have \(D-e=2\) and \(k^*\in\{2,\text{none}\}\): the run could show \(\beta'=1<k^*\), \(\beta'=k^*=2\), or \(\beta'\) finite with \(k^*\) none; the second occurred for the three- and four-variable sets, the third for pigeons \(0\) and \(1\). The lemma's hypotheses hold there: a field, a proper degree-\(3\) pseudoideal, errors of degree \(1\) within the window. No parameter ledger applies: the witness verifies no budget of the goal.

New mathematics. lem:leading-form-killer-bound: the top parts of a closure's members form a graded pseudoideal, and a surviving killer within the window reduces to one whose leading form avoids it, giving the graded lower bound \(\beta'\); errors spanning a unit modulo the closure have no surviving killer, which \(\beta'\) can miss. check:leading-form-functional-pigeons: on the six-pigeon functional system at degree \(3\), \(\beta'\) equals the least surviving killer degree \(2\) on the two sets without linear survivors, certifies that no killer of all variables survives, and stays at \(2\) for the variables of two pigeons, where none survives.

The cycle could have given a lower bound beyond domain models; it gave one, tight at the computed sets, and located where it can miss.

Generic combinations and principal kernels

16 October 2026 · Working proof; restatement of the two-sided specialization clause with an \(\mathbb F_2\) example · Principal joint kernels. Produced by claude-code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning medium).

Earlier entries. The item's entries are the two-sided Frobenius entry, whose follow-up reads “Continuing the coding-product item still needs a scalar-pencil rank bound derived from source structure”, the product-code comparison, whose follow-up reads “Continuing. The coding-product item and its child retain the unresolved source-specific rank estimate”, and the Harris-certificate entry, whose follow-up reads “Continuing. The item asked for a structural bound on the joint row space of actual error maps”.

Owed attempt. The Harris-certificate entry named “its sub-idea's product-code test on generic weighted errors, under the tuple-to-pencil reserve”, and the two-sided Frobenius entry asked to compare product-code bounds with the generic weighted error. Made: under the reserve the joint row space is the image of multiplication by one generic weighted error over an extension, (a) below, a product \(\langle g\rangle\cdot U\) with a one-dimensional factor. Every product-code bound degenerates there: the Schur-product Kneser theorem the comparison entry read (Mirandola–Zemor, its thm:kneser) gives a lower bound, here at most the exact value \(\dim U\) minus the annihilator's dimension; in evaluation models the dimension is that of \(U\) restricted to the support of \(g\), the excluded union-of-supports count; and outside evaluation models multiplication in \(V_D/J\) is no coordinatewise product. So the test gives no upper bound.

Best outcome. At the goal's own parameters, an upper bound on the joint rank of actual error maps below their summed ranks that is not one of the excluded kinds, beating the summed-rank budget of thm:certified-repair-composition; failing that, a statement of which kinds the endpoint can still admit, since lem:factor-ideal-domination and lem:domain-model-stacked-rank already classify the savings found.

Question. joint-error-savings excludes savings by domination, “the common kernel being the annihilator of one element of the window”. In the window of lem:two-sided-frobenius-compression, is every common kernel of that form, over which field and at which degree?

General statement. cor:generic-principal-kernel: in the reserve window of lem:two-sided-frobenius-compression, and in every domain model with no reserve, a generic combination \(E(\lambda)=\sum_i\lambda_iE_i\) over a large enough extension has as annihilator the scalar extension of the common kernel, so a joint saving is one combination's rank deficit; over the base field no element of the errors' degree need do so, though one of higher degree may.

Generic principal kernel

Statement. In (a) and (b) polynomials and \(V_K\) follow the convention of lem:two-sided-frobenius-compression; in (c) \(V_K\) is all polynomials of degree at most \(K\); in (d), on the Boolean cube, polynomials are multilinear. Let \(J\) be an \(\mathbb F_p\) degree-\(D\) pseudoideal containing old Boolean or \(\mathbb F_p\)-domain consequences, \(w\) of degree at most \(b\) and \(E_1,\dots,E_r\) of degree at most \(e\), all with \(\mathbb F_p\) coefficients, \(U\le V_K\) an \(\mathbb F_p\)-subspace, \(M_i:U\to V_D/J\), \(u\mapsto[wE_iu]\), \(N=\bigcap_i\ker M_i\), and \(\rho\) the rank of \((M_i)_i\). (a) If \(b+K+e+(p-1)\min(K,e)\le D\), then for \(\mathbb F_q\supseteq\mathbb F_p\) with \(q>\rho\) and \(\lambda\in\mathbb F_q^r\) uniform, with probability at least \(1-\rho/q\), \(\{u\in U\otimes\mathbb F_q:wE(\lambda)u\in J\otimes\mathbb F_q\}=N\otimes\mathbb F_q\), and \(u\mapsto[wE(\lambda)u]\) has rank \(\rho\). (b) Under (a), \(\sum_i\operatorname{rank}M_i-\rho=\sum_i\operatorname{rank}M_i-\operatorname{rank}(u\mapsto[wE(\lambda)u])\). (c) Domain models, with no reserve: if \(J\) is the space of polynomials of degree at most \(D\) vanishing on a finite \(X\subseteq\mathbb F_p^n\), \(w=1\), \(K+e\le D\), and the vectors \((E_i(x))_i\), \(x\in S=\bigcup_i\operatorname{supp}E_i\), fall into \(h\) projective classes, then for \(q\ge h\) some \(\lambda\in\mathbb F_q^r\) has \(\operatorname{supp}E(\lambda)=S\), and for it the annihilator of \(E(\lambda)\) in \(U\otimes\mathbb F_q\) is \(N\otimes\mathbb F_q\). (d) Over \(\mathbb F_p\) itself no element of degree at most \(e\) need have annihilator \(N\): for \(p=2\), \(X=\{0,1\}^3\), \(D=4\), \(U=V_2\), \(E_1=x\), \(E_2=y\), \(N\) is spanned by \((1+x)(1+y)\), no \(g\) of degree at most \(1\) over \(\mathbb F_2\) has annihilator \(N\), and \(x+\omega y\) over \(\mathbb F_4\) does; the element \(x+y+xy\) of degree \(2=D-K\) over \(\mathbb F_2\) does too.

Proof. (a) Under the reserve, lem:two-sided-frobenius-compression gives the pencil \(\sum_it_iM_i\) over \(\mathbb F_p(t)\) the kernel \(N\otimes\mathbb F_p(t)\), so its rank is \(\dim U-\dim N=\rho\), and its specialization clause keeps the kernel for uniform \(\lambda\in\mathbb F_q^r\) with probability at least \(1-\rho/q\) (a nonzero \(\rho\times\rho\) minor is homogeneous of degree \(\rho\) in \(t\)). The specialization is \(u\mapsto[wE(\lambda)u]\) on \(U\otimes\mathbb F_q\) into \((V_D/J)\otimes\mathbb F_q\); its kernel always contains \(N\otimes\mathbb F_q\), and rank \(\rho\) forces equality. (b) follows. (c) Membership in \(J\) is vanishing on \(X\), and \(K+e\le D\) keeps every product \(E_iu\), \(u\in U\), within degree \(D\); so \(\ker M_i\) is the set of \(u\in U\) vanishing on \(\operatorname{supp}E_i\), and \(N\) the set vanishing on \(S\). For \(x\in S\), \(H_x=\{\lambda:\sum_i\lambda_iE_i(x)=0\}\) is a hyperplane of \(\mathbb F_q^r\), and it depends only on the projective class of \((E_i(x))_i\); \(h\) hyperplanes through \(0\) cover at most \(h(q^{r-1}-1)+1<q^r\) points when \(h\le q\), so some \(\lambda\) avoids all of them, and then \(\operatorname{supp}E(\lambda)=S\) (off \(S\) every \(E_i\) vanishes). The annihilator of \(E(\lambda)\) in \(U\otimes\mathbb F_q\) is then the set vanishing on \(S\), which is \(N\otimes\mathbb F_q\), since vanishing on \(S\) is a set of \(\mathbb F_p\)-linear conditions. (d) Here \(\dim V_2=7\), restriction from \(V_2\) to functions on the cube is injective, and by (c)'s description \(N\) is the set of \(u\in V_2\) vanishing off the two points \((0,0,z)\): \((1+x)(1+y)(\alpha+\beta z)\), of degree at most \(2\) only when \(\beta=0\). For \(g\) of degree at most \(1\) the annihilator is the set of \(u\in V_2\) vanishing on \(\operatorname{supp}g\). Over \(\mathbb F_2\) such \(g\) is zero, one, or the indicator of an affine half-space, of \(0\), \(8\) or \(4\) points: support \(0\) gives \(V_2\), support \(8\) gives \(0\), and a half-space is an affine square on which every function has degree at most \(2\), so restriction from \(V_2\) onto its four points is surjective and the annihilator has dimension \(3\). None is \(N\). The projective classes of \((x,y)\) on \(S\) are \((1,0),(0,1),(1,1)\), so \(h=3\) and (c) applies over \(\mathbb F_4\): \(x+\omega y\) takes the values \(1,\omega,1+\omega=\omega^2\) there. Finally \(x+y+xy\) is the indicator of \(S\) over \(\mathbb F_2\).

Hypotheses, each with its step. The reserve and the prime field are used only in (a), through lem:two-sided-frobenius-compression, whose proof needs them; \(q>\rho\) is its specialization bound. The \(\mathbb F_p\) coefficients of \(w\) and the \(E_i\) are that lemma's actual errors. In (c), \(K+e\le D\) is the step identifying kernels with vanishing; \(w=1\) only shortens the statement (a weight multiplies every map by the same vanishing condition on \(\operatorname{supp}w\)). (b) needs only (a).

Degenerate cases. \(r=1\): \(E(\lambda)=\lambda_1E_1\), trivially. \(\rho=0\): every \(u\) kills, and any \(\lambda\) works. \(N=0\): a combination whose annihilator is \(0\). Errors in \(J\): \(M_i=0\), and they drop out. \(q\le\rho\): (a) gives nothing, as in (d) at \(q=4<\rho=6\), where (c) still applies.

Nonvacuity. The example of (d) satisfies every hypothesis of (a) and (c): \(p=2\), the degree-\(4\) vanishing ideal of \(\{0,1\}^3\), which contains the Boolean domain consequences, \(w=1\), \(U=V_2\) of dimension \(7\), errors of degree \(1\) with \(\mathbb F_2\) coefficients, \(0+2+1+1\cdot1=4\le D\), individual ranks \(4\) and \(4\), stacked rank \(\rho=6\), a saving of \(2\); (a) applies over \(\mathbb F_8\) and larger, (c) over \(\mathbb F_4\). No parameter ledger applies: the witness verifies no budget of the goal.

Endpoint consequence. joint-error-savings lists excluded kinds of saving, among them “domination, the common kernel being the annihilator of one element of the window”. Two readings go to the next scheduled review. As a property of a family's kernel, over an extension, the clause excludes every family in the reserve window by (a), and every domain-model family by (c), so the endpoint would be unattainable there by its wording; read at the base field it depends on the degree allowed to the element: at the errors' degree \(e\), and at the degree \(\sigma\) with \(K+\sigma+e\le D\) that lem:factor-ideal-domination allows, which in (d) is \(\sigma\le1=e\), it is a genuine restriction, as (d) shows; at degree \(D-K\), which needs only \(K+\deg g\le D\), (d)'s family is excluded by \(x+y+xy\), directly by vanishing. As a mechanism, a saving obtained only by exhibiting one annihilator, the clause leaves families in the reserve window admissible when a bound comes from elsewhere, and (a) is the reformulation it rules out. The entry does not choose between them.

Relations. (a) is a restatement of the specialization clause of lem:two-sided-frobenius-compression in annihilator language; (c) is its domain-model version without the reserve, the support count of lem:domain-model-stacked-rank seen through one element; (d) bounds the degree at which the base-field principality of lem:factor-ideal-domination can hold.

New mathematics. cor:generic-principal-kernel: under the two-sided reserve, and in every domain model without it, a joint kernel is, over a large enough extension, the annihilator of one generic combination, so the joint rank is one combination's rank; over the base field an element of the errors' degree can fail to exist while one of degree \(D-K\) exists.

Goal progress. Unchanged. The necessary implication, an all-parameter joint saving of an admitted kind, is not advanced; the entry reduces any saving in the reserve window to one generic combination's rank, and shows that the endpoint's domination clause is ambiguous in a way that decides whether the reserve window and domain models can meet it at all. Bearing. None at the goal's own parameters: no saving is obtained. The cycle could have given a product-structure upper bound on the joint row space; under the reserve that row space is one product with a one-dimensional factor, where product-code bounds degenerate.

Reviewer's suggestions, unverified

  • Pang's cutoff \(\Delta+K+d\le D\) lacks the reserve's extra \((p-1)\min(K,e)\), so (a) needs that reserve on top of Pang's window. Meta. The stand-in objections share one habit: reporting a conclusion in the form most convenient for the next step (a queued fix, a pointer to a rule, a passed run, an unsearched novelty) rather than in the form its evidence supports. The change is to write each report sentence from its evidence file, the search log, the run output or the commit, before its conclusion; the finisher's Record search and Owed attempt checks in tools/finish-turn.py enforce two of these.

The way of working behind all three is writing a sentence from the shape of the argument rather than from the instance it is about, and treating a correction as wording to insert rather than a new statement to check; it shows also in the leading-form entry's unchecked survival remark. The change is that a corrected sentence counts as a new claim, checked at the witness before it is sent back, which AGENTS.md now states for the author, not only for the reviewer.

The approximator of a family is \(P=\prod_{j=1}^t(1-q_j^{p-1})\) with each \(q_j\) in the family's span, chosen in Lemma onestep by the rank condition of Corollary descent applied to the current \(P\); it is a product of \((p-1)\)th powers depending on the family through rank conditions, so it is not \(\mathbb F_p\)-linear in the input, and the \(S\) families are combined only at the end of Theorem common, by summing their ranks. The linear case of the reviewer's suggestion does not occur; what remains is a joint form of the recurrence, below.

General statement. lem:marginal-refinement-gain: in Pang's setting, refining one family's approximator by his one-step choice, made on the joint kernel \(W_\nu\) of the other families, enlarges the joint kernel of all families by at least \((1-1/p)\) times the family's marginal rank on \(W_\nu\) one degree window down, and by at most its marginal rank at the window; joint Hilbert monotonicity holds; and the marginals can all vanish while the joint rank is full, so no refinement of one family contracts the joint rank at every state; one simultaneous round of all families can gain nothing either.

Marginal refinement gain

Statement. Over \(\mathbb F_p\), let \(\mathcal C_D\) be a degree-\(D\) pseudoideal in \(n\) variables containing the Boolean axioms, \(V_k\) all polynomials of degree at most \(k\) (as in Pang; \(N_n(k)\) counts multilinear monomials, and for \(k\ge n\) both \(\varphi(k)\) and \(N_n(k)\) are constant, so no \(K\le n\) is needed), families \((g_{\mu,i})_i\), \(\mu\in[S]\), of degree at most \(d\), approximators \(P_\mu\) of degree at most \(a\), \(Z_\mu(k)=\{f\in V_k:P_\mu g_{\mu,i}f\in\mathcal C_D\ \forall i\}\), \(Z(k)=\bigcap_\mu Z_\mu(k)\), \(\varphi(k)=\dim V_k-\dim Z(k)\), and for a family \(\nu\), \(W_\nu(k)=\bigcap_{\mu\ne\nu}Z_\mu(k)\) and \(m_\nu(k)=\dim W_\nu(k)-\dim Z(k)\). Let \(K\ge d\) and \(a+K+pd\le D\). (a) Joint monotonicity: \(\varphi(k)/N_n(k)\) is nonincreasing for \(0\le k\le K\). (b) There is \(q\in\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb F_p}\{g_{\nu,i}\}\) such that, with \(P_\nu\) replaced by \(P_\nu'=P_\nu(1-q^{p-1})\) and the other approximators kept, the new joint kernel \(Z'(K)\) satisfies \(\left(1-\tfrac1p\right)m_\nu(K-d)\le\dim Z'(K)-\dim Z(K)\le m_\nu(K)\); the upper bound holds for every refinement of family \(\nu\) alone. (c) There are states with \(\varphi(K)>0\) and \(m_\nu(K)=0\) for every \(\nu\): over \(\mathbb F_2\), \(\mathcal C_3\) the degree-\(3\) vanishing ideal of \(\{0,1\}^2\), \(K=d=1\), \(P_\mu=1\), and the families \(\{1+y\}\), \(\{x+y\}\), \(\{y\}\), with \(\varphi(1)=3\). (d) A round refining every family at once, each with its own \(q_\nu\), need not gain either, even when \(\varphi(K-d)>0\): over \(\mathbb F_2\), \(n=4\), \(\mathcal C_4\) the degree-\(4\) vanishing ideal of \(\{0,1\}^4\), \(K=d=1\), all \(P_\mu=1\), and the six families \(\{x_i,x_j\}\), \(i<j\), with \(\varphi(1)=5\) and \(\varphi(0)=1\): for every choice of \(q_{ij}\in\operatorname{span}\{x_i,x_j\}\), the refined joint kernel in \(V_1\) is still \(0\). So no bound of the form gain \(\ge c\,\varphi(K-d)\) holds for one round with any \(c>0\), even one depending on \(S\), \(n\) or \(K\); dependence on \(S\) could enter only through an additive loss term.

Proof. (a) Pang's proof of his Lemma hilbert uses only that \(x^\alpha Z(k)\subseteq Z(k+|\alpha|)\) for \(k+|\alpha|\le K\), that the Boolean axioms lie in \(Z(k)\) for \(k\ge2\), and that \(Z(k)=Z(K)\cap V_k\); each holds for every \(Z_\mu\), by absorption of \(\mathcal C_D\) within degree \(a+d+K\le D\), and so for their intersection. (b) Restrict the maps \(M_i:f\mapsto([P_\nu g_{\nu,\alpha}g_{\nu,i}f])_\alpha\) of Pang's Lemma onestep to the \(\mathbb F_p\)-subspace \(W_\nu(K-d)\). Corollary descent's condition \(\ker_EM(\lambda)\subseteq\ker_EM(\lambda^p)\) on \(V_{K-d}\otimes E\) restricts to \(W_\nu(K-d)\otimes E\) by intersecting both sides, so Lemma generic-descent applies there and gives \(q=\sum_ic_ig_{\nu,i}\) with \(\operatorname{rank}\bigl(f\mapsto([P_\nu g_{\nu,\alpha}qf])_\alpha\bigr)\ge(1-\tfrac1p)\operatorname{rank}\overline M\) on \(W_\nu(K-d)\); as in Pang's proof, \(\ker\overline M=Z_\nu(K-d)\cap W_\nu(K-d)=Z(K-d)\), so \(\operatorname{rank}\overline M=m_\nu(K-d)\). The left side is \(\dim\bigl(qW_\nu(K-d)+Z_\nu(K)\bigr)/Z_\nu(K)\), which is at most \(\dim\bigl(qW_\nu(K-d)+Z(K)\bigr)/Z(K)\) since \(Z(K)\subseteq Z_\nu(K)\). Now \(qW_\nu(K-d)\subseteq Z'(K)\): for \(f\in W_\nu(K-d)\) and \(\mu\ne\nu\), \(P_\mu g_{\mu,i}qf\in\mathcal C_D\) by absorption (degree at most \(a+d+K\)), and \(P'_\nu g_{\nu,i}qf=P_\nu g_{\nu,i}f(q-q^p)\in\mathcal C_D\) as in Pang's proof (degree at most \(a+K+pd\)); and \(Z(K)\subseteq Z'(K)\) since \(Z_\nu(K)\subseteq Z'_\nu(K)\), again as there. This gives the lower bound. For the upper bound, \(Z'(K)=Z'_\nu(K)\cap W_\nu(K)\subseteq W_\nu(K)\), whatever \(P'_\nu\) is. (c) Membership in \(\mathcal C_3\) is vanishing on the square, and \(V_1\), of dimension \(3\), restricts bijectively onto the functions on any three of its four points. The families' supports are \(\{y=0\}\), \(\{(1,0),(0,1)\}\) and \(\{y=1\}\); \(Z_\mu(1)\) is the set of \(f\in V_1\) vanishing on the support, \(Z(1)=0\), so \(\varphi(1)=3\); each union of two supports has at least three points, so \(W_\nu(1)=0\) and \(m_\nu(1)=0\) for every \(\nu\). The hypotheses: \(a=0\), \(K=d=1\), \(a+K+pd=3\le D\). This \(\mathcal C_3\) is Pang's own degree-\(3\) space for the Boolean axioms alone, so (c) is a state of his construction at its start. (d) Membership in \(\mathcal C_4\) is vanishing on the cube, and every product involved has degree at most \(1+1+2=4\). Initially \(f\in V_1\) kills family \(\{i,j\}\) exactly when it vanishes where \(x_i=1\) or \(x_j=1\), so the joint kernel is the set of functions in \(V_1\) vanishing at every nonzero point, which is \(0\); \(\varphi(1)=\dim V_1/\mathcal C_{\le1}=5\), and \(\varphi(0)=1\). After the round, \(P'_{ij}=1+q_{ij}\), and \(f\) kills the family exactly when it vanishes where \(q_{ij}=0\) and \((x_i,x_j)\ne(0,0)\). Each of \(0,x_i,x_j,x_i+x_j\) vanishes at one of the nonzero patterns \((0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\) of \((x_i,x_j)\), so \(f\) must vanish at every point whose \((i,j)\)-pattern is that forbidden one. The set \(A\) of points where \(f\) may be nonzero therefore avoids one nonzero pattern on every pair of coordinates, so, read as a family of subsets of \([4]\), it shatters no pair, and by the Sauer–Shelah lemma \(|A|\le\binom40+\binom41=5\). A nonzero function of degree at most \(1\) on \(\mathbb F_2^4\) is nonzero on at least \(8\) points, so \(f=0\).

Hypotheses, each with its step. \(K\ge d\) places \(W_\nu(K-d)\) in degree at least \(0\); \(a+K+pd\le D\) is used for \(P'_\nu g q f\) and Corollary descent, \(a+K+d\le D\) for absorption by the other families; the Boolean axioms give Pang's \(g^p\equiv g\) and his Lemma hilbert's multilinearity; the prime field is Corollary descent's.

Degenerate cases. \(S=1\): \(W_\nu=V\), \(m_\nu=c_{P_\nu}\), and (b) is Pang's Lemma onestep with the upper bound added. A family whose errors already lie in \(\mathcal C_D\): \(Z_\nu=V\), \(m_\nu=0\), and refining it changes nothing. \(W_\nu(K)=Z(K)\): (b) says family \(\nu\)'s refinement cannot help, as in (c). \(1\in\mathcal C_D\): every kernel is everything, and \(\varphi=0\).

Nonvacuity. The example of (c) satisfies every hypothesis: \(p=2\), a degree-\(3\) pseudoideal containing the Boolean axioms on two variables, three families of degree \(1\), \(P_\mu=1\) of degree \(a=0\), \(K=d=1\), \(a+K+pd=3=D\); the state has \(\varphi(1)=3\), individual ranks \(2,2,2\), and all marginals \(0\). Refining one family there leaves the joint rank \(3\), by the upper bound in (b). A second step can gain, by direct computation outside (b)'s budget (after the first refinement \(a=1\) and \(a+K+pd=4>D\)): with \(q_1=1+y\), \(P'_1g_1=y(1+y)\) vanishes on the square, so \(Z'_1(1)=V_1\); refining family \(2\) with \(q_2=x+y\) then gives \(Z'_2(1)=V_1\), and the joint kernel becomes \(Z_3(1)\), a gain of \(1\), where (b)'s formula would give \(0\), since \(m_2(0)=0\), though (b) does not apply there. The example of (d) satisfies the same hypotheses with \(n=4\), \(D=4\), \(a=0\), \(a+K+pd=3\le4\), and \(S=6\). No parameter ledger applies: the witness verifies no budget of the goal.

Relations. (b) with \(S=1\) is Pang's Lemma onestep, and its lower bound is the same argument on a subspace domain; (a) is his Lemma hilbert for an intersection of kernels; (c) is a lattice phenomenon, the marginals of an intersection of kernels can all vanish, here because the three kernels are independent lines, spanned by \(y\), \(1+x+y\) and \(1+y\), so every pairwise intersection is \(0\); compare the non-distributivity recorded in prop:unit-flag-kernel-gap. (d) is consistent with Pang's condition, which fails there at \(t=1\) (\(S=6\), \(\eta=\tfrac12\cdot\tfrac15\), \(S(1-\eta)>1\)); it shows only that no multiplicative round bound holds.

New mathematics. lem:marginal-refinement-gain: a refinement of one of Pang's families gains at least \((1-1/p)\) times its marginal rank one window down and at most its marginal rank at the window; joint normalized ranks are monotone; and all marginals can vanish while the joint rank is full; and one simultaneous round of six pair families on \(\{0,1\}^4\) gains nothing although the joint rank one window down is positive.

Block-additive killer degree in domain models

16 October 2026 · Working proof; finite product domains with disjoint variable blocks · Block-local killers and idempotents. Produced by claude-code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning medium).

The item asked for an effective common denominator”, the first naming its sub-idea on Pang's \(q\) and the OR reading, the second the disjoint-block lower bound.

Owed attempt. The family-killer entry named “the sub-idea, a lower bound for every surviving killer on disjoint blocks”. Made: (a) and (b) below prove it exactly, for disjoint blocks in domain models. Best outcome. At the goal's own parameters, an exact degree for surviving common killers of block-local errors, and a comparison of the idempotent route with it, sharper than lem:cylinder-killer-degree's transversal bound where that bound is not attained; for Pang's families on disjoint blocks it would say how far below the product of lem:pang-family-killer a killer can go.

General statement. lem:block-additive-degree: over any field, on a finite product \(X=\prod_\nu X_\nu\) with the blocks in disjoint variables, the least degree of a nonzero function supported in a product set \(\prod_\nu A_\nu\) is the sum of the blocks' least degrees, and degree is additive on products of block functions (a standard tensor-degree fact, proved here in this setting); so block-local errors in a domain model have surviving common killers of least degree \(\sum_\nu m_\nu\), a span-type separating idempotent, vanishing off the union of the errors' supports, is forced to be that union's indicator, whose degree can exceed \(\sum_\nu m_\nu\) by a factor of the block size on cubes, while a general idempotent protecting a \(0/1\)-valued least killer, where one exists, costs only \(\sum_\nu m_\nu\), and the least degree of a killer nonzero at a given point is the sum of the blocks' pointwise least degrees.

Block-additive degree

Statement. Let \(F\) be a field, \(X_\nu\subseteq F^{B_\nu}\) finite nonempty sets for disjoint variable blocks \(B_1,\dots,B_S\), and \(X=\prod_\nu X_\nu\). The degree \(\delta(f)\) of a function \(f\) on \(X\) (or \(X_\nu\)) is the least degree of a polynomial agreeing with it. (a) For nonempty \(A_\nu\subseteq X_\nu\), let \(m_\nu\) be the least \(\delta\) of a nonzero function on \(X_\nu\) supported in \(A_\nu\). The least \(\delta\) of a nonzero function on \(X\) supported in \(\prod_\nu A_\nu\) is \(\sum_\nu m_\nu\); and for nonzero \(f_\nu\) on \(X_\nu\), \(\delta(\prod_\nu f_\nu)=\sum_\nu\delta(f_\nu)\). (b) Let \(\mathcal C_D\) be the polynomials of degree at most \(D\) vanishing on \(X\), and \(E_{\nu,i}\) polynomials in the variables of \(B_\nu\), of degree at most \(e\), with supports \(Z_\nu=\bigcup_i\operatorname{supp}E_{\nu,i}\subsetneq X_\nu\) on \(X_\nu\). For \(k+e\le D\), the polynomials of degree at most \(k\) killing every \(E_{\nu,i}\) modulo \(\mathcal C_D\) and not in \(\mathcal C_D\) exist exactly when \(k\ge\sum_\nu m_\nu\), with \(m_\nu\) for \(A_\nu=X_\nu\setminus Z_\nu\). (c) In the setting of lem:idempotent-common-denominator with \(C=\mathcal C_D\) the degree-\(D\) vanishing ideal of a finite set \(X\) and errors \(w_i\) with union of supports \(U\): every \(s\) of degree at most \(D-\max_i\deg w_i\) with \(sw_i-w_i\in\mathcal C_D\) for all \(i\) and vanishing off \(U\) on \(X\), in particular a span generator \(s=\sum_ia_iw_i\), agrees with \(1_U\) on \(X\); so \(\deg s\ge\delta(1_U)\), and \(1-s\) has degree at least \(\delta(1_{X\setminus U})\). (d) For block-local errors as in (b), \(\delta(1_{X\setminus U})=\sum_\nu\delta(1_{A_\nu})\), which can exceed \(\sum_\nu m_\nu\) by a factor \(b\): on \(X_\nu=\{0,1\}^b\) with \(Z_\nu=\{0\}\), \(m_\nu=1\) and \(\delta(1_{A_\nu})=b\). (e) Without the condition of vanishing off \(U\): if \(p\) is a surviving common killer, \(0/1\)-valued on \(X\), with \(\deg p+\max_i\deg w_i\le D\) and \(2\deg p\le D\), then \(s=1-p\) satisfies \(sw_i-w_i\in\mathcal C_D\) and \(sp\in\mathcal C_D\), and \(1-s=p\); so the idempotent lemma with protected element \(p\) reaches \(\deg p\), which is \(\sum_\nu m_\nu\) when some least killer is \(0/1\)-valued, as always over \(\mathbb F_2\); over \(\mathbb F_3\) on \(X=\{0,1,2\}\) with \(Z=\{0\}\), \(m=1\) (the function \(x\)) while every nonzero indicator supported in \(A=\{1,2\}\) has degree \(2\). (f) Protecting one point: for \(x_0\in\prod_\nu A_\nu\), the least \(\delta\) of a function supported in \(\prod_\nu A_\nu\) and nonzero at \(x_0\) is \(\sum_\nu m_\nu(x_0)\), where \(m_\nu(x_0)\) is the least \(\delta\) of a function supported in \(A_\nu\) and nonzero at \(x_{0,\nu}\); it can exceed \(\sum_\nu m_\nu\): over \(\mathbb F_2\) on the block \(\{0,1\}^3\) with \(A_\nu=\{x_1=0\}\cup\{(1,1,1)\}\) and \(x_{0,\nu}=(1,1,1)\), \(m_\nu=1\) while \(m_\nu(x_0)=2\).

Proof. (a) Fix a degree-compatible monomial order on all variables; its restriction to each block is one. Let \(G_\nu\) be the reduced Gröbner basis of the vanishing ideal \(I_\nu\) of \(X_\nu\). \(\bigcup_\nu G_\nu\) is a Gröbner basis of \(J=\sum_\nu I_\nu\): S-pairs within a block reduce to zero, and those from different blocks have coprime leading monomials and reduce to zero by Buchberger's first criterion. So the standard monomials of \(J\) are the products of block standard monomials, \(\prod_\nu|X_\nu|=|X|\) of them. \(J\) is contained in the vanishing ideal \(I\) of \(X\), and \(\dim F[x]/I=|X|\) since evaluation onto the functions on a finite set is surjective; so \(J=I\), and the normal forms represent every function on \(X\) exactly once. For a degree-compatible order the normal form of a polynomial has degree at most its own, so \(\delta(f)\) is the degree of \(f\)'s normal form, which is the degree of its leading monomial. Let \(\Phi_\nu\) be the functions on \(X_\nu\) supported in \(A_\nu\), with a basis of normal forms in echelon form, distinct leading monomials; then \(m_\nu\) is the least degree of these leading monomials, every nonzero element of \(\Phi_\nu\) having one of them as leading monomial. The functions on \(X\) supported in \(\prod_\nu A_\nu\) are spanned by the products of such basis elements; each such product is a sum of products of block standard monomials, so it is its own normal form, with leading monomial the product of the factors' leading monomials, and distinct tuples give distinct products. A nonzero combination therefore has as leading monomial the largest product present, of degree at least \(\sum_\nu m_\nu\), attained by the product of minimal-degree elements. The same leading-monomial argument gives \(\delta(\prod f_\nu)=\sum\delta(f_\nu)\). (b) For \(k+e\le D\) every product \(fE_{\nu,i}\) has degree at most \(D\), so membership in \(\mathcal C_D\) is vanishing on \(X\); \(f\) kills \(E_{\nu,i}\) exactly when \(f\) vanishes on the cylinder \(\operatorname{supp}E_{\nu,i}\times\prod_{\mu\ne\nu}X_\mu\), and all of them exactly when \(f\) is supported in \(\prod_\nu A_\nu\); \(f\notin\mathcal C_D\) means \(f\ne0\) on \(X\). Apply (a). (c) \(s\) vanishes off \(U\) by hypothesis; at \(x\in\operatorname{supp}w_i\), \(s(x)w_i(x)=w_i(x)\ne0\) gives \(s(x)=1\); the degree hypothesis puts \(sw_i-w_i\) in degree \(D\), where membership is vanishing. A span generator vanishes off \(U\) because each \(w_i\) does. (d) \(X\setminus U=\prod_\nu A_\nu\), so \(1_{X\setminus U}=\prod_\nu1_{A_\nu}\) and (a) gives the sum. On \(\{0,1\}^b\), \(x_1\) vanishes at \(0\) with degree \(1\), and constants do not, so \(m_\nu=1\); \(1_{A_\nu}=1-\prod_j(1-x_j)\) is multilinear with the monomial \(x_1\cdots x_b\) of coefficient \(\pm1\), and multilinear polynomials are the normal forms on the cube, so \(\delta(1_{A_\nu})=b\). (e) \(sw_i-w_i=-pw_i\), which vanishes on \(X\) as \(p\) kills \(w_i\), within degree \(D\); \(sp=p-p^2\) vanishes on \(X\) as \(p\) is \(0/1\)-valued, within degree \(2\deg p\le D\). On \(\{0,1,2\}\) over \(\mathbb F_3\) the functions supported in \(\{1,2\}\) with values in \(\{0,1\}\) are \(1_{\{1\}},1_{\{2\}},1_{\{1,2\}}\), each of degree \(2\) since a degree-\(1\) polynomial vanishing at \(0\) is \(cx\), not \(0/1\)-valued unless \(c=0\). (f) By the echelon argument of (a), the functions in \(\bigotimes_\nu\Phi_\nu\) of degree at most \(d\) are spanned by the products of basis elements with total degree at most \(d\), since a combination's degree is the largest leading-monomial degree present. Evaluation at \(x_0\) is the product of the block evaluations on such products. A function of degree \(d\) nonzero at \(x_0\) is a combination of products of total degree at most \(d\), one of which is nonzero at \(x_0\), so each factor is nonzero at \(x_{0,\nu}\) and \(d\ge\sum_\nu m_\nu(x_0)\), the least degree of a block element nonzero at \(x_{0,\nu}\) being attained by a basis element by the same echelon argument; the product of such elements attains it. In the example, a nonzero function of degree at most \(1\) over \(\mathbb F_2\) is affine, with support the whole cube or a half-space of four points; two distinct half-spaces meet in \(0\) or \(2\) points, so the only half-space inside the five-point \(A_\nu\) is \(\{x_1=0\}\), and the only such function is \(1+x_1\), zero at \((1,1,1)\); so \(m_\nu=1\) and \(m_\nu(x_0)\ge2\). The function \(1_{(0,0,0)}+1_{(1,1,1)}\) is supported in \(A_\nu\), nonzero at \(x_{0,\nu}\), and has degree at most \(2\), since over \(\mathbb F_2\) the coefficient of \(x_1x_2x_3\) is the sum of its values, here \(0\).

Hypotheses, each with its step. Finiteness of the \(X_\nu\) gives the Gröbner basis and the dimension count; disjoint variable blocks give coprime leading monomials across blocks and distinct products; \(k+e\le D\) in (b), the degree bound in (c) and the two bounds in (e) are the steps where membership in \(\mathcal C_D\) becomes vanishing; \(Z_\nu\ne X_\nu\) makes \(A_\nu\) nonempty, without which no killer survives; vanishing off \(U\) in (c) is what forces \(s=1_U\), and (e) shows the conclusion fails without it; (f) needs only \(x_0\in\prod_\nu A_\nu\), and read as the cost of an idempotent protecting \(p=1_{x_0}\), also \(\deg f+\max_i\deg w_i\le D\) and \(\deg f+\deg p\le D\). The field is arbitrary.

Relations. (a) is the standard additivity of degree over tensor products in disjoint variables, folklore for Boolean functions, stated and proved here for finite product sets over any field; it is registered for its consequences. lem:cylinder-killer-degree gives the transversal number \(\tau\) for cylinder errors on one-hot product domains. Where each block is one one-hot coordinate, every block function has degree at most \(1\), \(m_\nu=[Z_\nu\ne\emptyset]\), and (b) equals \(\tau\). For cylinder errors on disjoint blocks of several coordinates, \(\tau=\sum_\nu\tau_\nu\), the cylinder lemma gives \(m_\nu\ge\tau_\nu\), so \(\sum_\nu m_\nu\ge\tau\), with equality when the cylinder lemma's attainment condition holds in each block and strict inequality possible: on the block \(\{0,1\}^2\) with cylinders \(\{x_1=1\}\) and \(\{x_1=0,x_2=1\}\), \(\tau_\nu=1\) while \(A_\nu\) is the origin and \(m_\nu=2\). Neither lemma implies the other. (c) is the domain-model reading of lem:idempotent-common-denominator's span generator, the OR of the errors' nonvanishing, as the reviewer of that entry read it. For Pang's families in the cube's vanishing ideal, on disjoint variable blocks and within degree \(D-e\), (b) gives the least killer degree; since \(q_\nu^{p-1}\) vanishes on \(U_\nu\), \(m_\nu\le(p-1)d\) when \(q_\nu\) is not identically zero on the block (for \(t>1\) any factor's \(q_j\) serves), so the product killer of lem:pang-family-killer, of degree at most \(S(p-1)d\), dominates it.
