Route review of the transfer line: domain-model killer degrees and a proper-closure test

16 October 2026 · Route review, no claim registered · Ordinary review of the transfer line. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, low reasoning).

Question. The goal review of 16 October moved cycles to effective-annihilator-degree. Six research entries later, what does the line prove, what does the goal need from it, and which test decides whether it can give that?

General statement. No claim is registered: the review assesses lem:transversal-killer-basis, lem:cylinder-killer-degree, lem:top-degree-killer-transfer, lem:graded-domain-pairing, lem:leading-form-killer-bound, lem:block-additive-degree and the joint-savings results of the period, and sets the next test.

The line's general claim. In domain models, where the closure is the degree-\(D\) part of the vanishing ideal of a finite set, the first surviving common killer degree of errors is exact: a transversal number on cubes and one-hot product domains (lem:transversal-killer-basis, lem:cylinder-killer-degree), additive over disjoint blocks (lem:block-additive-degree). At the top degree of the product pigeonhole system, whose degree-\(n\) closure is proper and unsatisfiable, monomial errors on distinct holes reduce to the domain model (lem:top-degree-killer-transfer), so there the killer degree is the transversal number, \(\tau(K_4)=3\) at \(m=5\), \(n=4\). Graded duality pairs only cubes (lem:graded-domain-pairing) and gives proper closures a lower bound blind to axioms' constant terms (lem:leading-form-killer-bound). Idempotent denominators pay indicator degrees, unless they protect a least killer.

What the goal needs. effective-annihilator-degree asks for an explicit bound on the first filtered degree of an annihilator preserving a protected class in a faithful model of the closures the repair uses, Pang's proper \(C_D\) at his cutoff \(\Delta+K+d\le D\), or a strictly cheaper certificate on an unbounded family, with the consequence for repair. The line's exact results hold in domain models and at the top degree of the product pigeonhole system, where the inhomogeneous axioms enter the window only as themselves; no result covers a window containing multiples of those axioms, which is where Pang's closures live.

Falsification attempt. The line's implicit hope is that killers modulo a proper closure behave as in a domain model. Tested against the record: check:functional-factor-kernels found the functional pigeonhole system's common kernels at \(K=1\) equal to the domain model's plus the relations, consistent with the hope; ex:support-saving-not-inherited shows ranks in a proper quotient differ from the domain model's (a saving of \(54\) against \(11\)), refuting the transfer of ranks; check:leading-form-functional-pigeons shows a proper closure removing every survivor when the errors span a unit through an inhomogeneous axiom, and finds least surviving killer degree \(2\) for two sets without linear survivors. What is untested is the kernel space at \(K=2\), where multiples of the pigeon axioms enter.

Assessment. The line is exact in domain models, and at the top degree of the product pigeonhole system it is exact modulo a proper closure; elsewhere it bounds no killer degree modulo a proper closure whose window contains multiples of its inhomogeneous axioms. The six research entries of the period, #entry-2026-10-16-cylinder-killers, #entry-2026-10-16-gorenstein-domains, #entry-2026-10-16-initial-pseudoideal-bound, #entry-2026-10-16-principal-joint-kernels, #entry-2026-10-16-marginal-refinement and #entry-2026-10-16-block-killer-degree, each declared no bearing. The Alon–Füredi lead of the last review, left Not run, has its one-point case, the Combinatorial Nullstellensatz degree \(\sum_i(|S_i|-1)\) of a grid function supported at one point, as a case of lem:block-additive-degree (a) with one-variable blocks; the theorem itself, on the least number of nonzeros of a polynomial of given degree on a grid, covers arbitrary supports and is not given by (a).

Obstacle

No recorded statement relates killers modulo a proper closure to vanishing on a set when the window contains multiples of the inhomogeneous axioms: lem:top-degree-killer-transfer works at the top degree of the product pigeonhole system, where those axioms enter only as themselves, using the independence of the unplaced-pigeon indicators, and check:functional-factor-kernels covers the functional system at \(K=1\). At \(K=2\) the least surviving degree is known for two sets, but not the kernel space or which killers survive.

Architecture review

Necessary target. For every proper Pang closure \(C_D\) in his setting (any prime \(p\), families of degree at most \(d\), \(t\) factors, \(\Delta+K+d\le D\)), a degree \(k\) and a polynomial \(f\) of degree at most \(k\) killing every error modulo \(C_D\) and preserving the protected class, with \(k\) bounded explicitly below Pang's \(K\) on an unbounded family, or a certificate as cheap. Two readings of the protected class: the base class \(1\), \(f\notin C_D\); and the weight class the repair needs, \(wf\notin J_D\). Downstream. Through thm:certified-repair-composition the target would supply the killing step of the repair; substituting such an \(f\) for the multiplier that thm:finite-grid-repair constructs needs a lemma not in the record (any \(f\) killing the weighted adaptive errors with \(wf\notin J_D\) can take its place), and lowering \(K\) also changes Pang's \(\eta\), his rank budget and his simulation cutoff (cor:pang-observation-calibration). So the target gives the killing step at the goal's parameters; the repair at a lower cutoff is not established until that lemma and the recomputed budget are proved.

Extra requirements. The current approach demands exact least degrees and works where membership is literal vanishing; the target needs only an upper bound below \(K\) and only derivability modulo \(C_D\). The exactness can be weakened: a killer of degree below \(K\) suffices. The domain-model setting cannot stand in for the target: it is what Pang's closures are not, so the demand that is wrong for the goal is the setting, not the precision.

Independent alternative. The review's medium reviewer, given only the goal statement and fourteen registered results with the route withheld (review record), proposed a sandwich: killing is proved in the domain sub-closure \(B_D\subseteq C_D\) generated by the Boolean and monomial axioms, where the line's exact degrees hold, since \(fE\in B_D\) implies \(fE\in C_D\); survival is proved through a normal-form operator of the proper closure, such as Razborov's for the pigeonhole principle; the open step is a locality product rule for that operator. It explains why no ring-level theorem can be expected: the control \(k[t]/(t^{m+1})\) of prop:multiplier-transfer-limits has a one-point spectrum and unbounded annihilator degree. Compared with the current route, the alternative keeps the line's domain-model results as the killing half and supplies the missing survival half by an operator. The record has a candidate: prop:pigeonhole-quotient-count (near-half notebook), conditional on Razborov's Claims 3.5 and 3.11, counts the pigeonhole quotient with linear pigeon sums by its irreducible terms below degree \((n+1)/2\).

Rank normalization. The line's degrees are measured in domain models, and the goal's in the proper quotient; ex:support-saving-not-inherited shows the two give different ranks for the same errors. The target is a degree, so relative contraction does not replace it; the test below therefore measures every quantity modulo \(C\cap V_2\), the proper quotient's relations, not in the domain model.

Decision. Adopt the sandwich, and give the next research cycle to the test below, which measures both halves and a joint effect at once; then return cycles to joint-error-savings, restoring the order the user stated for the goal's objectives, which the goal review had departed from by its own rule; the test's joint quantity (ii) bears on that line too. Route decisions records the restoration.

Decisive test. Test disposition. New operation, for (ii) and (iii); (i) is the \(K=1\) comparison repeated at \(K=2\) and adds no operation. Operation. On the functional pigeonhole system over \(\mathbb F_2\) with \(6\) pigeons and \(5\) holes at \(D=3\), proper (check:functional-factor-kernels), at \(K=2\), for the error sets \(F_3=\{x_{00},x_{11},x_{22}\}\) and \(F_4=F_3\cup\{x_{33}\}\), decompose the excess of \(\operatorname{Ann}^{(2)}_C(F)\) over \(\operatorname{Ann}^{(2)}_H(F)+(C\cap V_2)\), \(H\) the closure of the monomial axioms (the domain model of partial matchings), into three quantities, all modulo \(C\cap V_2\): (i) each single error's excess, \(\operatorname{Ann}^{(2)}_C(x_v)\) over \(A_v+(C\cap V_2)\) with \(A_v=\operatorname{Ann}^{(2)}_H(x_v)\), measured by the full degree-\(3\) closure; (ii) the joint defect, the failure of \(\bigcap_v\bigl(A_v+(C\cap V_2)\bigr)=\bigcap_vA_v+(C\cap V_2)\), computed from the \(A_v\) and a basis of \(C\cap V_2\) alone; (iii) the dimension of surviving domain killers, \(\bigl(\operatorname{Ann}^{(2)}_H(F)+(C\cap V_2)\bigr)/(C\cap V_2)\), with an example such as \(x_{20}x_{01}\) for \(F_3\); the total excess minus the part already in \(\bigcap_v(A_v+C\cap V_2)\) is the cancellation part. Prediction. Untested: the \(K=1\) check found no excess, and nothing predicts \(K=2\). Outcomes: (iii) positive is the sandwich's killing half surviving in the proper closure; (iii) zero would refute that half, for the protected class \(1\), at this instance; (i) positive would be killers from cancellations among degree-\(3\) members (a lift of the restricted closure \(C_2(5,4)\) through \(x_v=1\) lands in \(A_v+(C\cap V_2)\) already, by the reviewer's sketch, so it cannot produce one); (ii) positive would be a joint effect of the proper closure, not a union of supports, and not covered by cor:generic-principal-kernel, whose reserve fails here (\(0+2+1+1=4>3\)); whether it is a saving the joint endpoint admits depends on the reading of its domination clause, property or mechanism, which cor:generic-principal-kernel records as ambiguous. Trivial cases. Duplicating an error changes no kernel; errors in \(C\) impose nothing; sets containing all variables of one pigeon have no survivor (lem:leading-form-killer-bound (e)) and are excluded; sets with linear killers from the monomial axioms are excluded; \(H\subseteq C\) makes every quantity nonnegative, and every space contains \(C\cap V_2\), so only dimensions modulo it carry information; \(\operatorname{Ann}(F_4)\subseteq\operatorname{Ann}(F_3)\). Power. The instance lies outside Pang's window: with \(K=2\), \(d=1\) and \(\Delta\ge1\), his cutoff needs \(D\ge4\), and at \(5\) holes the functional system is refuted at degree \(4\); it is a proxy for a proper closure of an unsatisfiable system with linear axioms acting in the window, and its outcome bears on no goal-parameter instance directly. A window instance needs a board proper at degree \(4\), eight holes by the record (check:augmented-php-degree-small-boards), with \(72\) variables and about \(1.09\) million multilinear monomials of degree at most \(4\), beyond the pure-Python closure. The \(6\times5\) instance has \(30\) variables and \(4526\) monomials of degree at most \(3\); the three runs of check:leading-form-functional-pigeons on it took \(28\), \(31\) and \(37\) seconds (research/provenance/session-records/leading-forms). Each of (i) to (iii) is undecided by the cited bounds at both sets; the restriction to the four-hole system gives no information on (i), its lift landing in \(A_v+(C\cap V_2)\) and its upper bound through \(C_3(5,4)\) being vacuous, that system being refuted at degree \(3\). The window instance's base, the functional system on eight holes, has refutation degree \(5\) and a degree-\(4\) closure of dimension \(143643\) computed by the compiled tool (check:augmented-php-degree-small-boards), so it is reachable there. Attempt. From the cited statements: lem:factor-span-domination gives the transported killers and shows they add nothing beyond a direct killer; lem:leading-form-killer-bound bounds the least degree by \(2\), the value found; a single member \(x_{ab}P_i\) times an error lies in \(C\cap V_2\) already, so an excess needs cancellation among degree-\(3\) members; neither statement describes the kernel spaces. The attempt stopped at those cancellations, which need the closure's degree-\(3\) part. Record search. Searches for common kernels of the functional pigeonhole system at \(K=2\), for restriction, intersection defects and the restricted system, and for the functional system's refutation thresholds returned check:functional-factor-kernels (\(K=1\), and refutation degree \(3\) at three and four holes, \(4\) at five), lem:factor-ideal-domination, check:leading-form-functional-pigeons (least degrees, not spaces), check:clique-factor-kernels (\(K=1\)), prop:unary-closure-modulo-occupancy and lem:weighted-restriction-transport (other systems), none at \(K=2\).

General statement. conj:functional-kernel-transfer: for the functional pigeonhole system over \(\mathbb F_2\) with \(n+1\) pigeons and \(n\) holes, at every proper degree \(D\) and \(K\le D-1\), the common kernel in \(V_K\) of a set of variables modulo the closure \(C\) is the common kernel modulo the closure \(H\) of the monomial axioms plus \(C\cap V_K\). General statement. lem:native-detection-count: \(m\) old functionals in rectangle forms detect the stacked kernel only if its rank \(r\) is at most \(m\) times the dimension of the span of the products \(E_iv\), \(v\) of degree at most the slack \(L\), modulo the pseudoideal; over every finite field, \(m\) functionals, the first normalized, suffice at every slack when \(m\) times the least column rank \(c\) of the stacked image is at least \(r\); and at Pang's full degree the slack is at least \(\Delta+d\), so his errors meet thm:common-moment-radical's reserve whenever \((p-1)K\le\Delta+d\).

Native detection count

Statement. Over a field \(F\), let \(V_k\) be the polynomials of degree at most \(k\) in \(n\) variables, \(J_D\subseteq V_D\) a degree-\(D\) pseudoideal (closed under multiplication by a variable within degree \(D\)), \(J_k=J_D\cap V_k\), \(W=V_D/J_D\), \(E_1,\ldots,E_{S'}\) errors of degree at most \(e\), \(U\subseteq V_K\), and \(L\ge0\) with \(e+K+L\le D\). Let \(T:U\to W^{S'}\), \(u\mapsto([E_iu])_i\), with kernel \(C\), image \(Y\) and rank \(r\). An old functional is a linear \(\mu:V_D\to F\) vanishing on \(J_D\); for old functionals \(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_m\), the rectangle forms are the coordinates of \(\Phi_L(u)=\bigl(\mu_j(E_iuv)\bigr)_{i,j,v}\), \(v\) over a basis of \(V_L\). (a) \(C\subseteq\ker\Phi_L\), and \(\ker\Phi_L=C\) implies \(r\le m\dim Z_L\), \(Z_L\) the image of \(\operatorname{span}\{E_iv:i,\ v\in V_L\}\) in \(V_{e+L}/J_{e+L}\); in particular \(r\le m\,S'\dim V_L\), and \(r\le m\,S'\,N_n(L)\) when \(J_D\) contains the Boolean axioms (\(N_n(L)\) multilinear monomials of degree at most \(L\)). (b) Let \(F=\mathbb F_q\), and let \(c\) be the least dimension of \(\operatorname{span}\{y_1,\ldots,y_{S'}\}\subseteq W\) over nonzero \(y=(y_i)\in Y\) (\(c=\infty\) when \(r=0\)). If \(mc\ge r\), some old functionals \(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_m\) give \(\ker\Phi_L=C\) for every admissible \(L\); if \(1\notin J_D\) and \(m\ge1\), they can be chosen with \(\mu_1(1)=1\). (c) So over \(\mathbb F_q\) the least \(m\) with \(\ker\Phi_L=C\) lies between \(\lceil r/\dim Z_L\rceil\) and \(\lceil r/c\rceil\le r\); for \(S'=1\), \(c=1\), and at \(L=0\) the least \(m\) is \(r\) over every field, the components of \(Y\) then spanning a space of dimension \(r\). (d) For Pang's errors \(P_\mu g_{\mu,i}\), \(e=\Delta+d\), \(w=1\): his selection cutoff \(\Delta+K+d\le D\) allows \(L=0\), where a \(p\)-linear form \(\mu(E\,u_1\cdots u_p)\), of degree \(e+pK\), does not fit; his simulation's cost \(K+\max(2\Delta+2d,\Delta+w)\le D\), stated on the same \(D\) for his Proposition 5.1 in the downstream-realization paragraph of the record of cor:pang-observation-calibration, gives \(L=D-\Delta-d-K\ge\Delta+d\), so thm:common-moment-radical's reserve \(b+e+pK\le D\) holds whenever \((p-1)K\le\Delta+d=(p-1)dt+d\), for instance when \(K\le dt\).

Proof. (a) If \(u\in C\), each \(E_iu\in J_D\), and \(E_iuv\) is a combination of monomial multiples of \(E_iu\) of degree at most \(e+K+L\le D\), so it lies in \(J_D\) and every \(\mu_j(E_iuv)=0\). For fixed \(j\), the coordinate \(u\mapsto\mu_j(zu)\) with \(z=E_iv\) depends only on the class of \(z\) in \(V_{e+L}/J_{e+L}\): if \(z\in J_{e+L}\), \(zu\in J_D\) by the same closure. So for each \(j\) the coordinates span a space of functionals of dimension at most \(\dim Z_L\), and \(\operatorname{rank}\Phi_L\le m\dim Z_L\); if \(\ker\Phi_L=C\), that rank is \(\dim U-\dim C=r\). \(\dim Z_L\le S'\dim V_L\); with the Boolean axioms in \(J_D\), \(v\) and its multilinear reduction differ by multiples of \(x_k^2-x_k\) of degree at most \(L\), so \(\dim Z_L\le S'N_n(L)\). (b) Old functionals \(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_m\) are the rows of a linear map \(M:W\to F^m\), and every \(M\) arises. The coordinates with \(v=1\) are \((My_i)_i\) for \(y=T(u)\), so \(C\subseteq\ker\Phi_L\subseteq\ker\Phi_0\), and it suffices that \(\ker\Phi_0=C\): that no nonzero \(y\in Y\) has \(M\) vanishing on \(\operatorname{span}\{y_i\}\). For one \(y\), the maps vanishing on that span, of dimension at least \(c\), number at most \(q^{m(\dim W-c)}\); \(y\) and its nonzero multiples give the same span, so at most \((q^r-1)/(q-1)<q^r\) spans occur, and the bad maps number less than \(q^{r+m\dim W-mc}\le q^{m\dim W}\), the number of all \(M\). If \(1\notin J_D\), the maps whose first row takes the value \(1\) at the class of \(1\) number \(q^{m\dim W-1}\); for one \(y\) the bad ones among them number at most \(q^{m(\dim W-c)-1}\), since the condition fixes one coordinate of the first row in a direction independent of those vanishing on the span unless \([1]\) lies in that span, in which case there are none; so fewer than \(q^{r+m\dim W-mc-1}\le q^{m\dim W-1}\) are bad. (c) The lower bound is (a); the upper bound is (b) with \(m=\lceil r/c\rceil\), and \(c\ge1\); for \(S'=1\) every nonzero \(y\) spans a line, so \(c=1\), and at \(L=0\), \(Z_0\) is spanned by \(E_1\), so \(m\ge r\). (d) Pang's errors have degree at most \(\Delta+d\), the approximator of degree \(\Delta=(p-1)dt\) times an input of degree at most \(d\); with \(D\ge K+2\Delta+2d\), \(L=D-\Delta-d-K\ge\Delta+d\), and \(b+e+pK=\Delta+d+pK\le D\) exactly when \((p-1)K\le L\).

Hypotheses, each with its step. \(e+K+L\le D\) and the pseudoideal closure give \(C\subseteq\ker\Phi_L\) and the dependence on classes in (a); the Boolean axioms only replace \(\dim V_L\) by \(N_n(L)\); the finite field is used only in (b)'s count, for every \(q\ge2\) (over an infinite field the same conclusion needs the least rank over the algebraic closure, which can be smaller: \((e_1,e_2),(-e_2,e_1)\) has least rank \(2\) over \(\mathbb R\) and \(1\) over \(\mathbb C\)); \(1\notin J_D\) is used only for the normalization; old functionals are exactly the maps \(M\) on \(W\). The conclusions concern the stacked kernel of fixed errors, with no class protected; survival of a multiplier is a separate condition.

Degenerate cases. \(r=0\): every \(u\) is in \(C\), and \(m=0\) functionals detect it. \(S'=1\): \(c=1\), and at \(L=0\) the least \(m\) is \(r\), which contains prop:repair-cost-controls' rectangle obstruction for one scalar combination, its case \(m=1\). \(r=0\) with \(m=0\): the normalization is void. \(J_D=V_D\): \(W=0\), \(r=0\). A satisfiable domain model, \(J_D\) the degree-\(D\) part of a vanishing ideal: (a) to (c) hold unchanged.

Nonvacuity. Over \(\mathbb F_2\), \(n=3\), \(J_2\) the degree-\(2\) part of the Boolean ideal, \(U=V_1\), errors \(x_1,x_2\), \(e=K=1\), \(D=2\), \(L=0\): \(u=\alpha+\beta x_1+\gamma x_2+\delta x_3\) with \(x_1u\) and \(x_2u\) vanishing on the cube must vanish wherever \(x_1=1\) or \(x_2=1\), which forces \(u=0\), so \(C=0\) and \(r=4\); \(\dim Z_0=2\), so at least two functionals are needed; \(u=1+x_1\) gives \(y=(0,x_2+x_1x_2)\), whose span is a line, so \(c=1\) and (b) guarantees \(m=4\). Instance of prop:repair-cost-controls, \(n=3\), \(D=4\), \(U\) the multilinear polynomials of degree at most \(2\), errors \((1+\ell)x_1,(1+\ell)x_2\) (the prop's multiplier, written \(\ell\) here), \(L=0\): \(c=1\) for every \(\ell\) in the span (for \(\ell=x_1\) or \(x_2\) one error is \(0\) on the cube, for \(\ell=x_1+x_2\) both are \(x_1x_2\), for \(\ell=0\) see the next paragraph), so (b) gives only \(m=r\). No parameter ledger applies: the witness verifies no budget of the goal.

The instance \(\ell=0\). Here \(W\) is the functions on \(\{0,1\}^3\), \(U\) the functions with \(\sum_au(a)=0\) (the coefficient of \(x_1x_2x_3\)), \(C\) is spanned by \((1+x_1)(1+x_2)\), and \(r=6\). With \(w_j\) the function representing \(\mu_j\), the coordinates are \(\langle f_j,u\rangle\) and \(\langle g_j,u\rangle\), \(f_j\) and \(g_j\) the restrictions of \(w_j\) to \(\{a_1=1\}\) and \(\{a_2=1\}\); \(\ker\Phi_0=C\) exactly when the \(f_j,g_j\) span all functions on the six points with \(a_1=1\) or \(a_2=1\), since the annihilator of \(C\) is those functions plus the constant. Two functionals give at most four vectors, so \(m\ge3\). Three suffice: on the blocks \(A=\{100,101\}\), \(B=\{010,011\}\), \(\Gamma=\{110,111\}\), take \(w_1=(A{:}\,e_1,\ B{:}\,e_2,\ \Gamma{:}\,e_1)\), \(w_2=(A{:}\,e_2,\ B{:}\,e_1,\ \Gamma{:}\,e_2)\), \(w_3=(A{:}\,e_1,\ B{:}\,e_1,\ \Gamma{:}\,0)\); then \(f_3\) is \(A{:}\,e_1\), \(f_1-f_3\) is \(\Gamma{:}\,e_1\), \(g_1-\Gamma{:}\,e_1\) is \(B{:}\,e_2\), \(g_3\) is \(B{:}\,e_1\), \(g_2-B{:}\,e_1\) is \(\Gamma{:}\,e_2\), and \(f_2-\Gamma{:}\,e_2\) is \(A{:}\,e_2\), all six. So the least \(m\) is \(3=r/S'\), the lower bound of (c), while (b) gives \(6\).

Baseline. Transversal degree of block families

16 October 2026 · Working proof · cube domain model only · Block families against Pang's summed criterion. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, low reasoning).

At the goal's own parameters, an exact joint common-multiplier degree for an unbounded family of Pang-type families, against which his summed criterion \(S(1-\eta)^t<1\) of cor:pang-observation-calibration can be measured, and which beats it; a domain model gives the exact degree, but a saving there is a union of supports, which joint-error-savings excludes, so at best the result calibrates the summed criterion and gives no admitted saving.

General statement. lem:block-family-multiplier-degree: on the cube, for coordinate families on the blocks of a hypergraph \(H\), with approximators nonzero at some nonzero pattern of their block, the least degree of a surviving common multiplier is at least the transversal number \(\tau(H)\), and Pang's own factors on a chain of forms attain it over every prime field; over \(\mathbb F_2\) with \(|B|-1\) factors per block every choice satisfies the hypothesis, so on all \((t+1)\)-subsets the degrees over choices range from \(n-t\) to \(n\) (the upper end, through \(\delta_0\), when \(K\ge n\) and \(n+a+1\le D\)), both attained at \(t=1\), while Pang's summed criterion with \(t\) factors certifies nothing at any \(K\) once \(\binom n{t+1}\ge2^t\).

Block-family multiplier degree

Statement. Over a field \(F\), let \(Q=\{0,1\}^n\), let \(\mathcal C_D\) be the degree-\(D\) part of the ideal of the Boolean axioms \(x_i^2-x_i\) (so a polynomial of degree at most \(D\) lies in \(\mathcal C_D\) exactly when it vanishes on \(Q\)), and let \(H\) be a family of nonempty blocks \(B\subseteq[n]\), with transversal number \(\tau(H)\), the least size of a set meeting every block, equal to \(n-\alpha(H)\) for \(\alpha(H)\) the largest size of a set containing no block. For each \(B\in H\) take the family \((x_i)_{i\in B}\) and an approximator \(P_B\in F[x_i:i\in B]\) of degree at most \(a\); call \(f\) of degree at most \(K\) a common multiplier when \(fP_Bx_i\in\mathcal C_D\) for all \(B\in H\), \(i\in B\), with \(K+a+1\le D\), and surviving when \(f\) is nonzero on \(Q\) (equivalently \(f\notin\mathcal C_D\): the class \(1\) is kept alive). (a) If each \(P_B\) is nonzero at some nonzero \(v_B\in\{0,1\}^B\), every surviving common multiplier has degree at least \(\tau(H)\). (b) Over \(\mathbb F_p\), with an ordering \(b_1,\ldots,b_{|B|}\) of each block, the product of Pang's factors \(P_B=\prod_{j<|B|}\bigl(1-(x_{b_j}-x_{b_{j+1}})^{p-1}\bigr)\), of degree \(a=(p-1)(\max|B|-1)\), is nonzero on \(Q\) exactly at the patterns \(0\) and \(1_B\), and when \(\tau(H)+a+1\le D\), \(\pi_T=\prod_{i\in T}(1-x_i)\) for a least transversal \(T\) is a surviving common multiplier of degree \(\tau(H)\). (c) Over \(\mathbb F_2\), every product \(P_B=\prod_{j=1}^s(1+q_j)\) of \(s\le|B|-1\) of Pang's factors, \(q_j\in\operatorname{span}\{x_i:i\in B\}\), satisfies the hypothesis of (a); with \(s\ge|B|\) factors \(q_j=x_{b_j}\) give \(P_B=[x_B=0]\), and \(f=1\) is a common multiplier of degree \(0\). (d) Over \(\mathbb F_2\), for \(H\) all \((t+1)\)-subsets of \([n]\), \(t+1\le n\), and \(t\) factors per block: every surviving common multiplier has degree at least \(n-t\), and when \(D\ge n+1\) the least degree over all choices is \(n-t\); Pang's criterion \(S(1-\eta)^t<1\) with these \(t\) factors, \(S=\binom n{t+1}\), \(d=1\) and \(\eta=\tfrac12N_n(K-1)/N_n(K)\), fails as an inequality at every \(1\le K\le n\) when \(\binom n{t+1}\ge2^t\), in particular for every \(n\ge2t+1\). (e) Over \(\mathbb F_2\), for \(H\) all pairs of \([n]\), \(n\ge4\), and one factor per pair, some choice forces every surviving common multiplier to be a multiple of \(\delta_0=\prod_i(1+x_i)\), of degree \(n\); and \(\delta_0\) is a surviving common multiplier for every approximator when \(K\ge n\) and \(n+a+1\le D\).

Proof. Since \(\deg(fP_Bx_i)\le K+a+1\le D\), the condition \(fP_Bx_i\in\mathcal C_D\) says that \(fP_Bx_i\) vanishes on \(Q\): \(f(x)P_B(x_B)=0\) at every \(x\in Q\) with \(x_B\ne0\). (a) At a point with \(x_B=v_B\ne0\), \(P_B(v_B)\ne0\), so \(f\) vanishes on the cylinder \(\{x:x_B=v_B\}\), whose coordinate set is \(B\). The cube is the product domain of lem:cylinder-killer-degree with factors \(\{0,1\}\), base state \(0\) and \(x_{j,1}=x_j\), whose degree is the multilinear degree; by its part (a), a nonzero function vanishing on the union of these cylinders has degree at least \(\tau(H)\). A polynomial of degree at most \(K\) represents a function of degree at most \(K\), so \(\deg f\ge\tau(H)\). (b) On \(Q\), \(x_{b_j}-x_{b_{j+1}}\in\{-1,0,1\}\), and its \((p-1)\)th power is \(1\) exactly when it is nonzero, so \(P_B=1\) exactly where \(x_B\) is constant and \(0\) elsewhere; hence \(P_Bx_i\) is, as a function on \(Q\), the indicator of \(x_B=1_B\). If \(\pi_T(x)\ne0\) then \(x_T=0\), and \(T\) meets \(B\), so \(x_B\ne1_B\): \(\pi_TP_Bx_i\) vanishes on \(Q\), its degree is at most \(\tau(H)+a+1\le D\), and it lies in \(\mathcal C_D\). \(\pi_T(0)=1\), so \(\pi_T\) survives; this is the basis element of lem:transversal-killer-basis (a) for the up-set generated by the blocks. (c) The forms \(q_1,\ldots,q_s\) on \(\mathbb F_2^B\) have a common kernel of dimension at least \(|B|-s\ge1\), which contains a nonzero \(v_B\), and \(P_B(v_B)=1\). With \(q_j=x_{b_j}\) for every \(j\le|B|\), \(P_B=1\) only at \(x_B=0\), where every \(x_i\), \(i\in B\), vanishes. (d) A set containing no \((t+1)\)-subset has at most \(t\) elements, so \(\tau(H)=n-t\); by (a) and (c), every choice of \(t=|B|-1\) factors forces degree at least \(n-t\), and over \(\mathbb F_2\) the chain of (b) has \(t\) factors and \(a=t\), so it attains \(n-t\) when \(n-t+t+1\le D\). For the criterion, \(N_n(K-1)\le N_n(K)\) gives \(\eta\le\tfrac12\), so \(S(1-\eta)^t\ge\binom n{t+1}2^{-t}\ge1\) when \(\binom n{t+1}\ge2^t\); for \(n\ge2t+1\), \(\binom n{t+1}\ge\binom{2t+1}{t+1}=\binom{2t+1}t\ge\binom{2t}t\ge2^t\). (e) Take \(q_{\{i,i+1\}}=x_{i+1}\) for \(i\in[n]\), indices modulo \(n\), so that \(f\) must vanish where \(x_i=1\) and \(x_{i+1}=0\); take \(q_{\{1,3\}}=x_1+x_3\), which forces vanishing where \(x_1=x_3=1\) (the pair \(\{1,3\}\) is not a cycle pair since \(n\ge4\)); give the other pairs any nonzero form. A nonzero point other than \(1_{[n]}\) has a cyclic step from a \(1\) to a \(0\), and \(1_{[n]}\) has \(x_1=x_3=1\); so \(f\) vanishes at every nonzero point and is a multiple of \(\delta_0\) on \(Q\), of degree \(n\) unless zero. Conversely \(\delta_0P_Bx_i\) vanishes on \(Q\) since \(\delta_0\) is supported at \(0\), where \(x_i=0\).

Hypotheses, each with its step. \(K+a+1\le D\) turns membership into vanishing on the cube, in the first step; one nonzero pattern at which \(P_B\) is nonzero, per block, forces the cylinder in (a), and this is its weakest form: without it, as for \(s\ge|B|\) factors in (c), the family imposes nothing; the Boolean axioms make the domain the cube, as lem:cylinder-killer-degree needs; nonempty blocks make the cylinders proper and \(\tau(H)\) finite; the field enters only in (c) to (e), where Pang's factors \(1-q^{p-1}\) with \(p>2\) need not be nonzero at a nonzero Boolean pattern (over \(\mathbb F_3\), \(q=x_1+x_2\) gives \(P_B=1\) only at \(x_B=0\), so one factor already kills a pair family), so (c) to (e) are stated over \(\mathbb F_2\), and (b) holds over every \(\mathbb F_p\); \(1\le K\le n\) and \(d=1\) are Pang's in (d). The conclusions hold for the protected class \(1\) in the cube's Boolean ideal, the domain model, and are not shown for any proper closure of an unsatisfiable system.

Degenerate cases. \(H\) empty: \(\tau=0\) and \(f=1\). A block of size \(1\): its only nonzero pattern is \(1\), and \(f\) must vanish where \(x_b=1\). A block whose approximator vanishes at every nonzero pattern imposes nothing and leaves (a) for the others. \(t+1=n\): one block, \(\tau=1\), and \(n-t=1\). \(n=3\) in (e): the cyclic pairs are all pairs and \(1_{[3]}\) is not forced, so (e) needs \(n\ge4\).

Nonvacuity. Over \(\mathbb F_2\), \(n=4\), \(H\) all pairs (\(t=1\), the families of lem:marginal-refinement-gain (d)), chain approximators \(1+x_a+x_b\), \(a=1\), \(K=3\), \(D=5\), so \(K+a+1=5\le D\): the multiplier \((1+x_1)(1+x_2)(1+x_3)\) has degree \(3=n-t\) and is nonzero at \(0\); by (a) no choice of one-factor approximators admits one of degree at most \(2\); by (e) the cyclic choice admits none below degree \(4\), and \(\delta_0\) has degree \(4\) with \(4+1+1=6>5\), so at \(D=5\) that choice admits no surviving multiplier at all; \(\binom42=6\ge2\), and the inequality of Pang's criterion fails at every \(K\), while his theorem's range \(\Delta+K+d\le D\) is \(K\le3\) there. No parameter ledger applies: the witness verifies no budget of the goal.

Baseline. The indicator of the origin \(\delta_0=\prod_i(1-x_i)\), of degree \(n\), kills every error for every approximator, since every error vanishes at \(0\), and survives; the lemma adds the matching lower bound \(\tau(H)\) for every admissible choice, the chain attaining it (a saving of \(t\) degrees on all \((t+1)\)-subsets), and, in (e), that a choice can lose that saving entirely.

Relations. (a) is lem:cylinder-killer-degree (a) applied to the cylinders forced by the approximators; (b) is the basis element of lem:transversal-killer-basis (a) after the approximators turn the errors into the monomials \(x_B\), and that lemma's last clause, the vertex-cover number for Pang's \(t=1\) pair families with \(q=x_a+x_b\), is the case of (b) with blocks of size \(2\). The elementary baseline is \(\delta_0\), of degree \(n\), which survives for every choice; what (a) and (b) add is that over \(\mathbb F_2\) with at most \(|B|-1\) factors per block no approximator choice goes below the transversal number, and the chain reaches it, a saving of \(t\) degrees on all \((t+1)\)-subsets, while (e) shows that a choice can also lose them all. It strengthens part (d) of lem:marginal-refinement-gain, which shows one round from \(P=1\) gaining nothing at \(K=1\) for the six pairs on four coordinates: by (a), no one-factor choice admits a multiplier below degree \(3\). The Sauer–Shelah threshold named in that entry, impossibility when \(\sum_{j\le t}\binom nj<2^{n-K}\), is weaker than (d)'s \(K<n-t\), since \(\sum_{j\le t}\binom nj\ge2^t\). lem:block-additive-degree concerns errors local to the blocks of a product domain; the forced cylinders here overlap, and it does not give (a). cor:monomial-code-approximation, read by statement, concerns the disjoint-block mixture model with codes chosen per block and \(K/v\) below \(\tfrac12\); its families are not the complete \((t+1)\)-uniform ones, and the two do not compare directly.

New mathematics. lem:block-family-multiplier-degree: on the cube, coordinate families on the blocks of a hypergraph, with approximators nonzero at a nonzero pattern of their block, admit no surviving common multiplier below the transversal number, and Pang's factors on chains of forms attain it over every prime field; over \(\mathbb F_2\) on all \((t+1)\)-subsets with \(t\) factors the degree over choices lies between \(n-t\) and \(n\), the upper end attained for pairs by a cyclic choice, while Pang's summed criterion with \(t\) factors certifies nothing at any \(K\) once \(\binom n{t+1}\ge2^t\); some choice with \(|B|\) factors gives degree \(0\).

Linearly certified module repairs are scalar

16 October 2026 · Working proof · scope: certificates semilinear over a ring map · Module and matrix repairs. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, low reasoning).

It came from the user's question whether repair can be abstracted from multiplication to maps with several inputs, multilinear in some of them, and their remark that the modules may carry relations among their generators; it bears on joint-error-savings, since a repair acting on a module might kill several errors where no single polynomial of the same degree does.

Best outcome. At the goal's own parameters, a repair by an element of a module, with survival still following from the old system's hardness, that kills Pang's errors below the least degree of any scalar repair of them; thm:certified-repair-composition and thm:finite-grid-repair construct one at Pang's \(K\), which it must beat.

General statement. lem:module-repair-factorization: a repair of the old proof system into any filtered module \(N\), free or with relations, is an element \(\nu\in N\) (modulo the module's closure); if its survival is certified by a map from \(N\) into a filtered commutative algebra \(S\), compatible with multiplication modulo the target closure up to a ring map \(\phi:R\to S\), then that map's value at \(\nu\) is an \(S\)-valued repair of the \(\phi\)-image system, a scalar repair of the old system when \(S=R\) and \(\phi\) is the identity; first-order differential certificates into the old closure, on systems whose differentiated variables carry Boolean axioms, yield scalar repairs on the window \(\deg(a_jm)\le D-K\); and every repair, scalar or module, implies that the protected class lies outside the closure of the axioms with the weighted errors added.

Module repair factorization

Statement. Over a field \(k\), let \(R=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\), \(V_d\) the polynomials of degree at most \(d\), and axioms \(a_1,\ldots,a_r\). Let \(N\) be an \(R\)-module, given by any generators and relations, with a filtration \(F_0N\subseteq F_1N\subseteq\cdots\), \(x_iF_jN\subseteq F_{j+1}N\), and \(J_N\subseteq F_DN\) a degree-\(D\) pseudo-submodule (closed under each \(x_i\) within \(F_DN\)). Let errors \(E_1,\ldots,E_s\), a protected \(w\) of degree at most \(b\), and \(\nu\in F_KN\) with \(b+K\le D\) and \(\deg(wE_i)+K\le D\). Call \(\nu\) a module repair when \(a_jm\nu\in J_N\) for every axiom and monomial \(m\) with \(\deg(a_jm)\le D-K\) (soundness), \(wE_i\nu\in J_N\) for all \(i\) (killing, as in thm:certified-repair-composition) and \(w\nu\notin J_N\) (survival). (a) A linear \(T:V_{D-K}\to F_DN\) with \(T(x_iq)-x_iT(q)\in J_N\) whenever \(\deg q<D-K\) satisfies \(T(q)-q\,T(1)\in J_N\) for all \(q\): compatible repairs, exactly or modulo \(J_N\), are multiplications by \(\nu=T(1)\) (exactly: lem:cyclic-repair-map). (b) Let \(S\) be a commutative \(k\)-algebra with a filtration by subspaces \(S_0\subseteq S_1\subseteq\cdots\) (for \(S=R[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)\), \(\varepsilon\) of degree \(0\)), \(\phi:R\to S\) a \(k\)-algebra map with \(\phi(x_i)\in S_T\), \(J'\subseteq S_{D'}\) a subspace closed under multiplication by each \(\phi(x_i)\) within \(S_{D'}\), and \(\beta:F_DN\to S_{D'}\) linear with \(\beta(F_jN)\subseteq S_{Tj+\sigma}\), \(TD+\sigma\le D'\), \(\beta(J_N)\subseteq J'\) and \(\beta(x_iu)-\phi(x_i)\beta(u)\in J'\) for \(u\in F_{D-1}N\). If \(\beta(w\nu)\notin J'\), then \(f=\beta(\nu)\in S_{TK+\sigma}\) is a repair of the image system: \(\phi(a_jm)f\in J'\), \(\phi(wE_i)f\in J'\), \(\phi(w)f\notin J'\). With \(S=R\), \(\phi\) the identity, \(T=1\) and \(J'\) the old closure at degree \(D+\sigma\), it is a scalar repair of the old system at parameter \(K+\sigma\). For \(N=R/I\), the maps of (b) with \(\phi\) the identity are given by their value \(f\) at \(1\), which must satisfy \(If\subseteq J'\) within degree. (c) If \(N=R^m\) with coordinate shifts \(\sigma_j\) and \(J_N=B^{-1}\bigl(\bigoplus_lJ_D\bigr)\cap F_DN\) for a matrix \(B\) whose rows have shift at most \(0\), every module repair yields a scalar repair \(f=(B\nu)_l\) at parameter \(K\); for a shifted direct sum, \(f=\nu_j\). (d) For a derivation \(\partial=\sum_kp_k\partial/\partial x_k\) and \(\phi_\partial:R\to R[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)\), \(g\mapsto g+\varepsilon\,\partial g\), the maps of (b) over \(\phi_\partial\) are the first-order differential certificates, \(\beta(gu)\equiv g\beta_0(u)+\varepsilon\bigl(g\beta_1(u)+\partial g\,\beta_0(u)\bigr)\). Take \(J'=J+\varepsilon J\) for the old closure \(J\subseteq V_{D'}\), containing the Boolean axioms \(a_k=x_k^2-x_k\) and closed under variables within degree \(D'\). If \(f=f_0+\varepsilon f_1\) is a repair of the image system as in (b), soundness reaches \(a_k\) itself, and \(\deg(p_k(2x_k-1)^2f_0)\le D'\), then \(f_0\) and \(f_1\) each satisfy soundness and killing as scalar repairs against \(J\), and one of them survives: a differential certificate into the old closure yields a scalar repair of degree at most \(\deg f\). (e) For every module repair, \(A=\{g\in V_{D-K}:g\nu\in J_N\}\) is a degree-\((D-K)\) pseudoideal containing every \(a_jm\) and every \(wE_im\) within degree \(D-K\), and not \(w\): \(w\) lies outside the degree-\((D-K)\) closure of the axioms with the weighted errors \(wE_i\) added, and some functional vanishing on that closure is nonzero at \(w\).

Proof. (a) By induction on \(\deg q\), for monomials: \(T(x_im)\equiv x_iT(m)\equiv x_i(m\,T(1)+j)\) with \(j\in J_N\), and \(x_ij\in J_N\) since \(\deg(x_imT(1))\le D\) places it in \(F_DN\) and \(J_N\) is closed there; linearity extends it. (b) The same induction with \(\phi\): \(\beta(x_im\nu)\equiv\phi(x_i)\beta(m\nu)\equiv\phi(x_i)(\phi(m)f+j')\) with \(j'\in J'\), and \(\phi(x_i)j'\in J'\) by the closure of \(J'\), its degree being at most \(T(D-K)+TK+\sigma\le D'\); so \(\beta(g\nu)-\phi(g)f\in J'\) for \(\deg g\le D-K\). Soundness and killing give \(a_jm\nu,\ wE_i\nu\in J_N\), so \(\beta\) carries them into \(J'\), and \(\phi(a_jm)f,\ \phi(wE_i)f\in J'\); \(\phi(w)f\equiv\beta(w\nu)\notin J'\). For \(N=R/I\), \(\beta(g\cdot1)\equiv gf\) and \(\beta(I\cdot1)=\beta(0)=0\), so \(If\subseteq J'\) within degree. (c) If \(w\nu\notin J_N\), then \(B(w\nu)\notin\bigoplus_lJ_D\), so some coordinate \(\beta=\pi_l\circ B\), \(R\)-linear of shift at most \(0\), has \(\beta(w\nu)\notin J_D\), and \(\beta(J_N)\subseteq J_D\) by the definition of \(J_N\); (b) applies with \(\phi\) the identity, \(\sigma\le0\), \(J'=J_D\). For the direct sum take \(B\) the identity. (d) \(\phi_\partial\) is a ring map because \(\partial\) is a derivation, and expanding \(\phi_\partial(g)(\beta_0+\varepsilon\beta_1)\) gives the displayed form. For \(g\in R\), \(\phi_\partial(g)f=gf_0+\varepsilon(gf_1+\partial g\,f_0)\), which lies in \(J+\varepsilon J\) exactly when \(gf_0\in J\) and \(gf_1+\partial g\,f_0\in J\). Soundness at \(a_k\) gives \(a_kf_1+p_k(2x_k-1)f_0\in J\); \(a_kf_1\in J\), as a multiple of an axiom within degree, so \(p_k(2x_k-1)f_0\in J\); multiplying by \(2x_k-1\) and using \((2x_k-1)^2=4a_k+1\) and \(4p_ka_kf_0\in J\) gives \(p_kf_0\in J\) (in characteristic \(2\), \(2x_k-1=1\) and this is immediate). Hence \(\partial g\,f_0=\sum_k\partial_kg\,(p_kf_0)\in J\) within degree, and the conditions become \(gf_0\in J\) and \(gf_1\in J\): each of \(f_0,f_1\) satisfies soundness (\(g=a_jm\)) and killing (\(g=wE_i\)); survival, \(\phi_\partial(w)f\notin J+\varepsilon J\), means \(wf_0\notin J\) or \(wf_1+\partial w\,f_0\notin J\), that is \(wf_0\notin J\) or \(wf_1\notin J\). (e) \(A\) is closed under each \(x_i\) within degree \(D-K\) because \(g\nu\in F_DN\) there and \(J_N\) is closed; soundness and killing put the \(a_jm\) and \(wE_i\) in it, so it contains their closure at degree \(D-K\), and \(w\notin A\) by survival; a functional separating \(w\) from \(A\) exists by finite dimension.

Hypotheses, each with its step. Compatibility of \(\beta\) modulo \(J'\), up to \(\phi\), is the whole of (b): it turns \(\beta(g\nu)\) into \(\phi(g)f\); the closure of \(J'\) under each \(\phi(x_i)\) carries the induction; the degree bounds \(T\), \(\sigma\) and \(TD+\sigma\le D'\) keep every product in \(S_{D'}\); \(\beta(J_N)\subseteq J'\) is what makes survival follow from the target system's hardness; the pseudo-submodule closure of \(J_N\) is used in (a) and (e); (d) uses the Boolean axioms \(a_k\) of every variable with \(p_k\ne0\), soundness reaching each \(a_k\) (\(D-K\ge2\)) and the degree room \(\deg(p_k(2x_k-1)^2f_0)\le D'\), which follows from the window when \(T(D-K)\ge T+2\) and binds only at its edge. The field is arbitrary. The conclusions hold for every protected class \(w\), the base class \(1\) included. For the old system's own hardness \(J'\) must be its closure at degree \(D'\); another \(J'\) gives a repair of another system. In (b) for \(N=R/I\), \(\beta\) is determined by \(f\) only modulo \(J'\), and on the image of \(V_D\) when \(F_DN\) is the induced filtration.

Degenerate cases. \(N=R\), \(\beta\) the identity: (b) is the scalar repair itself. \(\nu=0\), or \(J_N=F_DN\): no survival. No errors: (e) gives the old hardness at degree \(D-K\). A satisfiable domain model: a design of the extended system exists if some point is a common zero of the axioms and the errors with \(w\ne0\), by evaluation there. \(N=R/I\) with \(I\ni1\): \(N=0\), no survival.

Nonvacuity. Over \(\mathbb F_2\), \(n=1\), the Boolean axiom \(x^2+x\), \(D=2\), \(N=R^2\) with \(J_N=J_2\oplus J_2\), \(J_2=\operatorname{span}\{x^2+x\}\), error \(E=x\), \(w=1\), \(\nu=(1+x,0)\), \(K=1\): soundness asks \(a_jm\nu\in J_N\) for \(\deg(a_jm)\le1\), vacuous here since the axiom has degree \(2\); \(wE\nu=(x+x^2,0)\in J_N\); \(w\nu=(1+x,0)\notin J_N\); (c) with \(B\) the identity returns \(f=1+x\). This witness exercises neither soundness nor a non-diagonal \(B\); the general hypotheses are met. No parameter ledger applies: the witness verifies no budget of the goal.

New mathematics. lem:module-repair-factorization: repairs into any filtered module, free or with relations, are elements of it modulo its closure; a survival certificate into an algebra \(S\) compatible with multiplication up to a ring map turns a module repair into an \(S\)-valued repair of the image system, a scalar repair of no larger degree when \(S=R\), in particular on free modules with product or matrix-preimage closures; first-order differential certificates into the old closure, on systems whose differentiated variables carry Boolean axioms, yield scalar repairs on the window \(\deg(a_jm)\le D-K\); every repair implies the extended system's hardness at degree \(D-K\).

Statement. (b) If \(P\in GL_k(R)\) with \(\deg P,\deg P^{-1}\le p\) makes \(P\rho(x_i)P^{-1}=\operatorname{diag}(\phi_1(x_i),\ldots,\phi_k(x_i))\), and \(T(D-K)+\deg\nu+2p\le D'\), then some \(b\) gives a substitution repair \(\phi_b(a_jm)f,\ \phi_b(wE_i)f\in J\), \(\phi_b(w)f\notin J\) with \(f=(P\nu)_b\), of degree at most \(\deg\nu+p\). (c) For \(\rho(x_1)=\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}x_1&q\\0&0\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)\), \(q\in R\), and \(\rho(x_i)=x_iI\) for \(i\ge2\), \(\rho(g)=\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}g&q\,\Delta_1(g)\\0&\sigma(g)\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)\), with \(\Delta_1(g)=(g-g|_{x_1=0})/x_1\) and \(\sigma\) the substitution \(x_1\mapsto0\). (d) In (c), if \(x_1^2-x_1\) is an axiom, \(D-K\ge2\) and \(D-K+\deg q+\deg\nu_2\le D'\), then every repair yields either the substitution repair \(\nu_2\) with \(\sigma\) (when \(\sigma(w)\nu_2\notin J\)) or the scalar repair \(f_1=\nu_1+q\nu_2\), of degree at most \(\max(\deg\nu_1,\deg q+\deg\nu_2)\). (e) Over any field with \(n\ge2\), the Boolean axiom \(x_1^2-x_1\), \(\rho(x_1)=\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}0&x_2\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)\) (characteristic polynomial \(t^2-x_2\), whose eigenvalues lie outside \(R\), though not outside \(R/J\) when \(x_2\) is Boolean) and \(\rho(x_i)=x_iI\) for \(i\ge2\), with \(D-K\ge2\) and degree room \(D-K+\deg\nu+2\le D'\), every repair yields a substitution repair by \(x_1\mapsto1\) with multiplier \(x_2\nu_2\) or by \(x_1\mapsto x_2\) with multiplier \(\nu_2\). (f) Over any field, for any \(k\) and any \(\rho(x_1)\) commuting with \(\rho(x_i)=x_iI\), \(i\ge2\), with the Boolean axiom \(x_1^2-x_1\), \(D-K\ge2\) and room \(T(D-K)+T+\deg\nu\le D'\): with \(u_1=\rho(x_1)\nu\) and \(u_0=\nu-u_1\), \(\rho(g)\nu\equiv g|_{x_1=1}u_1+g|_{x_1=0}u_0\pmod{J^k}\) for \(g\) in the window, and every repair yields a substitution repair by \(x_1\mapsto1\) with a coordinate of \(u_1\) or by \(x_1\mapsto0\) with a coordinate of \(u_0\); (f) covers the settings of (d) and (e) at its own room, with repairs of its own form; (e)'s \(x_1\mapsto x_2\) form, which needs no Boolean \(x_2\), is a combination of (f)'s two forms when \(x_2\) is Boolean, since \(g|_{x_1=x_2}\equiv x_2\,g|_{x_1=1}+(1-x_2)\,g|_{x_1=0}\).

Proof. (a) As in the last part of lem:module-repair-factorization: \(\{g\in V_{D-K}:\rho(g)\nu\in J^k\}\) is closed under each \(x_i\) within degree, since \(\rho(x_ig)\nu=\rho(x_i)(\rho(g)\nu)\) and \(J^k\) is closed under \(\rho(x_i)\), of degree at most \(T(D-K)+\deg\nu\le D'\); it contains the axiom multiples and weighted errors, hence their closure; survival gives a coordinate \(l\) with \(\tau(w)\notin J\). (b) \(P\rho(g)P^{-1}=\operatorname{diag}(\phi_b(g))\), both sides being algebra maps agreeing on generators. For \(g\) with \(\rho(g)\nu\in J^k\), \(P\rho(g)\nu=\operatorname{diag}(\phi_b(g))P\nu\) has coordinates \(\phi_b(g)(P\nu)_b\) in \(J\), \(P\) carrying \(J^k\) into \(J^k\) within the degree room; and if every \(\phi_b(w)(P\nu)_b\) were in \(J\), then \(\rho(w)\nu=P^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\phi_b(w))P\nu\) would be in \(J^k\); so some \(b\) survives. (c) \(\rho(x_1)^j=\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}x_1^j&qx_1^{j-1}\\0&0\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)\) for \(j\ge1\), and \(\rho(x_i)\), \(i\ge2\), are scalar; for \(g=x_1^jg'\), \(g'\) free of \(x_1\), \(\rho(g)=g'\rho(x_1)^j\), whose entries are \(g\), \(qg/x_1=q\Delta_1(g)\), \(0\) and \(0\) for \(j\ge1\), and \(g'I\) for \(j=0\), where \(\Delta_1(g)=0\) and \(\sigma(g)=g\); linearity gives the formula. (d) The second coordinate of \(\rho(g)\nu\) is \(\sigma(g)\nu_2\), which lies in \(J\) for every axiom multiple and every \(wE_i\) by soundness and killing; if \(\sigma(w)\nu_2\notin J\), \(\nu_2\) with \(\sigma\) is a substitution repair. Otherwise: soundness at \(a=x_1^2-x_1\) gives \(a\nu_1+q(x_1-1)\nu_2\in J\), and \(a\nu_1\in J\), so with \(h=q\nu_2\), \((x_1-1)h\in J\) and \(h\equiv x_1h\); then \(q\Delta_1(g)\nu_2=\Delta_1(g)h\equiv\Delta_1(g)x_1h=(g-\sigma(g))h\), and \(\sigma(g)h=q\,\sigma(g)\nu_2\in J\) whenever \(\sigma(g)\nu_2\in J\), within the degree room; so the first coordinate \(g\nu_1+q\Delta_1(g)\nu_2\equiv g(\nu_1+h)\) modulo \(J\) for every axiom multiple, every \(wE_i\) and \(g=w\). Hence \(f_1=\nu_1+h\) kills and is sound, and \(wf_1\equiv e_1^{\mathsf T}\rho(w)\nu\); survival, with \(\sigma(w)\nu_2\in J\), puts the first coordinate outside \(J\). Equivalently, the involution \(Q=\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}1&q\\0&-1\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)\) gives \(Q\rho(x_1)Q=\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}x_1&(x_1-1)q\\0&0\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)\), diagonal modulo the relation soundness supplies. (e) Identify \((u_0,u_1)\) with \(u_0+u_1y\) in \(S=R[y]/(y^2-x_2)\): \(\rho(x_1)(u_0,u_1)=(x_2u_1,u_0)\) is multiplication by \(y\), and \(J^2\) becomes \(J\oplus Jy\); write \(f=\nu_1+\nu_2y\). Soundness at \(x_1^2-x_1\), whose image is \(y^2-y=x_2-y\), gives \((x_2-y)f=x_2(\nu_1-\nu_2)+(x_2\nu_2-\nu_1)y\in J\oplus Jy\), so \(\nu_1\equiv x_2\nu_2\). For \(g=g_0+x_1g_1\) with \(g_0,g_1\) free of \(x_1\) (every \(g\) is so modulo multiples of \(x_1^2-x_1\), a reduction that does not raise degree, on which \(\rho(\cdot)\nu\) lies in \(J^2\) by soundness), \(\rho(g)\nu\) is \((g_0+g_1y)(\nu_1+\nu_2y)=(g_0\nu_1+x_2g_1\nu_2)+(g_0\nu_2+g_1\nu_1)y\equiv x_2\nu_2\,g|_{x_1=1}+\nu_2\,g|_{x_1=x_2}\,y\), using \(\nu_1\equiv x_2\nu_2\) by closure within the degree room. Both components lie in \(J\) for every axiom multiple and weighted error, and survival puts one component of \(\rho(w)\nu\) outside \(J\): a substitution repair by \(x_1\mapsto1\) with \(x_2\nu_2\), or by \(x_1\mapsto x_2\) with \(\nu_2\). (f) Soundness at \(a=x_1^2-x_1\) gives \(\rho(a)\nu=\rho(x_1)u_1-u_1\in J^k\), so \(\rho(x_1)u_1\equiv u_1\) and \(\rho(x_1)u_0=u_1-\rho(x_1)u_1\equiv0\). For \(g=g_0+x_1g_1\), \(g_0,g_1\) free of \(x_1\) (every \(g\) modulo multiples of \(a\), without raising degree), \(\rho(g)=g_0I+g_1\rho(x_1)\), so \(\rho(g)\nu=g_0(u_0+u_1)+g_1u_1=g|_{x_1=0}u_0+g|_{x_1=1}u_1\). If \(\rho(g)\nu\in J^k\), then \(\rho(x_1)\rho(g)\nu=\rho(x_1g)\nu\in J^k\) by closure within the room; write \(x_1g=x_1\,g|_{x_1=1}+a\,c'\) with \(\deg c'\le\deg g-1\); \(\rho(x_1g|_{x_1=1})\nu=g|_{x_1=1}u_1\) exactly, and \(\rho(ac')\nu=\rho(c')\rho(a)\nu\in J^k\), built from \(\rho(a)\nu\in J^k\) by applying the \(\rho(x_i)\) one monomial factor at a time, each intermediate of degree at most \(T(D-K+1)+\deg\nu\le D'\); so \(g|_{x_1=1}u_1\in J^k\), and then \(g|_{x_1=0}u_0\in J^k\). So every coordinate of \(u_1\) is sound and kills with \(x_1\mapsto1\), and every coordinate of \(u_0\) with \(x_1\mapsto0\); \(\rho(w)\nu\notin J^k\) puts \(w|_{x_1=1}u_1\) or \(w|_{x_1=0}u_0\) outside \(J^k\), giving a coordinate that survives.

Hypotheses, each with its step. Commuting \(\rho(x_i)\) make \(\rho\) an algebra map and \(M_\rho\) a module; closure of \(J\) under polynomial multiples within degree gives the closure of \(J^k\) under \(\rho(x_i)\) in (a), the passage through \(P\) in (b), with the room \(2p\), and the multiplications by \(q\) and \(\Delta_1(g)\) in (d); (c) is a computation of \(\rho(g)\) from the generators' matrices and uses only their commuting; \(\deg(wE_i)\le D-K\) places the weighted errors in (a)'s window; the Boolean axiom \(x_1^2-x_1\) with \(D-K\ge2\) gives \(h\equiv x_1h\) in (d), \(\nu_1\equiv x_2\nu_2\) in (e) and the idempotence of \(\rho(x_1)\) on \(u_0,u_1\) in (f); the rooms \(D-K+\deg\nu+2\le D'\) in (e) and \(T(D-K)+T+\deg\nu\le D'\) in (f) keep the reductions and the application of \(\rho(x_1)\) inside \(V_{D'}\). The field is arbitrary. The conclusions hold for every protected class \(w\).

Native certificate lower bound on the cube

16 October 2026 · Working proof · Pang-type families over \(\mathbb F_2\) on the cube · Native functional growth. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, low reasoning).

General statement. lem:native-functional-growth: on the cube over \(\mathbb F_2\), for a Pang family of \(s\) linear inputs with a \(t\)-factor approximator \(\prod_k(1+q_k)\) and an input outside the span of the \(q_k\), every set of old functionals whose rectangle forms of slack \(L\) detect the family's stacked kernel on \(V_K\) has at least \(N_{n-t-1}(K)/(s\,N_n(L))\) members, which for fixed \(s\), \(t\) and \(K\) grows like \(n^{K-L}\); applied at the largest admissible slack, it grows with \(n\) exactly when \(K\) exceeds that slack (and \(s\) grows more slowly than \(n^{K-L}\)).

Native functional growth

Statement. Over \(\mathbb F_2\), let \(J_{D'}\) be the degree-\(D'\) part of the Boolean ideal in \(n\) variables, a family of linear forms \(g_1,\ldots,g_s\) with approximator \(P=\prod_{k=1}^t(1+q_k)\), \(q_k\in\operatorname{span}\{g_i\}\) (kept to match the family's form; the proof works for any linear \(q_k\)), errors \(E_i=Pg_i\) (the form of Pang's approximators and errors, as the marginal-refinement entry read them from his Section 4 and lem:marginal-refinement-gain states them), \(U=V_K\), and slack \(L\) with \(t+1+K+L\le D'\). If \(g_1\notin\operatorname{span}\{q_1,\ldots,q_t\}\), then the stacked rank \(r\) of \(u\mapsto([E_iu])_i\) is at least \(N_{n-t-1}(K)\), and every \(m\) old functionals whose rectangle forms \(\mu_j(E_iuv)\), \(v\in V_L\), detect the stacked kernel satisfy \(m\ge N_{n-t-1}(K)/(s\,N_n(L))\). Since detection at slack \(L\) implies it at every larger admissible slack, the bound is to be read at the largest admissible \(L\); for \(d=1\) at the least degree Pang's simulation allows, \(D=K+\max(2t+2,\,t+w)\), \(\Delta=t\), that is \(L_{\max}=\max(t+1,\,w-1)\) (a larger \(D\) raises it), and for fixed \(s\), \(t\), \(K\) the bound grows with \(n\) exactly when \(K>L_{\max}\).

Proof. On the cube \(E_1\) is the indicator of \(A=\{q_1=\cdots=q_t=0,\ g_1=1\}\), nonempty and affine of dimension at least \(n-t-1\) because \(g_1\) lies outside the span of the \(q_k\). Within degree, membership in \(J_{D'}\) is vanishing on the cube, so \(E_1u\in J\) exactly when \(u\) vanishes on \(A\), and the rank of \(u\mapsto[E_1u]\) on \(V_K\) is the dimension of the restrictions of \(V_K\) to \(A\). An affine change of coordinates of \(\mathbb F_2^n\) making \(A\) a coordinate subcube preserves degree, and restriction of degree-\(\le K\) polynomials to a subcube of dimension \(a\ge n-t-1\) gives all its functions of degree at most \(K\), of dimension \(N_a(K)\ge N_{n-t-1}(K)\). The stacked rank is at least this one error's rank. By lem:native-detection-count (a), detection by \(m\) functionals at slack \(L\) forces \(r\le m\dim Z_L\le m\,s\,N_n(L)\). If detection holds at slack \(L\), it holds at every admissible \(L'\ge L\): \(V_L\subseteq V_{L'}\) gives \(\ker\Phi_{L'}\subseteq\ker\Phi_L\), and \(C\subseteq\ker\Phi_{L'}\) by lem:native-detection-count (a). For \(d=1\), \(\Delta=t\) and \(L=D-\Delta-d-K\) at \(D=K+\max(2t+2,t+w)\) give \(L_{\max}=\max(t+1,w-1)\); the ratio \(N_{n-t-1}(K)/N_n(L)\) grows like \(n^{K-L}\).

Hypotheses, each with its step. The cube domain model is used for membership as vanishing and for the rank as a restriction count; \(\mathbb F_2\) and linear inputs are used in the one step that makes the support of \(E_1\) an affine subspace, the factor \(1+q_k\) being Pang's \(1-q_k^{p-1}\) at \(p=2\); \(g_1\) outside the span of the \(q_k\) makes \(A\) nonempty of dimension at least \(n-t-1\); \(t+1+K+L\le D'\) is lem:native-detection-count's window for errors of degree \(t+1\). Over any field with the Boolean axioms in \(J\), \(r\ge\dim V_K|_{\operatorname{supp}E_1}\) still holds; only the affine count needs \(\mathbb F_2\). The conclusion concerns detection of the stacked kernel, with no protected class.

Degenerate cases. Every input in the span of the \(q_k\): then \(Pg_i=0\) on the cube and \(r=0\). \(t=0\): \(A=\{g_1=1\}\), of dimension \(n-1\). \(s=1\): \(m\ge N_{n-t-1}(K)/N_n(L)\). \(K\le L\): the bound is at most about \(1/s\) and excludes nothing; at \(p=2\), \(d=1\), thm:common-moment-radical's reserve is \(K\le\Delta+d=t+1\le L_{\max}\), which \(K\le L\) alone does not give.

Nonvacuity. \(t=1\), \(s=2\), \(g_1=x_1\), \(g_2=x_2\), \(q_1=x_2\), \(K=3\), \(L=2\), \(D'=7\) (\(2+3+2\le7\), Pang's tight degree for \(w\le3\)): at \(n=8\), \(N_6(3)=42\), \(N_8(2)=37\), so \(m\ge42/74\), that is \(m\ge1\), which any nonzero \(r\) gives; the bound bites from about \(n=30\) at \(s=2\): at \(n=40\), \(N_{38}(3)=9178\), \(N_{40}(2)=821\), \(m\ge6\); at \(n=100\), \(m\ge16\) (both at \(s=2\), computed for this entry from the binomial sums). No parameter ledger applies: the witness verifies no budget of the goal.

Joint-savings goal review: domination read as mechanism; twisted splits lose a window degree at tight room

16 October 2026 · Route review; no claim registered; the Attempt's twist-window trade is a sketch for the next entry · Joint-savings goal review. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, low reasoning).

Question. Twelve research entries on effective-selection since the goal review of 16 October (factor-domination review) and one review on it (transversal review) left joint-error-savings unchanged, all with no bearing at the goal's own parameters (the article tags of the record). The open-item count has not dropped, so this review is goal-level. It settles the domination clause that principal joint kernels left to it, assesses the user-picked matrix generalization after its first two entries, and asks whether the next cycles stay on this statement.

General statement. The line's general claim is that the joint action of actual errors can be bounded below the sum of their ranks by their structure, in the protected quotient, with a gain in a sufficient multiplier budget or admissible range. Since the last goal review the line added lem:top-degree-axiom-inertness, check:functional-factor-kernels, lem:factor-span-domination, lem:fi-system-windows, cor:hole-occupancy-kernels, cor:generic-principal-kernel, lem:marginal-refinement-gain, lem:native-detection-count, lem:block-family-multiplier-degree, lem:module-repair-factorization, lem:twisted-certificate-reduction and lem:native-functional-growth. This review registers no claim; its Attempt below gives the argument the next entry registers.

Obstacle

Every certificate the line has found reduces to one of the three excluded kinds, and each new representation tried since the last goal review lands in one of them. Common kernels in the functional pigeonhole system at \(K=1\) and \(K=2\), at \(D=3\) over \(\mathbb F_2\) on two boards, are the sum of the frame's kernel and the relations (check:functional-factor-kernels, check:functional-kernels-k2); transported killers are spans of products of factor killers (lem:factor-span-domination); in the reserve window and in domain models every joint kernel is one generic combination's annihilator (cor:generic-principal-kernel); module repairs certified linearly are scalar (lem:module-repair-factorization); twists of one Boolean variable split into substitution repairs when the room is \(T(D-K)+T+\deg\nu\le D'\) and \(D-K\ge2\) (lem:twisted-certificate-reduction); and native rectangle certificates of Pang-type families with linear inputs over \(\mathbb F_2\) on the cube, at fixed \(s\), \(t\), \(K\), need a number of functionals growing with \(n\) beyond the largest slack (lem:native-functional-growth). What the line is stuck on is unchanged: a joint saving of none of the excluded kinds. What is new is that the user's generalization from multiplication to compatible maps on modules, the one structural change of setting tried, has so far reproduced the two mechanisms already known: scalar multipliers (Pang) and, through substitutions, restrictions (Braun).

Falsification attempt. The review tried to falsify the claim that repairs on free modules twisted by commuting matrices, with Boolean twisted variables, add nothing beyond restrictions and multipliers, by the twist of several variables at the room for fewer splits that the twisted-module entry named. The Attempt below gives restriction repairs from every such repair, but only at a smaller window, a weaker object; whether the window loss is real is the decisive test, so the claim is neither falsified nor established.

  • geometric-repair-application: resolved as a working proof; no change, no cycle spent.
  • joint-error-savings: unchanged; twelve research entries and one review since the last goal review (Obstacle).

Architecture review

Necessary target. For joint-error-savings: on a nontrivial unbounded family of actual errors, an all-parameter bound on their stacked rank in one protected quotient, strictly below the summed count, from hypotheses checkable on the errors and the system, giving a better sufficient multiplier budget or admissible range after costs; at Pang's parameters, an effective count \(c<S\) in \(S(1-\eta)^t\) that survives the adaptive choices. Downstream. Through lem:exact-common-kernel-selection any such certificate feeds thm:certified-repair-composition; through cor:pang-observation-calibration an effective count \(1<c<S\) cuts \(t\), and the degree \(\Delta=(p-1)dt\), by about the factor \(\ln S/\ln c\), up to rounding of \(t\); through lem:module-repair-factorization a module repair implies the extended hardness at \(D-K\), so a matrix repair cheaper than every scalar one would feed the same composition. Weaker than the goal's general theorem, and the explicit consequence this statement asks for.

Extra requirements. Two demands go beyond what repair needs. First, a rank saving: lem:exact-common-kernel-selection shows that repair needs only the exact criterion, a protected class surviving on the common kernel, which can hold when no saving does. The user's goal names savings beyond summed ranks, so the statement keeps the saving and the review records that the exact criterion is the weaker sufficient endpoint. Second, the domination clause, “the common kernel being the annihilator of one element of the window”, which principal joint kernels left open. The readings its words allow are these (the reviewer's stage-one list, checked here against cor:generic-principal-kernel and lem:factor-ideal-domination): - Field: an element over the base field, or one over an extension. Over an extension, every reserve-window family and every domain-model family is excluded (cor:generic-principal-kernel (a), (c)). Only proper closures without the reserve stay admissible, so the endpoint becomes narrow and turns on an artefact of the method. - Degree of the element: at most \(e\), at most \(\sigma\) with \(K+\sigma+e\le D\), at most \(D-K\), or at most \(b\); the window of degree at most \(D-K\) contains the others, which are not otherwise ordered (\(b\le D-K\) since \(b+K\le D\)). Its example (d) is principal over \(\mathbb F_2\) at degree \(2=D-K\) and not at degree \(1\). - Equality against containment: under containment the clause becomes a common-killer condition, which overlaps the exclusion of products of killers. - Property against mechanism. As a property, the clause excludes every family whose kernel happens to be principal. As a mechanism, it excludes a saving whose proof only exhibits the common kernel as one element's annihilator and then bounds that element's rank by its own single count. The review adopts the mechanism reading, over any field, with equality. Under it the endpoint stays attainable and nontrivial in the reserve window of proper closures (domain models stay excluded by the support clause, every domain-model saving being a union-of-supports count by lem:domain-model-stacked-rank), and it excludes what “merely representing the same kernel” already aims at. A bound on one generic combination's rank counts only when it comes from the errors' joint structure and is neither a support count nor a product of killers. This keeps open the head item's next attempt on the linearity of Pang's choice. What can be weakened is the requirement that the saving hold on arbitrary families: a saving on the actual error families of one application is enough.

Independent alternative. In its first stage the medium reviewer (review record) received the goal's open statements and the line's registered results only, with its one open conjecture (conj:functional-kernel-transfer, evidence at \(D=3\), \(K\le2\) on two boards). It proposed a product-overlap (Koszul) bound. With \(W_i\) the image of the dual of \(T_i:u\mapsto[E_iu]\) and \(K+e_i+e_j\le D\), \(\operatorname{im}T^*_{E_iE_j}\subseteq W_i\cap W_j\), by pseudoideal closure, so the saving \(\sum_i\operatorname{rank}T_i-\operatorname{rank}(T_i)_i=\sum_i\dim(W_i\cap\sum_{j<i}W_j)\) is at least \(\sum_i\operatorname{rank}((T_{E_iE_j})_{j<i})\). For \(B\supseteq C\), a domain model, the ranks over \(C\) dominate those over \(B\), so support intersections give lower bounds on the saving that hold in the proper quotient itself. The author checked both inclusions. The bound is the full form of the chain the last goal review recorded from its own first stage, “the joint rank is at most \(\sum_jr_j-\sum_{j\ge2}\operatorname{rank}_C(E_jE_{b(j)})\) for any parents \(b(j)<j\)”. Its new part is the transfer as a lower bound, which ex:support-saving-not-inherited does not contradict, since that correction concerns the full union count. Compared with the route, the bound gives \(0\) exactly where products lie in \(C\), the families lem:factor-ideal-domination covers. Its certificate is still a support-intersection count. The last review recorded its own reviewer's unverified claim that near Pang's threshold, with nearly independent supports, the product ranks are second order; that claim is an untested hypothesis, since \(\dim V_K|_{S_i\cap S_j}\) is an interpolation dimension, not a set density. So it gives saving lower bounds that survive the proper quotient, where ex:support-saving-not-inherited showed the full count does not, and it is not yet shown to be a mechanism for an effective count \(c\ll S\). It is listed below as a suggestion rather than adopted.

Rank normalization. Ranks of scalar certificates are measured in \(V_K/(C\cap V_K)\). A twisted repair's kernel lives in \(R^k/J^k\) with the twisted action, a different quotient; the comparison with scalar and restriction repairs is made through the split of the Attempt, which maps it to repairs measured in \(J\) itself, so losses and survivors are compared there. Relative contraction is the form Pang's recurrence uses, and an effective count is a relative statement of the same kind.

Decision. Core: joint-error-savings stays the worked statement, and so does the user's order: the user-picked matrix-multiplier-repair keeps its spell, two of four entries spent. The next entry is lemma-first: it registers the twist-window trade of the Attempt, then runs the decisive test, re-posed at tight room after the first draft's instance was found decided by its own Trivial cases. The domination clause takes the mechanism reading, which this review writes into the open statement. The product-overlap bound waits as a suggestion, for the review after the matrix item's spell, which can promote it beside the head item's test of the linearity of Pang's choice.

Decisive test. Trivial cases. With no twisted variable a repair is scalar. A vector \(\nu\) with one nonzero split component \(u_\sigma\) is already a substitution repair. Duplicating a coordinate of \(\nu\), or conjugating \(\rho\) by a constant invertible matrix, changes no split. When the room pays every split, lem:twisted-certificate-reduction (f), applied variable by variable as its follow-up review showed, gives substitution repairs at the full window. This decides the first draft's instance: \(\deg\nu=0\), \(T=1\) and \(D-K=2\) give room \(T(D-K)+T+\deg\nu=3\le D'=3\), as the reviewer found. Power. The Attempt bounds every twisted repair on Boolean twisted variables: it gives substitution repairs at window \(D-K-(t-s)\) when the room pays \(s\) of \(t\) splits, with multipliers of degree at most \(\deg\nu+tT\). The test therefore asks whether the \(t-s\) window degrees can be gained. The smallest instance where they can be is \(t=1\), \(s=0\), at room exactly \(T(D-K)+\deg\nu=D'\). There only the top-degree conditions, \(\deg g=D-K\), can fail to separate, and the reviewer's lift places the split pieces in \(J_{D'+T}\) instead, where survival can be lost.

The instance lies outside the goal's parameter window. Its outcome bears on whether module repairs can ever beat substitution-times-multiplier repairs, which decides whether the user-picked item has an application to joint-error-savings. Attempt. Take commuting \(\rho\) of entry degree at most \(T\), Boolean axioms \(x_i^2-x_i\) on \(x_1,\dots,x_t\), \(D-K\ge2\) and room \(T(D-K)+\deg\nu\le D'\). Put \(u_0=\nu-\rho(x_1)\nu\) and \(u_1=\rho(x_1)\nu\).
  • The identity. For \(g=g_0+x_1g_1\) with \(g_0,g_1\) free of \(x_1\), \(\rho(g)\nu=\rho(g_0)(u_0+u_1)+\rho(g_1)u_1=\rho(g|_{x_1=0})u_0+\rho(g|_{x_1=1})u_1\) exactly, since \(\rho\) is an algebra map. Every \(g\) has this form modulo axiom multiples of no higher degree, which soundness sends into \(J^k\).
  • Separation below the top degree. If \(\deg g\le D-K-1\) and \(\rho(g)\nu\in J^k\), then \(\rho(x_1)\rho(g)\nu\in J^k\), since its degree is at most \(T(D-K)+\deg\nu\le D'\). Since \(x_1g=x_1g|_{x_1=1}+(x_1^2-x_1)g_1\) with \(\deg((x_1^2-x_1)g_1)\le D-K\), soundness gives \(\rho(g|_{x_1=1})u_1\in J^k\), and then \(\rho(g|_{x_1=0})u_0\in J^k\).
  • Survival splits as \(\rho(w)\nu=\rho(w|_{x_1=0})u_0+\rho(w|_{x_1=1})u_1\).
  • The split. Each coordinate of \(u_\varepsilon\) gives a substitution repair in the sense of lem:twisted-certificate-reduction (b): a multiplier \(f\), possibly involving \(x_1\), with \(\phi(g)f\in J\) for the substitution \(\phi\colon x_1\mapsto\varepsilon\) and \(J\) the original closure. It is not a repair of the restricted system in its own closure. Its window is \(D-K-1\): soundness, and killing of weighted errors with \(\deg(wE_i)\le D-K-1\); the top-degree errors are dropped. Its vector has degree at most \(\deg\nu+T\), and the room \(T(D-K-1)+\deg\nu+T=T(D-K)+\deg\nu\) is unchanged.
  • Induction. \(t\) twisted Boolean variables give substitution repairs on \(x_1,\dots,x_t\) at window \(D-K-t\) with no extra room, and at window \(D-K-(t-s)\) with \(sT\) of extra room.
It may correspond to the case split of lem:branching-tree-degree, whose registered statement uses an asymmetric case split in which the smaller side pays one degree; the correspondence is not checked. The Attempt stops at the top degree: whether \(\rho(g|_{x_1=1})u_1\in J^k\) for \(\deg g=D-K\) at tight room. The split is a few-line answer to the item's named next attempt, so it is the next entry's lemma, and the test is posed past it. Test disposition. New operation. Operation. The ring is \(\mathbb F_2[x]\) with the Boolean axioms among the axioms and soundness modulo \(J\), as in lem:twisted-certificate-reduction, the closure \(J_3\) computed by tools/pc_closure.py on the multilinear representatives.
