Twisted repairs split into substitution repairs

16 October 2026 · Working proof · architecture test decided on a degenerate instance · Twist-window trade. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, low reasoning).

Picked. The user: “On next cycles, prioritize that modules + matrices idea at least for some time (give it the usual 4 cycles + extensions if deserved treatment)”. This is the item's third entry.

Earlier entries. The item's entries are the module-repair entry, whose certificates semilinear over a ring map give scalar repairs, and the twisted-module entry, whose follow-up named “many twisted Boolean variables at room for fewer splits than variables”; the goal review turned that attempt into this entry's lemma and posed its decisive test.

Best outcome. At the goal's own parameters, a module repair that kills Pang's errors with a protected class at a degree below every scalar and substitution repair, which would lower the multiplier budget of thm:certified-repair-composition beyond what lem:module-repair-factorization's scalar repairs reach; failing that, the exact cost at which twisted repairs reduce to substitutions times multipliers.

General statement. lem:twist-window-trade: with the variables beyond \(x_1,\dots,x_t\) untwisted, a twisted repair on Boolean twisted variables splits into substitution repairs of \(x_1,\dots,x_t\), losing for each split the room does not pay one window degree: soundness and killing above the reduced window are dropped. Twisted variables that the closure defines linearly in untwisted ones cost nothing, with no Boolean axiom: the repair is scalar on the window. In a domain model the split keeps the full window, measured in the degree-\((D'+T)\) part of the same vanishing ideal.

Twist-window trade

Statement. Over a field, let \(R=k[x]\), \(J\) the degree-\(D'\) closure of axioms \(a_j\), and \(\rho:R\to\operatorname{Mat}_k(R)\) given by commuting \(\rho(x_i)\) of entry degree at most \(T\ge1\). Call \(\nu\in R^k\) a twisted repair at window \(D-K\) with room \(R_0\) when:

  • soundness: \(\rho(a_jm)\nu\in J^k\) for \(\deg(a_jm)\le D-K\);
  • killing: \(\rho(wE_i)\nu\in J^k\) for the errors with \(\deg(wE_i)\le D-K\);
  • survival: \(\rho(w)\nu\notin J^k\);
  • room: \(T(D-K)+\deg\nu\le R_0\le D'\).
Put \(u_0=\nu-\rho(x_1)\nu\) and \(u_1=\rho(x_1)\nu\). (a) Let \(x_1,\dots,x_t\) carry Boolean axioms \(x_i^2-x_i\), and let \(\rho(x_i)=x_iI\) for \(i>t\).
  • For \(g\) of degree at most \(D-K-1\), \(\rho(g)\nu\in J^k\) implies \(\rho(g|_{x_1=0})u_0\in J^k\) and \(\rho(g|_{x_1=1})u_1\in J^k\).
  • For \(w\) multilinear in \(x_1\), \(\rho(w)\nu=\rho(w|_{x_1=0})u_0+\rho(w|_{x_1=1})u_1\). For other \(w\) this holds modulo \(J^k\), when soundness reaches \(\deg w\).
  • So one of the vectors \(u_\varepsilon\) is a twisted repair of the substituted map \(g\mapsto\rho(g|_{x_1=\varepsilon})u_\varepsilon\), measured in \(J\). Its window is \(D-K-1\): soundness and killing of degree \(D-K\) are dropped. Its vector degree is at most \(\deg\nu+T\), and the room is unchanged.
  • After all \(t\) splits the action is scalar, and some coordinate of some \(u_\sigma\), \(\sigma\in\{0,1\}^t\), is a substitution repair of \(x_1,\dots,x_t\mapsto\sigma\), at window \(D-K-t\).
  • With room \(R_0\ge T(D-K)+sT+\deg\nu\), the first \(s\) splits keep the window and the result has window \(D-K-(t-s)\).
  • The conclusion has content only when \(D-K>t-s\).
(b) Let \(x_1,\dots,x_s\) be twisted and \(\rho(x_i)=x_iI\) for \(i>s\). Let each \(x_i-\ell_i\), \(i\le s\), be an axiom, with \(\ell_i\) of degree at most \(1\) in the untwisted variables, and \(D-K+\deg\nu\le D'\). Then \(\rho(g)\nu\equiv g\nu\pmod{J^k}\) for every \(g\) of degree at most \(D-K\): the twisted repair is the scalar repair with the coordinates of \(\nu\) as multipliers, at the full window. No Boolean axiom is needed, and (b) uses neither the entry bound \(T\) nor the room of the definition. (c) Let \(J\) be the space of polynomials of degree at most \(D'\) vanishing on a finite set \(X\) (a domain model), let \(x_1^2-x_1\) be an axiom, and let \(D-K\ge2\). For every \(g\) of degree at most \(D-K\) with \(\rho(g)\nu\) vanishing on \(X\), both \(\rho(g|_{x_1=\varepsilon})u_\varepsilon\) vanish on \(X\), with degree at most \(T(D-K)+T+\deg\nu\le D'+T\). So the split keeps the full window, measured in the degree-\((D'+T)\) part of the same vanishing ideal. Survival is unchanged, since a polynomial not vanishing on \(X\) lies in no degree part.

Proof. The identity: for \(g=g_0+x_1g_1\) with \(g_0,g_1\) free of \(x_1\), \(\rho(g)\nu=\rho(g_0)u_0+\rho(g_0+g_1)u_1=\rho(g|_{x_1=0})u_0+\rho(g|_{x_1=1})u_1\), since \(\rho\) is an algebra map. A \(g\) of degree at most \(D-K\) has this form modulo multiples of \(x_1^2-x_1\) of no higher degree, which soundness sends into \(J^k\). (a)

  • Separation. If \(\deg g\le D-K-1\) and \(\rho(g)\nu\in J^k\), its entries have degree at most \(T(D-K-1)+\deg\nu\). Multiplying by the entries of \(\rho(x_1)\) stays in \(J\) within \(T(D-K)+\deg\nu\le D'\), so \(\rho(x_1g)\nu\in J^k\). Since \(x_1g=x_1g|_{x_1=1}+(x_1^2-x_1)g_1\) with \(\deg((x_1^2-x_1)g_1)\le D-K\), soundness gives \(\rho(g|_{x_1=1})u_1\in J^k\), and the identity gives \(\rho(g|_{x_1=0})u_0\in J^k\).
  • The new repair. Applied to axiom multiples and weighted errors of degree at most \(D-K-1\), this is soundness and killing of the substituted maps. The identity at \(w\) splits survival, so one of the two survives.
  • Room. The new vectors have degree at most \(\deg\nu+T\), and \(T(D-K-1)+\deg\nu+T=T(D-K)+\deg\nu\), so the next split, on \(x_2\) acting on \(u_\varepsilon\) by commuting, has the same room.
  • Paid splits. With room \(T(D-K)+sT+\deg\nu\), the first \(s\) splits are made at the full window by lem:twisted-certificate-reduction (f)'s argument. That argument holds with the other variables still twisted, since \(\rho(x_1^2-x_1)\rho(g_1)\nu=\rho(g_1)\rho(x_1^2-x_1)\nu\) by commuting, at degree at most \(T(D-K+1)+\deg\nu\). The \(i\)-th paid split needs \(iT\le sT\) of extra room. The unpaid ones follow by the separation step.
  • The last split. Once every twisted variable is substituted, \(\rho\) acts by scalars, and the coordinates separate.
(b) Substituting \(x_1\mapsto\ell_1\), then \(x_2\mapsto\ell_2\), and so on, writes \(g=\bar g+\sum_{i\le s}(x_i-\ell_i)h_i\), where \(\bar g\) is \(g\) after all \(s\) substitutions and \(\deg h_i\le\deg g-1\). No step raises degree, since \(\deg\ell_i\le1\). Each \((x_i-\ell_i)h_i\) is an axiom multiple of degree at most \(D-K\), so soundness gives \(\rho((x_i-\ell_i)h_i)\nu\in J^k\). Then \(\rho(g)\nu\equiv\rho(\bar g)\nu=\bar g\,\nu\), since \(\bar g\) involves only untwisted variables. Finally \(g\nu-\bar g\nu=\sum_i(x_i-\ell_i)h_i\nu\) is a sum of axiom multiples of degree at most \(D-K+\deg\nu\le D'\), so it lies in \(J^k\). (c) At a point \(p\in X\):
  • \((\rho(x_1g)\nu)(p)=\rho(x_1)(p)\,(\rho(g)\nu)(p)=0\);
  • \((\rho((x_1^2-x_1)g_1)\nu)(p)=\rho(g_1)(p)\,(\rho(x_1^2-x_1)\nu)(p)=0\), by soundness at \(x_1^2-x_1\), of degree \(2\le D-K\).
So \(\rho(g|_{x_1=1})u_1\) vanishes on \(X\), and then so does \(\rho(g|_{x_1=0})u_0\). Their degrees are at most \(T(D-K)+T+\deg\nu\). In a domain model membership is vanishing plus a degree bound.

Hypotheses, each with its step.

  • Part (a). That \(\rho\) is an algebra map is used in the identity, and commuting in the later splits. The Boolean axiom on \(x_i\) makes \((x_i^2-x_i)g_1\) a sound multiple. The room is the closure step. \(\rho(x_i)=x_iI\) for \(i>t\) makes the last action scalar, so that coordinates separate. \(D-K>t-s\) is nontriviality only, used by no step.
  • Part (b). Soundness at the axioms \(x_i-\ell_i\), \(\deg\ell_i\le1\), and \(\ell_i\) untwisted are the steps. \(D-K+\deg\nu\le D'\) is the final membership. A closure member \(x_i-\ell_i\) that is not an axiom needs soundness extended to closure members, which lem:twisted-certificate-reduction (a) gives within its room.
  • Part (c). The domain model is membership as vanishing. Soundness at \(x_1^2-x_1\), with \(D-K\ge2\), is the second vanishing.
  • The field is arbitrary throughout.

Degenerate cases.

  • \(t=0\) in (a), or \(s=0\) in (b): nothing to split or substitute.
  • \(\rho(x_1)=x_1I\): \(u_1=x_1\nu\), and the split is the scalar repair split by cases.
  • \(u_1=0\) or \(u_0=0\): one piece only, already substituted.
  • \(D-K\le t-s\) in (a): the reduced window is empty and (a) says nothing.
  • \(\ell_i\) constant in (b): \(x_i\) is fixed by an axiom, and the substitution is by that constant.

Nonvacuity. Plainest bound. On these witnesses the scalar repair \(\nu\) and lem:twisted-certificate-reduction (f) are the plain objects; (f) needs room \(4\) where the witnesses have \(3\), so it gives nothing there, and the cube's domain model makes (c) apply to the (a) witness.

  • Part (a), at tight room, a case lem:twisted-certificate-reduction (f) does not cover. Take \(n=2\), Boolean axioms on \(x_1,x_2\) over \(\mathbb F_2\), \(\rho(x_1)=\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}0&x_2\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)\), \(\rho(x_2)=x_2I\), \(\nu=(x_2,1)\), \(E=x_1+x_2\), \(w=1\), \(D=3\), \(K=1\), \(D'=3\) and \(T=1\).
    • Room: \(1\cdot2+1=3\le3\), tight, while (f) needs \(2+1+1=4\le3\), which fails.
    • Soundness: \(\rho(x_1^2+x_1)\nu=(x_2^2+x_2,0)\in J^2\).
    • Killing: \(\rho(x_1+x_2)\nu=(x_2+x_2^2,0)\in J^2\).
    • Survival: \(\nu\notin J^2\).
    • Pieces: \(u_1=(x_2,x_2)\) and \(u_0=(0,1+x_2)\). The substitution repair \(x_1\mapsto1\) with multiplier \(x_2\) at window \(1\) gives \((1+x_2)x_2\in J\) and \(x_2\notin J\).
    This \(J\) is the cube's domain model, so (c) covers the same witness at the full window. A witness of (a) in a proper closure that is no domain model is not given here; finding one is the next attempt.
  • Part (b), with the reviewer's witness, checked here: the same \(\rho\) and Boolean axioms, the axiom \(x_1+x_2\) (\(\ell=x_2\)), \(E=x_2\notin J\), \(w=1\) and \(\nu=(0,1+x_2)\).
    • \(u_1=(x_2+x_2^2,0)\).
    • \(\rho(x_1^2+x_1)\nu=(x_2+x_2^2,x_2+x_2^2)\in J^2\), and \(\rho(x_1+x_2)\nu=(x_2+x_2^2,x_2+x_2^2)\in J^2\).
    • The multiples of \(x_1+x_2\) by \(m=x_1\) and \(m=x_2\) also lie in \(J^2\), at degree \(3\).
    • \(x_2\nu\in J^2\), and \(\nu\notin J^2\).
    • (b) gives the scalar repair \(1+x_2\).
  • Part (c): the (a) witness, in the cube's domain model.
No parameter ledger applies: the witnesses verify no budget of the goal.

Baseline. Without the twist, the scalar repair \(\nu\) is the plain object, and lem:twisted-certificate-reduction (f) splits a twisted variable when the room pays \(T\). Part (c) is the observation that in a domain model membership is pointwise vanishing, so degree bookkeeping alone is at stake. What the lemma adds is the unpaid split at one window degree, and the free untwisting of linearly defined variables.

Relations.

  • (a) adds to lem:twisted-certificate-reduction (f) the unpaid split; paid splits of several variables were already available from (f) variable by variable, as the goal review recorded.
  • (b) and (c) are new cases.
  • The substitution repairs are those of lem:module-repair-factorization (b), with \(\phi\) the substitution.
  • The cost of a split may correspond to the asymmetric case split of lem:branching-tree-degree; not checked.

Architecture test. Decided. The goal review's test is decided without computation by part (b). That test is the fractional-substitution quotient on the functional pigeonhole system with six pigeons and five holes at \(D'=3\), \(K=1\), \(\deg\nu=1\). Every variable is linearly defined by its pigeon axiom, \(x_{ij}=1+\sum_{j'\ne j}x_{ij'}\) over \(\mathbb F_2\), an axiom of degree \(1\) inside the window. So for every error set and every twisted variable, \(f_1\equiv x_1c\pmod{J_3}\), and the quotient is zero.

  • The review's outcome, a zero quotient everywhere, occurred. The review said that outcome would close the item as Developed.
  • This entry departs from that rule, as a decision. The instance was decided by its linear axioms, a structure the review's Trivial cases did not list, so the outcome says nothing about closures without such members.
  • Whether Pang's systems have members \(x_i-\ell_i\) of degree \(1\) in their degree-\((D-K)\) closures is an untested hypothesis, with no source read. The entry's hedges concern other matters: the correspondence with lem:branching-tree-degree, and its own process. The product pigeonhole system has none below its top degree. By lem:top-degree-axiom-inertness, as cor:hole-occupancy-kernels records, its closure below degree \(D'\) consists of the polynomials vanishing on the hole-respecting assignments \(Y\). \(Y\) contains the all-zero assignment and every single-variable one, so no nonzero polynomial of degree at most \(1\) vanishes on it.

Owed attempt. The twisted-module entry named several twisted Boolean variables at room for fewer splits, first at \(n=4\), \(\deg\nu=0\), \(T=1\) with three twisted variables. That named instance gives no \(D\), \(K\) or \(D'\), so the number of splits its room pays is not fixed. Part (a) answers it for every value: with room \(T(D-K)+sT+\deg\nu\le D'\), the three splits give substitution repairs at window \(D-K-(3-s)\).

New mathematics. lem:twist-window-trade: with the other variables untwisted, twisted repairs on Boolean twisted variables split into substitution repairs, at one window degree or \(T\) room degrees per split, the dropped window losing soundness and killing above it; linearly defined twisted variables cost nothing and need no Boolean axiom; in a domain model the window is kept, measured at degree \(D'+T\).

Selection gain. Unchanged: the lemma reduces module repairs to substitution and scalar repairs and lowers no rank.

Goal progress. Unchanged. The matrix generalization reduces, at a stated cost, to substitutions and multipliers; no saving at Pang's parameters follows. Bearing. None at the goal's own parameters: whether Pang's systems have linearly defined variables in their closures is untested, and the case without them at tight room is not decided here. The cycle could have found the window loss real on the review's instance; that instance turned out to be decided by its linear axioms.

Record search. Searches for a linearly defined variable untwisting a twisted repair returned lem:twisted-certificate-reduction, lem:module-repair-factorization, lem:pair-variable-repairing (definitions of product variables, another object) and historical lem:substitution; none states (b). For the next attempt, a search for the top degree of the product pigeonhole system, its unplaced-pigeon indicators and twisted repairs returned lem:top-degree-killer-transfer and lem:cylinder-killer-degree. The first is the scalar fact a twisted repair there must beat: at the top degree, monomial errors gain no killer from the pigeon axioms. It also returned cor:hole-occupancy-kernels, whose registered statement gives at \(D=n\) that \(c\) of degree at most \(n\) lies in \(C\) exactly when \(c|_Y\) lies in the span \(P_Y\) of the unplaced-pigeon indicators, \(Y\) the hole-respecting assignments.

Smallest case. The next attempt is a proper closure without linear definitions at tight room: the product pigeonhole system with four pigeons and three holes at its top degree \(D'=3\), over \(\mathbb F_2\), proper since by the same inertness \(1\notin J_3\), \(Y\) being nonempty, with \(K=1\), \(D-K=2\), \(T=1\), \(\deg\nu=1\), room \(2+1=3\), twisted variable \(x_{00}\), and the error pairs \((E,w)\) of distinct variables with \(x_{00}\in\{E,w\}\). Its pigeon axioms have degree \(3>D-K\), so they never enter soundness, and (b) and (c) do not apply. Plainest bound. At \(k=1\) every twisted repair is a substitution. In the inert range at \(D=n\), \(K+e\le n-1=2\), cor:hole-occupancy-kernels makes every scalar kernel a support count on \(Y\). So the plain bound fixes the scalar and substitution side of the comparison, and leaves open only whether a realizable \(k=2\) pair falls outside \(\{rc\}\). By cor:hole-occupancy-kernels, the degree-\(3\) memberships, the killing conditions \(v\,f_1\) and the soundness conditions \(x_{i0}f_1\), are restrictions to \(Y\) lying in the span \(P_Y\) of the unplaced-pigeon indicators, and degree-\(2\) survival is non-vanishing on \(Y\). The test is the goal review's Operation on this board, with matrix size \(k=2\):

  • the linear conditions on \((c,f_1)\) modulo \(J_3\), with \(\deg f_1\le2\);
  • the quotient by \(\{rc\}\), taken modulo \(J_3\);
  • the realizability search for any element outside \(\{rc\}\).
The comparison is with substitutions of multiplier degree at most \(\deg\nu\), the form \(f_1\equiv rc\). At tight room a full-window substitution with multiplier \(u_\varepsilon\), of degree \(\deg\nu+T\), exceeds \(D'\) by definition. A caution for reading the quotient: with \(w=x_{00}\) and \(E=v\), any \(f_1\) with \(vf_1\) vanishing on \(Y\) is a solution, for example a variable of another pigeon in \(v\)'s hole, and it may be of the form \(rc\) with \(r=1\). An earlier draft reduced the test to whether \(\rho(x_1)\) keeps components inside \(P_Y\). That reduction, the reviewer's suggestion, is withdrawn: the soundness term \(\rho(g_1)\rho(x_1^2-x_1)\nu\) does not vanish on \(Y\), and for \(\deg g=2\) the piece has degree \(4>D'\). Not decided here; the reviewer found nothing in (a) to (c) or the cited records that decides it.

"Plus" for a sum of subspaces has no mechanical signal, and none is claimed.
  5. Adding a written rule to AGENTS.md broke the one-place principle. Wrong: the Instance check sentence sits inside the Decisive test rule it serves, not beside a second statement of it, and the finisher enforces it.

Meta. The way of working behind the right objections is reaching for a private shortcut when the committed path feels slow: scratch replace scripts instead of tools/replace_text.py, a reply before its check, a fix to one sentence instead of the class. The change is to take the committed path for every edit and every answer. tools/hooks/bash_guard.py now enforces this for scratch edits, and the queued build for deferred questions. The same habit recurred inside this cycle in another form: the review's test was chosen by the instrument at hand, the board the record had computed, and not by reading that board's structure, its linear axioms, which decided the test. The change is to read the structure of an instance before choosing it. The Trivial cases rule in AGENTS.md now names this structure.

General statement. cor:top-degree-twist-scalar applies to the product pigeonhole system at its top degree, over any field and with any numbers of pigeons and holes. A twisted repair whose protected weight is a hole variable \(x\), and whose errors are variables other than \(x\), needs a survivor of its pair conditions. Such a survivor exists exactly when the conditions touch at most \(K'\) holes, and then a scalar repair \(xm\) of degree \(\tau\) does the same job. check:product-board-twist confirms it on the board with four pigeons and three holes, and validates the script.

Top-degree twist scalarity

Statement. Let \(J=C\) be the degree-\(n\) closure of the product pigeonhole system with \(m\) pigeons and \(n\) holes, over any field, in the multilinear ring or with Boolean axioms. Let \(Y\) be the hole-respecting assignments and \(x=x_{ab}\) a hole variable. Let \(S\) be a set of variables other than \(x\), let \(P=\{x_{kb}:k\ne a\}\cup S\), and let \(1\le K'\le n-1\).

  • Put \(F=\{f\in V_{K'}:pf\in C\text{ for all }p\in P\}\).
  • Let \(\tau\) be the number of distinct holes the variables of \(P\) lie in: \(1\) plus the number of holes other than \(b\) that \(S\) touches, when \(m\ge2\).
Then \(F\not\subseteq C\) if and only if \(\tau\le K'\). When it holds and hole \(b\) is touched (\(b\in H\), for instance \(m\ge2\)), \(f=x\prod_{j\in H\setminus\{b\}}\bigl(1-\sum_kx_{kj}\bigr)\), with \(H\) the touched holes, lies in \(F\setminus C\) and has degree \(\tau\). That is the scalar repair with multiplier \(m=\prod_{j\in H\setminus\{b\}}(1-\sum_kx_{kj})\), of degree \(\tau-1\le K'-1\): \(xm\) satisfies the same conditions and survives. Consequence for twisted repairs. On this system at any window \(W=D-K\ge2\) with room \(TW+\deg\nu\le n\), take a twisted repair whose weight is \(x\), whose errors are the variables of \(S\), and whose twisted variable is \(x\) with the other variables untwisted. By the identity of lem:twist-window-trade, some coordinate gives an \(f_1\in F\setminus C\) with \(K'=T+\deg\nu\le n-1\). So, with \(b\in H\), a scalar repair with multiplier of degree \(\tau-1\le T+\deg\nu-1\) exists for the same errors. At \(T=1\), or whenever \(\tau\le\deg\nu+1\), that degree is at most \(\deg\nu\), and the twist adds nothing beyond a scalar repair. For \(T\ge2\) the scalar multiplier can exceed \(\deg\nu\), though it is still a valid scalar repair. Only the necessary direction is used.

Proof.

  • Each \(p=x_{kj}\in P\) is a monomial error of degree \(1\) on one hole. For \(f\) of degree at most \(K'\) with \(K'+1\le n\), lem:top-degree-killer-transfer (monomial errors on distinct holes, all \(m,n\)) gives \(pf\in C\) exactly when \(f\) vanishes on the support of \(p\) on \(Y\), the cylinder \(\{s_j=k\}\).
  • By lem:top-degree-axiom-inertness, as recorded in cor:hole-occupancy-kernels, \(C\) below degree \(n\) is the vanishing ideal of \(Y\). So \(f\notin C\) exactly when \(f\) is nonzero on \(Y\).
  • Hence \(F\not\subseteq C\) exactly when some function of degree at most \(K'\) vanishes on the union of the cylinders and is nonzero on \(Y\). On \(Y\), with base state empty, lem:cylinder-killer-degree makes the least degree of such a function the transversal number of the cylinders' coordinate sets. These are single holes, so the transversal number is \(\tau\).
  • The killer. At hole \(b\) take the state "pigeon \(a\)": no cylinder assigns it, since \(x\notin S\) and the partners \(x_{kb}\) have \(k\ne a\). Its indicator is \(x\). At every other touched hole take the state "empty", which no cylinder assigns, with indicator \(1-\sum_kx_{kj}\). By the same lemma their product attains degree \(\tau\). It vanishes on every cylinder, through the factor at that cylinder's hole, and it is nonzero at the assignment putting pigeon \(a\) in hole \(b\) and leaving the others empty, which lies in \(Y\).
  • The consequence. A twisted coordinate's \(f_1\) satisfies \(x_{kb}f_1\in C\) (soundness at the hole axioms \(xx_{kb}\)) and \(Ef_1\in C\) (killing \(xE\)), and some coordinate survives with \(f_1\notin C\). That is the twist-window entry's pair identity with \(g_0=0\).

Hypotheses, each with its step.

  • The top degree \(D'=n\) and \(K'+1\le n\) are the hypotheses of lem:top-degree-killer-transfer.
  • \(K'\le n-1\) gives the vanishing-ideal description of survival.
  • Errors that are variables other than \(x\) make each condition a degree-one monomial error and leave the state "pigeon \(a\)" free at hole \(b\).
  • \(b\in H\), given by \(m\ge2\), carries the degree of the killer: without it the product has degree \(\tau+1\), and on the slice \(x=1\) any multiplier must vanish on the \(\tau\) cylinders, so no scalar repair of degree at most \(K'\) exists when \(\tau=K'\).
  • \(T=1\), or \(\tau\le\deg\nu+1\), is what makes the scalar multiplier's degree at most \(\deg\nu\) in the consequence.
  • The field is arbitrary. \(\mathbb F_2\), and Booleanity of products, enter only the comparison with substitutions \(x\mapsto r\) in the computation, where every \((r^2-r)m\) vanishes in the multilinear ring.
  • The number of pigeons is arbitrary.
Not covered: a weight that is not a hole variable; errors through \(x\) or of degree above \(1\); the other weight, \(E=x\) with \(w=v\), which is served by the substitution \(x\mapsto0\) with multiplier \(1\) only when every error is divisible by \(x\); and more than one twisted variable.

Degenerate cases.

  • \(S\) empty with \(m\ge2\): \(\tau=1\), and the killer is \(x\) itself, the scalar repair \(m=1\).
  • \(m=1\): no partners, \(\tau\) counts the holes of \(S\) alone, and when \(S\) does not touch hole \(b\) the scalar half fails: the killer has degree \(\tau+1\) (with \(S\) empty, \(\tau=0\) and the killer \(x\) has degree \(1\)).
  • \(\tau>K'\): no survivor of degree at most \(K'\), so no twisted repair of this form exists.
  • \(K'=n\): outside the hypotheses; the transfer and the survival description fail there.

Nonvacuity. Plainest bound. The scalar repairs of degree \(\tau-1\) are the plainest class, and the corollary shows they decide every set. Four pigeons, three holes, \(x=x_{00}\), \(K'=2\), \(S=\{x_{01}\}\): \(\tau=2\le2\). Over \(\mathbb F_2\) the killer is \(f=x_{00}(1+x_{01}+x_{11}+x_{21}+x_{31})\).

  • \(x_{k0}f\in C\), since each term contains the hole axiom \(x_{00}x_{k0}\).
  • \(x_{01}f=x_{00}x_{01}(x_{11}+x_{21}+x_{31})\in C\), since each term contains a hole axiom \(x_{01}x_{k1}\) (and \(x_{01}(1+x_{01})=0\)).
  • \(f\) is nonzero at the assignment putting pigeon \(0\) in hole \(0\) alone.
The computation found the different member \(x_{00}(1+x_{01})\) of \(F\setminus C\), of the same degree. The scalar repairs of degree \(\tau-1\) are the plainest class, and the corollary shows they decide every set; recorded results decide the computation. No parameter ledger applies: the witness verifies no budget of the goal.

Baseline. Without the twist, scalar repairs; lem:top-degree-killer-transfer and lem:cylinder-killer-degree already give their least degree for monomial errors. The corollary adds that the twisted pair conditions with weight a hole variable reduce to the same killer problem, so that a twist cannot do better there.

The computation, as validation

Setup. research/results/common_multiplier_product_twist_20261016/product_twist.py, written and committed before the corollary was seen, uses tools/pc_closure.py. It runs on the product pigeonhole system over \(\mathbb F_2\) with four pigeons and three holes at \(D'=3\). Its closure has dimension \(178\) of \(299\) monomials and is proper. The twisted variable and weight are \(x_{00}\), and the error sets are every nonempty set \(S\) of the other eleven variables, \(2047\) in all.

  • For each \(S\) it decides whether \(F_S\) (\(K'=2\)) has a survivor, whether a product \(rm\) of linear forms survives in it, and whether a scalar \(x_{00}m\) with \(\deg m\le1\) does.
  • Its positive control is a synthetic closure where a sum of two products survives and no product does. It tests the product search, which the corollary makes unnecessary; no control could fail on the decisive comparison of survivors with scalar repairs.
  • The first run failed that control, which then used one condition variable \(v\): \(1+v\) survived trivially, since \(v(1+v)=0\) in the multilinear ring. It was redesigned with three.
Both runs are saved beside this entry (run1_control_failed.txt, run2.txt).

Result. From product_twist.json, \(247\) of the \(2047\) sets have a survivor, all \(247\) have a scalar repair of degree \(1\), and no set has a survivor without one. The corollary predicts this: \(\tau\le2\) exactly when \(S\) avoids touching both holes \(1\) and \(2\), and the nonempty such sets number \(2^7+2^7-2^3-1=247\). So the count validates the script. Two cases by hand: \(S=\{x_{01},x_{02}\}\) has \(\tau=3\) and no survivor, as computed; \(S=\{x_{01}\}\) gives the scalar repair \(x_{00}(1+x_{01})\), as computed.

With hole \(b\) touched, a scalar repair of degree \(\tau-1\le T+\deg\nu-1\) then serves the same errors, at most \(\deg\nu\) when \(T=1\). check:product-board-twist confirms the count \(247\) on the board with four pigeons and three holes.

General statement. conj:monomial-kernel-transfer extends conj:functional-kernel-transfer from variable errors to monomial errors. It covers the functional pigeonhole system with \(n+1\) pigeons and \(n\) holes, at a proper degree \(D\), \(K\le D-1\), any set of monomial errors \(E\) with \(K+\deg E\le D\). It states that the common kernel in \(V_K\) modulo the closure \(C\) equals the kernel modulo the closure \(H\) of the hole and functionality axioms, plus \(C\cap V_K\). check:block-pair-kernels confirms it on six sets at \(K=1\), \(D=3\), with six pigeons and five holes.

Scope. The conjecture keeps the parent's \(m=n+1\), the only case with evidence (over \(\mathbb F_2\)).

  • It drops the condition that each monomial lie on distinct pigeons and holes. A monomial on one pigeon or one hole lies in \(H\subseteq C\), so \(uE\) lies in \(H\) for every \(u\in V_K\). Such an error constrains neither side, and the equality is unchanged. Dropping the condition makes the statement more general.
  • With \(\deg E=1\) it contains the parent.
  • The field enters only the computation; whether a proof needs \(\mathbb F_2\) is open.

The computation

Setup. research/results/common_multiplier_block_pairs_20261016/block_pairs.py reuses the kernel code of three_quantities.py (the transfer test) and tools/pc_closure.py. It runs on the functional pigeonhole system over \(\mathbb F_2\) with six pigeons and five holes, at \(D=3\), \(K=1\), \(\dim V_1=31\), with \(C\cap V_1\) the six pigeon axioms. Its expectations were committed before the run.

Functional killer transfer below half the holes

16 October 2026 · Working proof, for degrees up to half the holes · Functional killer transfer. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, low reasoning).

Where we stand. Unchanged: an obstruction for monomial errors in the basis range, beside the transfer test already summarized

Earlier entries. The item's latest entries are the block-family entry, which named the pair families on the six-by-five board, and the block-pair entry, which found no killer beyond the domain model's on six sets and named “a proof of conj:monomial-kernel-transfer at \(K=1\) through prop:exact-operator-criterion: whether \(R(x_ax_bt)\) factors through the restricted board's operator”.

Owed attempt. The block-pair entry's attempt is made, below, and its question is answered in another form. For the numbering adapted to an error \(E\), \(R(x_Er)\equiv x_Er\) modulo \(H\) for every \(r\in\operatorname{span}(T_K\cap B_K)\) with \(K+|E|\le D\): multiplication by \(x_E\) keeps the image of \(R\). The restricted-board form is shown in one direction only (below). The proof holds at every \(K\), for every monomial error, over every field, at \(D\le\lceil N/2\rceil\).

Best outcome. A proof that the pigeon axioms add a killer to some family of monomial errors would be a joint saving of the admitted kind; a proof that they add none closes monomial errors on this system as a source. At the goal's own parameters Pang's errors are not monomials, so either outcome bears only on where a saving can come from. The recorded results to beat are check:block-pair-kernels and check:functional-kernels-k2, finite checks at one or two sizes, behind the open conj:monomial-kernel-transfer.

General statement. lem:admissible-numbering-transfer: on the functional pigeonhole system at \(D\le\lceil N/2\rceil\), over any field and for any number of pigeons, a set of monomial errors gains no killer from the pigeon axioms whenever one numbering of pigeons and holes keeps every product of a dance-admissible matching monomial with an error admissible or zero. lem:functional-killer-transfer: every single monomial error has such a numbering. cor:nested-hole-joint-transfer: sets of errors whose hole sets are nested have one, under a hole-room condition.

Setting

Setting. The functional pigeonhole system with \(m\) pigeons and \(N\ge1\) holes over a field: Booleanity, hole axioms \(x_{ij}x_{i'j}\), functionality axioms \(x_{ij}x_{ij'}\), pigeon axioms \(Q_i=1-\sum_jx_{ij}\), in the multilinear ring. \(V_K\) is the space of multilinear polynomials of degree at most \(K\). \(C\) is the degree-\(D\) PC closure of all axioms, and \(H\) that of the hole and functionality axioms alone, which is the span of the non-matching multilinear monomials of degree at most \(D\). For \(X\in\{C,H\}\) and a polynomial \(E\), \(\operatorname{Ann}_X(E)=\{u:uE\in X\}\), for \(u\in V_K\) with \(K+\deg E\le D\).

  • Modulo \(H\), every polynomial of degree at most \(D\) is a combination of matching monomials \(x_t\), \(t\) a partial matching, \(T_d\) those of degree at most \(d\) (IPS, Definition 2.1). The product \(x_tx_E\) is \(x_{t\cup E}\) when \(t\cup E\) is a matching and lies in \(H\) otherwise.
  • From Impagliazzo, Pudlák and Sgall (ECCC TR97-042, pages 3–6, read in this cycle from the rendered pages), for a fixed numbering of pigeons and holes:
    • A pigeon dance on a matching moves the pigeons in increasing order, each to a larger hole, every step staying one-to-one (Definition 2.3).
    • \(B_d\) consists of the \(x_a\), \(a\) a partial map to holes or to \(0\) (the factor \(Q_i\)), whose matching part admits a dance (Definition 2.5). Membership depends only on \(a\), so \(B_K=\{x_a\in B_D:|a|\le K\}\).
    • For \(d\le\lceil N/2\rceil\), \(B_d\) is a basis of \(\operatorname{span}(T_d)\) (Proposition 2.8).
    • The degree-\(d\) closure of the \(Q_i\) in that span is \(K_d=\operatorname{span}(B_d\setminus T_d)\). Theorem 2.9's proof gives the inclusion of the closure in that span. The elements of \(B_d\setminus T_d\) are multiples of axioms derivable in degree \(d\), which gives the reverse inclusion.
    • No step of these uses more pigeons than holes: Lemma 2.6 uses only \(y+2x\le n\).
  • Since \(B_K\subseteq B_D\) and Proposition 2.8 holds at \(K\) and at \(D\), an element of \(\operatorname{span}(T_K)\) has the same unique expansion in \(B_K\) and in \(B_D\). Hence \(K_D\cap\operatorname{span}(T_K)=\operatorname{span}(B_K\setminus T_K)=K_K\).
  • So \(C\) is \(H\) plus the lift of \(K_D\), and \(C\cap V_K\) is \(H\cap V_K\) plus the lift of \(K_K\). A member of \(H\cap V_K\) times \(x_E\) is a combination of non-matching monomials of degree at most \(D\), so it lies in \(H\).

The criterion

Lemma (admissible numbering transfer). Let \(D\le\lceil N/2\rceil\), let \(F\) be a set of monomial errors with \(K+|E|\le D\) for each \(E\in F\), and suppose one numbering of pigeons and holes has the following property. For every \(E\in F\) that is a matching and every \(x_t\in T_K\cap B_K\) with \(t\cup E\) a matching, \(x_{t\cup E}\in B_D\). Then \(\bigcap_{E\in F}\operatorname{Ann}_C(x_E)\cap V_K=\bigcap_{E\in F}\operatorname{Ann}_H(x_E)\cap V_K+(C\cap V_K)\).

Proof. Every relabelling of pigeons and holes maps the axiom sets to themselves, so \(C\) and \(H\) do not depend on the numbering, while \(B_d\) is taken for the given one.

  • The inclusion \(\supseteq\) holds since \(C\supseteq H\) and \((C\cap V_K)x_E\subseteq C\), the product having degree at most \(D\).
  • For \(\subseteq\), let \(u\in V_K\) with \(ux_E\in C\) for all \(E\in F\). Modulo \(H\), \(u\) is a combination of \(T_K\). By Proposition 2.8 at degree \(K\), \(u\equiv k+r\) with \(k\in K_K\) and \(r=\sum_{t\in T_K\cap B_K}c_tx_t\).
  • For each \(E\), \(kx_E\in K_D\), so \(rx_E\in K_D\) modulo \(H\). A non-matching \(E\) has \(x_E\in H\) and constrains nothing.
  • For a matching \(E\), by the property, \(rx_E=\sum_tc_tx_tx_E\) is modulo \(H\) a combination of elements of \(T_D\cap B_D\). Distinct \(t\) with the same \(t\cup E\) may cancel, which is harmless. Since \(B_D\) is a basis and \(K_D=\operatorname{span}(B_D\setminus T_D)\), the combination lies in \(K_D\) only if it is zero, that is \(rx_E\in H\).
  • So \(r\in\bigcap_E\operatorname{Ann}_H(x_E)\), and \(u\) is \(r\) plus \(k\) plus a member of \(H\cap V_K\), the last two lying in \(C\cap V_K\). \(\square\)

The operator form. In the notation of prop:exact-operator-criterion, \(r=R(u)\), and the property says \(R(x_Er)\equiv x_Er\) modulo \(H\). The restricted-board form holds in one direction: \(x_E\) times the closure of the restricted board, whose pigeon axioms are the \(Q_i'\) with the holes of \(E\) removed, lies in \(K_D\). Indeed \(x_EQ_i'=x_EQ_i\) modulo \(H\) for pigeons \(i\) outside \(E\).

Single errors

Lemma (functional killer transfer). For every \(N\ge1\), every \(m\), \(D\le\lceil N/2\rceil\), every set \(E\) of variables and \(K+|E|\le D\): \(\operatorname{Ann}_C(x_E)\cap V_K=\operatorname{Ann}_H(x_E)\cap V_K+(C\cap V_K)\).

Proof. If \(E\) is not a matching, both sides are \(V_K\); if \(E=\varnothing\), both are \(C\cap V_K\). Let \(E\) be a matching of size \(e\ge1\).

  • Case \(N\ge2\). Number so that \(E=\{(p_k,e+1-k):k=1,\dots,e\}\), with \(p_1<\dots<p_e\) the last \(e\) pigeons. Let \(x_t\in T_K\cap B_K\) with \(t\cup E\) a matching, and \(t_0=t\setminus E\).
    • A sub-matching of a matching with a dance has one: restrict each step to the remaining pigeons. So \(t_0\) has a dance.
    • \(t_0\) uses no pigeon of \(E\) and no hole in \(\{1,\dots,e\}\). Its dance moves upward, so it never enters those holes, the pigeons of \(E\) never block it, and its pigeons precede \(p_1\).
    • Then \(p_1\), at hole \(e\), moves to an unoccupied hole above \(e\): there are \(N-e-|t_0|\ge N-K-e\ge1\) of them, since \(K+e\le D\le\lceil N/2\rceil\le N-1\). Then \(p_k\), at hole \(e+1-k\), moves to hole \(e+2-k\), vacated by \(p_{k-1}\).
    • So \(t\cup E\) has a dance, and \(x_{t\cup E}\in B_D\). The admissible numbering transfer lemma gives the claim.
  • Case \(N=1\). Then \(D\le1\), so \(K=0\) and \(E=\{(i,1)\}\). The degree-\(1\) closure is \(\operatorname{span}(Q_1,\dots,Q_m)\), the hole and functionality axioms having degree \(2\), and \(x_{i1}=1-Q_i\) is not in it: \(x_{i1}=\sum_jc_jQ_j\) forces \(c_i=-1\) and \(c_j=0\) for \(j\ne i\), from the coefficients of the variables, and the constant term is then \(-1\ne0\). So \(cx_{i1}\in C\) only for \(c=0\), while \(\operatorname{Ann}_H(x_{i1})\cap V_0=0\) and \(C\cap V_0=0\). Here the property fails, since \(x_{i1}\) has no dance, so the case is checked directly. \(\square\)

Nested hole sets

Corollary (nested hole joint transfer). Let \(D\le\lceil N/2\rceil\) and let \(F\) be a set of matchings whose hole sets form a chain under inclusion, \(\Pi\) the set of their pigeons. Suppose that for each \(E\in F\), with \(s_E=|E|\), \(K+s_E\le D\) and \(K+2s_E+\min(|\Pi|-s_E,K)\le N\). Then the joint transfer of the admissible numbering transfer lemma holds for \(F\).

Proof. Number the holes so that each hole set in the chain is an initial segment: the smallest first, then each larger set's new holes. Number the pigeons so that \(\Pi\) comes last, in any order. Fix \(E\in F\), with hole set \(\{1,\dots,s\}\), \(s=s_E\), and \(x_t\in T_K\cap B_K\) with \(t\cup E\) a matching.

  • As before, \(t_0=t\setminus E\) has a dance, uses no pigeon of \(E\), and has no hole in \(\{1,\dots,s\}\). Its dance stays above \(s\), and the pigeons of \(E\) never block it.
  • Run that dance in pigeon order. The pigeons of \(t_0\) outside \(\Pi\) all move before any pigeon of \(\Pi\). At its turn, a pigeon of \(E\) moves to a hole above \(s\) that is unoccupied and is not the target of a later move of a pigeon of \(t_0\) in \(\Pi\).
  • Holes above \(s\): \(N-s\). Excluded: the current positions of the pigeons of \(t_0\), at most \(K\); the future targets of the pigeons of \(t_0\) in \(\Pi\setminus E\), at most \(\min(|\Pi|-s,K)\); the holes taken by earlier pigeons of \(E\), at most \(s-1\). The room condition leaves at least one.
  • The pigeons of \(t_0\) still reach their targets, which no pigeon of \(E\) takes. So \(t\cup E\) has a dance, and the property holds for this one numbering and every \(E\in F\). \(\square\)
The room condition is this bookkeeping's bound, which reserves every current position and future target. It is not shown to be needed: for one error the single-error lemma needs only \(K+s\le N-1\), using vacated holes of \(E\).

Hypotheses, each with its step.

  • \(D\le\lceil N/2\rceil\): Proposition 2.8 and Theorem 2.9 at degrees \(K\) and \(D\). The single-error lemma's free hole needs only \(K+|E|\le N-1\), which this implies for \(N\ge2\).
  • \(K+|E|\le D\): the products \(x_tx_E\) and \((C\cap V_K)x_E\) must lie in the degree-\(D\) space.
  • The number of pigeons: none. No cited step uses \(m>N\), so the statements hold for every \(m\). For \(m\le N\) the system is satisfiable, and the statements still describe its truncated closure.
  • The corollary's nested hole sets: the dance of \(t_0\) avoids \(E\)'s holes because \(t_0\) has none of them and they form an initial segment. Its room condition is the count of free holes above \(s_E\).
  • The field: none; the cited basis is over any field.
The criterion and the single-error lemma hold for every \(K\le D-|E|\), the corollary for every \(K\) meeting its room condition.

Degenerate cases.

  • \(E=\varnothing\) (\(x_E=1\)): both sides are \(C\cap V_K\).
  • A non-matching \(E\): \(x_E\in H\), and both sides are \(V_K\).
  • \(K=0\) and \(E\) a nonempty matching: \(cx_E\in C\) only for \(c=0\).
  • \(N=1\): proved directly above.
  • A corollary set with one element: the single-error lemma under a stronger room condition.
  • \(F\) empty: both sides are \(V_K\).

Nonvacuity. The single-error lemma at six pigeons and five holes, \(D=3\), \(K=1\), \(E=\{(0,0),(1,1)\}\): \(D=3=\lceil5/2\rceil\) and \(K+2=3\). It agrees with check:block-pair-kernels (single excess \(0\)), and at \(K=2\), \(E=\{(0,0)\}\), with check:functional-kernels-k2. Every \(N\ge1\) with \(D=\lceil N/2\rceil\) qualifies, so the parameters are unbounded. Plainest bound. On the witness the containment \(\supseteq\) gives no equality, and the bare count leaves an excess of up to \(25-16=9\).

The corollary at the same board:

  • The crossing set \(\{x_{00}x_{11},x_{01}x_{10}\}\), \(s=2\), \(\Pi=\{0,1\}\), \(K=1\): \(1+4+\min(0,1)=5\le5\). This agrees with check:block-pair-kernels.
  • The same-hole set \(\{x_{00},x_{10}\}\) at \(K=2\): \(2+2+\min(1,2)=5\le5\). This agrees with check:functional-kernels-k2. At \(K=2\) a same-hole set with \(|\Pi|=3\) fails the condition (\(2+2+2=6\)); at \(K=1\) every same-hole variable set meets it (\(1+2+1=4\)).

General statement. lem:top-window-twist-scalar: on the product pigeonhole system with Boolean axioms at its top degree \(n\ge2\), with \(m\ge2\) pigeons, over any field, a twisted repair at window \(n\) whose twisted variables are hole variables on distinct pigeons and distinct holes satisfies \(\rho(g)\nu=g\nu\) for every polynomial \(g\). Top-window twist scalarity

Setting. As in lem:twist-window-trade: \(R=k[x]\) over a field, \(\rho:R\to\operatorname{Mat}_k(R)\) an algebra map given by commuting \(\rho(x_i)\) of entry degree at most \(T\ge1\), and \(\nu\in R^k\) a twisted repair at window \(D-K\) with room \(R_0\):

  • soundness, \(\rho(a_jm)\nu\in J^k\) for \(\deg(a_jm)\le D-K\);
  • killing, \(\rho(wE_i)\nu\in J^k\) for \(\deg(wE_i)\le D-K\);
  • survival, \(\rho(w)\nu\notin J^k\);
  • room, \(T(D-K)+\deg\nu\le R_0\le D'\).
Here \(J=C\) is the degree-\(n\) closure of the product pigeonhole system with \(m\) pigeons and \(n\) holes together with the Boolean axioms \(x_{ij}^2-x_{ij}\): hole axioms \(x_{ij}x_{kj}\), \(i\ne k\), and pigeon axioms \(P_i=\prod_j(1-x_{ij})\) of degree \(n\). \(Y\) is the set of hole-respecting assignments. A variable \(v\) is twisted when \(\rho(v)\ne vI\).
  • Membership. By lem:top-degree-axiom-inertness, whose statement covers Boolean axioms among the generators, the closure \(H\) of the hole and Boolean axioms is the degree-\(n\) part of the vanishing ideal of \(Y\). The proof of cor:hole-occupancy-kernels (d) then applies word for word: a polynomial \(c\) of degree at most \(n\) lies in \(C\) exactly when \(c|_Y\in P_Y=\operatorname{span}\{1_{Z_i}\}\), \(Z_i\) the points of \(Y\) where pigeon \(i\) is unplaced.
  • Cylinders. For an untwisted \(x_{kb}\) and \(f\) of degree at most \(n-1\): \(x_{kb}f\in C\) exactly when \(f\) vanishes on \(\{s_k=b\}\). Indeed \((x_{kb}f)|_Y\) vanishes off that cylinder, and a combination \(\sum_i\lambda_i1_{Z_i}\) vanishing off it is zero: at points with \(s_k=\bot\), placing one other pigeon \(i\) or none gives \(\lambda_i=0\) for \(i\ne k\) and then \(\lambda_k=0\). So the membership forces \(x_{kb}f|_Y=0\).

Lemma (top-window twist scalarity). Let \(n\ge2\), \(m\ge2\), \(D'=n\), and let \(\nu\) be a twisted repair at window \(D-K=n\) whose twisted variables are hole variables on distinct pigeons and distinct holes. Then:

  • \(T=1\) and \(\deg\nu=0\);
  • \(\rho(x)\nu=x\nu\) for every twisted \(x\), and \(\rho(g)\nu=g\nu\) for every \(g\in R\);
  • such a repair exists exactly when the weight \(w\) is a repair: \(w\notin C\) and \(wE_i\in C\) for every error \(E_i\) within the window.

Proof. The room \(Tn+\deg\nu\le n\) with \(T\ge1\) gives \(T=1\) and \(\deg\nu=0\), so \(\nu\) is a constant vector. Fix a twisted \(x=x_{ab}\) and a coordinate \(f=c+\sum\beta_{ij}x_{ij}\) of \(\rho(x)\nu\), of degree at most \(1\). Pigeon \(a\) carries no other twisted variable, so \(\rho(P_a)\nu=\prod_{j\ne b}(1-x_{aj})(\nu-\rho(x)\nu)\), \(\rho\) being an algebra map. Its coordinate \(h=\prod_{j\ne b}(1-x_{aj})(\nu_c-f)\) has degree at most \(n\), and soundness puts it in \(C\). Modulo the Boolean axioms within degree \(n\), \(h\) may be taken multilinear. On \(Y\) the product is the indicator of \(s_a\in\{b,\bot\}\), and \(h|_Y=\sum_i\lambda_i1_{Z_i}\).

  • At points with \(s_a=j\ne b\), \(h=0\). With the other pigeons unplaced, \(\sum_{i\ne a}\lambda_i=0\). Placing one pigeon \(i\ne a\) in a hole other than \(j\), which \(n\ge2\) allows, gives \(\lambda_i=0\). So \(h|_Y=\lambda_a1_{Z_a}\).
  • At \(s_a=\bot\): \(\nu_c-f(y)=\lambda_a\) for every placement of the others. A single pigeon \(i\ne a\) in a hole \(j\), the rest unplaced, gives \(\beta_{ij}=0\) for all \(i\ne a\) and all \(j\). So \(f=c+\sum_j\beta_{aj}x_{aj}\).
  • Cylinders. For a pigeon \(k\ne a\), which \(m\ge2\) gives, the hole axiom \(xx_{kb}\) has degree \(2\le n\), and \(x_{kb}\) is untwisted, hole \(b\) carrying no other twisted variable. So soundness gives \(x_{kb}f\in C\), and \(f\) vanishes on \(\{s_k=b\}\). The point with only \(k\) placed, in \(b\), gives \(c=0\). Adding \(a\) in a hole \(j\ne b\) gives \(\beta_{aj}=0\).
  • At \(s_a=b\): \(h=0\), so \(\nu_c-\beta_{ab}=0\). Hence \(f=\nu_cx\), that is \(\rho(x)\nu=x\nu\).
  • Every \(g\). For a scalar polynomial \(p\) and any variable \(v\), \(\rho(v)(p\nu)=p\,\rho(v)\nu=pv\nu\), the twisted case by the above and the untwisted case by definition. By induction on the factors of a monomial, \(\rho(v_1\cdots v_r)\nu=v_1\cdots v_r\nu\), and by linearity \(\rho(g)\nu=g\nu\).
  • Existence. Survival gives a coordinate with \(\nu_cw\notin C\), so \(\nu_c\ne0\) and \(w\notin C\). Killing at that coordinate gives \(\nu_cwE_i\in C\), so \(wE_i\in C\). Conversely, if \(w\) is a repair, \(k=1\), \(\nu=1\), \(\rho(g)=g\) is one, untwisted. \(\square\)

Consequence on the instance. Three pigeons, two holes, twisted \(x_{00}\) and \(x_{11}\), weight \(w=x_{00}\), error \(x_{11}\). By the lemma, a repair exists exactly when \(x_{00}x_{11}\in C\). It is not: if \(x_{00}x_{11}|_Y=\sum_i\lambda_i1_{Z_i}\), the point \(s=(0,1,\bot)\) gives \(\lambda_2=1\). The points \((0,\bot,\bot)\), \((\bot,1,\bot)\) and \((\bot,\bot,\bot)\) give \(\lambda_1+\lambda_2=0\), \(\lambda_0+\lambda_2=0\) and \(\lambda_0+\lambda_1+\lambda_2=0\), hence \(\lambda_2=0\), a contradiction. So at window \(2\) and room \(2\) no twisted repair of this kind with weight \(x_{00}\) kills \(x_{11}\), and no scalar one does either.

Hypotheses, each with its step.

  • Window \(n\): the pigeon-axiom step uses soundness at \(P_a\), of degree \(n\). The room at \(D'=n\) then forces \(T=1\) and \(\deg\nu=0\). Below window \(n\) the conclusion fails: at window \(n-1\) with \(D'=n\), the substitution \(x_{11}\mapsto0\) is sound and not scalar (Suggestion checked).
  • \(n\ge2\): the hole axioms of degree \(2\) lie in the window, and the pigeon step places a pigeon in a second hole. At \(n=1\) the conclusion is false: with \(m\ge2\), \(k=1\), \(\nu=1\) and \(\rho(x_{00})=x_{10}\), the window \(1\) holds only the pigeon axioms \(1-x_{i0}\). \(\rho(1-x_{00})=1-x_{10}\) lies in \(C\), and the room is \(1\le1\), but \(\rho(x_{00})\nu\ne x_{00}\nu\).
  • \(m\ge2\): the cylinder step needs a pigeon \(k\ne a\). At \(m=1\) there are no hole axioms, and \(f\) keeps the free terms \(\beta_{aj}x_{aj}\).
  • Distinct pigeons: \(\rho(P_a)\) factors with one twisted factor. Distinct holes: the partner \(x_{kb}\) in the cylinder step is untwisted. When both fail, a pigeon permutation \(\rho(x_{ij})=x_{\sigma(i)j}\) with \(\nu=1\) is a sound, non-scalar map, by the reviewer's example; whether each alone is needed was not checked.
  • The field: none. The Boolean axioms enter the Membership step, where the closure of the hole and Boolean axioms is the degree-\(n\) part of the vanishing ideal of \(Y\).
  • Commutation of the \(\rho(x_i)\) is used only through \(\rho\) being an algebra map.
The conclusion holds for every twisted repair in this class, every weight and every error set.

Degenerate cases.

  • No twisted variable: \(\rho(g)=gI\), and the lemma is the definition.
  • \(\nu=0\): survival fails, so there is no repair.
  • \(k=1\): \(\rho(x)\) is a linear substitution, and the lemma forces \(\rho(x)\nu=x\nu\). A linear substitution of \(x\) is sound at window \(n\) only as the identity.
  • \(m=1\) and \(n=1\): see the Hypotheses; at \(n=1\) the conclusion is false.

Nonvacuity. Three pigeons, two holes, \(k=2\), \(\nu=(1,0)\), \(\rho(x_{00})=x_{00}I+x_{20}E_{12}\) and \(\rho(x_{11})=x_{11}I+x_{21}E_{12}\), other variables scalar, weight \(x_{00}\), error \(x_{10}\).

  • The matrices commute, since \(E_{12}^2=0\), and have entry degree \(1\). Both are twisted, on distinct pigeons and holes.
  • \(E_{12}\nu=0\), so \(\rho(g)\nu=g\nu\), and soundness holds, the axioms, Boolean ones included, lying in \(C\).
  • Killing holds since \(x_{00}x_{10}\) is a hole axiom.
  • Survival: \(x_{00}|_Y\notin P_Y\). The points \((\bot,\bot,\bot)\), \((0,\bot,\bot)\) and \((1,\bot,\bot)\) would force \(\lambda_0+\lambda_1+\lambda_2=0\), \(\lambda_1+\lambda_2=1\) and \(\lambda_1+\lambda_2=0\).
  • Room: \(1\cdot2+0=2\).
The witness exercises only the branch where the twist vanishes on \(\nu\). Plainest bound. lem:twist-window-trade (a) splits both twists at one window degree each, leaving window \(0\), and gives nothing here. cor:top-degree-twist-scalar covers one twist only.

General statement. cor:twist-open-band: on the product pigeonhole system with Boolean axioms, over any field, take a twisted repair whose twisted variables are \(t\) hole variables on distinct pigeons and distinct holes, the others untwisted. At window \(n\ge2\) with \(m\ge2\) it is scalar on \(\nu\). When \(TW+tT+\deg\nu\le n\), it reduces to a substitution repair at its full window. So a twisted repair outside the scalar and substitution classes, with \(m,n\ge2\), needs \(W\le n-1\) and \(TW+tT+\deg\nu\ge n+1\).

The open band

Setting. As in lem:twist-window-trade: \(R=k[x]\), \(\rho\) an algebra map given by commuting \(\rho(x_i)\) of entry degree at most \(T\ge1\), \(\rho(x_i)=x_iI\) for the untwisted variables, and \(\nu\) a twisted repair at window \(W=D-K\) with room \(R_0\), \(TW+\deg\nu\le R_0\le D'\). \(R_0\) appears only in the room clause, so any value in that interval may be taken. Here \(D'=n\), and \(J=C\) is the degree-\(n\) closure of the product pigeonhole system with \(m\) pigeons and \(n\) holes and the Boolean axioms. The twisted variables \(x_1,\dots,x_t\) are hole variables on distinct pigeons and distinct holes.

Corollary (twist open band).

  • (a) If \(W=n\), \(n\ge2\) and \(m\ge2\), then the room forces \(T=1\) and \(\deg\nu=0\), and \(\rho(g)\nu=g\nu\) for every \(g\): the repair is scalar.
  • (b) If \(TW+tT+\deg\nu\le n\), then for some \(\sigma\in\{0,1\}^t\) some coordinate of \(u_\sigma\) is a substitution repair of \(x_i\mapsto\sigma_i\) at window \(W\), in \(C\), with multiplier degree at most \(\deg\nu+tT\). This part holds for any twisted variables carrying Boolean axioms, on any system, with \(D'\) in place of \(n\).
  • (c) With \(m\ge2\) and \(n\ge2\), a twisted repair that is neither scalar on \(\nu\) nor reducible to a substitution repair at its own window needs \(W\le n-1\) and \(TW+tT+\deg\nu\ge n+1\).

Proof.

  • (a) is lem:top-window-twist-scalar, whose hypotheses are those stated. The room \(Tn+\deg\nu\le n\) gives \(T=1\) and \(\deg\nu=0\).
  • (b) Take \(R_0=D'=n\). Then \(R_0\ge TW+sT+\deg\nu\) for \(s=t\), and lem:twist-window-trade (a) says the first \(t\) splits keep the window. Its splits use the Boolean axioms \(x_i^2-x_i\), and its other variables are untwisted. After the \(t\) splits the action is scalar, and some coordinate of some \(u_\sigma\) is a substitution repair of \(x_i\mapsto\sigma_i\), measured in \(J=C\), at window \(W\), of vector degree at most \(\deg\nu+tT\).
  • (c) With \(m,n\ge2\), a repair outside both classes is in neither case. Not (a) means \(W\ne n\), and the room \(TW+\deg\nu\le n\) gives \(W\le n\), so \(W\le n-1\). Not (b) means \(TW+tT+\deg\nu\ge n+1\). \(\square\)

Remark, a sketch. A domain-model route would give (b) one degree short. Below degree \(n\) the closure is the vanishing ideal of \(Y\) (lem:top-degree-axiom-inertness). lem:twist-window-trade (c), which needs \(W\ge2\), splits one twist at the full window in a domain model. Iterating it over \(t\) twists, with every degree at most \(n-1\), would give (b) when \(TW+tT+\deg\nu\le n-1\). The iteration is not written out, so this is a sketch, not registered, and (b) already covers its range.

The band. With \(T=1\), the band is \(W\le n-1\) with \(W+\deg\nu\ge n+1-t\), under the room \(W+\deg\nu\le n\).

  • \(t=1\): \(W+\deg\nu=n\), so \(\deg\nu\ge1\): one twist at tight room.
  • \(t=2\): \(W+\deg\nu\in\{n-1,n\}\), with \(W\le n-1\).
  • Larger \(t\): \(W+\deg\nu\ge n+1-t\).

Part (b) holds for every twisted repair on Boolean variables in its range; part (c) for twists on distinct pigeons and holes with \(m,n\ge2\).

Joint-savings goal review: under joint transfer the closure only lowers support savings; test moved to a linear error no numbering reaches

16 October 2026 · Goal-level route review · Band review. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, low reasoning).

Where we stand. Unchanged: a review that changes no result; its decision keeps the worked statement and the user's order

Question. Six research entries ran on joint-error-savings since the selection review:

  • the twist-window entry: twisted repairs split into substitution repairs;
  • the product-board entry: one twist with a hole-variable weight reduces to a scalar repair;
  • the block-pair entry: six block-pair sets on the six-by-five functional board gain nothing from the pigeon axioms;
  • the functional-transfer entry: the pigeon axioms add no killer to a monomial error below half the holes, and none to a joint set with one admissible numbering;
  • the top-window entry: twists on distinct pigeons and holes act as scalars at the top window;
  • the band entry: outside one band, every such twist is scalar or a substitution repair.
All six report goal progress unchanged, and the last thirty-one research entries declared no bearing, by the count compute.sh start printed when this review began. This review asks what the line still needs for the goal, whether the proxies it works on can supply it, and whether to keep working the statement (Core) or switch.

General statement. The line's general claim, from its proved results: on the proxy systems studied, product and functional pigeonhole closures and domain models, every joint saving found is a union of supports, a domination by one annihilator or a product of killers, and every module repair reduces to scalar or substitution repairs.

  • lem:functional-killer-transfer and lem:admissible-numbering-transfer: in the functional system below half the holes, the pigeon axioms add no killer to monomial errors, singly, or jointly under one admissible numbering.
  • cor:nested-hole-joint-transfer and check:six-by-five-numberings: such numberings exist for nested hole sets with room, and for three of the four recorded six-by-five sets.
  • lem:twist-window-trade, lem:top-window-twist-scalar and cor:twist-open-band: twisted repairs reduce to substitutions or scalars outside one band.
What the goal needs is a structural saving outside those kinds on a nontrivial unbounded family, measured in the protected quotient, that improves a multiplier budget after composition costs.

Obstacle

The line is stuck on the absence of a mechanism. The one place where its proxies differ from domain models is the pigeon axioms in a proper closure. In the functional system below half the holes, those axioms were proved transparent to monomial errors: with an adapted numbering, the projection onto the dance basis commutes with multiplication by the error, so every killer is the domain model's plus the closure's low-degree part. Module repairs were proved to reduce to the scalar and substitution classes everywhere but one band. So the proxies supply no saving of the admitted kind where they have been analysed. The remaining places are:

  • joint monomial sets with no admissible numbering, such as a triple whose hole sets cover all holes, where the computed excess is still zero;
  • the twist band, \(W\le n-1\) with \(TW+tT+\deg\nu\ge n+1\);

Necessary target. The weakest endpoint that serves the goal: one nontrivial unbounded family of actual paid errors on which, by a mechanism other than supports, domination or products of killers, the common kernel is certified nonzero outside the protected quotient at a multiplier degree below the summed-rank budget, after all composition costs. By lem:exact-common-kernel-selection the composition needs only that the common kernel is not contained in \(J\), so the certificate, not a rank count, is the endpoint. Downstream. Through lem:exact-common-kernel-selection and thm:certified-repair-composition, such a certificate gives a repair with a multiplier of the certified degree, which is the second open statement itself, not a weaker one.

Extra requirements. The route demands more than the target in two ways.

  • It works on pigeonhole proxies with monomial errors, chosen because their closures are computable. The goal asks about actual paid errors. Wherever joint transfer holds, the proxies' errors give at most support savings (Rank normalization), so this demand should be weakened: the errors tested should be ones the transfer results do not reach.
  • It measures savings as rank differences, where the target needs only a certificate of nonvanishing. That demand is justified only as a way to find certificates, and can be dropped where a certificate is found directly.

Independent alternative. The review's medium reviewer, first given only the goal, the open statements and the registered results (review record), answered open questions. Its answers are suggestions, unverified except where said.

  • It wrote the saving dually, as linear relations among error-twisted functionals.
  • It proposed a Koszul product-rank bound: when \(K+2e\le D\), \(\ker E_i+\ker E_r\subseteq\ker(E_iE_r)\), so the joint codimension is bounded by the single codimensions minus those of the product errors' kernels, in the same proper quotient. It noted that the bound reduces to inclusion–exclusion of supports wherever transfer holds.
  • It proposed symmetrization over a group acting on the errors, which on invariant multipliers costs one orbit representative's rank, with the domination clause to be checked. Two readings remain: if the clause excludes a proof that only exhibits the common kernel as one element's annihilator, symmetrization is excluded on the invariant part; if the clause is read as excluding only that, symmetrization exhibits only the invariant part of the kernel and may count. This review does not decide between them.
  • It suggested, and this review checked, that wherever joint transfer holds on the functional system the saving modulo the closure is the support saving minus a nonnegative correction (Rank normalization). It named first tests for the third and fourth statements, and a test on Pang's own errors in the cube's proper closure, not compared here.
The current route was then revealed for comparison and correctness. The adopted change is narrower than either alternative: move the test to errors the transfer results do not reach, where the Koszul bound can differ from supports.

Rank normalization. Losses and survivors are measured in the same quotient, and the comparison bounds the route. Work modulo \(H\), whose degree-\(D\) part in the multilinear ring is the degree-\(D\) vanishing ideal of the set \(M\) of partial matchings, by Möbius inversion over the down-closed set \(M\). Suppose the joint identity \(\bigcap_E\operatorname{Ann}_C(E)=\bigcap_E\operatorname{Ann}_H(E)+C_K\) holds for a set of errors, with \(C_K=C\cap V_K\), \(K+e\le D\le\lceil N/2\rceil\), supports \(S_i\) on \(M\) and \(S=\bigcup S_i\). Then, with \(Z_i\) the functions vanishing on \(S_i\) and \(C_K/(Z_i\cap C_K)\cong C_K|_{S_i}\), each rank is \(\dim V_K|_{S_i}-\dim C_K|_{S_i}\), and the stacked rank is \(\dim V_K|_S-\dim C_K|_S\). The saving modulo \(C\) is therefore \(\bigl[\sum_i\dim V_K|_{S_i}-\dim V_K|_S\bigr]-\bigl[\sum_i\dim C_K|_{S_i}-\dim C_K|_S\bigr]\). The first bracket is the domain model's union-of-supports saving, an excluded kind. The second is nonnegative, since \(C_K|_S\) injects into \(\bigoplus_iC_K|_{S_i}\), a function vanishing on every \(S_i\) vanishing on \(S\). So under joint transfer the closure can only lower the support saving. The argument is the reviewer's, checked here; it is not registered, and the next research entry registers it. Relative contraction does not apply: no absolute smallness is claimed.

Decision. Core: joint-error-savings stays the worked statement, in the user's order, with the test moved to errors that the transfer results do not reach. The proof of lem:admissible-numbering-transfer passes to polynomial errors. Its step reads, in the functional-transfer entry: “for a matching \(E\), by the property, \(rx_E=\sum_tc_tx_tx_E\) is modulo \(H\) a combination of elements of \(T_D\cap B_D\)”. Summing over the monomials of \(E=\sum c_Ex_E\), each with the property under one numbering, \(rE\) is such a combination, and it lies in \(K_D\) only if it is zero. So the joint transfer holds for any polynomial errors of degree at most \(D-K\) whose matching monomials share an admissible numbering. This is an argument for the next research entry to register, not a claim of this review. Missing a hole is necessary for such a numbering, not sufficient. An error's representative modulo the closure's degree-one members also matters, as the Decisive test's Attempt shows.

Clearing hole \(h\) from \(E_1\) by adding \(\sum_ic_iQ_i\) forces \(c_i=[i=h]\), so at most one hole can be cleared, and every linear representative uses at least four of the five holes. Attempt. Tried before posing, over the linear representatives.

  • A representative that clears no hole uses all five holes, and missing a hole is necessary for an admissible numbering: at \(t=\varnothing\) a monomial with a pigeon in the top hole has no dance.
  • The representatives that clear one hole are \(E_1+Q_h\), \(h\le4\), images of \(E'=E_1+Q_4\) under the simultaneous permutation of pigeons and holes \(0\) to \(4\), which fixes \(E_1\) and \(C\). So \(E'\) stands for all of them.
  • In any admissible numbering for \(E'\) the cleared hole \(4\) is the top hole: any other top hole holds the pigeon of some monomial of \(E'\), which at \(t=\varnothing\) cannot move.
The dance rule (Impagliazzo, Pudlák and Sgall, ECCC TR97-042, Definition 2.3, page 4) moves the pigeons in increasing order, each to a strictly larger hole, every step staying one-to-one. The matching monomials of \(E'\) are \(1\), \(x_{jj}\) and \(x_{4j}\) for \(j\le3\). Two pigeons in the top two used hole positions, with the top hole free, therefore dance only if the one in the higher position moves first: the other, moving first, takes the top hole and leaves no larger hole for it. The single-variable \(t\) below lie in \(B_1\), each having a free larger hole. With \(h\) the hole at the fourth position and \(h'\) at the third, the monomial \(x_{4h}\) with \(t=x_{hh'}\) needs pigeon \(4\) before pigeon \(h\); the monomial \(x_{hh}\) with \(t=x_{4h'}\) needs pigeon \(h\) before pigeon \(4\). So no numbering has the property for \(E'\), and the criterion decides no representative. The Attempt stops there: no recorded argument gives \(\operatorname{Ann}_C(E_1)\). Record search. Closure degree locality

Lemma (closure degree locality). On the functional pigeonhole system with \(m\) pigeons and \(N\) holes, over any field, let \(C_d\) be the degree-\(d\) closure of all axioms. If \(d\le D\le\lceil N/2\rceil\), then \(C_D\cap V_d=C_d\). In particular, for \(E\) of degree at most \(e\) and \(K+e\le d\), \(\{u\in V_K:uE\in C_D\}=\{u\in V_K:uE\in C_d\}\).

Proof. By Proposition 2.8 and Theorem 2.9 at degrees \(d\) and \(D\) (Impagliazzo, Pudlák and Sgall, as read in the functional-transfer entry), \(C_d\) is \(H_d\) plus the lift of \(K_d=\operatorname{span}(B_d\setminus T_d)\), and \(C_D\) likewise, \(H_d\) being the span of the non-matching monomials of degree at most \(d\). Reduction modulo \(H\) is the projection onto matching monomials, so a polynomial \(f\) of degree at most \(d\) has its non-matching part in \(H_d\) and its matching part in \(\operatorname{span}(T_d)\). The functional-transfer entry's Setting shows that \(B_d=\{x_a\in B_D:|a|\le d\}\) and that an element of \(\operatorname{span}(T_d)\) has the same expansion in \(B_d\) and in \(B_D\), so \(K_D\cap\operatorname{span}(T_d)=K_d\). Hence \(f\in C_D\) exactly when its matching part lies in \(K_d\), that is, when \(f\in C_d\). The kernel statement is the case \(f=uE\), of degree at most \(K+e\le d\). \(\square\)

Against the record. The functional-transfer entry's Setting proves the case \(d=K\) (“\(C\cap V_K\) is \(H\cap V_K\) plus the lift of \(K_K\)”) by the same argument. The lemma is that degree fact at a general \(d\), registered as refining it.

Hypotheses, each with its step.

  • \(d\le D\le\lceil N/2\rceil\): Proposition 2.8 and Theorem 2.9 at degrees \(d\) and \(D\), for the bases and the closures' descriptions.
  • For the kernel form, \(\deg(uE)\le d\), implied by \(K+e\le d\).
  • The number of pigeons and the field: any, as in the cited basis.

Degenerate cases. \(d=D\): trivial. \(E=0\): both kernels are \(V_K\). \(d=0\): \(C_0=0\), no axiom having degree \(0\), so the lemma says \(C_D\cap V_0=0\), that is, \(C_D\) is proper.

Nonvacuity. Six pigeons, five holes, \(D=3=\lceil5/2\rceil\), \(d=2\), \(K=1\), \(e=1\): \(1+1\le2\le3\). The dense errors below are kernels at \(D=3\) that, by the lemma, are those of the degree-\(2\) closure. Plainest bound. Without the lemma, \(C_d\subseteq C_D\cap V_d\) gives only one inclusion.

Baseline. Without an idea: \(C_d\subseteq C_D\cap V_d\). The lemma adds equality below half the holes, the recorded degree fact at a general degree.
