Top-degree linear killer and saving monotonicity

17 October 2026 · Refutation and working proof; conjecture and finite check over F_2 · Top-degree killers. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, low reasoning).

Where we stand. Unchanged: a research entry on the head item at its spell boundary; the open statements are unchanged

Earlier entries. The item's latest entries are the dense-linear entry, whose follow-up names “the basis expansions of the exceptional products \(x_{p,N-3}x_{q,N-2}\)”, and the functional-transfer entry.

Owed attempt. The dense-linear entry named the reviewer's route for a proof of conj:linear-kernel-transfer at \(K=1\), \(D=2\), through the basis expansions of the exceptional products. It was not made, because the falsification test came first: run across board sizes before a proof was invested in, it refuted the conjecture at three holes, so a proof of it at \(K=1\) cannot exist. The expansion route would bear on the corrected statement below only through a different argument.

Best outcome. A killer the pigeon axioms add to a linear error beyond every domain model, on an unbounded family, with a joint saving it produces. At the goal's own parameters it would give nothing directly, the boards being far from Pang's or Braun's; it would show whether proper closures can be a source of admitted savings at all. The recorded results to beat are lem:admissible-numbering-transfer, check:dense-linear-kernels and ex:support-saving-not-inherited.

General statement. lem:saving-monotonicity: over any field, enlarging the kernels of a family of error maps never raises its saving, so modulo a closure \(C\) containing a subspace \(H\) the saving of errors is at most the saving of the spaces \(\operatorname{Ann}_H(E_i')\cap V_K\), for every choice of representatives. ex:top-degree-linear-killer refutes conj:linear-kernel-transfer at three holes. conj:representative-sum-transfer: over \(\mathbb F_2\), below half the holes, a linear error's kernel modulo \(C\) is the sum over its linear representatives of their domain kernels, plus \(C\cap V_K\). check:top-degree-partition-kernels gives the excesses and the sum equality at the cases computed.

A refutation at three holes

Setting. The functional pigeonhole system (Booleanity, hole and functionality axioms, pigeon axioms \(Q_i=1-\sum_jx_{ij}\), multilinear ring) with four pigeons and three holes, at \(D=2=\lceil3/2\rceil\) and \(K=1\); \(C\) is the degree-\(2\) closure of all axioms, \(H\) that of the hole and functionality axioms, spanned by the non-matching monomials, and \(C\cap V_1=C_1=\operatorname{span}\{Q_i\}\) by lem:closure-degree-locality (\(2\le\lceil3/2\rceil\)).

Refutation (top-degree linear killer). Over any field, \((1-x_{12}-x_{22})(x_{10}-x_{21}+c\,x_{22})\equiv x_{10}Q_2-x_{21}Q_1\) modulo \(H\) for every scalar \(c\). Over \(\mathbb F_2\), with \(E=x_{10}+x_{21}+x_{22}\) and \(u=1+x_{12}+x_{22}\), this gives \(u\in\operatorname{Ann}_C(E)\); the kernel \(\operatorname{Ann}_C(E)\cap V_1\) has dimension \(7\), while the largest \(\operatorname{Ann}_H(E')\cap V_1+C\cap V_1\) over the \(16\) linear representatives \(E'\equiv E\) is \(6\), and \(u\) lies in none of them. So conj:linear-kernel-transfer, an \(\mathbb F_2\) statement whose evidence was one size with five holes, is false at three holes.

Proof. Modulo \(H\), a product of two variables in one row or one column is zero, and \(x^2=x\). The factor \(1-x_{12}-x_{22}\) kills \(x_{22}\): \(x_{22}-x_{12}x_{22}-x_{22}^2=0\). On the rest, \((1-x_{12}-x_{22})(x_{10}-x_{21})=x_{10}-x_{21}+x_{12}x_{21}-x_{10}x_{22}\), the products \(x_{12}x_{10}\) and \(x_{22}x_{21}\) being zero. Also \(x_{10}Q_2=x_{10}-x_{10}x_{21}-x_{10}x_{22}\) (dropping \(x_{10}x_{20}\)) and \(x_{21}Q_1=x_{21}-x_{21}x_{10}-x_{21}x_{12}\) (dropping \(x_{21}x_{11}\)), so \(x_{10}Q_2-x_{21}Q_1=x_{10}-x_{21}-x_{10}x_{22}+x_{12}x_{21}\), the terms \(x_{10}x_{21}\) cancelling. Both products have degree \(2\le D\) and lie in \(C\). The dimensions are computed over \(\mathbb F_2\): witness.json replays the error from linear_sizes.py's seed (there \(E+Q_3\) and \(u+Q_3\), which leave every kernel unchanged), checks \(uE\in C\) by an elimination independent of tools/pc_closure.py, finds \(u\) in none of the \(16\) representatives' domain sides, and gives \(C\)-side \(7\) by both routes against the best domain side \(6\). \(\square\)

Structural reason. The killer uses two pigeon axioms at once: the cross term \(x_{10}x_{21}\) occurs in both \(x_{10}Q_2\) and \(x_{21}Q_1\) and cancels between them, while a single representative \(E+q\) absorbs a combination of pigeon axioms into the error only once. So the reason applies to every transfer statement that compares with one representative at a time, such as conj:linear-kernel-transfer; it does not apply to single monomial errors, where lem:functional-killer-transfer proves transfer at every \(D\le\lceil N/2\rceil\), the top included, nor to monomial families with one admissible numbering (lem:admissible-numbering-transfer), nor to the sum over representatives, which the computed cases match.

Hypotheses, each with its step.

  • Three holes, for this pair: for the family \(u=1+S_1+S_2\), \(E=x_{10}+x_{21}+S_2\) with \(S_p=\sum_{j\ge2}x_{pj}\), which is this pair at \(n=3\), the same computation leaves \(\sum_{j\ne k\ge2}x_{1j}x_{2k}\), zero only at \(n=3\); for the literal \(u\), \(E\) above at \(n\ge4\) the leftover is \(\sum_{k\ge3}(x_{10}x_{2k}+x_{21}x_{1k})\).
  • The field: any, for the identity; \(\mathbb F_2\) for the dimension computation and for the conjecture refuted.
  • \(D\ge2\): the products \(x_{10}Q_2\), \(x_{21}Q_1\) lie in the closure.
At more holes, check:top-degree-partition-kernels finds killers of the same kind by computation.

Degenerate cases. The identity needs pigeons \(1\), \(2\) and holes \(0,1,2\); a board with fewer holes has \(D=2>\lceil n/2\rceil\), outside the conjecture's range.

Nonvacuity. The board satisfies the conjecture's hypotheses: \(n+1=4\) pigeons, \(n=3\), \(D=2\le\lceil3/2\rceil\), \(K+1\le D\). Plainest bound. The containment gives the \(C\)-side at least every domain side; the bare count gives the excess at most \(\dim V_1-\dim(C\cap V_1)=13-4=9\) minus the domain part. Tried. Both on this instance: \(7\ge6\) and \(7-6\le9\); the proof's own step used alone, the identity, gives \(u\in\operatorname{Ann}_C(E)\), and the excess only once \(u\) is shown outside the domain sides, which is the computed part.

Saving monotonicity

Lemma (saving monotonicity). Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional space over any field and \(A_i\subseteq B_i\subseteq V\) subspaces, \(i=1,\dots,M\). Write \(s(A)=\sum_i\operatorname{codim}A_i-\operatorname{codim}\bigcap_iA_i\). Then \(s(B)\le s(A)\); for \(M=2\), \(s(A)=\operatorname{codim}(A_1+A_2)\). Consequently, let \(C\) be a degree-\(D\) PC closure, \(H\subseteq C\) any subspace, \(E_i\) errors of degree at most \(D-K\), and \(E_i'\) representatives with \(E_i-E_i'\in C\) of degree at most \(D-K\). Then the saving of the multiplication maps \(V_K\to V_D/C\) (summed ranks minus stacked rank) is at most \(s\) of the spaces \(\operatorname{Ann}_H(E_i')\cap V_K+C\cap V_K\), and so at most \(s\) of the spaces \(\operatorname{Ann}_H(E_i')\cap V_K\), where \(\operatorname{Ann}_H(E')=\{u:uE'\in H\}\).

Proof. It suffices to enlarge one space, \(A_1\) to \(B_1\), by \(\delta=\dim B_1-\dim A_1\). Then the first codimension falls by \(\delta\). Writing \(R=\bigcap_{i\ge2}A_i\), the map \((B_1\cap R)/(A_1\cap R)\to B_1/A_1\) is injective, so the intersection grows by at most \(\delta\) and its codimension falls by at most \(\delta\); hence \(s\) does not rise. For \(M=2\), \(\operatorname{codim}A_1+\operatorname{codim}A_2-\operatorname{codim}(A_1\cap A_2)=\operatorname{codim}(A_1+A_2)\). For the consequence, the rank of \(u\mapsto uE_i\) modulo \(C\) is \(\operatorname{codim}\operatorname{Ann}_C(E_i)\) in \(V_K\), and the stacked rank is \(\operatorname{codim}\bigcap_i\operatorname{Ann}_C(E_i)\). Then \(\operatorname{Ann}_H(E_i')\cap V_K\subseteq\operatorname{Ann}_H(E_i')\cap V_K+C\cap V_K\subseteq\operatorname{Ann}_C(E_i)\): for \(uE_i'\in H\subseteq C\), \(uE_i=uE_i'+u(E_i-E_i')\), the second term a closure member times \(u\) within degree \(D\); and \(cE_i\in C\) for \(c\in C\cap V_K\), the closure being closed under multiplication by variables up to degree \(D\). Two applications of the first part give both bounds. \(\square\)

Against the record. ex:support-saving-not-inherited says that the containment of the domain closure in the proper one “gives only that each rank and the stacked rank can drop”. The lemma corrects that sentence: the saving drops too, for every family and every choice of representatives. Its recorded figures obey it, \(11\le54\). lem:domain-model-stacked-rank's clause that domain savings “carry into Pang's proper quotient” was corrected by that example; the lemma gives the general inequality in the other direction. lem:factor-ideal-domination and lem:restriction-rank-overlap, which the resemblance check listed, are other statements on kernels and restriction ranks (antitone ranks and submodularity in ideals); neither is a more general version or a special case. The band review's Rank normalization stated an equality with a nonnegative correction under joint transfer; the inequality needs no transfer.

Hypotheses, each with its step.

  • \(A_i\subseteq B_i\): the injectivity step. The field and \(M\): any.
  • For the consequence, \(C\) a closure (closed under multiplication by variables within degree \(D\)), \(H\subseteq C\) any subspace, \(\deg E_i\le D-K\) and \(\deg(E_i-E_i')\le D-K\): the products \(uE_i'\), \(u(E_i-E_i')\) and \(cE_i\) stay in degree \(D\).

Degenerate cases. \(M=1\): \(s=0\) on both sides. \(A_i=B_i\): equality. \(B_i=V\): \(s(B)=0\le s(A)\).

Nonvacuity. The \(45\) pairs of four-by-three hit errors in pair_saving.json, with \(H\) the hole and functionality closure and \(D=2\), \(K=1\): the \(33\) pairs whose errors are not congruent modulo \(\operatorname{span}\{Q_i\}\) have saving \(4\) modulo \(C\) against \(5\) at the best representatives, and the \(12\) congruent pairs (all of the tied ones, rep_sum_more.json) have \(6\) against \(6\), one kernel twice. The direction “never raises” is the lemma itself and is not tested by these runs. Plainest bound. The summed-rank bound gives each saving at most the smaller single rank, \(6\); the lemma gives the domain value, \(5\) on the \(33\) pairs.

Baseline. Without an idea: each rank and the stacked rank can drop under containment. The lemma adds the saving's direction; it is elementary, the cokernel of \(V/\bigcap A_i\to\bigoplus V/A_i\) mapping onto the one for the \(B_i\).

Top-degree partition kernels

Setup. Scripts in research/results/common_multiplier_linear_sizes_20261017/, each committed before its run, on the functional pigeonhole system over \(\mathbb F_2\) with \(n+1\) pigeons and \(n\) holes. The single excess of a linear error is the dimension of \(\operatorname{Ann}_C(E)\cap V_K\) minus the largest \(\dim(\operatorname{Ann}_H(E')\cap V_K+C\cap V_K)\) over its linear representatives.

  • linear_sizes.py, at \(D=2\), \(K=1\), \(n=3\) to \(6\): two diagonal sums, \(24\) random errors, five pairs (one at \(n=6\)).
  • row_search.py, exhaustive over errors on the constant and the rows of pigeons \(\{1,2\}\) (\(n=3,4,5\)) and \(\{0,1,2\}\) (\(n=4\)).
  • top_search.py, the partition errors \(E_A=\sum_{j\in A}x_{1j}+\sum_{j\notin A}x_{2j}\), which by the hole symmetry depend only on \(|A|\), at the top degree \(D=\lceil n/2\rceil\), \(K=D-1\), \(n=3,4,5\); independent_top.py recomputes it without tools/pc_closure.py; top_n6.py predicts \(n=6\).
  • rep_sum.py and rep_sum_more.py compare \(\operatorname{Ann}_C(E)\) with \(S(E)\), the sum over all representatives of their domain kernels, plus \(C\cap V_K\).
The independent route describes \(C_d\) as \(T=\operatorname{span}(H_d,\ mQ_i:\deg m\le d-1)\). Clearly \(T\subseteq C_d\). If \(p\in T\) has degree at most \(d-1\), then \(p\in C_d\cap V_{d-1}=C_{d-1}\), which by induction is the corresponding span at \(d-1\), so \(xp\in T\) for each variable \(x\); hence \(T\) is closed and equals \(C_d\). This uses lem:closure-degree-locality at every level \(d\le\lceil n/2\rceil\).

Result. From the saved outputs:

  • Below the top (\(D=2\), \(n=5,6\)): every error tested has single excess \(0\): \(28\) singles and five or one pairs per size, and all \(2047\) errors on two rows at six by five.
  • At \(D=2\) as the top (\(n=3,4\)): one random error of \(28\) at four by three; \(12\) of \(127\) and \(12\) of \(511\) errors on two rows, and \(72\) of \(8191\) on three rows at five by four, all with single excess \(1\).
  • Partition errors at the top: single excess by \(|A|\) is \(0,1,1,0\) at \(n=3\); \(0,0,1,0,0\) at \(n=4\); \(0,0,12,12,0,0\) at \(n=5\), \(D=3\), \(K=2\) (\(C\)-side \(332\) against \(320\)); the independent route agrees at every entry. At \(n=6\), \(D=3\), \(K=2\), the committed prediction passed: \(|A|=3\) gives \(542\) against \(527\), excess \(15\), and \(|A|=0\) gives \(469\) against \(469\).
  • Representative sums: \(\dim S(E)=\dim\operatorname{Ann}_C(E)\) for the ten listed four-by-three hits (\(7\) against single best \(6\)), the ten listed five-by-four hits, the partition error \(|A|=2\) among them (\(8\) against \(7\)), the six-by-five partition errors \(|A|=2,3\) (\(332\) against \(320\)) and the seven-by-six one \(|A|=3\) (\(542\)). The containment \(S(E)\subseteq\operatorname{Ann}_C(E)\) is asserted in code for the last; for the others it rests on the lemma's proof. Not covered: the two unlisted four-by-three hits, the two unlisted five-by-four two-row hits and the \(72\) three-row hits.

Controls. \(x_{00}\) gives excess \(0\) at every size and \(S(x_{00})=\operatorname{Ann}_C(x_{00})\); \(x_{00}+Q_0\) has a trivial-representative domain side below its \(C\)-side at every size (\(6,8,10,12\) against \(9,12,15,18\) for \(n=3\) to \(6\), linear_sizes.json); the transported-killer instance gives excess \(1\); the six-by-five diagonal sums give \(C\)-side \(7\) at \(D=2\) as at \(D=3\), which lem:closure-degree-locality predicts. rep_sum.py's positive control, the sum at least the best single side, can hardly fail; rep_sum_more.py's checks that each listed hit reproduces single excess \(1\). Failed runs are kept: the first independent run, whose hand-written reduce returned non-canonical remainders and gave negative excesses (independent_top_run1.json); pair_saving.py's first two runs, which failed their own controls by taking the domain saving as a maximum and then by asserting a gap that representative sums close (logs exceptional-products-8906a7ce8d and -1327a09273); and two launches of rep_sum_more.py refused or failed before computing (an uncommitted script, then a pickling error).

Nonvacuity of the check. Each comparison is a dimension that one extra killer changes, and the excesses found show the code sees them. Plainest bound. Containment gives every excess at least \(0\) and every representative sum at most the \(C\)-side; neither decides any entry.

The corrected conjecture

Conjecture (representative sum transfer). Over \(\mathbb F_2\), on the functional pigeonhole system with \(n+1\) pigeons and \(n\) holes, at \(D\le\lceil n/2\rceil\) and \(K+1\le D\), every single linear error \(E\) has \(\operatorname{Ann}_C(E)\cap V_K=\sum_{E'}\operatorname{Ann}_H(E')\cap V_K+C\cap V_K\), the sum over its linear representatives \(E'\equiv E\) modulo \(C\cap V_1\). The containment \(\supseteq\) always holds. Both sides are unchanged under \(E\mapsto E+q\), \(q\in C\cap V_1\), and \(E\equiv0\) gives \(V_K\) on both. Evidence: the equality wherever the single excess is \(0\) (trivially) and at the \(23\) errors with positive single excess on which the sum was computed, at four sizes. It refines conj:linear-kernel-transfer, which took the largest single representative, covered families of errors and is refuted; this one covers single errors only.

New mathematics. ex:top-degree-linear-killer: at four pigeons and three holes the identity \((1-x_{12}-x_{22})(x_{10}-x_{21})\equiv x_{10}Q_2-x_{21}Q_1\), valid over any field, gives over \(\mathbb F_2\) a killer outside every single representative's domain side, refuting conj:linear-kernel-transfer. lem:saving-monotonicity: modulo a closure containing a subspace \(H\), the saving of errors of degree at most \(D-K\) is at most the saving of their \(H\)-kernels, for every choice of representatives, over any field. check:top-degree-partition-kernels: over \(\mathbb F_2\), single-representative excesses occur at the top degree \(D=\lceil n/2\rceil\), \(K=D-1\), for \(n=3,4,5,6\), and not below the top at \(n=5,6\) in the errors tested; at the \(23\) positive cases where it was computed, the kernel is the sum of representatives' domain kernels. conj:representative-sum-transfer states that sum form for single linear errors.

Plainest bound. The containment \(S(E)\subseteq\operatorname{Ann}_C(E)\) is the plainest bound; it gives one direction only. Own statements. \(H\) is the degree-\(D\) vanishing space of the partial matchings \(X\) in the multilinear ring: every non-matching monomial vanishes on \(X\); and if a multilinear \(f=\sum c_Tx_T\) of degree at most \(D\) vanishes on \(X\), then for each matching monomial \(m\), \(0=f(1_m)=\sum_{T\subseteq m}c_T\), the sum over matching \(T\) since non-matching ones vanish at \(1_m\), and \(X\) being downward closed, induction on \(|m|\) gives \(c_m=0\); the quotient \(U=V_K/(H\cap V_K)\) is the same in this presentation. With that, lem:saving-monotonicity and lem:domain-model-stacked-rank together answer the savings question for the pure \(H\)-kernels: the \(H\)-savings are union-of-supports counts and bound the savings modulo \(C\). They do not decide the conjecture, which is about kernels, nor whether the mixed spaces \(\operatorname{Ann}_H(E')+C\cap V_K\) have savings of another kind.

General statement. lem:native-rectangle-upper-bound: on the cube, for errors supported on nonempty subcubes, \(\sum_iN_{a_i}(\max(K-L,0))\) old functionals, sums of point evaluations over translated Hamming balls, detect the stacked kernel on \(V_K\) in rectangle forms at slack \(L\); for one error the least number lies between \(N_a(K)/N_a(L)\) and \(N_a(\max(K-L,0))\). check:native-upper-ranks verifies the construction for \(a\le7\), \(K\le3\), and the exact least number \(\lfloor a/2\rfloor+1\) at \(K=2\), \(L=1\) for \(a=3\) to \(9\).

Native rectangle upper bound

Setting. Over a field \(k\), \(J_{D'}\) is the degree-\(D'\) part of the ideal of the Boolean axioms \(x_i^2-x_i\) in \(n\) variables, so that within degree \(D'\) membership is vanishing on the cube \(\{0,1\}^n\); an old functional is a linear functional on \(V_{D'}\) vanishing on \(J_{D'}\). Following lem:native-detection-count, for errors \(E_1,\dots,E_s\) of degree at most \(e\), \(U=V_K\) and slack \(L\) with \(e+K+L\le D'\), old functionals \(\mu_1,\dots,\mu_m\) detect the stacked kernel \(\ker T\), \(T(u)=([E_iu])_i\), when \(\ker T\) equals the set of \(u\) with \(\mu_j(E_iuv)=0\) for all \(i\), \(j\) and \(v\in V_L\). \(N_a(d)=\sum_{k\le d}\binom ak\), and \(B_d\subseteq\{0,1\}^a\) is the set of points of weight at most \(d\).

Lemma (native rectangle upper bound). Let each \(E_i\in V_e\) be a polynomial whose function on the cube has as support a nonempty subcube \(A_i\) of dimension \(a_i\), that is, the set where some coordinates take fixed values; over \(\mathbb F_2\) an affine subspace with an affine coordinate system serves as well (as for Pang's errors \(E_i=Pg_i\) with linear inputs, \(A_i=\{q_1=\dots=q_t=0,\ g_i=1\}\), in lem:native-functional-growth's proof). Let \(\phi_i:\{0,1\}^{a_i}\to A_i\) be the coordinate map (over \(\mathbb F_2\), an affine one), and for each \(y\) of weight at most \(\max(K-L,0)\) let \(\lambda_{i,y}=\sum_{z\in y\oplus B_L}E_i(\phi_i(z))^{-1}\delta_{\phi_i(z)}\), \(\oplus\) the coordinatewise sum modulo \(2\). These \(\sum_iN_{a_i}(\max(K-L,0))\le s\,N_n(\max(K-L,0))\) functionals are old and detect \(\ker T\). For \(s=1\) and \(A=A_1\) of dimension \(a\), the least number \(m_{\min}\) of old functionals detecting \(\ker T\) at slack \(L\) satisfies \(N_a(K)/N_a(L)\le m_{\min}\le N_a(\max(K-L,0))\); for \(K\ge L\), \(N_a(K)\le N_a(L)N_a(K-L)\), and the ratio of the two bounds tends to \(\binom KL\) as \(a\to\infty\).

Proof. A point evaluation vanishes on the Boolean ideal, so each \(\lambda_{i,y}\) is old. On the cube, \(E_iu\) vanishes exactly when \(u\) vanishes on \(A_i\), so \(\ker T=\{u:u|_{A_i}=0\text{ for all }i\}\), and for \(u\in\ker T\) every form is zero (each \(E_iuv\) has degree at most \(e+K+L\le D'\)). Conversely suppose all the forms vanish. Then \(\lambda_{i,y}(E_iuv)=\sum_{z\in y\oplus B_L}(u\circ\phi_i)(z)(v\circ\phi_i)(z)\), the weights cancelling \(E_i\). The map \(\phi_i\) preserves degree (it substitutes constants for the fixed coordinates; over \(\mathbb F_2\) an affine map), and the restrictions of \(V_L\) to \(A_i\) are all functions of degree at most \(L\) on \(\{0,1\}^{a_i}\).

  • The set \(y\oplus B_L\) is independent for degree \(L\): the evaluation of the multilinear monomials \(x_T\), \(|T|\le L\), at the points \(1_R\), \(|R|\le L\), is \([T\subseteq R]\), unitriangular over any field, so evaluation on \(B_L\) is bijective; the map \(z\mapsto y\oplus z\) is the substitution \(x_i\mapsto1-x_i\) for \(i\) in the support of \(y\), which preserves degree. So as \(v\) ranges over \(V_L\), \((v\circ\phi_i(z))_{z\in y\oplus B_L}\) takes every value, and the forms give \(u\circ\phi_i=0\) on \(y\oplus B_L\).
  • The union of the \(y\oplus B_L\) contains \(B_K\): a point of weight \(w\le K\) is a centre when \(w\le K-L\), and otherwise lies in \(y\oplus B_L\) for \(y\) obtained by removing \(w-(K-L)\le L\) of its coordinates; when \(K\le L\), \(B_K\subseteq B_L\) and the one centre \(y=0\) suffices.
  • \(B_K\) determines degree-\(K\) functions, by the same unitriangularity; this is lem:all-field-approximate-majority-certifier-barrier's statement that a nonzero multilinear polynomial of degree at most \(K\) meets the radius-\(K\) Hamming ball, there over any field. So \(u|_{A_i}=0\) for every \(i\).
For \(s=1\), the lower bound is lem:native-detection-count (a), \(r\le m\dim Z_L\), with \(r=\dim V_K|_A=N_a(K)\) and \(Z_L\), the span of \(Ev\) modulo \(J_{e+L}\), isomorphic through \(v\mapsto Ev\) to \(V_L|_A\), of dimension \(N_a(L)\). Every set of size at most \(K\) is a union of one of size at most \(L\) and one of size at most \(K-L\), so \(N_a(K)\le N_a(L)N_a(K-L)\); the leading terms \(a^L/L!\cdot a^{K-L}/(K-L)!\) against \(a^K/K!\) give the limit \(\binom KL\). \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step.

  • The cube (the Boolean axioms in \(J\)): membership as vanishing, and point evaluations as old functionals. The field: any, with subcube supports; \(\mathbb F_2\) only for affine supports, which need affine coordinates of \(\{0,1\}^n\).
  • Each \(E_i\) supported on a nonempty subcube: the weights \(E_i^{-1}\) on the support and the coordinate map preserving degree.
  • \(e+K+L\le D'\): the forms are defined on \(E_iuv\). Nothing else is used: the lemma holds at every \(K\), \(L\), \(n\), \(s\).

Degenerate cases. \(L=0\): \(B_0=\{0\}\), the functionals are weighted point evaluations at the \(N_a(K)\) points of \(B_K\), and the bounds agree, \(m_{\min}=N_a(K)\). \(K\le L\): one functional per support, so for \(s=1\), \(m_{\min}=1\). An empty \(A_i\) (over \(\mathbb F_2\), an input in the span of the \(q_k\)): \(E_i=0\) and no functional is needed for it.

Nonvacuity. Over \(\mathbb F_2\), \(n=5\), \(E=x_5\) (support the subcube \(x_5=1\), \(a=4\)), \(e=1\), \(K=2\), \(L=1\), \(D'=4\), so \(e+K+L=4\le D'\): the lemma gives \(N_4(1)=5\) functionals against the lower bound \(\lceil11/5\rceil=3\); native_upper.json gives rank \(11=N_4(2)\) for the five ball translates on \(\{0,1\}^4\), and exact_k2.json rank \(11\) with three sets. Over \(\mathbb F_2\) every old functional is a sum of point evaluations, and its forms on \(E\cdot\) depend only on its points in \(A\), so searching sets in \(\{0,1\}^a\) loses nothing. Plainest bound. lem:native-detection-count (c) at \(s=1\) gives \(m\le r=11\), and its (a) gives \(m\ge3\). Tried. Both on this instance; the lemma's covering step alone gives \(5\).

Multiplication-certified multilinear repairs are scalar

17 October 2026 · Working proof, for survival certified along multiplication (a corollary of lem:module-repair-factorization) · Multilinear repairs. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, low reasoning).

Chosen. This entry develops multilinear-proof-repair ahead of the head. It bears on joint-error-savings: a repair acting on several proof lines at once could kill errors carried by different lines below their least common scalar repair. It comes first because the user asked about it during the duality item's cycle, and because it is the kind of transformation that lem:module-repair-factorization, which settled single-line module repairs certified semilinearly over a ring map, left outside.

Best outcome. At the goal's own parameters, a repair of a product of Pang's proof lines, acting on the lines jointly, that kills the errors carried by the factors below the least scalar common repair; the recorded results to beat are thm:certified-repair-composition, which builds a scalar repair at Pang's \(K\), and lem:module-repair-factorization.

General statement. cor:multilinear-repair-scalar: over any field, a repair of a product of any set of proof lines by an element of a module over the tensor power of the ring, whose survival is certified by a map into the ring compatible along multiplication, gives a scalar common repair of all the lines' errors at parameter \(K+\sigma\), on the window \(\deg(a_jm)\le D-K\), against the degree-\(D'\) closure; conversely every scalar common repair is one, with \(\sigma=0\). For the least value of \(K+\sigma\), with \(D'=D+\sigma\), multiplication-certified multilinear repairs and scalar common repairs are equally strong.

Multilinear repairs are scalar

Setting. As in lem:module-repair-factorization: a field \(k\), \(R=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]\), axioms \(a_1,\dots,a_r\), \(V_d\) the polynomials of degree at most \(d\). Let \(\Lambda\) be any set of proof lines, finite or infinite, \(R'=R^{\otimes\Lambda}=k[x^{(t)}_i:t\in\Lambda,\ i\le n]\), \(x^{(t)}\) a copy of the variables for line \(t\), and \(\mu:R'\to R\) the multiplication map, \(x^{(t)}_i\mapsto x_i\), a \(k\)-algebra map of degree bound \(1\). Line \(t\) carries errors \(E_{t,1},\dots\in R\) and a protected class \(w_t\), with \(w_t=1\) for all but finitely many \(t\); write \(E_{t,i}^{(t)}\) for the error in the copy of line \(t\), \(w'=\prod_tw_t^{(t)}\) of degree \(b=\sum_t\deg w_t\), and give \(R'\) the axioms \(a_j^{(t_0)}\) of one fixed copy \(t_0\) (more copies' axioms may be added; they are not used). A multilinear repair is a module repair, in lem:module-repair-factorization's sense, in a filtered \(R'\)-module \(N\) with a degree-\(D\) pseudo-submodule \(J_N\): \(\nu\in F_KN\), \(b+K\le D\), \(\deg(w'E_{t,i}^{(t)})+K\le D\), soundness \(a_j^{(t_0)}m\nu\in J_N\) for \(\deg(a_j^{(t_0)}m)\le D-K\), killing \(w'E_{t,i}^{(t)}\nu\in J_N\), and survival \(w'\nu\notin J_N\). Its survival is certified along multiplication when a linear \(\beta:F_DN\to V_{D'}\) has \(\beta(F_jN)\subseteq V_{j+\sigma}\), \(D+\sigma\le D'\), \(\beta(J_N)\subseteq J\), \(\beta(x^{(t)}_iu)-x_i\beta(u)\in J\) for \(u\in F_{D-1}N\) and every \(t\), and \(\beta(w'\nu)\notin J\), where \(J\) is the old degree-\(D'\) closure.

Corollary (multilinear repairs are scalar). If \(\nu\) is a multilinear repair whose survival is certified along multiplication, then \(f=\beta(\nu)\in V_{K+\sigma}\) is a scalar common repair of all the lines' errors at parameter \(K+\sigma\), on the window \(\deg(a_jm)\le D-K\), against \(J\), with protected class \(\prod_tw_t\): \(a_jmf\in J\) for \(\deg(a_jm)\le D-K\), \(\bigl(\prod_tw_t\bigr)E_{t,i}f\in J\) for every \(t\), \(i\), and \(\bigl(\prod_tw_t\bigr)f\notin J\). Conversely, a scalar common repair \(f\) of all the errors with that protected class, at parameter \(K\) on that window, is the multilinear repair \(\nu=f^{(t_0)}\in N=R'\), certified along multiplication by \(\beta=\mu\) restricted to degree \(D\), with \(J_N=\mu^{-1}(J)\cap V'_D\) and \(\sigma=0\).

Proof. The first part is lem:module-repair-factorization (b) with the ring \(R'\), a polynomial ring over \(k\) (in infinitely many variables when \(\Lambda\) is infinite; (b)'s proof is an induction over monomials, each of which involves finitely many copies, so it applies unchanged), the algebra \(S=R\) with its degree filtration, \(\phi=\mu\), \(T=1\) and \(J'=J\): \(J\) is closed under multiplication by each \(\mu(x^{(t)}_i)=x_i\) within degree \(D'\), and the hypotheses of (b) are those listed. Its conclusion is \(\mu(a_j^{(t_0)}m)f\in J\), \(\mu(w'E_{t,i}^{(t)})f\in J\) and \(\mu(w')f\notin J\), and \(\mu(a_j^{(t_0)}m)=a_j\,\mu(m)\), \(\mu(w')=\prod_tw_t\), \(\mu(E_{t,i}^{(t)})=E_{t,i}\); as \(m\) ranges over the monomials of \(R'\) with \(\deg(a_j^{(t_0)}m)\le D-K\), \(\mu(m)\) ranges over the monomials of \(R\) with \(\deg(a_j\mu(m))\le D-K\), since \(m''\mapsto m''^{(t_0)}\) is a degree-preserving section of \(\mu\) on monomials. Conversely, for \(N=R'\) with the degree filtration and \(J_N=\mu^{-1}(J)\cap V'_D\), a pseudo-submodule because \(\mu\) is a ring map preserving degree and \(J\) is closed under variables within degree \(D'\ge D\), \(\nu=f^{(t_0)}\) has \(\mu(g\nu)=\mu(g)f\), so soundness, killing and survival of \(\nu\) are those of \(f\), the degrees agreeing because \(\deg(w'E_{t,i}^{(t)})=\deg\bigl(\prod_tw_t\cdot E_{t,i}\bigr)\) in these domains; \(\beta=\mu\) is compatible exactly. \(\square\)

Structural reason. Certification along \(\mu\) forgets which copy an error or an axiom sits in: every copy's variables act on the certificate as the old variables do. A module over \(R^{\otimes\Lambda}\) read through \(\mu\) is therefore an \(R\)-module, and lem:module-repair-factorization makes its repairs scalar. The reason applies to every certificate compatible along one ring map to \(R\), whatever the number of copies or the size of the module, and not to certificates that keep the copies apart. For the same reason an infinite set of lines adds nothing over one line carrying all the errors \(E_{t,i}\) with protected class \(\prod_tw_t\): \(\mu\) sends every error into \(R\), and the conclusion depends only on that set of errors and that product.

Hypotheses, each with its step.

  • Survival certified along multiplication: the whole of the first part, through (b).
  • The axioms of one copy: soundness for the old system, since \(\mu\) maps the multiples of one copy's axioms onto all the old multiples; further copies' axioms are not used.
  • The degree bound \(D+\sigma\le D'\): (b)'s window. The pseudo-submodule property of \(J_N\) is used only in the converse; (b)'s proof uses the closure of \(J\), not of \(J_N\).
  • All but finitely many \(w_t=1\): \(w'\) is a polynomial. The field, the set of lines and the axioms: any.

Degenerate cases. One line: \(\mu\) is the identity and the corollary is (b) with \(S=R\). A line with no errors contributes only its protected class. All \(w_t=1\): the protected class is \(1\). \(\nu=0\) or \(J_N=F_DN\): no survival.

Nonvacuity. The converse is the part the record does not state; the forward part is (b) itself. Over \(\mathbb F_2\), \(n=2\), the Boolean axioms \(x_i^2+x_i\), two lines with errors \(E_1=x_1\) and \(E_2=x_2\), \(w_1=w_2=1\), \(D=D'=4\), \(K=2\), \(\sigma=0\), \(N=R'\), \(J_N=\mu^{-1}(J)\cap V'_4\), \(J\) the degree-\(4\) part of the Boolean ideal. The scalar repair \(f=(1+x_1)(1+x_2)\) gives \(\nu=f^{(1)}\); so does the element \(\nu'=(1+x^{(1)}_1)(1+x^{(2)}_2)\), which mixes the copies and has \(\mu(\nu')=f\). Soundness is exercised: the axiom multiples of degree at most \(D-K=2\) are the axioms themselves, and \(\mu\bigl((x^{(1)2}_j+x^{(1)}_j)\nu\bigr)=(x_j^2+x_j)(1+x_1)(1+x_2)\in J\); killing gives \(x_1f=x_2f=0\) on the cube, and survival \(f(0)=1\). Plainest bound. On the cube a common scalar repair must vanish where \(x_1=1\) or \(x_2=1\) and not everywhere, so its degree is at least the transversal number \(2\) of the supports (lem:transversal-killer-basis (c), with \(2+1\le D\)), which \(f\) meets; that bound already decides the instance's question.

Baseline. Without an idea, repairing each line separately by \(\nu_t\) and multiplying gives \(\prod_t\nu_t\), whose survival can fail: over \(\mathbb F_2\), \(n=1\), the Boolean axiom, \(w=1\), line \(1\) with \(E=x\) and line \(2\) with \(E=1+x\) have separate repairs \(1+x\) and \(x\), whose product lies in \(J\), and no common repair exists, since it would vanish on the whole cube (historical:ex:mixedfailure is the analogue for design corrections). Every scalar common repair is a multilinear one; the corollary adds the converse.

Against the record. The forward part is lem:module-repair-factorization (b) applied to the ring \(R^{\otimes\Lambda}\) and the map \(\mu\), which is a substitution of the copies with trivially certified image axioms, as thm:certified-repair-composition allows; the new parts are the reading for several lines, any number of them, and the converse. The resemblance check also listed lem:twisted-certificate-reduction, lem:twist-window-trade, lem:top-window-twist-scalar and lem:cyclic-repair-map: the twisted ones concern a matrix action on one line, and lem:cyclic-repair-map is the exact case of (a) for one line; none is a more general version or a special case.

New mathematics. cor:multilinear-repair-scalar: multilinear repairs of a product of any set of proof lines, by elements of any module over the tensor power of the ring with survival certified along multiplication, give scalar common repairs of all the lines' errors at parameter \(K+\sigma\) on the same window, and conversely; for the least \(K+\sigma\) with \(D'=D+\sigma\) the two are equally strong. Owed attempt. None was named: the item had no earlier entry.

Smallest case. The next attempt is the combined-error reading. If line \(t\) holds \(w_t+E_t\), the product line has protected class \(w=\prod_tw_t\) and error \(E_c=\prod_t(w_t+E_t)-\prod_tw_t\), and a repair of the product kills \(wE_c\). Every term of \(E_c\) contains some \(E_t\), so when the degrees fit a common repair of the factors' errors also repairs the product: the combined repair's least degree is at most the common one's, and the question is whether it can be smaller.

  • Tried here by hand in a domain model, \(J\) the vanishing ideal of a finite point set \(X\) within degree, with room. A repair of the product must vanish on \(\{p:w(p)\ne0,\ \prod_t(w_t+E_t)(p)\ne\prod_tw_t(p)\}\), a subset of the common repair's set \(\{p:w(p)\ne0,\ E_t(p)\ne0\text{ for some }t\}\). Over \(\mathbb F_2\) the two sets are equal: where \(w(p)=1\) each \(w_t(p)=1\), and \(\prod_t(1+E_t(p))=1\) only when every \(E_t(p)=0\). So over \(\mathbb F_2\), in domain models, the combined-error reading saves nothing.
  • Over \(\mathbb F_3\) the sets differ: \(n=1\), the Boolean axiom \(x^2-x\), \(w_1=w_2=1\), \(E_1=E_2=x\), \(D=2\). Then \(E_c=(1+x)^2-1=2x+x^2\equiv3x=0\) modulo \(x^2-x\), so \(E_c\in J\) and \(f=1\) repairs the product line (survival: \(w f=1\notin J\)). A common repair of \(E_1=x\) must vanish at \(x=1\) and not at \(x=0\), so its degree is \(1\), attained by \(1-x\). The saving comes from the cancellation \((1+E_1)(1+E_2)=1\) at \(x=1\), which needs characteristic other than \(2\); the instance is a case of the reviewer's suggestion below (\(E\) takes the value \(-2\) at \(x=1\)), checked here. It is the extreme case: \(E_c\in J\), so the product line is exact and needs no repair; it does not exercise a combined degree strictly between \(0\) and the common one.
  • The first draft's instance (over \(\mathbb F_2\), \(\tilde f=1\), \(\tilde g=0\)) had product protected class \(0\), which no repair survives; it showed nothing, as the reviewer found.
Plainest bound. In a domain model a repair's least degree is an interpolation degree on its vanishing set, and on the cube with monomial supports a transversal number (lem:transversal-killer-basis); the sets above give both readings' bounds, and on the \(\mathbb F_3\) instance degrees \(0\) and \(1\). Two readings remain: the combined-error reading and survival certified by product designs. In domain models the combined-error reading saves nothing over \(\mathbb F_2\) and can save through cancellations \(\prod_t(w_t+E_t)(p)=\prod_tw_t(p)\) in odd characteristic, as at \(\mathbb F_3\) above. The next attempt is that reading on an unbounded family in odd characteristic, which Pang's Theorem 4.3 allows in its Boolean \(\mathbb F_p\) setup for every prime \(p\), as cor:pang-observation-calibration records it (read here from that registered statement, not from Pang's text): whether such cancellations lower the least repair degree of a product line below the common repair of its factors. A combined-error repair is a scalar repair of the one error \(E_c\), so the attempt compares two scalar least degrees, that of \(E_c\) and the common one of the \(E_t\), to which thm:certified-repair-composition applies directly; first a domain-model witness with a combined degree strictly between \(0\) and the common one, then a proper closure, where the domain-model description stops.

Parity product lines: repair degree ⌈ℓ/2⌉ against ℓ on the cube, none saved on matchings

17 October 2026 · Working proof, in domain models in characteristic other than \(2\) for \(D\ge\ell+\lceil\ell/2\rceil\) · Parity product repair. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, low reasoning).

Chosen. This entry continues multilinear-proof-repair rather than the head, common-multiplier-duality. It bears on joint-error-savings: the item's open reading is whether a product line's combined error can be repaired below the common repair of its factors' errors, a saving that comes from how the errors combine and not from their supports. It comes first because the item's last entry named this attempt and made its extreme case only.

Best outcome. At the goal's own parameters, an unbounded family of product lines whose combined error has a repair of strictly smaller degree than any common repair of the factors' errors, in a proper closure of a system the goal uses; the recorded result to beat is lem:transversal-killer-basis, which fixes the common repair's degree on the cube, and cor:multilinear-repair-scalar, which excludes the multiplication-certified class.

Owed attempt. The last follow-up named: first a domain-model witness with a combined degree strictly between \(0\) and the common one, then a proper closure. The first is made: the proposition below gives an unbounded family on the cube, combined degree \(\lceil\ell/2\rceil\) against common degree \(\ell\), and its part (c) shows that on the pigeonhole matching domain the saving disappears. The proper closure is not made; the two domain statements came first, and the Smallest case below reduces its first instance to four conditions on one closure.

General statement. prop:parity-product-repair: over any field of characteristic other than \(2\), on the cube \(\{0,1\}^n\) with \(1\le\ell\le n\) lines of protected class \(1\) and errors \(E_t=-2x_t\), every common repair of the errors has degree at least \(\ell\), attained when \(D\ge\ell+1\), while the product line's combined error has no repair of degree below \(\lceil\ell/2\rceil\) and one of that degree when \(D\ge\ell+\lceil\ell/2\rceil\), a saving in the repair's degree that needs the larger closure degree; on the pigeonhole matching domain, with diagonal errors \(-2x_{tt}\), both least degrees are \(\lceil\ell/2\rceil\).

Parity product repair

Setting. A field \(k\) of characteristic other than \(2\), \(R=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]\), the Boolean axioms \(x_i^2-x_i\), \(J\) the degree-\(D\) part of the closure they generate, and \(\ell\) lines, \(1\le\ell\le n\), line \(t\) holding \(1+E_t\) with \(E_t=-2x_t\) and protected class \(1\). The product line holds \(\prod_{t\le\ell}(1+E_t)\), with protected class \(1\) and combined error \(E_c=\prod_{t\le\ell}(1-2x_t)-1\), as in the combined-error reading of the multilinear repairs entry. A repair of errors \(E\) at parameter \(K\) is \(f\in V_K\) with \(a m f\in J\) for every axiom \(a\) and monomial \(m\) with \(\deg(am)\le D-K\), \(Ef\in J\) for each error, and \(f\notin J\).

Proposition (parity product repair). (a) If \(D\ge\ell+1\), the least degree of a common repair of \(E_1,\dots,E_\ell\) is \(\ell\), attained by \(\prod_{t\le\ell}(1-x_t)\). (b) If \(D\ge\ell+\lceil\ell/2\rceil\), the least degree of a repair of the combined error \(E_c\) is \(\lceil\ell/2\rceil\), attained by \(f_\ell=\prod_{i\le\lfloor\ell/2\rfloor}(1-x_{2i-1}-x_{2i})\), times \((1-x_\ell)\) when \(\ell\) is odd.

Proof. A polynomial \(g\) of degree at most \(D\) lies in \(J\) exactly when it vanishes on the cube: reducing \(x_i^2\) to \(x_i\) subtracts multiples \(m(x_i^2-x_i)\) of degree at most \(\deg g\), and a multilinear polynomial vanishing on the cube is zero. So for \(f\) of degree \(K\), soundness holds (each \(amf\) has degree at most \(D\) and vanishes on the cube), killing \(Ef\in J\) holds when \(\deg E+K\le D\) exactly when \(f\) vanishes where \(E\ne0\), and survival is \(f\) not vanishing everywhere on the cube.
(a) \(E_t(x)=-2x_t\) is nonzero exactly where \(x_t=1\), since \(2\ne0\). A common repair vanishes on the up-set with minimal sets \(\{1\},\dots,\{\ell\}\), whose transversal number is \(\ell\); by lem:transversal-killer-basis (c), with \(\ell+1\le D\), the least degree is \(\ell\), attained by \(\prod_t(1-x_t)\).
(b) On the cube \(1-2x_t=(-1)^{x_t}\), so \(E_c(x)=(-1)^{x_1+\dots+x_\ell}-1\) is \(-2\ne0\) where \(x_1+\dots+x_\ell\) is odd and \(0\) elsewhere; \(\deg E_c=\ell\), so killing is defined when \(\ell+K\le D\). A repair of \(E_c\) is therefore a polynomial nonzero somewhere on the cube that vanishes on the odd set \(O=\{x:x_1+\dots+x_\ell\text{ odd}\}\).
Upper bound. For \(a,b\in\{0,1\}\), \(1-a-b\) is \(0\) when \(a+b=1\) and \(\pm1\) otherwise. So \(f_\ell(x)\ne0\) exactly when \(x_{2i-1}=x_{2i}\) for each pair and, for odd \(\ell\), \(x_\ell=0\); then \(x_1+\dots+x_\ell\) is even. Hence \(f_\ell\) vanishes on \(O\), \(f_\ell(0)=1\), and \(\deg f_\ell=\lceil\ell/2\rceil\).
Lower bound. Let \(f\) be nonzero on the cube, vanish on \(O\), and have degree \(d\); its multilinear reduction \(g\) has degree at most \(d\) and the same values. Put \(y_i=1-2x_i\), an invertible affine change since \(2\) is a unit; on the cube \(y_i\in\{1,-1\}\), the functions are the multilinear polynomials in \(y\), uniquely, and a multilinear polynomial has the same degree in \(x\) and in \(y\) (the top part of \(y_S\) is \((-2)^{|S|}x_S\), and conversely). Write \(g=\sum_Sc_Sy_S\) and \(\chi=y_1\cdots y_\ell\), which is \(-1\) on \(O\) and \(1\) off it. Since \(g\) vanishes on \(O\), \(g=g\chi\) on the cube, and \(g\chi=\sum_Sc_Sy_{S\triangle[\ell]}\) because \(y_i^2=1\) there. By uniqueness \(c_S=c_{S\triangle[\ell]}\) for every \(S\). As \(g\ne0\), some \(c_S\ne0\), so \(c_{S\triangle[\ell]}\ne0\) and \(d\ge\max(|S|,|S\triangle[\ell]|)\ge\max(|S\cap[\ell]|,\ell-|S\cap[\ell]|)\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil\). \(\square\)

Proposition, part (c): the matching domain. Let \(Y\) be the partial matchings of \(m\ge\ell\) pigeons into \(h\) holes, \(h\ge\ell\) for even \(\ell\) and \(h\ge\ell+1\) for odd \(\ell\), with variables \(x_{ij}\); let \(J\) be the degree-\(D\) part of the closure of the Boolean, hole (\(x_{ij}x_{i'j}\)) and functionality (\(x_{ij}x_{ij'}\)) axioms, and take \(\ell\) lines with protected class \(1\) and diagonal errors \(E_t=-2x_{tt}\). If \(D\ge\ell+\lceil\ell/2\rceil\), the least degree of a repair of the combined error and the least degree of a common repair of the \(E_t\) are both \(\lceil\ell/2\rceil\): on \(Y\) the cube's saving disappears.

Proof of (c). A polynomial of degree at most \(D\) lies in \(J\) exactly when it vanishes on \(Y\): multilinear reduction stays within degree, the non-matching monomials are multiples of hole or functionality axioms, and the matching monomials \(x_N\) are independent on \(Y\) (\(x_N(M)=1\) exactly when \(N\subseteq M\), a triangular system). So, as on the cube, a repair of an error is a function nonzero on \(Y\) vanishing where the error is nonzero, and every function has a unique representative \(\sum_Nc_Nx_N\) over matchings \(N\), whose degree \(\max\{|N|:c_N\ne0\}\) is at most that of any polynomial representing it. The combined error is nonzero exactly on the matchings with an odd number of the edges \((t,t)\), \(t\le\ell\).
Upper bound. \(g_\ell=\prod_{i\le\lfloor\ell/2\rfloor}x_{2i-1,2i}\), times \(x_{\ell,\ell+1}\) for odd \(\ell\), is nonzero only on matchings containing all its edges; such a matching uses pigeon \(2i-1\) and hole \(2i\) (and pigeon \(\ell\)), so it contains no \((t,t)\) with \(t\le\ell\). Hence \(g_\ell\) is a common repair, and a combined one, of degree \(\lceil\ell/2\rceil\), nonzero on the matching of its own edges.
Lower bound. Let \(f\ne0\) on \(Y\) vanish on the odd-diagonal matchings, with representative \(\sum_Nc_Nx_N\) of degree at most \(\deg f\). Pick \(N\) with \(c_N\ne0\); let \(B\) be its edges other than the \((t,t)\), \(t\le\ell\), and \(T_B\) the indices \(t\le\ell\) whose pigeon and hole \(B\) leaves free, so that \(|T_B|\ge\ell-2|B|\) (each edge of \(B\) uses one pigeon and one hole) and \(N=B\cup\{(t,t):t\in U\}\) with \(U\subseteq T_B\). For \(S\subseteq T_B\) put \(f_B(S)=\sum_{B'\subseteq B}(-1)^{|B\setminus B'|}f(B'\cup\{(t,t):t\in S\})\), every argument being a matching. Since \(f(M)=\sum_{N'\subseteq M}c_{N'}\), Möbius inversion gives \(f_B(S)=\sum_{U'\subseteq S}c_{B\cup\{(t,t):t\in U'\}}\): as a function on the cube \(\{0,1\}^{T_B}\), \(f_B\) has the multilinear coefficient \(c_{B\cup\{(t,t):t\in U'\}}\) at \(x_{U'}\), nonzero at \(U'=U\), and degree at most \(\deg f-|B|\). Each \(f(B'\cup\{(t,t):t\in S\})\) has \(|S|\) diagonal edges among the first \(\ell\), so \(f_B\) vanishes where \(|S|\) is odd. By the lower bound of (b) on the cube \(\{0,1\}^{T_B}\) with all its \(|T_B|\) coordinates, \(\deg f-|B|\ge\lceil|T_B|/2\rceil\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil-|B|\) (when \(T_B=\varnothing\) the bound is \(0\)). So \(\deg f\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil\). A common repair also vanishes on the odd-diagonal matchings, so the same bound holds for it. \(\square\)

Structural reason. The combined error sees only the parity of the errors' supports, because each factor \(1+E_t\) is a sign; a parity set is cut out by half as many pairwise conditions as the union of the supports needs, and the sign basis shows no polynomial does better, since a function supported on even parity has a spectrum closed under complementing \([\ell]\). On \(Y\) a single edge variable \(x_{2i-1,2i}\) vanishes on the supports of two diagonal errors, so covering the union costs \(\lceil\ell/2\rceil\), the parity price; the Möbius coefficient charges each blocking edge to \(f\)'s degree, so neither reading goes lower.

Hypotheses, each with its step.

  • Characteristic other than \(2\): \(E_t\ne0\) where \(x_t=1\) in (a); \(E_c=-2\ne0\) on \(O\) in (b); the change \(y=1-2x\) in the lower bound. The upper bound \(f_\ell\) holds over every field (survival needs only \(f_\ell(0)=1\)). Over characteristic \(2\) the errors are \(0\).
  • \(D\ge\ell+1\) in (a), for lem:transversal-killer-basis (c) and killing \(E_tf\); \(D\ge\ell+\lceil\ell/2\rceil\) in (b), for killing \(E_cf\) at the attained degree. The lower bounds hold at every \(D\): they use only vanishing on the cube.
  • Boolean axioms: \(J\) is the vanishing ideal of the cube within degree; the Proposition is a domain-model statement, and a proper closure is not covered.
  • In (c): \(m\ge\ell\) pigeons and \(h\ge\ell\) holes for the diagonal errors; \(h\ge\ell+1\) for odd \(\ell\), for the last blocking edge of the upper bound only (the lower bound needs \(h\ge\ell\)); the hole and functionality axioms make \(J\) the vanishing ideal of \(Y\) within degree, the step that turns repairs into vanishing conditions; characteristic other than \(2\) for \(E_t\ne0\) where \(x_{tt}=1\), for \(E_c\) being nonzero exactly on the odd-diagonal matchings (\(-2\ne0\)), and through (b)'s lower bound. The common repair needs only \(D\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil+1\); \(D\ge\ell+\lceil\ell/2\rceil\) is what the combined repair needs.

Degenerate cases. \(\ell=1\): the combined error is \(E_1\), and both degrees are \(1\). \(\ell=0\) is excluded; with no lines \(E_c=0\) and the repair \(1\) has degree \(0\). Characteristic \(2\): excluded, the errors vanish. \(n>\ell\): the further variables do not enter, and the degrees are unchanged. In (c), \(\ell=1\): both degrees are \(1\), as on the cube; odd \(\ell\) with \(h=\ell\) holes: the lower bound \(\lceil\ell/2\rceil\) stands, the upper bound's last edge is missing and is not claimed.

Nonvacuity. Over \(\mathbb F_3\), \(n=\ell=3\), \(D=5\): \(f_3=(1-x_1-x_2)(1-x_3)\), of degree \(2\), is nonzero exactly at \((0,0,0)\) (value \(1\)) and \((1,1,0)\) (value \(-1\)), both of even parity, and vanishes on the four odd points; a common repair needs degree \(3\). The degree check below computes both least degrees for \(\ell\le6\), \(n\in\{\ell,\ell+1\}\), over \(\mathbb F_3\) and \(\mathbb F_5\): common \(\ell\) and combined \(\lceil\ell/2\rceil\) in all 24 cases. For (c), over \(\mathbb F_3\) with three pigeons, four holes, \(\ell=3\), \(D=5\): \(g_3=x_{12}x_{34}\), of degree \(2\), is nonzero only on matchings containing \((1,2)\) and \((3,4)\), which use pigeons \(1,3\) and holes \(2,4\) and so contain none of \((1,1),(2,2),(3,3)\); the hand computation below shows no linear repair, so both degrees are \(2\), where the cube gives \(3\) and \(2\). On \(g_3\)'s own coefficient \(N=B\) and \(T_B=\varnothing\), so the Möbius step's nonempty branch is exercised instead by \(\ell=2\) and \(f=1-x_{11}-x_{22}\): it vanishes on the matchings with exactly one of \((1,1),(2,2)\), is \(1\) on \(\varnothing\), and its coefficient on \(N=\varnothing\) gives \(B=\varnothing\), \(T_B=\{1,2\}\) and \(f_B=1-x_{11}-x_{22}\) on that cube, of degree \(1=\lceil2/2\rceil\); with \(B=\varnothing\) the alternating sum has one term. The inversion itself is exercised by the reviewer's witness \(\ell=3\), \(f=x_{12}(1-x_{33})\), at least three pigeons and three holes, \(D=5\): \(x_{12}=1\) excludes \((1,1)\) and \((2,2)\), and \(1-x_{33}\) is \(0\) when \((3,3)\) is present, so \(f\) vanishes on the odd-diagonal matchings and is \(1\) at \(\{(1,2)\}\); for \(N=\{(1,2),(3,3)\}\), \(c_N=-1\), \(B=\{(1,2)\}\), \(T_B=\{3\}\), and \(f_B(S)=f(\{(1,2)\}\cup\{(t,t):t\in S\})-f(\{(t,t):t\in S\})=1-x_{33}\), whose coefficient at \(U=\{3\}\) is \(-1=c_N\); the bound \(\deg f-1\ge\lceil1/2\rceil\) gives \(\deg f\ge2\), attained. Plainest bound. A nonzero multilinear polynomial of degree \(d\) is nonzero on at least \(2^{n-d}\) points of the cube. It gives the common degree \(\ell\) exactly (the support lies in \(\{x_1=\dots=x_\ell=0\}\), of size \(2^{n-\ell}\)) and for the combined repair only \(d\ge1\) (the support lies in the even set, of size \(2^{n-1}\)); the lower bound \(\lceil\ell/2\rceil\) is what the sign basis adds.

Baseline. Without an idea, a common repair of the factors' errors also repairs the product line (the trivial direction of the multilinear repairs entry), at degree \(\ell\), when the degrees fit: \(E_c\) has degree \(\ell\), so this needs \(D\ge2\ell\). The Proposition adds that the product line needs only \(\lceil\ell/2\rceil\), and no less, at \(D\ge\ell+\lceil\ell/2\rceil\). The saving is in the repair's degree \(K\), not in the closure degree: the combined reading needs \(D\ge\ell+\lceil\ell/2\rceil\) against \(\ell+1\) for the common one, and for \(\ell+1\le D<\ell+\lceil\ell/2\rceil\) the product line has no repair while the common repair exists.

Degree check. research/results/common_multiplier_parity_product_20261017/parity_product.py, committed before its run, computes each least degree as the least \(d\) at which the coefficients of degree at most \(d\) vanishing on the target set form a nonzero space, by exact rank over the prime field. It computes vanishing degrees of the two sets, which are the repair degrees in odd characteristic by the proof's first step. Over \(\mathbb F_3\) and \(\mathbb F_5\) it found common \(\ell\) and combined \(\lceil\ell/2\rceil\) in every case (parity_product.json, mismatches at odd \(p\): 0), with the support-size baseline printed beside each (\(\ell\) and \(1\)). Its control over \(\mathbb F_2\), asserted, gives the vanishing degree \(1\) of the parity set for every \(\ell\) (cut out by \(1+x_1+\dots+x_\ell\) there); there the errors vanish, so this is not a repair degree, and it shows that the lower bound's use of characteristic other than \(2\) is needed. The first run (parity_product_run1.json, the same degrees) neither printed the counts and baseline its docstring promised nor asserted the control; the review found this, and the script was corrected and rerun. It does not show anything beyond \(n\le7\) and these two primes; the proof covers the rest.

Against the record. Part (a) is lem:transversal-killer-basis (c) on singleton supports. The pairwise factor \(1-x_{2i-1}-x_{2i}\) has the form of the factor \(1-x_{12}-x_{22}\) in ex:top-degree-linear-killer's identity \((1-x_{12}-x_{22})(x_{10}-x_{21})\equiv x_{10}Q_2-x_{21}Q_1\) modulo the domain closure. The resemblance check also listed lem:module-repair-factorization and cor:multilinear-repair-scalar (repairs certified along a ring map, which do not cover a combined error), lem:top-window-twist-scalar (twists at the top window of the product pigeonhole system), lem:saving-monotonicity (savings of kernels, not the repair degree of one error) and claims on cube jets: none is a more general version or a special case, and none decides the next attempt on the matching domain.

New mathematics. prop:parity-product-repair: on the cube in characteristic other than \(2\), a product of \(\ell\) lines with errors \(-2x_t\) has a combined-error repair of degree exactly \(\lceil\ell/2\rceil\) at \(D\ge\ell+\lceil\ell/2\rceil\), while every common repair of the factors' errors has degree \(\ell\); the saving is \(\ell-\lceil\ell/2\rceil\) in the repair's degree, unbounded in \(\ell\), at the cost of a closure degree \(\ell+\lceil\ell/2\rceil\) against \(\ell+1\), and it comes from cancellation of errors in the product, which characteristic \(2\) excludes. On the pigeonhole matching domain the same errors on diagonal edges have common and combined degrees both \(\lceil\ell/2\rceil\): blocking edges give the common repair the parity bound, so for these cancelling errors the saving holds on the cube but not on the matching domain.

Selection gain. Unchanged for the composition's selection step: the saving is in the repair of one product line's combined error, not in the joint rank of the actual errors that selection measures, and it is shown only in a domain model.

Goal progress. Unchanged. The open statement asks for a saving in a proper protected quotient on the errors the goal's constructions produce; the Proposition is a domain-model saving on errors chosen to cancel, and its part (c) finds no saving on the pigeonhole matching domain, the domain model of the goal's pigeonhole systems, for diagonal errors, the only ones tried there. None at the goal's own parameters: no product line of Pang's or Braun's construction is shown to carry cancelling errors, the saving holds on the cube and disappears on the matching domain, and the proper closure is not reached. The cycle was spent on it because the item's open reading could have had no saving in odd characteristic anywhere, which would have closed the item; it has one on the cube, in the repair's degree at a larger closure degree, and none on the matching domain.

Matching domain, first by hand. Before part (c) was proved, its first cases were worked by hand; they are kept as its checks.

  • At \(\ell=2\). A common repair must vanish on matchings containing \((1,1)\) or \((2,2)\). The linear \(f=x_{12}\) does: a matching containing \((1,2)\) uses pigeon \(1\) and hole \(2\), so it contains neither; and \(f\) is \(1\) on \(\{(1,2)\}\). So the common degree is \(1\), and a combined repair, which must vanish on \(\{(1,1)\}\), also has degree at least \(1\): no saving at \(\ell=2\).
  • For every \(\ell\) with \(\ell+1\) holes, \(\prod_{i\le\lfloor\ell/2\rfloor}x_{2i-1,2i}\), times \(x_{\ell,\ell+1}\) when \(\ell\) is odd, is a common repair of degree \(\lceil\ell/2\rceil\) on \(Y\): each blocking edge uses the pigeon of one diagonal edge and the hole of another. So on \(Y\) the common repair already reaches the cube's combined degree, and the question is whether the combined degree is lower still.
  • At \(\ell=3\), with at least three pigeons and four holes. Let \(f=c+\sum_ea_ex_e\) vanish on the matchings with an odd number of the edges \((1,1),(2,2),(3,3)\). The singletons \(\{(t,t)\}\) give \(c+a_{tt}=0\) and the triple gives \(c+a_{11}+a_{22}+a_{33}=0\), so \(-2c=0\), \(c=0\) and \(a_{tt}=0\). Every other edge \(e=(i,j)\) is compatible with one of the three diagonal edges (it would have to meet pigeon or hole \(t\) for each \(t\le3\), and has one pigeon and one hole), so \(\{(t,t),e\}\) gives \(a_e=0\). Hence \(f=0\): the combined degree is \(2\), equal to the common one. No saving at \(\ell=3\).
  • A general bound, by the same restriction: if \(f\ne0\) on \(Y\) vanishes on the odd-diagonal matchings, take \(M\) with \(f(M)\ne0\), remove its diagonal edges to get \(M_0\), and let \(T\) be the indices \(t\le\ell\) whose pigeon and hole \(M_0\) leaves free. The matchings \(M_0\cup\{(t,t):t\in S\}\), \(S\subseteq T\), form a cube in \(Y\) (with at least \(\ell\) pigeons and \(\ell\) holes) on which \(f\) restricts to a nonzero function vanishing where \(|S|\) is odd, so prop:parity-product-repair's lower bound gives \(\deg f\ge\lceil|T|/2\rceil\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil-e\), with \(e\) the edges of \(M_0\) touching an index \(t\le\ell\). This bound left \(e\) unpaid; part (c) pays for it by extracting the coefficient of the blocking edges (Möbius inversion in \(B\)), whose degree \(|B|\) is charged to \(f\).

Smallest case. The next attempt is the proper closure: the functional pigeonhole system over \(\mathbb F_3\), whose pigeon axioms \(Q_i=1-\sum_jx_{ij}\) join the hole and functionality axioms, with the closure \(C\) of degree \(D\) containing the matching domain's \(J\). Killing is easier in \(C\) and survival harder, so neither bound of (c) transfers by itself.

The common repair \(x_{12}\) kills both errors in \(C\) already (\(x_{11}x_{12}\) and \(x_{22}x_{12}\) are axioms), so where \(x_{12}\notin C_3\) the common degree is at most \(1\), and it is \(1\) unless \(x_{11},x_{22}\in C_3\). At the product pigeonhole system's top degree the native count of monomial errors is the domain model's

17 October 2026 · Working proof, at the top degree of the product pigeonhole system · Top-degree native count. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, low reasoning).

Best outcome. At the goal's own parameters, the least number of native old functionals that certify a stacked error kernel in a proper closure of a system the goal uses, so that the cost of a native pairing is known there and not only in a domain model; the recorded results to beat are lem:native-rectangle-upper-bound and lem:native-detection-count, which bound that number on the cube (exactly known only at \(K=2\), \(L=1\) for \(a\le9\), check:native-upper-ranks).

Owed attempt. The item's last entry, the native upper bound, read in this session, named “the same count modulo a proper closure over \(\mathbb F_2\) at \(K>L\)”, first at \(K=2\), \(L=1\) on the product pigeonhole system with five pigeons and four holes at its top degree \(D=4\), its closure asserted proper first. It is made: the closure is proper, the count modulo it equals the domain model's, bracketed in general by (b), and at that instance it is \(6\) over every field, by (c).

General statement. prop:top-degree-native-count: for the product pigeonhole system at its top degree \(D=n\), over any field, and an error of degree \(e\ge1\) whose support satisfies the independence hypothesis of lem:top-degree-killer-transfer, the least number of old functionals that detect the error's kernel on \(V_K\) in rectangle forms at slack \(L\), with \(e+K+L\le n\), is the same modulo the proper closure as modulo the domain model; for a monomial error on distinct holes it lies between \(\lceil N(K)/N(L)\rceil\) and \(N(\max(K-L,0))\), \(N(d)=\sum_{k\le d}\binom{n-e}km^k\) for \(m\) pigeons, at every \(D\) with \(e+K+L\le D\le n\); at five pigeons, four holes, \(E=x_{00}\), \(K=2\), \(L=1\) it is \(6\).

Top-degree native count

Setting. Over a field \(k\), the product pigeonhole system with \(m\) pigeons and \(n\) holes has variables \(x_{ih}\), the Boolean axioms, the hole axioms \(x_{ih}x_{i'h}\) (\(i\ne i'\)) and the pigeon axioms \(Q_i=\prod_h(1-x_{ih})\) of degree \(n\). \(C\) is its degree-\(D\) closure and \(H\) the degree-\(D\) closure of the Boolean and hole axioms. \(Y\) is the set of hole-respecting assignments, each hole empty or holding one pigeon, a product domain \(\{0,1,\dots,m\}^n\). An old functional modulo a degree-\(D\) closure \(J\) is a linear functional on \(V_D\) vanishing on \(J\). Following lem:native-detection-count, for an error \(E\) of degree \(e\), \(U=V_K\) and slack \(L\) with \(e+K+L\le D\), old functionals \(\mu_1,\dots,\mu_c\) detect \(\ker T\), \(T(u)=[Eu]\), when \(\ker T\) is the set of \(u\in V_K\) with \(\mu_j(Euv)=0\) for all \(j\) and \(v\in V_L\); \(m_{\min}(J)\) is the least such number. \(S_E\subseteq Y\) is the support of \(E\) on \(Y\).

Proposition (top-degree native count). (a) At \(D=n\), \(1\notin C\); and if \(e\ge1\), the unplaced-pigeon indicators \(Q_1,\dots,Q_m\) restricted to \(Y\setminus S_E\) are linearly independent, and \(e+K+L\le n\) (so \(K+e\le n\)), then \(\ker T\) is \(\{u:u|_{S_E}=0\}\) modulo \(C\) and modulo \(H\), and the families of rectangle forms \(u,v\mapsto\mu(Euv)\) given by old functionals modulo \(C\) are exactly those given by old functionals modulo \(H\); hence \(m_{\min}(C)=m_{\min}(H)\). (b) If \(E\) is a monomial of degree \(e\ge1\) on \(e\) distinct holes, then at every \(D\) with \(e+K+L\le D\le n\), with \(N(d)=\sum_{k\le d}\binom{n-e}km^k\), \(\lceil N(K)/N(L)\rceil\le m_{\min}(C)\le N(\max(K-L,0))\). (c) At \(m=5\), \(n=4\), \(E=x_{00}\), \(K=2\), \(L=1\), \(D=4\), \(m_{\min}(C)=6\) over every field.

Proof. (a) By lem:top-degree-axiom-inertness, for the product pigeonhole system and \(D\le n\), \(H\) is the degree-\(D\) part of the vanishing ideal of \(Y\) and the members of \(C\) of degree below \(D\) are those of \(H\). So \(1\notin C\): it has degree \(0(b) For \(DLower bound. lem:native-detection-count (a) gives \(r\le m_{\min}\dim Z_L\), with \(r=\dim V_K|_{S_E}=N(K)\) and \(Z_L\) the span of \(Ev\) modulo the closure in degree \(e+L\); modulo \(H\) it is isomorphic through \(v\mapsto Ev\) to \(V_L|_{S_E}\), of dimension \(N(L)\), and modulo \(C\), a larger closure, its dimension is at most \(N(L)\), which only strengthens the bound. Upper bound. For each \(y\in S_E\) with a set \(F_y\) of at most \(\max(K-L,0)\) nonempty free holes, let \(B_y\) be the points of \(S_E\) that agree with \(y\) on \(F_y\) and have at most \(L\) nonempty holes in \(F\setminus F_y\), and \(\nu_y=\sum_{z\in B_y}\delta_z\), extended to an old functional as above. The monomials of degree at most \(L\) in the variables of \(F\setminus F_y\) evaluate unitriangularly on \(B_y\), so \(V_L|_{B_y}\) is every function on \(B_y\), and the forms \(\nu_y(Euv)=\sum_{z\in B_y}u(z)v(z)\), \(v\in V_L\), give every value of \(u\) on \(B_y\). A point with \(s\le K\) nonempty free holes lies in \(B_y\) for \(y\) its restriction to \(\min(s,\max(K-L,0))\) of them, so the \(B_y\) cover the determining set of degree-\(K\) functions, and the forms vanishing gives \(u|_{S_E}=0\). The number of centres \(y\) is \(N(\max(K-L,0))\).
(c) By (b), \(m_{\min}\ge\lceil91/16\rceil=6\). For six, each of the sums below is extended to an old functional modulo \(C\) by (a): let \(\nu_0\) be the sum over the \(16\) points of \(S_E\cong\{0,\dots,5\}^3\) with at most one nonempty free hole; its forms recover the coefficients of \(u\) of degree at most one. The quadratic coefficients \(c_e\) are indexed by the \(75\) edges \(e\) of \(K_{5,5,5}\), on the vertices (hole, pigeon). For an edge set \(G\), let \(\nu_G\) be the sum over the weight-two points of its edges; with \(v=1\) and \(v=x_k\) its forms give, modulo the known lower coefficients, the total \(\sum_{e\in G}c_e\) and the star sums \(\sum_{e\in G,\,e\ni k}c_e\). For \(G\) a spanning graph on the \(15\) vertices whose components are odd unicyclic, these determine \(c_G\): in characteristic other than \(2\) the unsigned incidence map has kernel of dimension \(|G|-15+(\text{bipartite components})=0\); over a field of characteristic \(2\), for \(G\) one odd \(15\)-cycle, the kernel is the cycle's indicator, on which the total is \(15\cdot1\ne0\). With the vertices identified with \(\mathbb Z_{15}\) (hole \(t\bmod3\), pigeon \(\lfloor t/3\rfloor+1\) of the five), the difference classes \(\pm1,\pm2,\pm4,\pm7\) are Hamiltonian \(15\)-cycles and \(\pm5\) is five triangles, all between different holes, together the \(75\) edges; this decomposition gives \(1+5=6\) functionals of rank \(91\) in characteristic other than \(2\). In characteristic \(2\) the triangles fail (their piece has rank \(11\)), and the union of classes \(\pm1\) and \(\pm5\) is split into two Hamiltonian cycles (listed in six_functionals.json), giving five Hamiltonian pieces. The forms' matrix has integer entries, so its rank over a field of characteristic \(2\) is its rank over \(\mathbb F_2\), which six_functionals.py computes as \(91\). \(\square\)

Structural reason. At the top degree the pigeon axioms are \(m\) functionals' worth of constraints, the unplaced indicators, and when those stay independent off the error's support, the points there absorb them; the rectangle forms of an error never look off its support, so for such errors the proper closure costs a native certificate nothing over the domain model. The bound in (b) is the cube's, with two states per coordinate replaced by \(m+1\) per free hole; and at \(K=2\), \(L=1\) the count is a decomposition of the complete multipartite graph of quadratic coefficients into pieces whose star sums are injective, as on the cube.

Hypotheses, each with its step.

  • \(D=n\), the top degree, in (a): \(C=H+\operatorname{span}\{Q_i\}\) uses that every pigeon axiom has degree exactly \(D\); below \(n\), \(C=H\), and (b) holds there too.
  • \(e\ge1\) and the independence of the \(Q_i\) on \(Y\setminus S_E\): the extension step only; a constant error has \(S_E=Y\) and is excluded. \(e+K+L\le D\): the forms are defined, and it gives \(K+e\le n\) for the kernels' agreement.
  • A monomial error on distinct holes, in (b) and (c): \(S_E\) a product domain with \(E=1\) on it. The field: any; in (c), characteristic \(2\) uses the repaired decomposition.

Degenerate cases. \(L=0\): the bounds give \(N(K)\le m_{\min}\le N(K)\), every form being one linear condition. \(K\le L\): \(m_{\min}=1\), one sum over all points with at most \(L\) nonempty free holes. \(e=n\): \(S_E\) is one point and \(m_{\min}=1\). A constant error: excluded by \(e\ge1\). \(m=1\) pigeon: \(S_E\) is a cube, and (b) is lem:native-rectangle-upper-bound's bound for one error whose support fixes coordinates to \(1\).

Nonvacuity. Five pigeons, four holes, \(D=4\), over any field, \(E=x_{00}\) (pigeon \(0\) in hole \(0\); \(e=1\)), \(K=2\), \(L=1\), so \(e+K+L=4\le D\). \(C\) is proper by (a). \(S_E\cong\{0,\dots,5\}^3\), and \(N(0)=1\), \(N(1)=1+3\cdot5=16\), \(N(2)=16+3\cdot25=91\), so \(6\le m_{\min}\le16\) by (b), and \(m_{\min}=6\) by (c). The independence holds (the empty assignment and, for each pigeon, the assignment placing only it in hole \(1\) lie off \(S_E\)). Plainest bound. Point evaluations on the \(91\) points with at most two nonempty free holes, each extended to an old functional by (a), detect the kernel with \(v=1\), so \(m_{\min}\le91\), and lem:native-detection-count (a) gives \(6\); the ball sums give \(16\), and (c) attains \(6\).

Six-functional check. research/results/common_multiplier_native_count_20261017/six_functionals.py, committed before its run, builds the six functionals' \(96\) forms on the \(91\) coefficients and computes their rank, over \(\mathbb F_2\) with tools/f2_span.py: the circulant decomposition has rank \(91\) over \(\mathbb F_3\) and \(\mathbb F_5\) and \(87\) over \(\mathbb F_2\) (the control, which shows the rank can fall short), and the repaired one \(91\) over \(\mathbb F_2\), \(\mathbb F_3\) and \(\mathbb F_5\) (six_functionals.json). It does not show the count at other parameters; the general formula below is a suggestion.

Joint-savings goal review: survival of a common killer as the working target

17 October 2026 · Route review (goal-level), assessment, no claim · Joint-savings goal review. Produced by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, low reasoning).

Where we stand. Six research entries since the band review. On the functional pigeonhole system, below half the holes, every kernel question sits at its window's top (lem:closure-degree-locality), and two dense linear errors gained no killer from the pigeon axioms (check:dense-linear-kernels); at the top degree \(D=2\) of four pigeons and three holes a linear killer outside every single representative's domain side exists (ex:top-degree-linear-killer), and for every choice of representatives the saving modulo a closure is at most its domain kernels' saving (lem:saving-monotonicity). The other four entries tested readings that could escape these bounds: native certificates on the cube (lem:native-rectangle-upper-bound) and at the product system's top degree (prop:top-degree-native-count, where the proper closure adds nothing); repairs of products of lines certified along multiplication, which are scalar (cor:multilinear-repair-scalar); and products whose errors cancel, which save repair degree on the cube and not on the matching domain (prop:parity-product-repair).

Question. Does the line have a mechanism for the second open statement, a structural joint saving modulo a proper protected quotient that improves a multiplier budget, and if not, what is it stuck on?

General statement. The line's general claim is joint-error-savings itself; the period's registered claims bound it from above: lem:saving-monotonicity makes every saving modulo a closure at most the saving of the domain kernels, and with lem:domain-model-stacked-rank and ex:support-saving-not-inherited the stacked proper rank is at most the restriction rank \(\dim U|_S\) to the union of the supports.

Obstacle

The line is stuck on lower bounds modulo the proper closure. Every recorded tool gives the joint action of errors from above: domain models give the stacked rank \(\dim U|_S\), and the proper closure can only lower it (saving monotonicity, the support bound). What the composition needs, through lem:exact-common-kernel-selection, is a common killer of degree at most \(K\) outside the closure, that is \(\operatorname{rank}(\rho,q)>\operatorname{rank}\rho\) modulo \(C\): a statement that a killer survives. The domain model supplies killers (lem:pang-family-killer, the blocking-edge products of prop:parity-product-repair, transversal products). Their survival in a proper closure is known in special cases: at the product system's top degree, where the closure is the domain model plus span conditions the support absorbs (lem:top-degree-killer-transfer, prop:top-degree-native-count), and for one Pang family, whose Fermat killer \(q\) survives unless it lies in the closure's degree-one part, a one-line membership. What has no general statement is survival where the summed condition fails, for several families at once, below the top degree, where the pigeon axioms act in every window; and no recorded result says which closure killers exist beyond the domain's there, except one identity (ex:top-degree-linear-killer). Reading the recorded transfer results for this, and the period's six entries, found none.

Falsification attempt. Try to show the endpoint impossible on the line's instances: if, on every proper closure the line uses, the kernels modulo the closure were the domain kernels plus the closure's degree-\(K\) part, then every saving would be the saving of the spaces \(\operatorname{Ann}_H+J\), at most the domain's union-of-supports saving and computed from it, and the endpoint, which excludes that mechanism, would have no instance there. The attempt fails: ex:top-degree-linear-killer is a killer outside every single representative's domain side, so the closure can add killers; but it is one error at the top degree, and no joint version is recorded. The falsification stays open; it is the Decisive test below in another form.

Architecture review

Necessary target. The weakest endpoint that serves the goal is unchanged from the band review: one nontrivial unbounded family of actual paid errors on which a common killer of degree at most \(K\) is certified outside the protected quotient below the summed-rank budget, by a mechanism other than supports, domination or products of killers, after all composition costs. Downstream. Through lem:exact-common-kernel-selection and thm:certified-repair-composition, such a certificate gives a repair with a multiplier of degree \(K\), which is the second open statement itself.

Extra requirements. The route demands more than the target in one way the blind stage made plain: it measures savings, a difference of ranks, where the composition needs only the survival of one common killer, a one-sided statement. A saving modulo the closure is bounded above by the domain's, so a saving-based route needs a lower bound on a difference of ranks; a survival-based route needs a lower bound on one rank, \(\operatorname{rank}(\rho,q)\), against an upper bound already recorded, \(\operatorname{rank}\rho\le\dim U|_S\). The demand for savings can be weakened to the demand for survival, provided the survival is where the summed condition fails (\(\sum_ar_a\ge h\)) and by a mechanism the endpoint admits; otherwise it is met trivially, by the summed condition or by one family's Fermat killer.

Polynomial numbering transfer and a linear criterion
